Dying can be frustrating, disappointing or simply funny. Every now and then after bad runs one can loose his cool and botch up subsequent runs by the second, so it's better to give it a pause. Brute-forcing was not a good tactic for me.
Ingeniously well done level generation which almost always makes the game beatable but often will success be directly connected to early loot crates. Not as often as your frequent stupid faults though. Jetpack-Shotgun combo is the supreme and most satisfying way to go but many times you'll have to do without them.
Mechanics are at the focal point and beating the game neither the easy or hard way will be possible without mastering them. Once you get the feel of movement, level patterns and the right enemy tactics though, things will become much more manageable.

The game play, if you can call it that, is basically a series of horrendous mini games, covered in internet memes and jokes that you will hate even more after playing this game. In order to make up the last $200 you play in three free to play games inside this game which generates coins for you, one of those mini games is a runner (hint! The game doesn’t have a graphical look, nor does the UI do it any favors either. Now I know this isn’t meant to be a serious game, but it’s on Steam which is a world wide store front!  But the menus in this game, oh god the menus. It is probably the worst UI I have ever come across, you have to see it to believe it.  The game’s sound effects and soundtrack are again, just pure awful; mute this game asap. Don’t put your ears through the torture.
Summer Sale has no difficulty levels at all. You will be able to 100% this game in less than half an hour. Yes you heard it, you can finish everything there is to do in this game in less time than it takes me to go for a number two.

Want to mute the music? Better restart the game. Want to change any option that matter? You better restart the game. Just no. it doesn’t even support 1080p.
I’m sorry Steam Community, but is it just me who is getting sick to death of this absolutely awful games making it onto our beloved store front? This is a browser game at best. There is no way on god’s green earth that this game should be on Steam. It is daylight robbery to have this game cost 79p!  Do yourself a huge favor and never look at, never mind purchase this game. Portal Knights is, at its base, Minecraft meets a vanilla RPG. There's something refreshing about it-- it's a little unpolished, but there's potential there for something greater.
You'd want this game if Minecraft left an itch for something with a bit more RPG, and you'd already played Terraria through, and probably Starbound...
High points; first time through, the worlds are pretty fun and interesting for a romp around. Structures can make a world much more interesting.  RPG elements are easily learned, fun to experiment with and flexible (resets for stats, talents are freely interchangeable). Spells can be used by all three classes leading to interesting variations between them.
Low points; early access means unpolished, the crafting system can be a bit of a grind and the notion of world-restricted items in a sandbox game seems a bit redundant. Personally, I need to take a break once in a while as the camera can get out of hand in tight spaces while in third person, and first person view is a bit stifling. Still, these areas will likely see improvement as time goes on.
The developers seem consistently involved and I joined after a large content patch which has presumably livened things up.

It's great to finally be able to play as Team RWBY! The voice acting is great and this game has incredible potential. I haven't played for very long, and I have only played as Yang so far, but I already have a lot of criticism of the game:
-The combat is both simplistic and overly difficult at the same time. You just click on your mouse for melee and ranged attacks, but it's the other aspects of combat that are frustratingly difficult. It's difficult to dodge in a direction because of the way the camera moves, and the fact that you can only build up your special attack gauge by combat is frustrating
-You die way too easily. I don't know if it's because the combat is difficult for me, but it feels like I die with only two hits, which is frustrating as hell
-The running animation is slow and wonky, but it's early access so I'll excuse that
-You can't pause the game. I understand that it's because it's multiplayer, but it also makes me wish that there was a single player mode so that I can try out all the characters without the pressure that online multiplayer brings
-You can't turn down the volume for special effects and combat so the game is L O U D
-There should be an introduction to the combat. Being thrown directly into combat isn't very beneficial in learning how to incorporate dodging and special attacks into combat, and a tutorial would really help
That being said, this game DID only come out a few days ago, AND it's still in very early access. And, like I said before, it has so much potential. I really hope that later on we'll be able to play as other teams and characters in RWBY. If you're a fan of RWBY, you should play it in order to give the developers much needed feedback. If you're not too into RWBY or haven't ever seen it, you should wait until it's later in development.

NOTE: THIS IS EARLY ACCESS & MY FIRST IMPRESSIONS! Overall RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a solid game for early access. The game plays like dynasty warriors, which they said, with objective gameplay areas towards the end of the levels. However I believe the missions will become similar and get old when they implement newer levels.
Combat in the game is solid and the abilities for the characters suit them well. For as hetic as the combat can get I wish they would implement a lock-on system, because its hard to focus on a single enemy when using melee attacks. The long range, gun, attacks our hard to target with unless you play as Yang or Wiess.  The enemies are fun to fight and increase in difficulty as you progress, as every game, but become difficult to solo 1v1 against the higher tier enemies. The high tier do not stagger on normal attacks and only on special attacks that at our upgraded to stagger, making it difficult to string combos
The combo system is interesting, however if you play as Blake stay near the back and shoot your gun and refill the entire super. The attacks becomes button mashing, with the occassional shoot attack to mix it up. I hope they add more combo options to add some more dynamic to the game.
The soundeffect volume is unadjustable which seems like a flaw if you want to hear the voices in combat.
Ruby Rose: probably the best character because of her attack range and AoE specials. When she is upgraded with her horizontal spin and AoE blast. Want to learn the game with ease play as her
Wiess Schnee: Has 1 AoE with 2 focus attacks 1 melee and 1 ranged. Her AoE is probably her best when upgraded for its healing and freezing effect. Her xxxxy attack when upgraded with the special freezes her oppponents. Her other 2 specials are good for the fact it adds diversity, other than that ehh.
Blake Belladonna: Probably the most lacking for the fact her aftershadow becomes worse as it upgrades. her dash strike is the best because it can be spammed when its upgraded along with a bigger super meter. Her blade beam is lacking in power, like all of her abilities. Her gun attack is her best because it is the fastest to fire and its range is godly.
YangsomethingLong: packs a big punch at close range, her gun covers a huge area in close quarters, her AoE is not as good as Ruby or Wiess but its still good. Her close range attacks are good without being upgraded and can give that edge when they are.
Ranking for characters goes Ruby,Wiess,Yang,Blake interms of power and abilities.

Ah Brothers,
A gem among my ever growing steam library.
My relationship with brothers is much like a classic love story, where the guy gets the girl and they enjoy pleasant happiness in each others company for a short while, until the fateful day comes where she is hit by a red bus and the boy spends the next few hours crying and browsing through steam fan art of her until he falls asleep and completely forgets about her the next day and continues his life as normal (My father often told me stories like that before bed)
To break the above down, Brothers is amazing and beautiful in every possible way and you shall have a huge amount of fun with it for a very short amount of time, which is in this case, 3 hours.
In 3 hours you can
-Run a marathon at an extremely good pace
-Roast a turkey
-blow up 720 balloons by mouth if you have a friend with you
I could go on but I know you're dying to hear what's so great about this game and have already read a fair bit into this review and are getting slightly tired of my feeble attempts at some form of humor to brighten up your day.
Brothers is a puzzle and story based "single player co-operational game" (take a minute to get your head around that concept before you continue) with outstanding style, gameplay, and soundtrack to give you an immensely immersive experience. When you consider that a film director was part of the core development team this is hardly surprising. This game truly feels more like a controllable movie, given the beauty and effort put in to make it more than just a game. You will be taken through crowded forests, beautiful farmlands, ice lakes, giant valleys and many more scenic landscapes on your journey. The story is simple but beautiful enough for you to put down your controller d of the game and just cry for a while (you wont feel like a PU$$Y, I promise).
The gameplay is another feature which stands out for me. The control scheme is just so tight, the puzzles are interesting and varied and by no means either too trivial too difficult.

So it's finally here the second game made by Matt Stone and Trey Parker that continues the story of the new kid who became king of elfs and wizards at the end of Stick of Truth. Now it's the next day, and the Coon has arrived from the "future" to ask the gang for help save Scrambles the missing cat for a 100$ reward in a town with a skyrocketing crime rate which turns out to be the result of a sinister political plot.
Now let's get to the good stuff by first answering the question: Is the game good? The answer is of course yes if you're a fan of the series and know what kind of humor you get from a South Park game, however it's unfortunatly a step down from its predecessor. The story is a bit weaker this time around and the jokes feel a bit more tame this time around though they do poke some fun at the madness that is identity politics, police brutality, race relations just to mention some aspects you might have a grin at.
The customization has been improved somewhat with more items to create and pick up as well as giving the player the abillity to multiclass which is something the devs should be given props for.
Unfortunatly the game has some major bugs and glitches that for some players can be completely game breaking, I was lucky to not encounter any of those I did however occationally encounter a glitch after doing a time fart which caused me to be unable to proceed combat as well as one black screen after a cutscene which i luckily got past by doing the segment again and skipping that cutscene entirely.
In terms of difficulty the game still is a bit too easy even on mastermind level. I only really had some slight problems during two or three boss battles where things got kind of challenging one of them being Morgan Freeman, that being said though; The new combat system does make it a little harder than the previous game
This game oddly enough is way harder on my machine than Stick of Truth often taking up massive amounts of resources on my processor.
The game really isn't that much longer than the Stick of Truth and you should be able to finish it in 12-14 hours
Another thing that irks me is that unlike Stick of Truth this game has very limited replayabillity value since you can easily do all the achievement and try all the classes in one playthrough wheras getting all the achievements in SoT was much harder since you had to pay attention not to miss any chinpokemons and/or items which you could only get during that one section and if you wanted to try all the classes you HAD to play through it again
So is this game worth buying?
Yes, however you might want to wait for a price drop, I'm having a really hard time finding a justification for its current price tag but if you're a fan of the show it's definitely a title you should pick up at some point

Short version: If you bought the first one, and enjoyed it, buy this one too. There are changes, but they're all good things.
Long version: I'm going to assume you've played the first game, although it isn't necessary to do so. This game tells it's own independent story, so you can jump into the franchise on the second game, no problem.
It follows the New Kid (you), on a journey to become a superhero, working with Cartman's "crime fighting" organization. Your main opposition is various townspeople and characters (fighting Mrs. Broflovski was a particular high point), and most fights are just as hilarious as the story itself. The game is littered with references to past South Park episodes, while also having a large repetoire of new jokes as well. It's an undeniably funny game, possibly moreso than the first, imo.
As with both games, though, the jokes start to wear a little thin. You hear most of them multiple times. I think this is a problem with no realistic solution though...just thought I'd mention it.
Combat: The system of the previous game is gone the way of the Dodo bird. Fights now take place on a grid, still turn-based combat, where you may move your character within a certain range of squares, and use abilities that target various short/med/long/AOE enemies. There is no blocking, but you hit a button to recover after a hit (and earn ultimate points, more on that in a sec). Through the game, you'll earn awesome, often funny, abilities and items that enhance the gameplay, making it very great for those who enjoy strategy in games. You team mates and enemies talk during every fight, and some of it is pretty damn funny. Unfortunately, you'll likely hear every qoute multiple times...so the jokes lose their luster.
Performing attacks, and various other things, fills a bar at the top of the screen. Once full, you can use 1 ultimate ability. Every fighting character has 1, and they're all powerful abilities that could be the difference between winning or losing.
Customization: My favorite thing in any game that has it. Customization has been slightly improved, offering plenty of costume options that can be mixed and matched. Personally, found most of them pretty dull or ridiculous, but they're there nonetheless. There is a trait (artifact) system that increases your power, and modifies various attributes (+allied health %, or +knockback combo damage %), there are multiple classes along with another set that you can choose a second class from. Each class has it own abilities, but your own are the only ones you can customize (team mate abilites are fixed).
The graphics are exactly what you'd expect. They perfectly match the art of the show.
Sound is great. Everything is voiced by the actors from the show, and most music in the game is from various songs they've done over the course of the show. Music not from the show tends be to great, epic superhero music. Really suites the game well. NOTE: I did once have a glitch where the game switched to the "Cash for Gold" song, and played it on a loop for over 30 mins. Whenever the music was supposed to change, it would change with the "Cash for Gold" song playing over the top of it. Honestly found this pretty damn funny.
Controls: I play almost every PC game on mouse and keyboard, and this one is a little odd to play, at times. It's totally managable, don't get me wrong, but you're gonna have to get used to some unusual combinations of key-presses (that require you to take your hands off the mouse). A lot of controls have changed from the first game, FYI. Overall, no big deals here.
Performance: For what it's worth, I got it running at 144 fps on High (lol). I've seen a couple of the glitches other people are complaining about, but nothing that interfered with me playing the game. I'm referring to the sound not lining up with the speaking animations, for example. Sometimes tutorial boxes pop up with no text in them. No crashes, BSODs, or black screens came up during my time. My PC is kind of a monster, though, so maybe that prevented some of the issues people are having.
SCORE- 8/10

Torchlight II is a fun and enjoyable dungeon game.
It's layout is similar to the Diablo style, and features 4 classes ; Engineer, Bereserker, Outlander, and Embermage. Each class has its clear ups and downs, and gameplay styles. Engineer plays a Tank role, doing heavy damage and sustaining multiple enemies. Berserker plays the role of classic Mellee, fast attack speeds and OK health. Embermage obviously is a Magician/Wizard character, and has a large variety of spells. Finally, Outlander is the Ranged Class, and uses classic weapons such as bows, and crossbows, but also incorporates Rifles and Pistols, with a nice, steady class build. All of the weapons are useable with each class, but more are (obviously) more useful than others depending on the role.
The layout of the world has great variety, and has everything from Zombie-Infested temples to Withered Deserts. It has clever details, and an almost cartoon-ish feel to it. Its not the etchy graphics of Diablo. The lighting is amazing, and has clear contrast against the landscape.
The enemies of Torchlight II also show great variety, although the 'Champion' monsters are just enlarged versions of common monsters for the area. Most monsters are undead creatures, but it still shows variety, instead of just saying "Skeleton" it says "Skeletal General" or something similar. The game even takes in local wildlife, like frogs. The enemies vary from each area, but some are common and occur in a lot of areas.
Finally, the game sports numerous pets, and are changeable through feeding them fish. You have to fish, to obtain fish. Occasionally, you might get a "Warsnout" which makes your pet a Jackal for 5 minutes. Then, if you catch a Big/Large fish, it increases the amount of time. THEN, if you catch a Giant fish, it permanently effects the pet. Sometimes you might catch fish containing and item, which is random. Most of the mods are also Pet-Related.
To conclude, Torchlight II is an amazing game, featuring 4 classes, a variety of landscapes, a variety of monsters, an aresenal of weaponry, and a seemingly never-ending supply of fish in the ponds.
A great, and affordable, dungeon crawler that borrows a lot of elements from the Diablo franchise. The art style is a little World of Warcraft cartoony, but it works for the genre.

The goal of Portal Knights is… to get to the end? It’s not very clear. Maybe because it’s still in early access, or maybe because I haven’t gotten past the second level. There are multiple levels, that are like floating islands, that you travel between to gather material. It is required travel, as each level only has a few of each type of resource. So that does lead itself to loading times. Overall, it’s an open sandbox game, with a lot of crafting (there are recipes, so you don’t have to sit there rearranging sticks in 100 different ways). You get to level up you character and spend attribute points, and talent points that you can rearrange on the fly. Once you choose a class, that character is stuck to it, but the attribute points can be reset with a craftable potion. The worlds are separate from the character, so you could have all three classes, and swap between them in the same world. This also means your personal inventory also travels with you, so you could take your high-level character into a brand new world and get a jump start. It does seem fun so far, just need to set myself some goals, and see where the game takes me.
Multiplayer is drop in drop out. Can only join steam friends or do lan play. The host starts up his own game, gets loaded into a world, and the other players just click join and pop on in. I had no issues with this process. Didn’t have to do any set up, there was no lag. Usually it takes an hour to get a multiplayer game going for all sorts of reasons, didn’t have any of those issues here.
Obviously this game will change, and if I keep playing it, I will probably update as time goes on.

Ok so here's the bottomline:  It's Mortal Kombat.  I've been playing it since the Coin Op days of MK1 and beyond.  I used to get into VERY heated arguements (and even the rare shoving match) with kids at the arcades when they would constantly b**h fight (i.e. corner fighting, constant sweeping or uppercutting.  Or Mileena's drop kick...).  So I really love this series.  I've taken the good with the bad and even droppped off with MK4 and Shaolin Monks.  But this game pretty damn sweet.  The story was good, the fighting is good, the different fighting styles bring a breath of fresh air to the tried and true system they've been improving upon since the beginning.  NetherRealm has put together one of the finest Mortal Kombat games in history, if I do say so myself.
HIGH VOLTAGE on the other hand...  they have produced one of the worst console to PC ports I've ever dealt with, hands down.  I managed to get through the story and mess with some other game modes before the two most recent patches.  After I receieved those updates, my sound is completely screwed up (not all effects and no voices are coming through any channels) the lag and choppiness has gotten worse and it freezes completely at random whether there's heavy particle action on screen or I and my opponent are just standing there.  Many bugs to fix and I'm not so confident we'll see a huge improvement anytime soon seeing as how the update for just one character was 16g and my problems got worse.
So why do I recomment it?  Because it's a good game and it deserves to be played.  In the hope that they'll fix the problems it has, of course.  It really is worth the money because it is such a great game.  But because of a poor job done by the porting company, I would advise waiting until the problems they have (if ever) get fixed.

Brothers is a puzzle and story based "single player co-operational game" (take a minute to get your head around that concept before you continue) with outstanding style, gameplay, and soundtrack to give you an immensely immersive experience. When you consider that a film director was part of the core development team this is hardly surprising. This game truly feels more like a controllable movie, given the beauty and effort put in to make it more than just a game. You will be taken through crowded forests, beautiful farmlands, ice lakes, giant valleys and many more scenic landscapes on your journey. The story is simple but beautiful enough for you to put down your controller d of the game and just cry for a while (you wont feel like a PU$$Y, I promise).
The gameplay is another feature which stands out for me. The control scheme is just so tight, the puzzles are interesting and varied and by no means either too trivial too difficult.
Brothers is a little gem that stands out for being totally awesome in its own way, so if you happen to already own an xbox controller and see this baby on sale, don't hesitate to pick this baby up

I'm not really sure how exactly should I review this game. But I want to do it anyway.
What is this game?
It's an adventure game where you play as two brothers who are on an important quest.
First of all, the controls... they are a bit confusing at times, but interesting - you control each brother with a separate trigger and analog stick on the controller.
Something... as if you played some coop adventure game like the Lego games, but by yourself, controlling both players at the same time. Yeah, it is as confusing as it sounds at first (at least this game has no attack or jump buttons, or it would've been insane and mind breaking).
And yes, the game REALLY requires a controller, since without it the whole concept of the game breaks and some "qte's", such as spinning two valve handles with the analog sticks are just not possible with a keyboard.
Still, the game was insanely overhyped for me, the gameplay was repetitive and the puzzles were obvious. The game really is easy and I don't know if it's even possible to die from something in it.
As it goes for the story... nothing really unusual, but it's nice and rather relatable. And it doesn't get boring for 3+ hours it takes to beat this game.
The graphics and music are often really good and they create a really nice atmosphere at times.
Overall, it's a nice little adventure game that brings something unique and interesting to the table. It might not be worth it for its full price tag for somebody, but as it goes for the sale price, it's definitely worth two or three dollars (depending on your region).

Tekken 7 PC
Graphics-wise we didn't get a downgraded version, if you own a mid-high range video card released within these 2 years your experience likely will be better than on PS4 Pro. Battle loading times on consoles range from 25 to 40 seconds, you'll likely achieve better results.
Ultra settings are above console versions, chromatic aberration (rainbow effect on the edges) can be disabled via an ini tweak (see
), a motion blur toggle is available. Runs even on integrated graphics.
Supports keyboard, dinput (up to 8) and xinput (up to 4) gamepads. You can rebind everything.
Awesome, fun and engaging. I can't say that I ever cared about the story in fighting games, but when it's presented in such great manner I can only say positive things about it. You get to explore the relations between a chunk of Tekken characters, you can see them talking (which is a rare sight), storytelling switches to fighting seamlessly. You get various difficulties and beginner assists. There are also character stories which include background info, one battle and amusing ending per character. If you ever played Ace Combat 4 then the main story presentation might remind you of it.
The base game provides you with weeks worth of content and high amount of replayability. Roster is big enough for you to find a character that you like. The amount of stages isn't big, but there's a lot of detail put into some and there are stages with surfaces that react to damage.
Personally, I've had a rather good online experience.
As a beginner myself I consider this game to be beginner-friendly. You're given the option to scale the difficulty to your liking, lowest difficulty (from what I've seen) is super easy and even on normal in story mode you get assists which you can use (the choice is yours). I would suggest checking out Treasure Mode and finding character which you like or at least a character with whom you'd be able to mash effectively. Start from there, eventually you will learn effective moves and remember enemy attack patterns. All you need is time and effort.
The music is powerful, modern and energizing, but might not be everyone's cup of tea. There's a lot of dubstep included, which won't make everyone happy.
On the bright side the audio adjusts to what's happening on the screen, sound design is absolutely fantastic and there is some variety in the music genres.
The sound effects are awesome, have an impact and are satisfying.
There's an in-game currency which you get by just playing the game. Fastest way to get it would be Treasure Battle or Online Tournaments. With the currency you can unlock cosmetics and gallery items (videos and artwork from all Tekken games).
You have two types of ranks: online and offline. Each character has its own rank. You can increase a character's online rank by winning online ranked matches against another real players. Upon reaching a certain threshold all of the characters get an online rank boost.
Offline rank is more simple. You play Arcade Battle or Treasure Battle with a particular character and you can increase the rank for the character by winning Promotion Matches.
When it comes to fighting games I'm an amateur. I can tell you the difference between the other Tekken games. 7 introduces Rage Mode: when your HP hits 25% or below you're able to do Rage Art (Supers/Finishers) or Rage Drive (Special Combo). Easy to perform, fun to use and blockable with some exceptions. Whenever a player is in Rage Mode it's fun to bluff or bait. Slow motion is a thing now and it's used when you're landing the final hit on your opponent (purely for dramatic effect). Stage destruction is also a feature included in this game. Some Einstein has just destroyed the no brainer concept of 'Whack a Mole'!
Seriously so much damn thinking is involved in this game that paracetemol will soon become your next best friend. The game never holds your hand and the difficulty curve is so ridiculous that even if i did a brain transplant with a quantum super computer that computer would just melt and immediately look for a walkthrough.
Thankfully there are several walkthrough's available which immediately makes me ask who are you people that produce these walkthrough's? I seriously thank all Gods of this world for such heavenly blessings. It humbles me to know that there are people with giant sized Moai brains who not only walk among us, but are willing to devote their time and almighty video recording skills to the common people who like me share the iq of a damp piece of seaweed. May the fanning of palm branches and grapes being dropped into your mouth be constantly rewarded to your steam profile thrones.
The game was produced within 2 months by 2 Ukrainian developers found here
. The speedy construction and delivery is all thanks to very minimal UI. There is no high scores, no timers, a limited repetitive soundtrack and 6 levels with a very basic backdrop which merely alternates in colour and sometimes direction. In a nutshell it’s just you and the puzzle.
The concept of this puzzle was largely inspired by the game 'Lights Out' the basic concept which is that the adjacent tiles to the one you press will systematically move in the opposite up or down direction. Hence the main goal is to turn all the tiles lights off on the map by having them eventually all pressed down. If you achieve this on all 100 + levels in the minimum moves possible you will be rewarded with the 'final puzzle'. A puzzle so great that it would cause a NASA Super computer to hide behind a couch scared.
The tile mechanics are slightly spiced up eventually with 'Special Tiles'. Tekken 7 GOTY
I LOVE Tekken, it's probably my favorite fighting franchise ever. It's a complicated game and it's not helped by a missing tutorial. However, it is a button masher friendly game so anyone can get in and win a few. But if you want to get better, you can learn how to move, block, and punish with a combo. That skill ceiling is what brings me back over and over again. There is no better feeling than juggling a dude into a wall and just grinding them into the dirt. There's a flow to the fighting that is so fun to get into.
Plus, the game worked at launch with a ton of playable characters, and the online works great. Billed as the epic conclusion of the Tekken Saga, this game has all the video and artwork from the previous Tekkens so you can see what you missed or learn the history of the Franchise.
This is a great game for beginners and long time fans. Tekken is back baby, get ready for the next battle.

A quality release from Bamco. Overall a solid fighting game with good netcode. That being said there's a lot more to be improved.
Single player content, it's lacking. I'm disappointed Tekken Force doesn't make it because they are focusing on story mode and improving the fighting system from what I heard. Then again I appreciate they re-imagining T4 Honmaru battle. Watching T5 intro was epic enough, experiencing the battle itself? That was incredibly fun! For treasure battle, while it's fun getting loot, it doesn't feel as fun as ghost battle in T6. I want to change it to 3 rounds-to-win with very hard diff but apparently game setting doesn't affect it. I don't know, 2 rounds game feels too short. Arcade mode is useless and hopefully the new game mode gives some replayability.
Customization, a wasted potential. With plethora of items (and t-shirts) it doesn't have some common items. I want to customize Jin with black business suit so I can look dapper when kicking butts but nope. Shaheen has it but it seems exclusive to him? We could have uniques but for common stuff like this it shouldn't be. And they could really add extra hair styles like seriously. They are probably aiming for DLC but yeah I guess I have to wait. EDIT: Missing costume set like Asuka Dojo outfit. it's unique and defines her as the Kazama-style practicioner.
Character specific story, it's embarrassing. They could've just do it like traditional arcade mode, a set of match with some cutscenes here and there and I'll be fine with it. Instead we only have a SINGLE match. Getting ending story after trashing Jinpachi or tryharding Azazel feels way more satisfying even all I get is cheesy ending because at least I put some effort into it.
Tutorial mode. While practice mode is fleshed out, it's raw. Newbie players usually like this: Play online > get rekt > take refuge in Practice Mode > test combos against unmoving target practice or spar with overly aggressive AI > come up online again > still get rekt > quit. Tutorial mode is great for basic fundamentals like getting up from the ground, spacing, etc. It helps to make new people get better and results more players online. EDIT:
Mortal Kombat X had it and it useful to showcase combos.
Some of those music are really good and I want to practice in Devil's Pit infinite stage because Azure is getting boring.
Online mode
-Recent player list so if you fought with good players you can add them to practice with you.
-Replay feature. I'd like to watch my losing match so I could figure out what needs to be improved or just want to show off that one close match. Street Fighter V which also use Unreal Engine 4 has this feature so no reason for Tekken 7 to exclude this one.
-An interface that show your friends that also playing so you can invite them to 1v1 or tournament.
-EDIT: This doesn't apply only to online mode but option to remember side fight (Left/Right/Always Ask/Random).
Gallery
While I appreciate the extensive artwork/movie gallery, there is no Tekken Music Player. Tekken 7 features double music every stage resulting in more awesome music from Namco Sound Team and yet there is no player for that. I get that we're on PC so you might suggest just turn on Youtube? Yeah, we shouldn't need 3rd party for that. But then again, I really appreciate for putting artwork from every Tekken series. I can't believe Tekken game is 20 years old and counting!
TL;DR Tekken 7 is a must-play for fighting game fans. There won't be new Tekken for at least next 5 years so play this one!

First, The basics.
RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a 4-player co-op Hack and Slash Action game based on the popular web series that weaboos refuse to admit is an anime. You play as the titular team RWBY, the deadliest, most heavily armed teenagers not to come from Japan. You must use said deadliness to murder all the baddies.
The gameplay reminds me a lot of Dynasty Warriors, except the standard enemies in Dynasty Warriors are about as deadly to you as a fart that happens on the other side of the universe. In Grimm Eclipse, if you aren't watching your back you can be easily beaten up by even the weakest of monsters. Also, unlike Dynasty Warriors, you can level up your character to improve their skill in combat.
Also unlike Dynasty Warriors, where you have more characters to pick from than there are riders on the world's busiest Subway. Grimm Eclipse has 4. And herein lies the biggest flaw in the whole game: There's just not much there. There are collectables, but they're just XP boosts and nothing more. The enemies never drop items, which is pretty much a stable in the Hack and Slash Genre.
Having only 4 Characters is a problem in the teamwork dynamic because each Character does have a specific role. Ruby can hit a lot of enemies at one time, Weiss can freeze enemies and fight well from a distance,  Yang does a lot of damage to single enemies, and...I haven't really figured out what Blake's role is. Moving through mobs I suppose?
The problem is that you can have more than 1 of the same character in a match, which has more that a few times left me on a team where I'm the only one not Playing Yang. And there's no easy way to switch characters after joining a game, and you can't see who everyone else is if you join a match in Progress. So if you pick Ruby and find out the team has a Ruby already, too bad. You can't give them the Weiss they're lacking. The voicework is fine, but even at its highest setting seems too quiet. Party banter depending on who is in your team would have been appreciated as well since that's one oof the high points of the show, character interactions.
On the plus side, the combat does flow well. Characters actually feel rather balanced, I mean, you can be good at anyone, and I saw pretty much every character topping the score charts at the end of each mission. And feeling incomplete is normal because it IS incomplete. So I'll let it slide that there are only 4 maps, something I'd let slide anyway because of how large they each are.
So Overall, Grimm Eclipse is a fun game for RWBY fans. But standard Hack and Slash Fans may get bored after a few hours. Take this recommendation as my belief that when finished, the game will be a very solid Hack and Slash game, and that right now, there's still fun to be had. Not a ton of Bugs, and it only ever crashed on me once, which for an early Access game puts it way at the top.

After being delayed to the tune of almost a year, this game STILL crashes quite frequently, and is thus unplayable.  I would have been perfectly willing to wait a little longer had they managed to release it without all of these bugs.  However, let's review what we can:
The storylines and dialogue are as crisp and compelling as we would expect from this franchise.  Lots of humor, Easter eggs, and the usual.As with Stick of Truth, TFBW does a really excellent job of making you feel like you're in an episode of South Park.
Gameplay and navigation are as clunky as ever; they have decided to keep the "mouseless" navigation that I hated so much in Stick of Truth.  Clues are found using 'Inspection Mode" and puzzles are solved using powers from your fellow superheroes.
An added bonus:  clothing no longer affects your combat power, so you can wear whatever you want!
Classes:  There are 12 classes currently, up from 3 in Stick of Truth.  You start out with one, then move to 2, then 3, then 4, and dventually you are able to choose from all 12.  Since your hero class informs your moves in combat the combat itself should have near-infinite replay value.
Combat:  As I said, your class(es) inform what powers you have during combat.  You are also able to choose from different heroes to be in your party, each with their own skills.  So again, there are enough variations that you should never get bored with the combat.
They retain the turn based combat here but add in a grid based system; participants are able to move a certain number of spaces per turn, and all combat powers have limitations based on these squares.  The upside is that it adds a nice cerebral element to the game; you need to choose a mixture of long and short range powers and combat buddies; do you prioritize range, or damage?  AOE or direct attacks?  How much healing/support do you need?  It reallty does make you think, and choose your powers and combat buddies effectively.
The downside is that the grid system sometimes limits the action.  On smaller grids you lock yourselves out of actions; on larger grids you spend a lot of time moving around.  Healing and reviving require precise positioning.
So at the end of the day, is this game worth $60?  Probably not right now.  The season pass DLC seems to hint at more content in the future which might make it more worthwhile.
But I can't recommend a game that has crashed every single time I have opened it.  Maye they'll release a patch/update that fixes it, so I can give it a strong recommendation!

Early this week I was browsing the Steam Store for something new to pick up and try, upon further searching through the store I came across this game, Moonlight. Moonlight is a very short, yet rewarding game, or so it was to me. It's a story driven platformer with a few light puzzles implemented into it. Once I loaded the game in you are greeted by the calm atmospheric tones of this absolutely beautiful soundtrack that just fits the entire game perfectly. Which brings me to the art style of the game, the art style of the game for me on a personal level is just amazing. I'm a huge fan of 2D/Bit games like these, add a little platforming and I'm sold. But the art style in general is very calming, thought the entire game (except one area) you have the Moon looming over head, always in sight casting it's glow on the "land" you walk, the blue over tone fits it all to perfectly and just makes it a calming theme. During your adventure you meet several characters in the village, some you might like at first, others might have to grown on you, but none the less the very short few minutes to spend helping these characters leave a lasting effect in your heart. You really start to feel attached to them and really want to hang around them more, but you must move on in your adventure. I'd like to say as much as I can about the ending without spoiling anything, but to be honest I can't think of anything I could say that wouldn't spoiler it. You'll just have to play it yourself and find out. I paid $4.99 for this game, for what I played and the enjoyment I got from it, I'd pay $10 easy for this game. I strongly recommend picking up and trying Moonlight out for yourself, oh and explore as much as you can, there's little hidden things here and there.
All in all, if I was a professional game reviewer I would give Moonlight a 10/10, to be honest I'm sitting here trying to think of some flaws this game has, sure there might be a few things that need fixing, but nothing game changing or anything that will change your experience.

Beetle Uprising is a refreshing little take on a 'genetics game', using the world of beetles. While it doesn't have a major studio behind it, it's clear that the team has emphasized quality of simulation as well as functional yet endearing graphics that help bring your colony alive.

The game mixes a few elements (part SimBeetle, part Command and Conquer (Lite), part Petrie Sim), but the big draw is evolving your bugs over time to your specifications.
This is the kind of game you can pick up and play for awhile, in small doses or longer sessions.
Highy recommended!

I only bought the game yesterday but so far it has been fun and a very promising. You start of with 2 beetles in your nest and from there on you build your beetle empire.
In your nest you can put down variuos objects for your beetles to keep them happy. You breed 2 of your beetles giving you a possbillity of 9 hatchlings with different stats whereby you can choose to keep 1 to be added to your colony. So with future selective breeding you can build on the traits you want for your beatles.
You can also go to the "world map" which basically is a map of a vacant lot with a few areas in it that are locked at the start and have to be explored with quests to get access to them. There are automated missions were you can sent out designated beetles on missions to gather items for your lair, or take missions whereby you are placed in charge of a group of "offspring" beetles to take on the other inhabitants in the yard.
In the first mission you need to kill a certain amount of bugs in the required time, it is pretty easy to get the three stars achiement by just chasing down all the enemy.
Pros:
- Fun to breed and try to build on the stats you want for your beetles.
- You need to plan your exploration missons, some of the enemy are stronger than you and you can't just storm in.
- Some missions require you rather avoid combat to achieve the objectives or lure enemy away from the main storm.
- The price is really cheap to give it a try.
Cons:
- Music can use a overhaul
- Placing of stuff from the back pack in the nest feel a bit clunky.
- Combat is very basic, you basically just direct your swarm to the waypoint and they engage on their own.
- You beatles consume food very fast and you need to keep sending them om missions to keep your stock piles up.
- After a couple of breeding cessions your original beetles become obsolete so you don't really get attached to any of the
beetles
- The game need some more depth, at the moment it feel as if you just have to rush breed to get your stats up, but I'm still early lvl into the game and might change the more I play.
Will be interesting to see how the game plays out in future but I think there is a lot of potential here.

This novel concept provides a different and fun approach to strategy games. It seems casual at first, but...
Fostering and building your beetle colony is full of choices and decisions:
- How much material to put in the nest, how fast? Beetles have needs now, but you should save some for the future.
- Do you get more nest materials, or more food, or try for some of each?
- How often should you explore, and how many risks can you afford?
- How long do you wait to foster top morale before sending your beetles into a battle?
- Which nearby enemy should you try to fight? Each has different benefits and varying risks.
- You need to breed more and better beetles, but each breeding can harm a parent permanently. When do you risk it, and with which beetles?
As you conquer regions and your nest enlarges, you get busier and busier balancing these many needs. It's amazing how this "simple" game draws you into more and more complicated choices.
One additional challenge is that the game is automatically "Iron Man." You either continue the current game, or start over. No "save scumming" is allowed. That makes risks more meaningful, since you must live with the results of your choices.
I was lucky and got a build the week before early access (due to game industry connections). The Early Access version has much improved help, which made learning far easier. More missions and regions are in development (just look at the "coming soon" notes on the map). I hear Iocane Studios is in contact with a composer for better music. In other words...
...unlike some Early Access games, this game is clearly in development (as of August 2017), and seems close to launch.
Get it now, before early access ends and the price rises. Besides, who can resist building an vast empire of beetles?

Clearly inspired by the classic
handheld game from the 90s,
is a decent little tiled-based puzzle game that's generally a relaxing experience, with simplistic graphics and a gentle background soundtrack. Of course, the puzzles themselves are key to the experience and in many cases present quite a stiff challenge, especially if you're aiming to solve the puzzles with the minimum possible number of moves - I'm not ashamed to admit to having referred to a guide to help with a fair few of them.
As you get towards the later puzzles, there are some interesting variants to the standard
puzzles, with special tiles that behave in different ways from standard ones, and it can be quite satisfying (albeit briefly) to work out each new mechanic and how best to make use of it to solve each puzzle. The one major criticism that I have with the game is linked with this, though, to an extent - while the game doesn't really need a tutorial as such (and doesn't have one), the puzzles don't necessarily come across in such a way as to teach techniques for solving later ones, instead feeling in large part to need a trial-and-error approach. Overall, though, the game easily justifies its low price, with its 120 puzzles providing a good length and the game's positives outweighing its drawbacks.

Unlike other people. I find there's something very satisfying to pushing buttons. It's like popping bubblewrap in a way -- especially because of its quite
graphic and sound design? The clack sound when you click is strangely meditative. So points for that I guess.
The game is difficult if you try to play it like a proper puzzle game, making you easily stressed and irritated, but for this game I like to just click in a somewhat educated manner -- not focusing on the game, but on some other distraction (videos/movies) until the puzzle ends up solving itself. Even when trying to solve in the least possible moves this kinda works if you just hit R all the time; although you'll be pushing for some time. If anything
use the guides to progress, even if you feel like it's cheating. This game isn't easy.
It is too minimalistic in some places. It could do with a proper settings page, like resolution, custom colour schemes, and a slider for sound and music which you can actually change inside levels. Though the game's biggest problem is its lack of additional features -- there quite easily be potential for randomly generated levels and workshop support (custom levels) since there's no real reason to start over unless you really like pushing buttons. However, this game is dirt cheap and the game is easily worth its price.
And also you can make words in your achievement showcase if you like that kind of thing.

If you're looking for some easy little clicking puzzles like Oik or Zup, you've come to the wrong place.  These puzzles actually make you work at solving.  In order to actually complete them and do them perfectly with the least amount of moves takes a lot of hard work and effort.  If you love to really delve in and solve puzzles then this is for you.  It's a very simple premise but the puzzles get harder as you go.  I like the added difficuly and nuances they've added to the later puzzles.  If you get stuck, fortunately there are guides to help.  I highly recommend for those who like to figure out more difficult puzzles.

This game saved my life. There I was, sulking in my depression, eating nothing but microwaved Kids' Cuisine every day, wishing my miserable excuse for a life would end. But then. Then it happened.
Conan came to me.
A dear, sweet, beautiful friend gifted me this game. I had no idea what to expect. I assumed it was just some random game sent to me as a joke. Little did I know, I was about to embark on a nonstop 3 hour journey that would forever change me.
As soon as I saw that small animated pig, my soul felt renewed. His eyes. His breathtaking, gorgeous eyes hypnotized me. It was as if he was speaking to me, right from his heart to mine. I felt him say, "Bread, everything is going to be okay. You will never feel alone again. You will know no more pain or suffering. I'm here now." At this point, I only had the game open for about 5 minutes, and there were already tears of joy streaming viciously down my face. I lifted my hands into the air, as if I was attempting to reach up to God, and I screamed, "I am alive! I am well! I am whole once more!" I could not contain my overwhelming happiness.
Once I calmed down a bit, I began my journey with Conan. We hid from the wolves. We bypassed the bees. We bravely crossed the ghosts. We did it all together. After hours of searching and strategic gameplay, we found them all. Every. Single. Truffle.
We laughed, we cried, we lost some, and we gained some. Throughout it all, the highs and the lows, Conan was with me. And I was with him. He is the best friend I have ever had. It was an experience I will hold onto in my memory until the day I leave this earth and go onto the afterlife, where I hope to meet him face to face someday. As soon as I see him walk through those pearly gates, his snout sniffing the ground for more delicious truffles, I will run to him. I will call out to him, "Conan! Conan! Come to me, my best friend! We are united once more!" We will hold onto each other in a strong, warm embrace. We will become one, in mind, heart, and soul. We will spend eternity in paradise together, endlessly searching for more truffles. No more wolves. No more bees. No more ghosts. Only happiness. Only love. Only us.
I highly recommend this game to anyone who feels lost. Anyone who feels alone. Anyone looking for the light at the end of the road.
Conan will be there for you, the way he is here for me.
He will help you.
He will comfort you.
He will save you.
He is not the hero we deserve, but he is the hero we were blessed with. Be good to him. He will be good to you.
5/5 stars. Without a single doubt, the best game I have ever been lucky enough to come across.

When I first bought Deponia I felt like it had the potential to be really great: nice art, story rich and lots of humor.
The game does have a nice design and interesting world but the plot is not very interesting and relies on dated tropes for comedy. I personally found most of the characters unlikeable (especially the protagonist) and the jokes to be immature, easy gags.
Perhaps the biggest problem Deponia has is its illogical gameplay and puzzle structure. Moving forward in the story generally requires trying every item in your inventory until something works with little to no reasoning. I found it easy to miss things because nothing really has a coherent structure.
I came back to this game about 4 times, trying to give it another shot based on all of the positive reviews I'd read. When I finally read the walkthrough, I quit immediately after seeing how unnessecarily complicated and random it was to complete tasks.
PROS:
- Good art
- Rich world
- Good sound
CONS:
- Illogical gameplay
- Requires a very specific sense of humour
- Unlikeable characters

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is not just a game, it's a wonderfully crafted emotional fairy tale and an amazing journey. The controls in the game are very easy to get used to; you control two brothers, each has its directional keys and an action key. On the Steam store page of this game it says “Notice: Brothers – A Tale of Two sons requires a controller to play”, but that’s not true at all. The game is perfectly playable with the keyboard. You can also play the game in co-op with your friend on one keyboard. Game mechanics are very simple and basic too; you'll mostly pull levers and solve simple platforming puzzles using both characters at the same time throughout the game. Even though the game has simple controls and mechanics the story, atmosphere, characters, the world around you and soundtrack are simply perfectly put together and those elements are where the game really shines. With all those elements combined the game evokes certain emotions in player through the whole journey and that’s the game’s strongest point; to make you really feel and care for the main characters. Through prologue, 7 chapters and epilogue you’ll visit various places with beautiful landscapes, environments and aesthetics. The only downside of the game for some people will be the fact that you can finish the whole game and get all achievements in 5 hours, at least I did, but even though I knew the game was short from other reviews and first impressions that never made me disappointed or not interested in this wonderful game. Brothers – A Tale of Two Sons is an amazing experience that you'll finish in one breath and I would strongly recommend it to everyone.

I have to say, this is leaps and bounds better than the first game.  First, literally zero issues running it.  No crashes, no bugs.  Ran perfectly smooth the entire time (though it's not exactly demanding).
Second, the gameplay is a lot more fun.  The positional strategy rpg style is a lot better than the straight JRPG style the first game attempted.  Unlike the Stick of Truth, I didn't get bored of the encounters.  I highly recommend playing at the hardest combat and social difficulties.  The boss fights were each memorable in their own way and weren't just straight forward "hit it until it's dead".  The skill system also allows for many styles of gameplay, you can run a build for anything from a standard fighter to a support only mage and still get through fights reliably.
Obviously, if you don't like the humor of South Park (specifically newer episodes) this game probably isn't for you.  The jokes, for the most part, are pretty crude but they're good for a cheap laugh and some shock value.  I personally thought this game was worth full price, but if it's too expensive for you, definitely grab it on sale!
I'd say the only thing about it that isn't great is that the puzzles are all really straight forward.  I didn't expect anything Talos level but it would have been nice to have to actually think about a couple of them.

What a lovely creation Portal Knights is.
As an RPG of course it has a few classes to choose from: Warrior, Ranger and Mage, abilities of whose are of course customisable. Combat is easy to get used to and is pretty fun. Various fun quests; some can be more challenging and take some time, some are very easy and fast to finish. Sandbox aspects are also great. Building is also pretty fun since all building blocks and furniture are looking very good. It also has multiple types of pets and vanity items. The game is a bit grindy, but what game would it be without a little challenge? Challenge only makes the things more fun, especially when it's rewarding.
Visuals are simply adorable and beautiful. Worlds have multiple types, each of them has it's unique appearance, various different enemies and resources as well as dungeons with more rewards and challenges.

Music is very relaxing. Probably one of the best ones I've encountered in sandbox games.
In general the game runs smoothly and brings a lot of enjoyment, especially on co-op.
Highly recommend it to those, who likes Sandbox and RPG games, enjoys teamwork and a bit of challenge.

This game is phenomenal. There are so many reviews describing the game and its mechanics, I thought I'd take the time to show how good it is on PC.
DE:MD is to 2016 what Crysis was to 2007. Even on lower settings, this game looks phenomenal. People are stuck in their thinking about how settings relate to graphical power - they assume that Ultra should be playable at over 60fps as long as you use a top-end card. Normally, even I would expect my GTX 980 to run most games on Ultra without a problem. However, this game recommends High if you have a 4GB GTX 980 card. Not VERY High, not Ultra, just High. This has caused a lot of upset - which is fine if High looked terrible, but it doesn't. It looks better than nearly every other game out there right now.
Those with £5000 gaming rigs are finding they can't hit a steady 60fps with everything turned up full, and it's not because the game is poorly optimised - on the contrary, compared to most other games, this game both looks and outperforms them at the right settings. It's important to remember that Ultra is not meant to be achieved by today's hardware; it is meant to be a setting that will still look good even in 5 years time, when technology has improved even further. This is a way of future-proofing this game's graphical potential for many years to come.
So when they tell you to use High or Medium, rest assured that the game will still look amazing by today's standards, it'll just look even better compared to the advancements in a few years - games in 2021 will only then be looking as good as DE:MK does on Ultra settings. It would be no different if they simply locked the V.High and Ultra settings and unlocked them in a patch in 2019. People would think, "Wow, they made so many improvements 3 years after the game released in this patch!" when the truth would be that the improvements were always there, they just weren't available until then.
I'm loving this game and it's a definite 9/10 for me.

I've double checked to see if I had missed anything, but this review is going to be mostly personal gripes with this game as the game is functional (as far as I could see within an hour).
1. It's about beetles, but only sorta.
The "sim" part of the game where you see the "life" of the beetles is redundant, and the beetles could have easily been replaced by literally anything, as what they sleep on, consume and PLAY with don't relate to beetles in any way.
I know that the game advertises the beetles as being a vague entity to ease the concept of them slowly mutating into different form and shapes as your breeding goes on, but it's definitely way too vague for me to feel that they're beetles at all.
Although beetles are known to live in groups, they're definitely not the same kind of hivemind as ants tend to be, so sticking with ants probably would have been a better idea.
2. RTS(?)
I was looking forward to doing some thought process as I have no experience in RTS games at all, generally clumping my units together and rushing towards different points of a map in offline games.
Sadly, this is just that. I might have missed some amazing in-depth RTS battles later on in the game as the first map is just destroying the enemy, but even, then, it was timed. Despite having a large margin even for the 3 star objective which was to destroy all enemy beetles under a minutes and a half, I wasn't given the option to divide my group of beetles to effectively destroy everything in record time, or to catch one of the beetles that had wanderd off into the corners of the map.
This might be an option later as I was in control of my "white" units, implying that i could take care of more unit groups later, but that's just an assumption.
3. The UI and the music
A minor detail from my part, as I've immediately turned off the music as it sounded like something that was royalty free and very jarring, replacing it with my own. The UI looks like that of a flash game, but again, if the two points above had been otherwise I couldn't have cared less.
I'll be following the game's development further in hope that this becomes something else, but right now, it's at the level of a phone game that i'd buy for about as cheap as 2FR (this game being 10 in swiss currency) as a time waster.

Wasted is a very strange game. It's a dungeon crawling, booze drinking, fallout parody. Opinions of others really don't mean much in this kind of game due to how polarizing the mechanics are. If you like the mechanics and theme, you'll have a fun time.
So the game is based around finding bottles of booze to give you buffs. These bottles are found in coolers (vaults, dungeons, whatever you want to call it) where there are tons of baddies in them. The game is roguelite, and truly embraces it too. If you die, any non important item on your person is lost forever.
However there are methods of saving that gear. The first and foremost is to drink a bottle of booze. This will knock you out and bring you home with everything in your inventory. Earlier levels of coolers have booze that will give you debuffs, but bottles deeper will give you great advantages. There also mailboxes which can only hold a few items. These mailboxes are accesible in the cooler and outside, these items will always be protected (even on multiple deaths). Also, if you die with hangovers (boosts from booze), you will lose those too.
The combat is a bit strange feeling at first, but quickly gets more entertaining when the ebb and flow is understood. There are many booze buffs that directly change how combat is played out too, like slowing down time while in the air, exploding in frost if they shoot a crit on you. Simply put, there are more active buffs than just percent bonuses.
Finally the worldbuilding. With all the smart people dead, idiots rule the world. This creates amazing and hillarious dialogue all throughout the game. I'll leave it at that because I truly don't want to spoil anything. Also, the background music is great as well as the radio music.
If you're ready to endure the frustration, you'll have a great time. Oh and there also has been a ton of quality of life updates too, which is sweet.

Being part of the 1.3% of masochists that managed to beat this game I have surprisingly mixed feelings about it, however I think the fact that it managed to keep me occupied for over 30 hours is enough for me to give it a positive review.
The game in itself is a rougue-lite FPS dungeon crawler with RPG elements taking inspiration from titles such as Fallout and The Binding of ISaac. The game's dungeons are compossed  of pre-designed rooms with random loot and enemies inside of them and the stats of your character are determined by your clothes and weapons, as well as permanent buffs that you can find in dungeons both of which can be lost if you die on a dungeon.
This basically means that rushing into dungeons with all of your money, best weapons and a character that you've been building for 8 hours can all be lost if you die and in order to make it somewhat "fair" the game contains a couple of features such as returning to your howse after drinking one of the aforemented permanent buffs (Or debuffs) and boxes to send your equipment back home so you can store back-up equipment for your next run in case you die.
Now, the main drawback of the game? The game is hard; stupid hard... in the beginning. The game is choke-full of newbie traps and mechanics that can easily get you killed if you don't know what you're doing. The best example that I can think of this is knockback (Which is the thing I died to 100% of the time later in the game); knockback in this game is reminiscent of old school platformers where a single strong hit can set you flying backwards all across a room, which wouldn't be much of a problem if it wasn't because you cannot defend yourself while stunned and as such the enemies can easily corner you and dispatch you.
Another element that adds difficulty in the beginning is the S.OB., a dungeon keeper with an absurd amount of armor and health armed with a minigun that will hunt you down if you linger on one floor for too long, which wouldn't be an issue if it wasn't because the game heavily encourages you to sneak around and scavenge the floors.
Both of these elements along with other small ones such as locked doors that contain extremely high level enemies behind, losing all of your equipment on perma dead, the first boosts obtainable in the beginning being permanent debuffs and traps scattered all over the place make the game hell on earth when first starting. However with some patience you can learn some quirks of the game such as getting buffs with the bartender before entering a dungeon, doing courier runs to obtain the best equipment and most importantly the patience required to fully stock yourself before heading into a dungeon to complete it.
Once you fully arm yourself though the game becomes stupid easy, after the first dungeon is done you get the most powerful single-shot weapon in the game, and if you do an optional quest you get the most powerful automatic weapon
. The only thing to do here from this point forward is getting the most powerful energy weapon and getting the best armor which really becomes absurdly easy.

CON's / Suggestions:
Animations, when going down a hill or down anything of the sort, your character decides to slide, once on level ground or going up hill it's fine, not a huge complaint, if anything just an issue that can be resolved.

So here's my review. To start with I want to say that it's an early acces game and if you aren;t okay with an unpolished game that's still got bugs in it, don't buy it. But if you don't mind finding issues with a very pretty and functional game, come help. I like the game so far but this is a list of things I've discovered about the game so the Dev's can know about it.
I've only watched a bit of the show but I do like the characters and I feel that each one is very well represented except Blake.As I played more of each character I discovered I like the way blake fights but she is almost impossible to use very well. She is a powerhouse at one on one engagements managing to 1 shot Ursa type grim but since this game is all about fighting hordes her gameplay is kind of bad. Her first two skills are good AOE attacks that cover areas decently but they do very little damage making it so clearing a small group can take three special bars. Her regualr attack combo is super strong but it has an issue that since she goes in the air, she con only hit one thing with it and if it happens to fall during the combo she doesnt actually kill it, her kit is very flashy and cool to look at but it is far from effective. She doesn't talk very much at all to the point that after three play throughs I'm decently sure that it's the right voice actor. This being said, Ruby and Yang feel as strong as you'd expect but Weiss feels kind of weak but that could be me being bad at her.
Another point that my friend and I noticed was that the level scaling isn't well balanced. It is very difficult to get multiple characters up to level 10. Characters stop walking sometimes when going down hill, my first game I experienced a bug where I was playing with a Weiss but her character model was blake and all her skills looked like odd verisons of blakes and we found that Yang was never not on fire after the skill activated (Not sure if thats a bug but seems like it.) I fell something should be done about the beowolfs because when they get in a group you cant hit them because they alternate swiping. The boar things that spin don't get dazed after spinning like it says, they just keep attacking.
My friend and I noticed that a lot of the lines seem to be pulled directly from the show giving it a kind of monotonaous  feel as the characters interact. On a similar note, the game's voice acting is super sparse, my friend was playing yang and found a treasure and thought it would be perfect to have her say the line "Hey look a pony." or whatever it is she says about the horse statue in the show. I feel personally that the characters need more interaction between eachother because that's something I really appreciated about the show. The music for the game is really nice, when exploring it's really peaceful but one issue in my opinion is that when you start fifghting the music doesn't change to match it, another thing I loved about rwby was the soundtrack but fighting enemies to the super relaxing exploration track until the big boss show up is not very good. On another note, with the exception of yang, the gun function on each weapon is almost useless due to low damage and single targetting or low attack speed.
All of this being said, the game is stunning, it's graphically beautiful with each area being unique in visuals and atmousphere, the soundtrack is great when it lines up right and each character handles ver differently which is needed in games like this. I have  no idea where this game is going but I do have a few suggestions that I personally would like to see.
More characters, granted I realize this is basically an alpha game so it's amazing it has four fully functioning characters and I think it would be really fun to have some more like Nora Pira and Ren, even Juane. They would each add a very unique element where ren would be fast and deal lwo damage but very quickly as where Nora would deal large damage more slowly and pira and Juane would be bale to guard. It would also add some veriety tot the game as oppossed to playing with three ruby's.
Horde mode, This feature would be nearly perfect for this game, put the characters in a area and send large number of increasingly difficult waves of grimm at them until they all die. This type of game mode is super popular usually and adds replayability to the game (It's been keeping the call of duty series going for YEARS) and I fell it would be great to get together with your friends and see how far you can go. This would also make it so everyone could actually try out and use all their skills  to see what works best  and how.
My friend brought up the point of character customization, not in a way that is fully design each cahracter, go make your models and goodluck, but more in a Soulcaliber kind of way. Choose character features, then choose from a list of stock weapons and then choose three skills from a list. I get that this would be difficult and wouldn't happen until the game is nearly done but I feel it would be kind of cool to run around and see other peoples characters and would add a depth of making the game personal to each person.
After the game is finished, it might be cool to release even a payed dlc story mode that actually takes you through the entire story of rwby from each characters perspective. This would improve the depth of the rwby story and add some background on the main characters lives well at the same time helping players who are new to the rwby universe get to know the story in a fun interactive way rather than just being dropped into a story that they don't know dealing with events and characters they know nothing about. Even having a lot of this portion being cutscenes from the show, then fighting the enemies that they fight in the show then cutscene and repeat. I feel it would also help solidify the game as canon and help point out where and when exactly in the story it takes place.
Essentially these are all of my thoughts on the game, It's good and when it's done it will probably be great, I really hope the dev's read this and take into consideration the points I brought up and if you do, please leave your thoughts in the comments so we can see. Thank you for your time and thank you for making this game.

There are a few noticable bugs in this game that I caught:
- The noise from airplanes and bombardments doesn't always correlate with the "noise" symbol that tells you you can shoot without being heard, and it's the symbol that's actually accurate. This is a bit more important if you're playing without UI help, but is nonetheless annoying if you are anyway.
- There are some glitches where you can save your game into an unwinnable state. One example is that if you save while hidden, you can sometimes load into a situation where an enemy sees you, probably due to how they get spawned in a load. This happened once to me when part of the objective involved not being seen. Another is when the alarm wouldn't shut off even though I proceeded to kill everyone on the map, and the objective wouldn't load while enemies were "alerted."
- This game likes to lock your cursor into the game in windowed mode, which is okay, but there were a few times after shutting down the game where it glitched out, and clicking made me click through my other windows and onto the desktop, which could only be resolved by restarting my computer. This is probably the most significant bug in the game.
- A funny one is when a soldier spotted me, and pathed to come investigate through a tank's patrol route. He kept walking without reacting to the approaching tank, and it ran him over and killed him.
- An enemy could see through walls a couple times, oddly enough. Not tarp or something with holes, concrete buildings.
That said, if you can work your way through all of this, the gameplay itself is enjoyable enough to be a time killer. My only real complaints would be:
1) There's supposed to be a story, but it's directionless and boring, and the campaign ends very suddenly and awkwardly, like they ran out of budget to keep going or something. Sniper Elite 2 had a more interesting one, and I can barely remember what it was about, so that tells you about this one's.
2) The zoom and sensitivity is messed up. The vertical sensitivity is way too low compared to the horizontal, which can be fixed by changing it in the options menu. What can't be fixed though, is that when aiming with your pistol, it still uses the zoomed in sniper scope sensitivity, so you have to drag your mouse really far to make the small adjustments to shoot enemies that are very close to you.
Other than that, there's a few small details, like how the antitank rounds instruction screen only popped up once and I accidentally clicked through it, and couldn't find a way back, but that's starting to get nitpicky.

Alright. For starters let me get this straight. I like dungeon crawlers but I always hate the term of "Rogue-like". I feel like randomly generated level layouts kill any sense of creativity and originality. But WASTED is an exception for me since it is a vastly unique and often at times frustrating due to some often odd or out of place design choices. For starters the game takes place in the year 1980 after a nuclear apocolyspe scorches the earth into a cell-shaded bleached paradise of booze riddled delight. WASTED focuses heavily on alcohol and the adverse effects of a radiated liquor called non other than "Booze" (Since it's infused with radiated ooze for that extra leukemia taste). Booze is a sought after substance that almost every "Waster" wants and you being a said "Waster" fall in this crowd of hangover indused mayhem. But enough liquor talk. The game seems to borrow heavy influence from the recent iterations of the Fallout franchise. In the beginning of the game you create a character, give them a name, and start trucking along in these "Coolers" to get the aforementioned Booze and a collection of loot which involves weapons, healing items, and clothing. During your crawl through the coolers you can find unmarked flasks and the legendary booze and both items give you either negative or postive boosts to help you achieve the ultimate buzz. Unmarked flasks give you a random buff that will stay with you until you go home and often or not you will get something really good or really bad. With booze you get permanent buffs that stay with your character but just like the flasks they give you good or bad effects and when you drink these you get a massive hangover and return home. The upside about the booze is that you know whats in them upon finding them. One thing you should know is to not get attached to your character because perma-death is in play meaning when you die. You die. That character is gone for good. But you do get a replacement but they don't carry on the acquired effects of the consumed booze which could be a good or bad thing since your now deceased character probably had alot of bad effects from the consumed booze and this new character may give you a second chance. If their is one thing that really boils my whiskey is a looming threat that hunts you while you're in the cooler. Upon entering a cooler or a new area you have a time limit before this hunter comes for you. Nontheless however I do feel like this game is very entertaining despite it's minor short comings. I say give it a try. But just remember for future reference when you got to a party. Don't drink from an unmarked container.
