is based on the old electronic handheld game
, where you press a square and it changes its polarity along with all adjacent squares (non-diagonal).  All lights that are on turn off, all lights that are off turn on.  The goal is to turn out all lights on the board/field.
differentiates itself from
by adding new features such as chains, locked buttons, "twin" tiles and more.   If you enjoy the old electronic game that's been recycled in quite a few other games,  then you might enjoy enjoy this title.  Just keep in mind that it's on the hard side.  The difficulty is pretty high...but as I said, I'm not a puzzle guru.

Deponia is a click and point adventure game with an overwhelming amount of charm, the game is set in a wasteland world filled with junk, and having a well for clean water makes you as rich as having a well of oil.
The music is a great addition to your immersion while playing the game, the music of the starting area in the game uses sounds and audio that wonderfully mesh together, the music to some not be very memorable, but it is definetely a great soundtrack
The plot of Deponia is relatively simple, Rufus, the main character is an inventor, and wishes to create an invention to get off his junk ridden planet to the upper class city in the sky Elyisum, His inventions fail time and time again when a girl from elysium falls from the sky and into Kuvaq, rufus' home town, Rufus seeing this as an opportunity to go to elysium attempts to help the girl get back.
The main protagonist Rufus is the primary source for the games charm, he is stubborn and brash, but he eventually becomes my favorite character in the whole game, his dark humor and rude personality helps make the character stand out and makes him different from most other game protagonist, Unfortunately, the first Deponia game features only a single character, with everyone else not feeling as special, this is fortunately fixed in later games.
unfortunately the click and point section fo the puzzles can be confusing and convuluted like many other click and point games, but the actual puzzle minigames can definetely be a challenge, often there is a lack of direction in the game, but I have of course completed the game with no walkthroughs, the game definitely tries to make you think outside the box and encourages you to try things you wouldnt think practical, but for Rufus regardless of how dangerous it is works completely!
TL;DR
Deponia is a great game with amazing Music, Art and humor, the puzzles can sometimes feel impractical but are entirely possible, I Highly recommend this game and its sequels especially if you like click and point games

I love this game. This reminds me of Dragon Quest Builders, which is one of the most enjoyable and most polished, block building sand box games out there. I have played Minecraft, Creativerse, Dragon Quest Builders, and now this game and there are some distinct differences. The main difference is that you can separate those four games into two primary groups based on the characteristics of each game. Minecraft and Creativerse are primarily, and almost exclusively, builder games. There is almost no story, no variety of monster, no quests or goals within the game itself. Combat is simple and pointless and all of this detracts from the replayability. DQB and Portal Knights, on the other hand, have many different monsters with different fight mechanics. They have bosses and quest-like mechanics. There is more of an adventure/rpg feel to them, in addition to the building aspect. I like the latter two for those reasons. I feel like there is more replayability when you can spend equal amounts of time crafting gear and fighting mobs, as you can building. It is my recommendation that you own one from each group, especially since Creativerse is free to play. Buy Portal Knights for its polished look and rpg style gameplay, and build until your hearts content on Creativerse or Minecraft. Or just do both in Portal Knights.

Required DX11 hardware. Before you buy this make sure your video card supports DX11. It doesn't matter if DX Diag says you have DX11 or 12, because you can have the latest DX installed and your video card may not support DX11 features.
Ignore "DirectX Version:" on the system tab on DXDiag. Mine said DirectX 12, but it doesn't work.
In Dxdiag click the display tab and ensure where it says "Direct 3D DDI:" and "Feature levels:" that it says 11, 11.1, or 12. If it says 10 or 10.1 you cannot run this game.

This early access game is pretty fun. Check the videos and you'll see it is a Minecraft/RPG hybrid. But the twists they put into the game, like making it so there are little worlds to explore instead of an infinite one, means there are natural breaks in gameplay.
This game still feels like early access. The core concepts of the game are there, it runs well, it just feels like it needs the content fleshed out more and balanced better. The games itemization creates non-linear difficulty, so as you approach a boss stuff gets harder whether because you've had all the upgrades since the last boss for a while, or because your elemental weapons don't line up and higher hitpoints and damage make that problem bigger.
This is one of the few action adventure style games with a third person and first person view and learning to switch between them makes the game feel far more fun. If you get started with the game and feel like building is clunky, switch to first person for that. If you feel like you have a hard time tracking combat well, switch to third person for combat. Sometimes in combat baddies will be on the other sides of trees, where switching to first person to be able to shoot them more easily makes sense.

Sniper Elite 3 is a third person shooter where you fight against German and Italian soldiers in Africa during World War 2.
Good stuff -
- Shooting Nazis.
- Hilariously over the top comedy gore with exploding eye sockets, brains, testicles, jaw bones, livers and lungs.
- Accurate shooting where you can shoot an enemy from 400 yards away through a tiny little gap and it feels satisfying to do too with great gun sounds.
- You can adjust the difficulty to you liking so you can make the shooting mechanics simmy or arcadey, there's a lot of choice.
- Fun linear story mode which keeps you moving forward with no pointless side missions like you get in a lot of shooters nowadays. I finished it in about 16 hours which is a pretty decent length in my opinion.
- More open level design than in the last game so you have more options in how to approach each combat situation. Choose stealth or full on Charles Bronson.
- Shooting Nazis!
The bad stuff -
- Enemy A.I is pretty dumb. You'll kill a guy and his friend who's standing right next to him won't even notice or you'll be in a doorway and enemies will line up behind eachother trying to get to you whilst you mow them down like dominos.
- Where's Hitler?
Well worth getting the next time it's on sale.

Even with only 1 tournament win under my belt (against other beginners, mind you), I feel like there's tons of room for improvement.
WITH THAT SAID, this definitely is the quintessential installment in the Tekken series. TTT2 may have had the largest roster, but with the "bound" mechanic removed, this feels much smoother and more efficient. The "rage" mechanic does peeve me a bit, but only because I feel that supers are overdone in most fighters these days. Regardless, it does add a good bit of flavor to the established fundamental gameplay.
The skill ceiling seems to be nearly limitless, but it's something to strive for this summer.

World 3-2: Ice Caverns, this world was very different than the previous.  Before I would just focus on getting to the bottom of the map as fast as possible, as the exit was always there.  The introduction of the endless abyss, made dropping down prematurely very perilous as I could fall off the map.
I had spent most of my resources going down the wrong side.  Scaling downward's blindly easily burned through my existing resources, I really wish I had a chance to buy a compass earlier.  I started my descent again, knowing that each step could be my last.  I reached a rather large gap which I had to time perfectly.
I make a jump toward it and... I miss!  I'm all but done for now as I descend into the abyss, when suddenly I see it on the edge of my screen, the exit.  At the exact same moment a parachute I had forgot about deploys.
As I try my hardest to steer my parachute right its too late and I slowly glide under the exit.
I make a last ditch effort and deploy a rope, but its no good, I'm stuck.  Right above me blocking the door are 2 layers of rock, my parachute has already deployed so I wont be able to get around it, even if I use another rope.  There's nothing else for me to move to so I'm trapped on this rope.
A ghost has already spawned to punish me for taking too long.  I'll be finished off in a few seconds.  When suddenly the first layer of rubble gets destroyed by a passing UFO blast.  One more blast in the right location and I'm free.  But the ghost is already breathing down my neck.  The second blast opens the way to my freedom, I throw another rope and jump for the exit and just as I was about to be killed.  I finished the level.
This game is brutal and unforgiving, but so rewarding when everything goes right.

After playing this for awhile, I realize that the game does have it's flaws in it's current state. Many. Just to address that a offline single-player mode should be added in later development since online only is just a little off-putting. Second: A save feature should added later since upgrading skills and leveling up seeming pointless at the moment since every time you play a game you reset back to lvl 1. The audio is great but audio in sounds really drone out the music even when music volume is maxed out sometimes so audio levels need to be adjusted later in development. Comabt is very fun but the special moves need some work more so on how to increase your special meter, personally i think a cooldown meter would be a lot better because it is so irritating that one hit breaks your combo meter espically when you need 12 hits to increase it by one block, hitboxes are another problem too since sometimes it feels and looks as close-range enemy attacks seem to hit me farther than usual which go in into the same issue with the special moves. Lastly some attack animations are missing from enemies, very very noticable when they are attacking the control center in those "protect the control tower" parts where you can clearly see them just standing in front of it while the area's health lowers. In conclusion this game still needs alot of work and improvements but this is why it's in early access state of development, the game is fantastic and loads of fun with other people but i'd say to wait maybe just a little longer to purchase since it still needs some improvement cause this has alot of potential. I still recommend it to RWBY fans and hack-and-slash fans, just don't expect perfection since this just released and is in early access

In addition to that, the "story" is brilliant, filled to the brim with jokes (mainly at Fallout's expense) and clever puns of all kind.
It's not perfect. The difficulty curve starts too steep, but due to how the game is, it's pretty easy to turn into an unstoppable killing machine, oneshotting everything but bosess. Also the ambient music is kind of meh, turning it off makes for a better experience IMO.

'Moonlight' is a peaceful, delightful game about helping one another (and playing with stylish hats ^_^). The tone, artwork and music are all lovely. While short (I beat it in 2 hours), it was a lovely experience.
---- PROS ----
- Great Artwork
- Lovely UI, Menus (yes, I notice stuff like that)
- Good dialogue with the characters
- Characters that have a lot of charm and personality. I particularly liked the clear emotions of the characters at different parts of the story.
- Beautiful calm, atmospheric music
- Simple to understand gameplay (all you do is jump and talk to people...though it gets a *bit* more complicated than that) ~_^
---- CONS ----
- Short. While lovely, the game can be beaten in about two hours. Know that going in. :)
- There were a few grammatical errors in the dialogue (I believe the dev said they're working on that, so that's good)
- I didn't like how the game defaulted to using the directional pad for movement instead of the left analog stick.(I think both should work right away.) Regardless, in the settings I was able to change movement to left analog stick. I still had to use the 'X' button to talk to people instead of the 'A' button (which I prefer), but it wasn't a big deal. I got used to it pretty quickly.
- This is sort of a nitpick with the trailer, not with the game itself. At over 4 minutes long, I think it shows too much. I mean, 'Moonlight' is not a long game, so as much of it should be preserved for the player to experience. I would think a minute long trailer - maybe a minute and a half showing a variety of gameplay (and nothing past the hot air balloon) - would be cool. Just a thought. ^_^
---- TL; DR ----
'Moonlight' is a calm, atmospheric platformer with a great look, soothing music and interesting characters. While short, it does what it does very well and I look forward to further work from the developer.
---- FINAL GRADE ----
8 out of 10

I've never really got into steam truth be told, but after watching my girlfriend and her friends playing this game on the tv, I wanted to try it for myself. I created an account just for this game basically. Although I'll get more I'm sure. Now, I could have played her game, but I wanted to really play it through and give my opinion.
I'd like to start with the only con that I can come up with, content. I'm not saying that I didn't get my money worth either! This was definitely worth my money. No, I'm talking about wanting more content. I sincerely wish, that there was more of this world. I wish there were more locations, more characters, more hats, more of these puzzles, and please ... more of this art and atmosphere!
With the one con out of the way, I can sum up this game's art and atmosphere pretty well with, simply beautiful! I tend to like detailed pixel art, and that isn't the case here. It's rather clean if you will, but there is just something about it. The details are not in the art itself, but more of a combined entity? It's all so very smooth and I don't know, it just makes you really enjoy the enviroment. The trees, especially the big one, is just something else! You can barely tell in some screen shots, but the light on the edges of all the bark is just awesome! The character art is very cute and charming. I do believe a little variation would have been interesting, but it feels hard to complain about it too much.
The music is phenominal to say the least. There is a media player in the game's menu, or I guess it is called the jukebox. Apparently there are only six tracks, but none of it is repetitive as the tracks are fairly long. It has a unique kind of sound, it's kind of oriental sounding in a way. It might not be something you would listen too outside of this game, but with the game's feel, it works well.
The story is also not something to be ignored, especially since the game relies on it heavily. The story as a whole is not the game's strongest point though, and without some very key elements, it would be dismissable. The key elements, are the characters telling that story. Each individual character seems to have a very real personality. You cannot help but create voices in your head for these little guys. Obviously Buko for the win, but all the characters seem to matter in their own little ways. The only gripe is that Kinubo, the character you play, has what seems to be a changing personality. He's all over the place some times. However, once I saw the ending, I think I get it. He's the player, he is the culmination of many different types maybe?
I want to wrap this up, but there is one thing I have to finish with, and that is this developer. I emailed him with a few questions about the game, and how many people worked on it etc. With the production level in this game, the art, the lack of any real bugs, I assumed it was a few people at least! It was interesting to find out that he is the only one. His "type" is something we need to see more of as well. He is extremely polite, helpful, and he even gave me a few keys for friends! I really enjoyed the game and the interaction with Monkeymaw, I hope for more, I wish him the very best!

Great game and a worthy successor to Human Revolution gameplay wise.  Story wise it falls a little short - the plot is compelling but much smaller in scope and feels like it was cut a little short.  Still worth picking up, especially on sale.

Deus Ex - Mankind Divided is pretty much Human Revolution squared. It features improved gameplay mechanics that previous installment lacked, such as: corner takedown, wider cover-to-cover movement, redesigned and more intuitive C.A.S.I.E. augmentation module and most importantly - better combat (if you like more straight-forward approach of progressing through the level). My point is, on the gameplay level, this game is one of the best this year had yet to offer.
Story is also great in my opinion. Sure, it's not in the same tier as the one in HR, but this game was intentionally meant to be some kind of introduction to the greater political and economical conspiracy that will be fully explained and unveiled in the third and final part of Jensen's trilogy. Make no mistake, plot presented in Mankind Divided is completely resolved, it has a logical beginning and ending. There are cliffhangers, but in this case, it makes you crave for more, and is not something games usually manage to achieve from player. The plot and general global story is dark, sophisticated, you will get the feeling of global conspiracy, constant doubt of who you can trust, who is a mole in your own agency. MD's story is basically a retired double-agent's dream come true.
Now for the most painful part of MD - in-game store and microtransactions. I don't support such business practice in an AAA game, but hear me out. These are NOT required if you play Deus Ex as it's meant to be played - AT ALL. I spent approximately 40 hours in this game so far, did every side-quest (every single one of the is easily found if you do a tiny bit of exploring), sold every unneeded weapon or item and I had never, ever any problem with credits or praxis points. My end-game stats are: 30+k credits and almost all of agumentations maxed out (excluding experimental agus - I didn't find them useful, except for remote hacking). What I'm trying to say is yes, there is an in-game store. Yes, it's♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥us off and yes, Square Enix made a bad call. But it's nothing game-breaking. The game itself is perfectly balanced, has amazing progression curve and if you like challenge and are feeling like earning your praxis points - you will be rewarded, generously. Good job Eidos, shame on you, Square.
Now for the Prague hub. I live in Prague and I found it quite beautiful in it's own way. Sure, most of the locations and names are made up or severely altered, but hey, it's devs' vision of it and I appreciate it. After all, it's an art. While the in-game world is pretty small compared to the titan of this generation, The Witcher 3, it's the depth thereof that makes it so fun to explore and simply traverse through it. Carefully designed apartments, labyrinths of underground tunnels, ventilation shafts, locked doors, windows, balconies all of these provide you with multiple paths to take and it's just so much fun to explore every single one of theme. Think of it like this: an inch wide, but a mile deep.
Also, soundtrack. If there is anything that immerses you into the game, it's the OST. Michael McCann once again proves that he is more than capable of composing spot-on ambients and themes. Respect.
Optimization was shaky at the launch, several players suffered a game-breaking error that made it impossible to progress the story, a few others were experiencing heavy FPS drops and stutter, and sometimes the game simply crashed from time to time (my case). However, these were mostly patched with a couple of updates. As for the optimization issues: more often than not I believe it's the players' inability to properly set the game's graphical options so that they would match their system's configuration. This often results in undeserved negative reviews, which in turn, decrease game's popularity, again, undeservedly. This game is NOTHING like Arkham Knight optimization-wise.
Finally, the Breach mode. Tried it, wasn't even remotely fun to me, later levels are designed to make you pay for the consumables and items, generally feels cheap - it just screams corporate bull*hit, noting new from Square Enix. My recommendation - avoid at all cost.
That's pretty much the review. I didn't plan to write an essay this long, but it just kept on pouring out of me and I felt like this game deserved a detailed review. I enjoyed this game royally, I plan to replay it multiple times, just like Human Revolution. What I love about this game, and Deus Ex series the most is that it rewards thinking, planning and logical conclusions based on limited facts and clues you come across. This is the second, and probably last, game of this year that I pre-ordered. Zero regrets, just like with the first one. I bought the season pass and can't wait for all of the content that has yet to come out.

So far I've found the game rather enjoyable. Shows all the signs of being just as quirky as the series including the trademark punkleman puns from barbara as Yang. currently only has the one campaign you can play through (as of 03/12/2015).
Replayabilty comes from playing the different characters and unlocking the skill tree through the achievments specific to each character and which are universal.

-Blake is ridiculously underpowered,
-Ruby is ridiculously overpowered.
-Sometimes, when you're htting an enemy with a combo, you will auto-target a different enemy and your combo may or may not hit.
Ok. That aside, the game on its own is very fun. Combos are intuitive and simple, but that doesn't mean you get bored with them, like spamming X, X, Y on lollipop chainsaw.
Ground combo leads into air combo, which you can finish early with a "strong(?)" attack or a dodge, there's no block button and both you and the monsters have invincibility frames, which are obvious to spot once you've heard that "clink".
Monsters are varied enough (at least for an alpha) and they're different enough from each other to be able to tell who's doing what.
Getting swarmed doesn't mean your death, but it certainly doesn't help your situation.
THERE IS NO BLOCKING. Youre not Kratos.
There's only one chapter, per se, with several levels in it.
Now, one thing I like that I don't know if it's a feature or not is that you can move as you revive someone. This makes it possible to revive someone in the middle of the swarm without taking a hit (possible, not likely)
There are two kinds of progression. Challenge unlocks and level unlocks.
- In one match you'll go from levels 1 to 10, which will be reset every time you leave.
- Challenge unlocks will allow you to unlock different upgrades during leveled unlocks. Tier 2 passives won't be unlocked until you make it to Lv10 once (As of right now, I strongly recommend playing as Ruby for this) Lv10 unlocks are permanent across characters, but the skill (Mastery) unlocks are skill-specific.
TL;DR - No escort quests, 10/10
----------
update
----------
Now that the game has been out for a bit, some people have unlocked everything and found an optimal strategy for killing more monsters, faster.
While I expect this will be what most people are looking to, I have to point out that exp is not shared.
As a new player, you are likely going to join a game where you won't reach Lv10 due to the sheer lack of kils. This means not unlocking your T2 passives, or your skill recharge passive.
My advice? Get a friend or two to play with you.

Now i am both a gamer and a RWBY fan and since this is a RWBY game... well... you know the drill, but ill try to be as objective as can be.
Now, this game is a hack and slash style action game with focus on horde battles primarily so if you arent into that kind of thing, at least for now, you might wanna hold of on buying it.
the game features 4 missions so far, 3 of which end with objective defence and the last ending with a moving objective survival fight. You will be running through a laid out course, fighting swarms of enemies as you approach the end, picking up exp buffs and artifacts hidden away through the level, the main goal of each mission seems to be leveling your characters and getting as strong as you can for the last objective.
The game is pretty restrictive of where you go and honestly, there dosent seem to be much reason for deviating from the path set out, each exp buff gives 25 exp and an artifact gives 100, but accounting for the time itll take you to get back to your teammates, it wont be worth it. low lvl monsters give 15 exp each so there really seems no point to it so far.
the level is also restrictive about where you can go as far as invisible walls go, granted you wont need to go there anyways but i guess its a feeling of freedom.
there are 4 playable characters in game and although they all come with the same kit (basic atk, ranged atk, aoe atk, single target atk, ult atk and dodge) they still manage to feel different in the way that they play and how the fights go.
Now, if you have never seen RWBY, will you be confused by playing this game? a little, its like playing Arkham Asylum with no prior knowledge of Batman, what do you expect? but the game is set OUTSIDE the main storyline so you wont have to worry about getting spoiled or being lost in the story.
Now to summarize a quick bit:
Pros
-Looks good graphically, attacks feel like the got punch or edge in them
-Characters play differently, fighting the hordes is both fun and dangerous, not too easy or hard
-Mission lenght is good, not too long and boring nor too fast
-Enemies feel different in attack patterns
-Difficulty adjust for if a player leaves/joins (also midgame joining)
Cons
-Adjustment issues (effect sound too high, BGM too low, voices too low)
-Glitches and pathing (stairs arent stairs but blocks, enemies sometimes stop up, boxes un-climbable)
-Settings menu (too few, cant rebind keys, not controller compatible)
And the big one
-Content (too little)
Now since this is Early Access some of these issues will probably see change.
And if the devs are reading as well:
What could make it better
-More characters (create your own in the style of Soul Calibur)
-More missions (seperately from the previous, where you start from lvl 1 again)
-More type of enemies
-More talents to unlock/raise max lvl
-Balancing (ranged atk. is simply to low dmg and cant be upgraded)

The buzz system helps to keep the gameplay feeling fresh even after the gunplay has worn out, as these are basically buffs you can grab mid run to either help you or hurt you.
Side quests: These are basically fetch quests, but have some pretty funny jabs at popular culture. Probably the best joke in the game comes from here,
That's about it terms of good things this game does.

A fun and addictive Action RPG in the vein of Diablo. Torchlight 2 expands on the success of it's predecessor with new characters, new expansive maps and dungeons, and co-op play.
Torchlight was a fanatasic little single-player indie RPG that brought a more lighthearted tone then the infamously popular Diablo franchise. However, despite it's addicting gameplay, it lacked any sort of co-op or internet play.
Torchlight 2 not only adds co-op and internet play to the mix, but expands upon all the elements that made the original a great game. If you are a fan of Diablo, you'll feel right at home with Torchlight 2's looting and questing system. Perhaps the only element that might turn some fans of the genre away is the more colorful, lighthearted graphics and story. Don't be decieved, though. This game doesn't lack any of the depth that veteren Diablo fans would come to expect. The story is sure to appeal to more mature players due to it's somewhat sophisticated invententory system and adjustable difficulty. The pet system is a really great addition that adds even more depth to the combat and inventory.
All in all, if you are a fan of Action RPG's or a fan of Diablo, you owe it to yourself to check this game out. It's a great game to play online or with friends. There are hundreds of quests and dungeons to explore, and lots of loot to collect.

If you want one of the best FGs on PC right now and mainly play multiplayer, TEKKEN 7 is a good choice.

Gameplay wise its Tekken, if you never played a Tekken before its a 3D Fighting Game which means you play itsplayed on a 3 dimensional playing field unlike a 2D fighter such as Street Fighter or Mortal Kombat.
Tekken is a 3D Fighters like Soul Calibur and Virtua Fighter. The combat is based around your characters four limbs, 1 for Left Arm, 2 for Right Arm, 3 for Left leg and 4 for Right Leg. It has a very high skill ceiling and a ton of moves, in fact the movelist may overwhelm you at first each character has 100+ moves which is pretty daunting compared to a Street Fighter.
That said this allows for a lot of unique and situational moves that keep the game fresh and exciting, it also allows for a lot of creative in playstyle. The customization is the one of the best among Fighting Games and you can unlock new costumes by essentially playing any mode. Every mode grants some in game currency known as Fight Money which can be used to purchase new costume pieces.
Treasure Battle is a mode which you can unlock more customization options. The Single Player story modes are a bit underwhelming, its probably the worse mode. One of the downsides to T7 honestly is the story mode and lack of features such as a Replay System.
The gameplay is amazing and deep, very little to complain about there. Actually one of my few complaints are regarding how you can press R1 to perform your Rage Art instead of doing the actual inputs as well as the ability to asign all your face buttons to a shoulder button allowing the user to mash out moves without performing them as intended.
Sadly Tekken 7 is one of the very few 3d fighters on the market today, its a must have for any 3D fighting fan and honestly if you're a fighjting game fan in general you should own this game as its one of the best fighting games period today.

I've owned and played every major Grand Theft Auto game since GTA 2 in 1999. It has been one of my favorite series as long as I have played video games. And now here I am, writing a review for GTA V, the supposed biggest and best one yet. I got this game in 2013 on release day for PS3. I bought it again for PS4. I bought it on sale a third time for PC. I know this game and this series very, very well.
I'll lay my point down right away. I don't recommend this game, because I don't like what Rockstar has done with the series as a result. The game itself works. You can buy it, you can play it. You can play the story and be entertained for 20 hours or so. GTA Online is an absolute trainwreck of half baked ideas and terrible execution, topped with what feels like zero effort to combat cheaters.
They made very clear what kind of market this game was aimed at. The story is considerably shorter than other games in the series, for a start. My first playthrough, in which I took my time, explored, and did side missions, was over in roughly 18 hours. GTA IV has an achievement for completing its main story in 20 hours.
The characters are not relatable. They are meant to be spectacles. The writing is at times shallow and inconsistent. If that's not what you're interested in playing GTA, then that won't bother you.
The entire game has pacing issues and arbitrary limitations. The story has a handful of invisible "checkpoints," before which chunks of content are cut off. You aren't really rewarded for exploring the world, in the way of weapons that you'd normally be unable to buy or unique vehicles. Some vehicles have a decent number of customization options, some don't, with no real explanation why. You can't make any decent money outside of the set piece heists in the story, even though there is an emphasis on spending money as you see fit.
A selling point is that this game has the most vehicles and the most weapons of any GTA game to date. It's a shame that all of them feel the same. All of the cars and trucks, with exceptions I can count on one hand, feel exactly the same. The sports cars accelerate a bit faster. That's about it. The weapons all feel the same, and unfortunately, that feeling is unsatisfying. All the guns share the same generic modernized look, sound weak, and don't handle differently enough from one another to develop a personal loadout. Every pistol feels the same, every assault rifle and machine gun feels the same, etc. It's filler.
Little bits of gameplay mechanics were added that had absolutely no place in a game like this. Things like cars explode if you land too hard, in a game famous for stunting and screwing around with cars. Needlessly frustrating things like trying to walk down a slope, then losing control as you ragdoll like you're having a stroke, not getting up until you come to a complete stop or eventually die. If you die in a cool way, you don't get to see the aftermath, you get your wasted message in slow mo and off you go.
The music selection isn't outright terrible, but it's considerably smaller. You will get tired of it soon, even if you listen to multiple stations. The "original score" isn't bad either, but it's rather bland.
The single player game has its flaws, but that is the reason you should buy this game if at all. The official multiplayer is a truly awful experience. I'll keep my reasons why brief: It is not fair, it is not maintained or moderated, it is not well connected, and it is not rewarding.
Chances are if you're someone who isn't new to the series, you've been through it all already, and you're reading the reviews to catch up on the latest drama or look for people who feel the same way you do. If you are reading this as a review though, I encourage you to look elsewhere. I would recommend Saints Row as a more enjoyable sandbox/shooter to this. I would recommend Mafia II as an infinitely better written game with a similar style of play. Hell, I'd recommend any GTA prior, though the old ones have technical issues these days.
I regret buying this, three times over.

I had this game on my WishList for the longest time because I was a bit iffy on the concept of it but thanks to a gracious friend I recieved it for my BirthDay and after a bit of play, I find I'm enjoying it a bit so far.
The basic premise is your typical procedural roguelike dungeon fare, Only in first person with a 1980s viber and general shooter feel. At first, You're presented with a character you can edit and customize a little and your first "Cooler" which is what they call pre-war cryogenic facilities. You have the option to take a tutorial, Or skip through the tutorial which is rather well presented whichever option you choose it feels a part of the story. Either way, Once inside these areas serve as your "Dungeons" and each seems to have a theme.. (Cooler A or "C-A", Your first one for instance, Appears to have been built for scientist and doctor types. No doubt there are other such facilities for civilians and such later.)
The entire purpose of these delvings is to find radioactive beer.. Which if drank will give you a "Perk" of sorts on the character who drinks it, Making them pass out and return "Home" with all their stuff and the new perk. This is an interesting mechanic as each Cooler has several floors, And the further you go down the more chances there will be booze with "Useful" perks while the higher up levels nearer the entrance will have more useless beers or lesser useful ones. It always breaks down to whether you think you can survive the harder areas and find better booze, Or return home and save your current build. Even if it means drinking a beer for a perk you might not want..
Whether you make it through the first facility or die, You'll eventually find yourself in a 'home' area. This will eventually be upgradable and can be used to store your crap between areas. Via certain objects and conversations you'll also unlock other coolers, Friendly settlements and hubs for services you can access with your car from here. Although when you die, You are presented with a random character, Customization, As well as more options for customization, Will come with upgrades to your home later so don't worry too much.
I enjoyed the humor of the games, And once you unlock your first settlement area you'll find yourself presented with npcs and characters and quests and things. Between the various characters, Locals and descriptions on the objects, The usual Adult Swim humor shines through which might be good or bad depending on your sense of humor.
Two mechanics I didn't like too much are the limited initial carrying space, And the "Timed" Hunter enemy. On each floor, There's a invisible timer ticking down that eventually releases a "Tank" type enemy called a "Purifier" into the maze with you. He stalks you and although you can outrun or even sneak past him depending how you play your character build, I found it annoying to be pressured into racing through each level or face losing my character. Fortunately there's a mod included in the files for the game that can disable him, With the only apparent drawback of doing so being not able to post scores for courier runs on the leaderboards. This is entirely optional however, And some people might like the faster hectic play of leavng that Purifier mechanic in there.
Overall I will give this a 10/10 and myself a kick in the butt for not having bought this earlier.

Now i am both a gamer and a RWBY fan and since this is a RWBY game... well... you know the drill, but ill try to be as objective as can be.
Now, this game is a hack and slash style action game with focus on horde battles primarily so if you arent into that kind of thing, at least for now, you might wanna hold of on buying it.
the game features 4 missions so far, 3 of which end with objective defence and the last ending with a moving objective survival fight. You will be running through a laid out course, fighting swarms of enemies as you approach the end, picking up exp buffs and artifacts hidden away through the level, the main goal of each mission seems to be leveling your characters and getting as strong as you can for the last objective.
The game is pretty restrictive of where you go and honestly, there dosent seem to be much reason for deviating from the path set out, each exp buff gives 25 exp and an artifact gives 100, but accounting for the time itll take you to get back to your teammates, it wont be worth it. low lvl monsters give 15 exp each so there really seems no point to it so far.
the level is also restrictive about where you can go as far as invisible walls go, granted you wont need to go there anyways but i guess its a feeling of freedom.
there are 4 playable characters in game and although they all come with the same kit (basic atk, ranged atk, aoe atk, single target atk, ult atk and dodge) they still manage to feel different in the way that they play and how the fights go.
Now, if you have never seen RWBY, will you be confused by playing this game? a little, its like playing Arkham Asylum with no prior knowledge of Batman, what do you expect? but the game is set OUTSIDE the main storyline so you wont have to worry about getting spoiled or being lost in the story.
Now to summarize a quick bit:
Pros
-Looks good graphically, attacks feel like the got punch or edge in them
-Characters play differently, fighting the hordes is both fun and dangerous, not too easy or hard
-Mission lenght is good, not too long and boring nor too fast
-Enemies feel different in attack patterns
-Difficulty adjust for if a player leaves/joins (also midgame joining)
Cons
-Adjustment issues (effect sound too high, BGM too low, voices too low)
-Glitches and pathing (stairs arent stairs but blocks, enemies sometimes stop up, boxes un-climbable)
-Settings menu (too few, cant rebind keys, not controller compatible)
And the big one
-Content (too little)
Now since this is Early Access some of these issues will probably see change.
And if the devs are reading as well:
What could make it better
-More characters (create your own in the style of Soul Calibur)
-More missions (seperately from the previous, where you start from lvl 1 again)
-More type of enemies
-More talents to unlock/raise max lvl
-Balancing (ranged atk. is simply to low dmg and cant be upgraded)
I like it

This game is fun. Simple, 80's nostalgic, simple, funny, simple, tubular. I think i mentioned simple.
Ok, on to the real review.
If you like (and i dare say love) semi challenging, perma-death, post-apocalyptic, tongue-in-cheek, first person shooting dungeon crawlers, this is the game for you. Man that was a mouth full. Also the music is pretty catchy.
If you get annoyed at dieing for no good reason, this is not the game for you. For example, I had a full set of power armour, all the extra inventory bags, minigun (and assorted other high level weapons) and tons of ammo. Started a new level, opened the door, right behind it was a trap that killed me without any chance to dodge. Shake it off champ and start a new character.
As i mentioned, the game is set in the post-apocalyptic nuclear world, where the nukes started flying in the 80's. Thus, the music, fashion (and i use that loosely) and manerisms of the 80's are still alive and well.  You start with a pistol and ratty t-shirt. Dive in, meet the locals, waste them and get wasted. The game will give you a couple laughs (especially if you grew up in the 80's) and you'll see a cameo (or two) of historical figures of the era.
To be honest, as of right now you only have three area's to explore with a handful of side quests. But, this game does hold a lot of potential for expansion, which i really hope the developer does. Either with free updates (which is asking a lot) or DLC. I would love to see more towns added to the game. But, at full price the game is close to not being worth it. Although, when on sale, it is a must buy.

This game is easily my game of the year for 2013. What first looked to me like a small-time indie game that probably wasn't worth my time ended up being one of the most phenomenal titles I've ever played.
This game tells an engaging story without a single word of spoken English; characters speak complete gibberish yet still convey emotion incredibly. It's only a 2.5-3 hour experience but it doesn't need to be any longer, it's the perfect length to finish in a single sitting and you will never feel that it has outstayed its welcome. The level and puzzle design is perfectly done, you should never need to think overly hard and you should always have a good idea of where you're meant to be going and what you're meant to be doing.
Graphically the game really holds its own. I can see this title being one of those timeless games that never quite looks outdated visually; it's bright, colorful and charming. It should also be noted that the control system is unusual but not bad at all, you control each brother with a separate analog stick and bumper and it works perfectly that way. Also, that's me recommending that you play this game with a gamepad, the keyboard controls work but are nowhere near as comfortable.
If you have any taste in games at all you should purchase this game, lock yourself away from any distractions, pick up your gamepad and play through this game in a single sitting. You won't regret it.
Brilliant.

This game is so good that as soon as I had finished it, I had to write a review.
BTW any possible tears you see in my eyes are fake, just ignore them for a bit. Brothers a tale of two sons had me in it's grasp for the entire game, from the simple but already intriguing beginning to the impressive ending.
It made me shed tears, block my throat and think about my existence and the life I've got.
It is a true piece of art. While it had me laydback in my chair in the beginning (I was vastly impressed by the way they made the controls and puzzle elements). But after a few minutes it had me on the tip of my chair and craving for more. The game isn't very long, and I recommend everyone to give it a bash. As well as just playing through it in one go, It ensures that you're kept into the story and gives a lot more power to the story.
You need a contoller to play this though, so if you don't have one...
I recommend you buying one and then buying this game, even if you're only going to use it for this game.
This game is a must-have and it would be a real shame to walk away from such a glorious story.
While I'm saying that Brothers has an awesome story, its story is told using not a single understandable word and to me this formula worked like a charm.

UPDATE AS OF 24/01/2016: DO NOT BUY MKX ON PC. THERE IS NO FUTURE CONTENT AVAILABLE FOR THE PC VERSION. I will personally be boycotting any future NRS/WB titles and I would encourage anyone else who bought this to vote with their wallets.
Mortal Kombat X is the successor to 2011's Mortal Kombat 9 which rebooted the franchise and undid some of the damage that the terrible PS2 games had done. It made itself known as a viable competitive fighting game and after both this and Injustice, Netherrealm began to gain credibility for their games.
As a long time Mortal Kombat fan (going back to MK1 on the Amiga!), I was hyped for MKX like many were. Now that the game has been out a few weeks, here's my rough thoughts:
+ Fully featured cinematic story which follows on from the events of MK9
+ Large cast of playable characters both new and old, including relatives of former characters
+ Beautifully presented
+ Tutorial is basic but does show you everything you need to fight at a simple level
+ More ways to make a mess of your opponent than ever before with 2 Fatalities per character and around 5 Brutalities per character as well as Quitalities if someone bails on you online. Fatalities and X-Rays look more gruesome than ever before and a couple do make you feel genuinely sorry for your opponent
+ Intuitive combat engine with multiple options to let you customize the experience.
+ Tons of different modes to play so you won't get bored, including a Krypt which is almost another game in itself
- The PC port is very poorly optimized. There are numerous crashes, frame drops, issues connecting to online, the list is almost endless. High Voltage Studios are somewhat well known for bad ports (MK9 port took a while to sort out but see Zone of the Enders HD if you want to read up on HOW bad it can get)
- Sky Temple in particular is almost unplayable for some people. I run the game on a i7 4790K with a GTX660 and I had to drop the resolution to 1280x720 in order for Sky Temple to run even remotely smoothly.
- People's saved games seem to randomly delete. This hasn't affected me personally and HVS have claimed to fix it but I can't guarantee anything.
- Not a current experience: By this I mean we're behind the console versions. There were balance tweaks (such as fixing Ermac gaining meter too easily in Mystic) that have been active on the console versions for a little while but PC is only getting them more than a week later. This means even if you were competitive you couldn't use the PC version to practice on because you're effectively playing an outdated version.
I'm not going to comment on the online play- it's been so temperamental since launch that it hasn't even been worth trying.
To keep this somewhat short:
Yes, absolutely...but do yourself a favour and buy the XBox One or PS4 versions (which are purely done by Netherrealm). Don't waste your time and money with this port. Honestly this is the worst PC game launch I have ever seen.
Update as of 24/01/16: Tyler Lansdown at Netherrealm has now confirmed that Kombat Pack 2 and the improved Netcode will NOT be arriving on the PC version of MKX. If you still want to play this get a used copy of PS4/XB1, do NOT buy the PC version if you care for any future updates. Absolutely disgraceful show by WB/Netherrealm. Don't buy a new copy; these guys don't deserve the money.

RWBY: Grimm Eclipse is a 4 player co-op action brawler that, even in its very early state, is exceptionally fun and shows great promise.  Players currently choose one of the four members of Team RWBY, and play through 3 levels fighting 5 types of enemies in hordes and waves.  While lacking the depth of something like DMC or Metal Gear Rising, each character does play slightly different, so adjusting your personal strategy to your chosen fighter is important to succeed, and is both satisfying and fun when you are firing on all cylinders.
That said, the game is still very early, albeit way better than most games that hit Early Access.  Combat needs to be made deeper, possibly with the addition of Heavy Attacks, stalled attack combos, and/or high speed motion attacks which are a hallmark of the show.  Certain special moves also need to be easier to use, such as Yang's Blast Wave, which is currently hard to land until you dump three skill points into it due to it having an awkward animation.  Music from the show is in the game, but it's used too sporadically, creating a lot of dead air inbetween the few fights where music is playing.  The fights that do feature music are feel more notable as a result, but ultimately, they are moments of good sound design amidst dead air.  The addition of dynamic music and more audio loops would be a good step to improve the audio design.  Visually the game is very nice, but the detail in the environments feels slightly at odds with the simpler character designs.  This is largely to taste though, as the show often features similar visuals.  Again, the visuals aren't bad, but some people will likely be turned off by the simpler cel-shading style.
Invisible walls also plague the environment, and there are animation glitches when characters walk down slopes, even so far as characters seeming to be randomly airborne to the point that fighting on a downhill results in doing raw aerial combos, which sadly do not have a purpose in the game yet.  The enemy selection is also lacking as well, with only about 4 real types of enemies (Burrowers, Walkers, Rollers, and Ursa) with two variants; Large types that have more health and strength, and Mutated, which explode on death.  Each enemy type does require different strategies to beat, especially when in a horde of enemies.  More enemy types, such as flying enemies or enemies against which projectile attacks are actually useful, exploding mutants non-withstanding.  True boss fights are also notably absent, with difficult fights largely just involving more enemies and more Ursa type enemies per wave.  Adding large scale, multi stage boss fights would be awesome, especially if they scale the terms of the fight to the number of players (i.e. requiring different mechanics depending on whether you are in solo or co-op play).  PVP play would also be a fun addition.  One idea would be to have players fight in the Vidal Tournament, randomizing sections of the field, and giving players a handful of points to spend on a build for that fight.
These are mostly gripes that you level at a finished game, however, and RWBY is far from complete.  But even in this early state, the game is very fun to play, which is what a brawler should be.  Deeper combat mechanics, more enemies, and just an overall polish are what remains, and if this is what Rooster Teeth are willing to call an early build, then Grimm Eclipse has a ton of promise.  Tripling the length of the game would bring it to about a $20-$30 value, but even then, the game is very replayable, and worth your time if you are a fan of either RWBY or action brawlers.

In its current form RWBY: GE has the framework for an action packed hack/slash 4 player co-op game. That being said though, the campaign currently out is way too short for me to recommend for the price. Maybe at 10 dollars until more stuff is added in. I know that 15 dollars (14.99) doesn't seem like much to Rooster Teeth but honestly I feel a tad cheated. There is only 1 game mode (that's ok) and it is the story mode I assume, however the issue of pricing became a concern when I found that the story mode has 5(Maybe more or less? I played 3 complete sets with 3 different groups and it kind of blurred) linear maps with holdout missions and nothing else. Experience points from crates are fought over (Why not share with the team? This is a cooperative game after all and artifacts count towards everyone already.) My biggest gripe would be the General Abilities which are unlocked by performing certain skills to kill enemies, reviving team-mates etc. In what universe are any of the player characters reasonably going to reach 200 kills using 1 of their abilities just to unlock a general ability like mastery? Some of the skills need work as well. I found myself only using 1 ability mostly because there is only about 1 per character worth investing in with the exception of Weiss who has a heal.
A good temporary fix for the game in its current state would be to have more Grimms per map and more waves of enemies during holdouts. This would help players get exp and pad out the gameplay because as it stands the game can be done in 30-45 minutes or so (feels like so much less)

First and foremost this game is BRUTALLY DIFFICULT. But if you're fine with that, then you may get some satisfaction with this game; otherwise don't bother, stick to Fallout and the likes. Now I spent 9 hours just to finish ONE cooler(which is like a vault in fallout) and felt greeeeeeeeeeeaaaaat satisfaction upon doing it. These are the basic mechanics of the game:
- This is a rogue-lite so there's a permanent upgrade but you can only get the upgrade once you've completed a cooler
- This is a permadeath but another character replaces the dead one(like in Rogue Legacy) but without any items
- All items that were on the dead characters stay lost unless stored in a shared stash(like the Courier Mailbox or your Home)
- You raid coolers which have multiple floors
- All floors are randomly generated
- A very high level enemy appears on every floor after a set amount of time if you quickly don't proceed to the next floor
Now I find this game fun because there's always a sense of thrill whenever you raid coolers because there's always danger. There are also rewards that the player can benefit. But the main selling point for me was that this game makes you think, and it makes you think hard and fast.

This is a great game in my opinion.
It has an art style similar to Borderlands and has a Fallout feel in terms of its gameplay, but with a faster pace.
The progression and save system is really well done in this game and makes you think twice before engaging into combat like an idiot. If you die, you lose your character and everything on them. However on floor B3 you discover post boxes which you can put stuff in. This lets you transfer items to your house so another character can use them. You can also put stuff in storage after you have a hangover, just incase you die.
Weapon variety is very small at the beginning, but increases as you progress further. I've come across about 15 different weapons now and I'm sure there's more to come.
The "invincible" purifier that appears if you take too long is very easy to outrun/outsmart and if you feel brave enough he is quite easy to kill. (He grants some good loot!) He is extremely slow and can be slowed down even further by laying down a tripping mine which will break his legs.
Overall, this game is definitely worth the £2 (got it on sale). I would argue a price tag of £10 is a bit much but the game has a lot of enjoyable content.

With solid controls and beautiful graphics, Zap Zone jumps right into action and will keep you entertained for a while.
It's a pac-man-like game with a couple of twists: you can shoot and lay mines to stop Zugs (the jelly-like monsters that hunt you throughout the game) from killing you.

Zap Zone is an extremely fun game, and brings you back to the days of burning stacks of coins in a local arcade cabinet, playing Pac-Man or Galaga. Zoey, the protagonist, is a nice nod to Pac-Man, but stays her own, with her quips being a nice touch. I recommend this game for anyone who wants to take a nostalgia trip back to the arcade cabinets of yesterday, or anyone who wants to have fun playing a simple but challenging game.

Tekken 7 is a game I waited many years for and it lived up to my expectations for the most part.
The story.... not so much.
Okay yeah, fighting games usually don't have the greatest of stories but recently Mortal Kombat X and Injustice 2 have recently shown that they can have well written stories, even if they're short.
I beat Tekken 7's campaign mode in just over three hours, and that was with a decent amount of restarts, particularly with the last couple of fights, and following typical fighting game story modes, the last (secret) fight is bs. Giving you limited health and forcing you to fight an enemy who can teleport and frequently blocks while also spamming ranged attacks? Whoever the hell designed this final fight is clearly a lunatic who loves watching people suffer.
Or maybe, maybe I just suck at fighting games. Who knows.
In fact, I was disappointed with the story, the game added ten new characters and most of them don't even feature in the story and are instead relegated to self-contained "stories" in the Character Episodes mode.
Oh and by "stories", I mean literally one fight per character which can be done in 40 secs and your reward? A cutscene thats usually a minute long. I had to bloody look up entries for the new characters on the wiki to find out their backstory, why even bother adding them if they're going to get next to no character development?
Shaheen, Claudio, Kazumi Mishima, and even Akuma guest starring from the Street Fighter series are just some of the new characters I've enjoyed playing so far. Akuma's really the only one who gets any storytime and all he's there for is to "avenge" Kazumi for her murder at Heihachi's hands.
Hopefully they add some form of additional content that fleshes out these characters.
Of course, most people don't get fighting games for the story, I'm kinda in the minority in that regard. What people get games like this for is, well, for the fighting. Tekken absolutely nails fighting in this, to be honest they pretty much perfected their combat system in 3 so there hasn't been too many changes since then.
One of these changes, however, is the addition of rage arts/drives, these work somewhat like the x-rays in the Mortal Kombat series but you don't charge up a meter to activate them, instead they only activate when your health reaches a critical level, so a well timed one can close the health gap between yourself and your opponent or completely decimate them.
Another change that I really admire is how when either you or your opponent are low on health and one of you goes to land the final blow, the game zooms in on you and slows the action down for a better look. It really makes you feel badass when you land the final blow like this, even more so when both of you throw one last desperate punch or kick at each other and you come out victorious by landing yours just a millisecond sooner.
Surprisingly, Tekken 7 doesn't have a tutorial mode to show you the basics, instead offering a practice mode to perfect combos (which I suck at still), considering its the 7th in the main series, maybe the devs assumed we don't need it, anyways the game is significantly easier to learn than the likes of Street Fighter, barring Akuma who keeps his moveset from that.
Treasure battle mode is my favourite mode in Tekken 7, its essentially an unlimited version of arcade mode where you can earn battle money and items to customise your characters with. You can also increase your payout per match by achieving bonuses such as a perfect round, streaks of over 10 etc.
Customisation itself is absolutely amazing, thus far I've fully customised three characters: my main, King, who I made into a steampunk version of himself, Leo, who I modelled after Raikov from MGS3 and Yoshimitsu, who I didn't model after anyone but ended up looking like he came straight out of Warframe. I'll probably make more at some point, if I can stop playing as King that is.
At the moment I don't really have much to say about online mode, so far I've played one tournament with some friends but due to connection issues it didn't go too well. From what I've seen by watching others stream it however, it seems to be surprisingly stable with next to no issues, barring the one I had.
In the 20+ hours I've already racked up in it thus far, Tekken 7 has quickly become one of my top fighting games, solely because of how accessible it is, the smooth combat and the in-depth customisation. If you're a fan of fighting games, this is a must.

WARNING- I have only played up to part way through act 2 of this game, but I have experience with all classes. I have not played the multiplayer.
If you like ARPGs, you have probably already bought this game, so do not need to to recommend it to you. I don't.
For what it's worth, Torchlight II is much better than it's predecessor, consisting of better, meatier combat as well as multiplayer and better difficulty. As an ARPG, it is near perfection, but as a game I find it somewhat lacking. Weapons like the shotgun and cannon could be meatier, and fighting with a melee character seems to lack impact. The game attempts to seem open world, but considering that I would have to clear out every area simply to keep up with levels, it misses the point entirely. In my opinion, the point of open world is that things are OPTIONAL- you could explore the nearby cave, or you could not. Removing that basically makes the concept useless. Mobility is done well, with dodging a powerful blow feeling very satisfying and fun, however there are some attacks that simply curve around to hit me again, removing the satisfaction. Bosses are similarly very satisfying, but also very dangerous and difficult to avoid- with a great feeling when you beat them.
The skill system is not innovative, but generally well done- nothing more to say here.
The dark music provides an interesting contrast to the cartoony art style, but I feel that the story simply isnt dark enough to fully support that contrast. However, most of the problems mentioned before are nitpicking, and the main game is stellar for its genre.
If you like ARPGs, you will love this game, but it wont turn you onto the genre if you hate them.

I don't really feel like going super in-depth with this review, but trust me when I say it's well worth $12.99.
The game pays homage to fallout in a great number of ways, and is primarily centered around vaults, or, "Coolers" in this case.  The lead developer (Mr. Podunkian) seems to be a very chill and open person when it comes to discussing development of the game with the community. He's very good at communicating current problems with the game, plans for future updates, as well as assorted development related mishaps and goings on that would typically be 'hush-hush' for most game developers.
Not-so-long story even shorter, this game feels like it has more heart than fallout (or at the very least the more recent ones of the series) with just a bit extra to really draw you in.
My only real complaint would be that the game feels like it gets exponentially more difficult as you progress, in terms of enemy health, weapon damage, and ammo scarcity. Granted yeah I get that's just the difficulty of the game bearing its teeth, but in my opinion I feel like it could afford to be smoothed down just a bit, as I feel it would make the whole experience just 'that' much more fun. On it's own though it's still great fun and I absolutely recommend it wholeheartedly.

I'd struggle to find anything bad about this game. I got it for free, from a friend, and thank ♥♥♥♥ I did because if he hadn't bought this for me I don't think I would have ever gotten to experience this masterpiece. The setting setting is a post apocalyptic 80s America, where all intelligent minds died in dysfunctional bomb shelters and the survivors fight over alchohol, which is just as great as it sounds. The writing and music are superb, and the voice acting is phenomenally accurate to the intended portrayal of the game's characters. The humor is one of my favourite parts, being the perfect amount of British sarcasm - I wouldn't be able to name another game that got a sharp exhale out of me from every single weapon tooltip.
As far as gameplay goes, it's dynamic, entertaining and entirely skill based. Surprisingly skill based, in fact, considering the nature of Roguelikes. However, more often than not you will always find yourself equipped with exactly the materials you need to survive, should you utilise them well. Enemies will shoot you, each other, and themselves whilst screaming American jibberish (just like real life) and still manage to pose quite a threat. You should never underestimate a yankie with a gun (also just like real life).
Graphically, it's runnable on my potato PC and still manages to look stunning. It's extremely stylised and does its job in making each of the randomly generated characters hilarious, and it does a good job at highlighting important objects such as temporary buffs (buzzes), traps, and storage containers.
Modding is incredibly easy, and the same friend that bought me the game also sent me his own modpack - You just drop the mod straight into the right folder, begin your game and it starts perfectly with no external launchers or workshop hassle. You can make new weapons, temp and perma buffs, and many other cool things with only a few lines of code and a texture file.

Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons. This game really touches your heart in many different ways. Before I dive into the specifics of the game, I'll go over the generalities. I'll have a more in-depth review of the ending for the people that have actually completed the game with analysis, themes, meanings, etc.
Brothers - A Tale of Two Sons is a story based puzzle game. The basic story revolves around two sons and their journey to help their father who has been struck with an illness. The brothers are forced to solve some puzzles guaranteed to make you think and help many different characters along the way. In this short 2-4 hour adventure, the game still managed to make me feel a genuine concern for each and every character introduced along the way. Not many games can really do that.
The controls are challenging, to say the least. Depending on whether you use a controller or the keyboard, the left joystick and left trigger control the older brother while the right stick and right trigger control the younger brother. Likewise, on the keyboard, WASD will control one of the brothers and the arrow keys will control another, the space bar and ctrl button taking place of the triggers. Despite these being the only controls in the game for movement and action, I found myself constantly confusing myself on which of the brothers I was controlling. This wasn't really a frustration, but it did allow for some amusing points in the game where both brothers would be running into a wall. As for the gameplay, the game pits you against puzzles throughout your adventure. The puzzle difficulty increases as the game progresses, but I wouldn't say that there were any puzzles that will keep you stuck in the game for more than 2 minutes. Many puzzles require the two brothers to use teamwork, leading to some rewarding moments upon completing a puzzle.
The graphics fit into the games core design and mood very well. Running on the unreal engine, the game runs very smooth and I encountered no significant FPS drops during the game. From being high up in the mountains to running across glacier ice caps, the game looked beautiful throughout. The game won't blow you away compared to games running on the more powerful engines of Battlefield and Crysis, but Brothers does its job very well. The music in this game is also top notch. The music definitely sets the mood and makes the player feel a certain way. Flawless execution there.
Even though I find many positives to say for the game, I feel that this kind of game wouldn't be fit for everyone. Although it may seem appealing to many people from reviews and video clips, this game is suited towards a more mature audience. If you are a type of person to play games seeking pure entertainment and wants the game to give you more than you put into it, I recommend you not buy it. I also think that the $15 pricing is a bit too steep. I really wanted to play this game for a while, and I only purchased it after it went on sale for $1.50. If you are willing to pay $15 for a 2-4 hour game, then by all means, do so. I do feel that the developers deserve that much, but the game doesn't give you $15 of content. Instead, it gives you a memorable gaming experience with many things to remember and think back on. This is the type of game that people will complete and spend a lot of time thinking about what just happened. What this game lacks in content it makes up for in memorability.
Final Rating: 9/10 (missing 1 point from length of actual game)
There will be many people that complete the game and do not see it as I do. However, the ending is a lot more dense then what you actually play through. If you put yourself in the shoes of the younger brother, the game does feel a lot more harder to bear. Your older brother just died. Throughout the whole game, you and your older brother were inseparable. If you went too far off, you would stop and you would call your older brother over. If your older brother went too far off, he would stop and call you over. If there was something that you couldn't do, you could do it with the help of your older brother. Your flaws in strength and inability to swim are gone with the help of your brother. If you couldn't reach something, your brother was there to boost you up. You became perfect. Unstoppable. With your brother by your side, nothing could go wrong. But now, he's dead.
You aren't immortal. Your flaws are back. If something goes wrong, you don't have your older brother to turn to. Not only that, you have to dig a grave for your brother and then bury him with your own hands. If you didn't think about this during your first playthrough, I suggest you replay that portion of the game and think about this. Upon burying your brother, you are taken back to your hometown. But you aren't taken back right away. You fly over the glaciers, through the mountains, past the castle. You are shown all the places that you have been to be able to get the medicine to heal your father. Getting through all these places would not have been possible without your older brother. When you arrive back to your hometown, you come across water. You can't swim, how are you going to get across? Normally, you would press the action button for the younger brother and grab onto the older brother. But this time, you press the action button of the older brother. Your brother's voice echos through your head as you swim for the first time across the lake. You come across a switch that you're too weak to pull. Again, you press the action button for the older brother and manage to pull the switch down. You come across a ledge you can't reach. Once again, you make it up while pressing the action button for the older brother. Using the action button for the older brother makes it seem that you are borrowing the strength of the older brother to do things that you normally couldn't. Keeping his older brother in mind, the younger brother is able to do things he would normally be unable to do in order to complete both of their goals: saving their father. The final cutscene shows the father crying over the older brother's grave, but the younger brother stands in silent mourning. The younger brother knows that even thought his older brother is gone, his voice will be with him and empower him to continue to push himself to do things beyond his own power.
Throughout the whole game, the younger brother is seen to have a close connection with the mother. The opening cutscene shows him mourning over his mother's death, midway through the game, the younger brother has a dream about his mother, and at the end of the game, he gets a vision of his mother who influences him to swim across the water. The older brother is seen to have a close connection with the father. After the initial opening cutscene, the older brother comes to the younger brother and asks for help to get their father to the doctor. Midway through the game, the older brother has a flashback to him and the father fishing. At then end of the game, those close connections are gone. It can be implied that the older brother-mother and the younger brother-father weren't as close as  younger-mother older-father. At the end of the game, the older brother is with the mother and the father is with the younger brother. With that, both bonds can become stronger.
Great game. If did not manage to see these connections on your first play through, I suggest going through the ending once more.

WayOut is a nice puzzle game where the objective is to push down all blocks in different shaped grids in minimum number of moves. When you press a grid, all adjacent blocks react to it. Also there are some special blocks react differently.
The game has no tutorial or any instructions but it's actually very easy to understand. Every time a new element added to the mechanic, the game gives a few easy tutorial-like puzzles that makes you get it in no time.
With the calm background music WayOut is a relaxing puzzle game until you reach the really frustrating levels. :)
There were some minor bug problems but the dev actually listens what people say and react to them. I'm sure all problems will be fixed in no time.
WayOut is a nice challenge for a very low price. Can't wait for the sequel. ;)

OLD: Combat is typical TEKKEN style, that is with loads of moves and very fast. Sometimes it's very hard to notice and appreciate the animation of the moves performed, which  becomes hectic and irritating.
NEW: Combat is great, because:
- loads of moves
- loads of natural combos and plenty of room to research your own combos
- critical properties on moves is a great addition
- slow-motion finishing hits
- counter-throws and parries, great
- crushing blows are present, great
- combat animation is superb, in particular reflecting all those states on critical hits
- stage (walls and ground breaking) interactions are satisfying
- coming after MKXL it took me time to adjust to the animation speed of this game (was hectic and could'nt read the moves visually), but once it grows on you then you really start to feel that it's almost a perfect pace of flow!
OLD: Little innovation, much of the same, but also a lot of good stuff is missing in this iteration like tag partners and some beloved characters.
NEW: Tag team partners should be implemented into this game to make it the ultimate Tekken experience!
OLD: Both RAGE moves are not to my liking and don't really mesh well in a game where sidestepping is present. This feature is usurplus.
NEW: RAGE once you know the depth of this feature, then it becomes clear how and why it adds to the overall depth of the combat.
OLD: A lot of stupid customization items that should have been never put into the game in the first place!
NEW: Stupid customization are there for certain ppl true, well on the plus side is that there are also usefull and fullfiling customization choices that enable you to cosplay your characters and transform them (visually) into someone else...
- mine's Axel Stone and Blaze Fielding, also Kage Maru :) It's too bad you can't customize King with another face (u can change masks, but not face :S)
- would welcome new customization options for weapons and some items from retro brawlers
OLD: No Bruce nor Iron King nor Lei!!!
NEW: Too bad indeed :(
- they should have been there without any excuses!!!
- on the plus, I learned to appreciate Bryan Fury a lot and he became my main (besides Kind and Josie and Asuka).
OLD: Offline gameplay modes are limited to treasure battles (ghetto version of Survival mode from the previous versions) and 5-enemy arcade (which is to short and unclimactic).
NEW: This still remains a stinker :((
- OFFLINE mode leaves a lot to be desired... at this point it merely slightly better than SF5
- Add survival mode as in previous iterations please!
- Return a *PROPER* arcade mode!
- Would be usefull to see frames data in the training mode ;)
OLD: After 2,5 hours I regret wasting 50E for this game, because it's overall lacking compared to Tag Team Tournament 2 (which IMHO was the best Tekken for me).
NEW: First couple of hours could be seen as an adjustment period, after that it was all candy and addiction :D Tekken TTT2 is still more engaging due to Bruce/Bryan tag team combos - loved that RPG factor :)
EDIT: Changed my mind after 90 hours of play time, therefore RE-EDITed the initial impression.
