I'll start by repeating what everyone else is already saying: running this game on high or ultra settings is extremely demanding. I have a mid-range PC and it is not performing well at all even at low settings. Time for a new graphics card, I guess!
I've finished the first mission so far and will update my review as I go. They've kept what works with the previous game and tweaked it to refine the gameplay. It seems like there are now far more ways to finish missions but I've found that the first few missions in a game are always like that and then as the game progresses the developers just phone it in on level design. Hopefully that isn't the case here; we shall see, I suppose.
I went with the stealth approach and was not disappointed. You are given more stealth augs at the beginning of the game to play around with but, as you can imagine, they are taken away after the tutorial mission. The new battery system takes a minute to get used to. It is similar to the previous game in which only a portion of it recharges automatically but it isn't as much as in Human Revolution; you are of course able to upgrade that as time goes on. It does make stealth takedowns more difficult as once you get to the "auto-recharge" portion of the battery guage you only have one attack before you have to wait for it to fill back up. Fortunatley, this doesn't take very long.
There wasn't much lore going on in the tutorial mission and I'm sure there are more terminals to hack / PDA's to read / etc in the later parts of the game. The world so far is beautiful, which is of course why my computer vomits while trying to render it. :D
The cutscene and on-rails-conversation going into the second area of the game was pretty buggy for me. Citizens would just pop into existence a few feet away from you and then you and your companion would walk right through them like they were ghosts. Some of the civilians would even be walking around and walking through essential characters (security guards) and walls. I will say that so far that is THE ONLY glitch I have run into with the game. Since we're all used to the first day of a games release being a nigh unplayable mess, this is way better than usual.
Gotta go to work for now; hope to tweak some graphic settings later tonight and see if I can get it more playable before I go splurge on a video card. If anyone has any recommendations on a decently priced modern card feel free to leave me a comment! I'm not as up to date on tech knowledge as I used to be.

Okay, so I just finished this game and let me tell you...it was EPIC! A lot of you Deus Ex fans (like me) will be wondering if this game is better than the previous one. Well I can tell you it is, not by too much as the previous game is a hard one to beat but I think this game tops it.
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided is such a great game with a solid story, enjoyable gameplay, smooth combat, awesome augmentations (more content) and amazing graphics. I only have a few minor issues with the game and one of them is the frame rate which most people will be aware of, some of the best PCs are having a tough time playing this game on max, even I played this game at meduim/high settings (you can see my PC specs on my steam profile) which I wasnt to happy about at first but even on medium/high the game looks outstanding, I cant really complain about the graphics at all. The developers have already talked about the frame rate issues on PC and they have said they they will be adding Direct X12 support on the first week of september.
Another problem I have with the game is the lip sync, it can be very poor at times. Now dont hate on me becasue I understand that lip sync is hard to get right and especially for this type of game (huge), you can tell the developers have tried their hardest and thats all we as gamers can ask for. Also Deus Ex games are more based around story and gameplay anyway so its not much of a problem, just thought id mention it.
To sum up this review, if you have a beast of a PC then I recommend this game as you will be able to play the game on high settings at about 30-50fps. But if you have a lower end PC then I would wait until they bring out DX12 support as this will increase FPS (smoother gameplay). The game will last around 15-25 hours depending on how you play the game, I finished it in about 19 hours and I enjoyed every second of it.
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided = 9/10 (Reviewed on PC) - Me
Deus Ex: Mankind Divided = 9.2/10 (Reviewed on Console) - IGN

***EARLY ACCESS REVIEW***
From the day one release of this game I'm gonna say this is a smash hit.
Too many games have been released on Steam's early access program in a barely playable, or sometimes not even playable state; however this game works great straight off the bat.
In brief the gameplay, which is obviously always a key factor in games, is incredibly fun and pretty addictive. The thrill of hacking, slashing and shooting through hoards of Grimm is brilliantly entertaining and with the four star characters, each with their own upgrades and perks to enhance their abilities adds a great replayability factor to the game.
The graphics are pretty ok for this early alpha of the game, the overall level design is pretty simple but still good looking, and the overall feel of the current areas are kinda immersive.
A few issues with video and audio options, for instance the battle sound effects are a bit loud without the option to decrease their levels since you can only change music and voice levels. A few bits of audio clips sound a bit raw and their is a bit of frame rate stutter (For me atleast).
Overall this is a great multiplayer game, a good time waster or just a good game to play with friends.

This game obviously has awesome gun mechanics (and that slow-mo kill camera is insanely, hilariously cool, especially when you use armor piercing bullets to blow up a vehicle and the surrounding nazis) but it also has great level design and level flow.  I felt like I could choose slow or fast combat, sneaky or loud, traps or whatever, and they were all very fun!  It definitely kept it from getting old, because you can just try playing the next level a little differently.
Mega kudos to the level designers btw.  The level design is fantastic.  Open parts, nooks and crannies, high/low, sound masking, just a ton of stuff to discover.  Easy quicksave and load system also lets you feel like you can try out mechanics and strategies without fear (which is awesome).
My only big gripe was that I couldn't disable depth of field (dof where some things are out of focus / blurry like a camera focus).  I know some people like that it's more "cinematic," but it got in the way quite a bit when trying to shoot, snipe, and survey the area with binoculars.  Hopefully the next in the series has a way to disable depth of field it, because I really want to play the next one, and can't wait!

This is a game designed by a sadist and targeted to masochists. Unless you don't mind losing your sanity keep away.
There are difficult games that are fair and others that aren't. Spelunky belongs to the latter category. First of all, there are things that can happen off-screen that are out of your control ex. a shopkeeper aggros from environment hazards. I really like rogue-like elements in games, it always keeps things interesting but if you keep things almost completely random you will end up with some very ridiculous level designs and other game elements. There were many runs where I had ridiculous amount of gold and couldn’t get a single shopkeeper with even a 3-pack bomb. Even in the secret level there was only one with one pack! Whole runs up to the temple where there was no jet pack in site etc. Also level designs where the key/1up was in an entirely inaccessible place or one where you had to waste 3-4 bombs in order to get it and level designs that are almost unwinnable unless you have tons of bombs. A more semi-random level design would have been preferable like for example in Super House of Dead Ninja or Risk of Rain.
Secondly the controls are really bad. The whip has good range in the front but has very limited range in the 45° angle. This makes enemies that are coming diagonally to you, very hard to hit and there are many of them. Also one of the worst things is the hanging from the edge. There is an item in the game that makes you hang all the time and instead of making things easier for you in most cases it makes them worst due to the bad controls. Designer could have included for example an option where only if you hold the jump button you could hang from an edge. Another example of bad controls is that you need to hold down + button to pick up an object. In the heat of battle this can be a big problem because it takes some time for hold down + button to register and you end up with no item. This has happened many times to me. The problem could have been solved simply by using a different button in the controller or keyboard as the “pick up item button”. Things like that were excused in the NES era where programmers were forced to do things like that due to hardware limitations but we are in the 21st century we have controllers with 15+ buttons what’s the point of using things like “down + button” anymore? Just to frustrate people?
Overall this game reminds of some NES era games. Instant deaths, no continues, a final boss that one shots you, bad controls, it’s all there. I believe Spelunky falls in the difficult-frustrating category rather than the difficult-fun category (Dark Souls, XCOM etc.). It’s a pity because with a few adjustments this game could have been a legend of the genre.

Deus Ex: Mankind Divided has an extraordinary amount of problems, most of them technical. My experience appears to lean on the more unusual side when it comes to how many bugs I encountered. If we ignore bugs, then we’re left with some baffling decisions they made for this game. I’m going to go through all of them before I cover what the game did well. Also, for those people concerned with extra DRM for whatever reason, DX:MD still uses Denuvo. Let’s begin.
Unfortunately, even after numerous patches since launch, some problems still persist. Besides the fluctuating framerate that I never resolved, my favorite example is the shooting range crash which still exists after they claimed to have patched it. I completed the shooting range tutorial 4+ times and crashed every single time I tried to exit or skip its cut-scenes. I just wanted ebook inside.
My quick save corrupted and the whole saving system malfunctioned. I thought I was saving for that section of game, but the save symbol was a deceitful lie. I had to spend an hour of troubleshooting to find out I did lose about an hour or more of active questing. I started saving much more frequently and made sure the saves saved which slowed down the pacing significantly.
I’ve seen doors kill people; I’ve seen stairs kill people. I’ve had major characters and the game tell me to spare the rest of their comrades or that I’ve been on major killing sprees. They scolded me as if I’d been murdering people and even convinced me that my Pacifist playthrough was ruined, but after beating the game, I received the Pacifist achievement. The game’s inclination to send you mixed signals and have unintentional deaths make non-lethal runs miserable so I’d recommend going stealth-action.
The loading times are absolutely atrocious. You might need to be wary if you have a 7200 RPM HDD for games instead of an SSD. My overly long playtime of 66 hours had around 3-4 hours spent on loading screens. Players that explore or do all the side-quests will have to use the subway system frequently. I did my best to complete everything I could before taking the train due to the long wait. They didn’t have the decency to include more than a handful of scenes during the 1+ minute load times in Prague when traveling between sides while using the subway. DX12 had my system take up to 2+ minutes per load so have a stopwatch handy to track the loading times for the DX version you want to use.
The game has some superfluous features such as Breach which isn’t interesting unless you want to compete again friends for score and time. Both Breach and Mankind Divided have micro-transactions. You can purchase credits, Praxis points, or the Breach nonsense. Fortunately, the main game seems to be properly balanced which makes the inclusion of those microtransactions even more out of place. Even some of the in-game collectables feel pointless as they unlock videos that were on Youtube already or extra content for Breach.
The main mystery seems fine and is mostly resolved by the end, but when it came to the meta-plot, the game ended on a cliffhanger in a post-credits cutscene.  It’s as if this game is merely the first part of another. Human Revolution handled it better overall despite the CYOEnding with how much it gave you to mull over and how the story elements were intertwined. Here, you don’t have as much to sink your teeth into and the conspiracy elements felt strangely separate from the main game. There are other cliffhangers too that involve other major and former major characters. At least you’ll still have some interesting life-and-death choices to make.
Here are some one-line complaints: many civilians could have been given their proper names according to their computer or pocket secretaries versus being labeled as “Civilian” in-game; the console UI makes inventory and the map slightly annoying; the lip syncing is awful, don’t look at it; takedowns will occasionally not line up correctly and which results in Jensen punching the ground angrily; and I’ve seen a major character stand over its dead body, talking to its phantom trapped my character in the floor.
The game has one boss fight that can be handled lethally or non-lethally. DX:MD doesn’t need to rely on boss fights and does well without having unnecessary ones. You’ll still run into other showdown type situations with specific characters should you decide to take a more aggressive approach to the game. There was at least one other encounter that I consider a boss fight had I not used my silver tongue to defuse the situation.
The variety to approach is strong with this title. You can persuade people to do what you want, hack doors, go through vents, move heavy things to access more vents, break grates in vents, hack various objects such as drones or cameras from a distance with the new Remote Hacking augmentation, break open walls, or be a psychotic serial killer. There seems to always be an alternate path or point of entry to reach your objective to accommodate different players and abilities.
DX:MD supports both non-lethal and lethal playstyles with interesting, new augments. I definitely liked the Tesla one which can electrocute multiple enemies in one go if upgraded. You can even give yourself a P.E.P.S. augment if you want to simulate Force Push. If you want to turn yourself into a moving fortress, take the Titan augment and laugh at the enemies’ attacks. Icarus Dash, an augment I suggest everyone take, let me have a good time. You can use it in the air or on the ground and the enhanced version lets you target where you want. Remember those swords in your arms from Human Revolution? You can shoot those now if you want.
There is plenty to explore for the obsessive player in this good looking game. Hidden apartments, pocket secretaries, doors concealing loot inside, and side missions. If you engage with the content, you’ll probably be entertained around thirty hours. If you just play through the main missions and touch nothing else, you’ll blow through the game quite quickly, especially if you decide to abuse the cloaking augment (try not to use it). Some of the side missions are pretty interesting, especially The Harvester and 01011000.
Unfortunately, my overall experience was frustrating and underwhelming. I did have fun with the game, but the bugs and overall storytelling soured me on the whole experience. If I were you, I’d only purchase this game during a sale as it only partially provided the triple-A polish I expected which seems to be an epidemic in 2016. I know I’ll be wary with future installments in this series.

It's like a speedrunner version of Borderlands in the Bethesda version of the Fallout universe. Unfortunately, the game does a very good job of pretending it has more depth than it really does. It is a high quality product, but there's not nearly as much content as the average player would expect if they spoke to any of the Ony Express folk.♥♥♥♥♥♥(a character in-game) informs the player of several cities and gives vague enough descriptions that it almost sounds like the game will take you there eventually. You never leave the coolers or Ony Express.
As far as gameplay goes, the controls are tight and feel good. This is a first person shooter with a heavy UI influence from Borderlands. It's quite fun once you figure out how items work and are able to get ahold of some "hangovers" (recurring buffs) and "buzzes" (temporary buffs). The visuals are generally fine considering the cartoonish nature of the product. I found it difficult to tell whether what I was shooting was what I was hitting at times due to an immense amount of thick particle effects on screen, but this is not a major issue once you get attuned with the gunplay more.

It's early access, so it's tough to give it a full review, but I kind of like it a lot more than I thought I would.  RWBY: GE has some weird targeting issues that need to be resolved and I'm not entirely convinced some of the specials are working properly, but just dropping into a beat em up is surprisingly enjoyable.  This is apparently the first campaign.  It's hard to review because I'm not sure that it is quite done yet as you spend a lot more time in the first area and less and less in the other two, but it is mainly dealing with waves of enemies along with the occasional sub-boss and a more objective based final task.
The combat is simple, yet still fun and engaging.  Each of the four characters has a main attack, a ranged attack that can end combos, three specials, and a dodge that you will definitely need to be using.  Specials are used for massive damage, but can only be recharged by maintaining a combo streak without getting hit.  I played online with strangers and didn't have any issues other than a host leaving once at the end of the level and having the game reset us to the beginning of a set of waves.  The online component encourages friendly competition, awarding extra experience for those who perform the best in waves and displaying a total k/d count at the end of every level.  One pretty neat feature is that the game also scales in multiplayer, so while the challenge in single player feels pretty good, things get even more crazy when you have a team of four playing together.
From what I understand, the game is meant to be a bit like a MOBA where none of your stats carry over from run to run so if the idea of mostly starting over doesn't appeal to you well....you'll just have to deal with it because that is how it works.
Keyboard controls felt awkard to me since you can't rebind as far as I know and using shift + WASD is a bit uncomfortable.  My 360 controller plugged in fine and the controls are quite a bit better since you can use the analog stick to move and LB to dodge.
It's a flashy game and it is fun to play with others.  There are some issues that I'm sure will be fixed as the game develops and right at the moment it is a bit short, but given it is early access it is really quite solid and I'm looking forward to seeing it progress more.  I'm not a diehard fan of the series, but I enjoy it enough to want to support a game for the series.  I never really thought they would bring the flashy combat over to a title and after trying out RWBY: GE tonight, I'm very glad they did!

The game is in a very early and rough state but there is a good deal of potential.
- Turn down mouse sensitivity.   It will feel extremely twitchy and it will be hard to build up the combo points needed to use one's special abilities otherwise.
- Certain characters are not as effective as others but this can be worked on with time or skill.
- There are audio issues.   The voice dialogue and music are nigh on non-existant or so quiet they can't be heard but what can be made out fits the feel of the show.   Turn on sub-titles in the meantime.
In short, for a very early version of the game, it is a lot of fun with a group and while, rough, is actually playable, has a good visual feel, and despite it's issues, is better than a good deal of other early access games floating about out there.
If you are a fan of the show and have some friends to log in with, grab it and enjoy.    If you have only a passing interest, perhaps wait for a later build to arrive that will iron out the issues within in but I think it will get to be a very enjoyable game by the time it finishes developement.

NEW: Combat is great, because:
- loads of moves
- loads of natural combos and plenty of room to research your own combos
- critical properties on moves is a great addition
- slow-motion finishing hits
- counter-throws and parries, great
- crushing blows are present, great
- combat animation is superb, in particular reflecting all those states on critical hits
- stage (walls and ground breaking) interactions are satisfying
- coming after MKXL it took me time to adjust to the animation speed of this game (was hectic and could'nt read the moves visually), but once it grows on you then you really start to feel that it's almost a perfect pace of flow!

You do get a core group that you can level up if they survive, but they only go to the 3rd rank and level up fast and you could only deploy a fraction of them, so there is no reason to give them priority over the noncore units. The medic and sniper are really powerful in the game. The medic can heal your infantry rather quickly and your infantry doesn't even die that easily even to tanks and even move at about the same speed. The AI is bad at threat assessment, just shoots whatever unit is the closets to them. The AI also doesn't react to being shot at if the unit is out of their visual range. There are secret objectives and side objectives, but I really didn't bother going out of my way for them. Pathfinding kind of sucks, you can blockade yourself on narrow paths or your units will go in all directions trying to avoid the traffic jam. Hero units are nothing special expect the tank stealing power one. Weather didn't change my tactics. Also, it seems like you can shoot through buildings.
There are 7 main missions each for the Russian, German, and Allies campaign. 4 for an UNISPIRING french one and two 6 alternative history missions. I only found the German campaign fun, because some of the mission felt more like a war than a skirmish.

South Park: The Fractured but Whole has one of the best innuendo titles I’ve ever seen. Ever. That includes porn.
I’d like to say that this level of cleverness remains constant throughout what is essentially a 10ish hour long South Park episode, but the humor (as with anything this long) is a bit uneven.  But it works, and any fan of South Park will enjoy the time spent with this game.
The gameplay is a little more tactical than its predecessor, but it still remains simplistic for the genre it occupies. That’s okay, as South Park: The Fractured but Whole is about the characters, story and toilet humor – all of which it pulls off near-flawlessly.
Unfortunately, there isn’t anything here for people who aren’t fans of South Park, and the gameplay certainly does nothing to draw in a novel audience. Beaten! - 49 Hours
Wasted is what you get when you mix a permadeath dungeon crawl, a traditional FPS, a loot system, RNG, and Fallout.  A floor-based shooter with loot and powerups. And death. A lot of death.
Game Loop: Traverse 11 floors of a dungeon(s) in an FPS. Kill or avoid enemies, manage inventory.  Every 3 levels, have the option to opt out by taking a beer (which also gives you some sort of stat modifier) at the end of the level. It's effects (negative or positive) stay with you when you go back. You start on floor 1 again, but with all the stuff you had on you.  Rinse an repeat until you feel ready to go further.
Pros:
- Fun!  Its a well made dungeon crawl with loot!
- Art style and setting. Not that it is impressive or anything.
- Ability to go home and store stuff for later runs.
Cons:
- Can be a bit hard
- In order to return to your home without dying, you drink a beer at the end of a series of levels. You get a choice of random ones. MOST of the time these are negative effects. So when you go out again, you have to deal with these effects in exchange for going home and stashing loot and money.
- If you take too long on a floor, the ai is sent to basically kill you. So you are encouraged to move fastm which in a rogue like is not usually a wise choice.
Protip:  The game only saves when it reloads a new character. So if you die and you have a bunch of perks,etc - ctrl-alt-del and exit. You will restart back with all your stuff when you get back in.

Curator Review:
This Rogue-Like Platformer has captured the hearts of thousands as it took the Steam Stores by storm in 2013. Take control of a novice spelunker and watch yourself turn into a masterful tactician of the game. With each dive you learn a little more about the game and the game pushes you further and further. The game is not only addictive with each successive dive but it is also elegant in its' fully destructible and procedurally generated terrain. This game is a piece of art with how it accomplishes entertaining players. Unfortunately, it does not have a story, and that is a big loss for me. That being said, there are few games that come better designed than this. 8.1/10

Yet another extremely attractive indie game where your playtime consists of meaningless runs where you ended up accomplishing literally nothing.
Similar in concept to games like The Binding of Isaac, Spelunky has you going through various randomised levels until you manage to not screw up enough to make it past all the unforgivable enemies and environments.
By unforgivable, I mean that everything moves fast, knockbacks with the power of The Thing, and your mercy invulnerability lasts for a small fraction of a second. Additionally, dynamite explodes instantly when grazed by blood splatter, all objects hurt and knock you back if they have even teeniest bit of velocity, and the League of Shopkeepers will hunt you down if a spider dies by an arrow trap at their doorstep.
Despite all the annoying bits of fake difficulty, Spelunky has that charming something that keeps you playing, and when you finally get out of the first set of levels, you can already feel the satisfaction and the need to push forward. That is something that few games manage to accomplish.
Quite worth the price tag, 4.5/5

After reading many other user reviews, I was worried I was gonna hate this game. Fortunately, this game (for me, at least) falls into the catagory of "very hard, unfair at times yet still
". As explained in the game's synopsis, each run has me being more cautious and learning from previous mistakes while still trying not to take too long due to the invincible ghost enemy appearing after a while. The controls and game physics aren't hard to get used to, and there's even a replayable tutorial that covers all the basic fundamentals of gameplay.
This game is very hard, but it is very manageable if you take your time through the levels; it takes 2 minutes and 30 seconds for the invincible one-hit-kill ghost to appear, and that's ample time to get to the exit. In all my hours of playing, the ghost has only been a serious issue less than 10% of the time. By not rushing through the levels, you're able to see a lot of traps and enemies ahead of time and prepare to tackle each level's challenges.
Edit: 282 deaths later and I finally beat the game (4-4 ending, not true ending). So this game IS possible. It just makes you feel terrible when you can't consistently make it to world 3 despite having beat the game. Looking back, I can safely say that everything the negative reviews say are 100% true. Prepare for that when you play.
Edit #2: On my 450th attempt, I cleared the game's true end. This game is far from impossible; it just takes great patience and dexterity. Even after completion, I still find myself playing it a lot. This game truly is a masterpiece of its kind.

Pros

- Lovely Environments
- Awesome Music
Cons
- If glitched out of bounds, it can be difficult to return in-bounds.
- Strange Running Glitch for going down hills that keeps them in a single frame of their running animation.
- Weiss is kinda..glowy..it makes it hard to tell details on her primarily white character model.
Glitches Discovered thus Far in this Early Access Version
- Glitch near first Reactor (or whatever they're called) where Weiss (but seemingly no one else) can exit through a cracked wall but is then stuck behind an invisible wall. Not game breaking, you can go back through the crack just fine.
- Glitch near a Crystal Formation in a Cave in Emerald Forest Pt. 2 where you can jump & attack to get out of bounds, getting higher up each time (note: only tried with Blake, Weiss, and Yang. Yang seems not to go through). If you fall in a bottomless pit, it'll break your Aura but not kill you, so you have to re-start. If you run around the outside, Invisible Walls will keep you from re-entering the area. You have to go back to the beginning of the level in order to fall back into bounds where an invisible wall is broken enough to pass through.
Some Recommedations for the Dev Team..
- It might be nice to allow players to save their characters upon leveling them up since re-leveling them in each playthrough can be a little tedious, honest.
- A targeting system, similar to the system used in the 3D The Legend of Zelda games & Hyrule Warriors, would be a nice addition, especially to make it easier to fight only the 'Big' enemies or to keep track of the Boarbatusk Grimm due to how fast they zoom past you.
Outside of Feedback on the game itself, I also have some suggestions for unlockables or DLC, whichever would be preferable to the Dev Team,
New Characters would be fun as unlockables and/or DLC. Some great choices would be Team JNPR, Penny, Team SSSN, Team CFVY (once Velvet's Weapon is officially unveiled), and perhaps even some non-student characters (since these characters would be more-or-less non-canon for the Story of the game anyway) such as Cinder, Neo, Emerald, Mercury, Winter, and perhaps even Qrow. Granted, I know this is a lot of characters, but I'm sure fans would pay for a good portion of them..especially some of the more popular ones like JNPR, Penny, Sun, Neo, and Cinder.
Alternate Costumes. What can I say, gamers love alternate costumes, especially if they're unlockable, though many would still pay for them as DLC. Pros:
- A amazing sinleplayer (more in depth review under this quick pros and cons) (single player is also very easy to cheat with no need for downloading mods, that is if you want to. )
- active online community with fun battles with each server being differant
- Custon battles you can start instantly with a randomize option if your bord and just want to fight
- MODS - SOOOOOOOO many great mods if thats your thing, not needed as the game without is still great but the option is what matters
Cons:
- it is an older game (however it runs and plays perficly fine)
- can be a bit grindy during single player but that is sort of part of it

Singleplayer:
A great and fairly detailed game were you start of with choosing  your backstory, effecting your starting stats, and then you can do pretty much what ever your want from being a leader of hundreds of low costing peseants to a powerful ally of the kings or even a mercant buying and selling goods.
There is a fairly large map full of differant kingdoms and alliences fighting and teaming up to take castles and raid villages, each with differant troops and thus having differant stregths and weaknesses.
You will start of your journey in one of the kingdoms and have to start low with hireing cheap workers from the villages that you sill train over many battles to one day even make your own kingdom.
The gameplay consists of a sort of top down map to travel on to differant kindoms and towns but on this world map there are other groups of looters and bandits etc. If you get into a encounter you will have options on how to handle the situation and if you choose you fight you will put you into a 3rd or 1st person perspective with your army which you can command to follow you etc. When in battle you will be able to use your equiped weapons inclueding crossbows, bows, swords, shields, axes, hammers, polearms, and even throwing wepions. You have multiple directions to attack with making combat fun and livly. You can also hire individuals with certain benefits and you can give them gear and train them to be good at skills (Like tracking) so you can focus on skills you want (e.g power draw) while still having the skill to alow you to track down foes on the map
There is also many quests to complete to gain honor and respect from mercants or kings giving you something to do :D
How to cheat:
However it can feel a little grindy at times with having to hire men and train so you can easily cheat to have even more fun and options if you want just by going into configue in the launcher, then when in game go to your characters page and click statistics then export character, once you have done this alt tab to your desktop then go into your documents and find mount and blade then find characters then choose that character you want to have the cheats. This will open up a file containing your characters stats money etc just ajust the numbers to your likeing then save the folder (only chage the numbers). Go back onto the game then click import character next to the export you used earlier and you will have the adjustments you made. You can also ctrl click on the map ith cheats to teleport and ctrl x on a troop selected in your party to give them xp
Multiplayer:
You can join a quite large amout of people in duals, battles, and sieges (sieges are sort of like capturing the base with you being able to break doors, climb ladders, and puch a tower to the walls and climb up) which are all great fun with the fighting being realy cool and enjoyable with directional attacks and trowing wepions etc
Bonus Custom battles:
Although they are not the focus of the game at all, i find my self experimenting with things like 200 archers vs 25 cavalry just for fun and it is just a nice little extra to the game!

I have read some reviews that say the game is extremely difficult, but fair. The first part is true, it can be extremely difficult. The latter part is a lie, it's not at all fair. Probably 1/4 of the times you die will be things you have no control over. Examples, you say? All of these are things that have happened to me while playing:
1. You find the exit to the level only to discover it is completely enclosed. You need a bomb to get in, but you're out of bombs.
2. A spider is hanging on the ceiling but you can't see it because your "score" card covers it up, so it drops on your head.
3. The exit is below you and the drop is far enough for you to take damage. You don't have a cape, parachute, jet pack, or rope (God help you if you get to the ice level without these items and/or a compass).
4. An explosive frog not even on screen gets hit by a Tiki spike trap, explodes in a shop, and that sets of all shopkeepers to immediately attack you.
5. A spitting cobra spits on a shop keeper.
And so on...the game is *really* stacked against you. Luck plays a big part. If you don't get certain items, the game becomes a LOT more difficult. That having been said, it's extremely fun and addictive. I just wish it were a little more "fair".

Since everyone is just talking about the price, I feel obligated to say that THE GAME is very good. You will find it hard, even in not reccomended reviews, to find people who say otherwise (although SOT was probably better). Yes of course the DLC and 60$ base game is way too steep a price but it's not a complete scam.
Do not buy this game if you are not a fan of south park. I thought this one was easy. In order to appreciate the jokes you have to like gender politics, politics in general, non-PC and, of course, farts (they have to go back to their roots eventually). But this game is the funniest game I've ever played (except for stick of truth of course).
The gameplay is improved. It really feels like your skills improve and you can try out a bunch of different combinations of classes and team builds. You also definitely feel a sense of character growth (you start very weak and end very strong). Also the lines and ultimate attacks are hilarious, you never really get tired of them (Tweek and Craig's gay couple attack is so funny).
There were a lot of shortcomings, even though the game was delayed TWICE. The game was buggy. I had to restart a few times and couldn't move at one point. Come on, this isn't a bethesda game. Good fans know it's worth it to wait for a complete game, it should have been delayed again. Also day 1 DLC is super cheeky, and the full game costs about $100. WTF?? Also, there needed to be more side quests!! Finishing ALL the side quests probably takes only about 25-30 hours.
Conclusion is that if this is on sale for 25-50% off, then it's a great game and you should buy it! At 50% i would give it a 9/10. But at full price, it really cuts it close to being worth it, so I would give it a 6/10.

I can recommend this game by saying Yeah it's still funny and you'll still get an okay RPG but...
It's not as good as the stick of truth but the reason for that is because obsidian was not involved (Ubisoft was a bad choice to allow to develop this game also their DRM is horrible why not just make me install securom while you're at it)
The game starts out in a really sub-par way that just doesn't feel as good or as fun as the original, you're offered a very lackluster opening tutorial that lacks any real depth or enjoyment that the first one did. In the stick of truth you are given a fast tutorial that is not only funny but also well rounded and leaves an opening for more.
The world looks bigger but it actually feels smaller in scale considering less enemies are scattered around the map in random locations until near the end where there are much more.
In the stick of truth Kyle's elves were all over the place and just felt like they were placed with care and never to close or too far apart. Where as in the fractured but-whole it's mostly butters minions and raisens girls occassionally thrown around and later ninjas but no super villians besides professor chaos, (seriously there should be other kids dressed as villians in this as another faction to fight)
The combat it self is decent and adds some much needed depth and challenge with it's grid based combat but also manages to feel wide as an ocean but as a deep as a puddle, removing things like blocking and countering makes certain fights feel much longer than need be, even with the "Press A to recover some health after being attacked" nonsense it still doesn't feel as good as the stick of truth.
During most fights with 4 heroes on my team I could only ever use 1-2 of them to actually attack a single enemy (which is a great strategy) due to some of their attacks being blocked by their own team mates which frustrated me and felt like I was pointlessly skipping turns to try to move a character across the battle grid to get them to an enemy they could fight.
Another flaw is it took way too much from the most recent seasons of south park. I understand that the world of south park should stay current, but I feel as though the games don't have to follow what happened previously in the past two seasons (or atleast let me beat up and defeat PC principle)
The stick of truth happily stood alone from the tv show's modern seasons and it was better for it by creating it's own bubble and world that felt oddly enough real and believable to the kids and the players. You felt as though you were really there in the stick of truth and along for the ride.
The game also lacks a-lot of set piece dressing, of course you see kids dressed as super heroes but you don't see any set pieces related to it no battle damage or massive destruction that effects south-park the same way a crashed UFO did in the stick of truth (it's basically like in the avengers civil war where they're fighting in an empty airport and not much damage is done around them)
Even when there is some mild changes to the town during the night where the kids sneak out it's mostly cleaned up by morning except towards the end where you see a few things laying around like beer kegs or maybe a few piles of trash but nothing that really matters or says "the kids were here at one point"
I was really disappointed and left feeling empty due to the sheer lack of any thing resembling the stick of truth's gameplay or ideas in practice. If it's not broke don't fix it, but apparently ubisoft's motto is "If it's working let's change it entirely and mess it up"
The game also has absolutely no collectables to find what so ever and a real lack of decent sidequests  leaving you to not really wanna explore things outside of finding different recipes and crafting materials for costumes or consumables.
Also there's never a really weight to anything your doing, you never feel that you aren't gonna be able to stop what's happening in south park, it just feels like a run of the mill episode as a opposed to a season with an ark and a climax.
when it comes to your fart powers you never feel like you earn them or gain any kind of cool benefits from them, you just get to a point and morgan freeman says "hey new kid come to my store and eat a taco and fart to glitch time"
The fart powers do shine when you and another hero most combined your powers to overcome a problem, but even then it feels as though these become over used and were added for extra padding to the game time.
The game also features bugs that cause it to crash or freeze up towards the end during important fights.
South Park The fractured but whole is an example of corporate meddling and fixing what isn't broken. It's damn clear by the sudden and poor meaningless ending boss fight and actual ending that it was not only rushed but forced to continue with crappy DLC.
It's definetly not a full price buy. this is a wait till it's 20 dollars in a year and get it then kind of game.
It's a fun game, so South Park-ie. But once done, there's nothing left. There's no point to replay it.

Still using Weiss’ 1 skill to freeze your opponents is an easy combo start of for any of your team members to play on. Likewise Blake’s 3rd ability can give ruby a nice set up for her reaper attack.
Because this is an alpha I’m not going to gripe on the small glitches or on the character movement frames.

DISCLAIMER:
This game has a lot of potential. For early access, potential is good enough for a positive review. I would not reccomend this if it were the final release though, don't buy this and expect a full and perfect game from this. It's in early access for a reason. It's not done yet.
First thoughts:
Overall RWBY Grimm Eclipse is a fun, fast paced game, that could definetly use a lot of polishing up. I personally love it, and therefore I'm going to do my best to mention the general flaws in this review, and the specefics in the forums so that this can be the best game possible when it launches.
Gameplay:
Combat is fast and fun. I've primarily played as Ruby and Yang, and it feels really powerful when you run into a giant pack of beowolves and slaughter ten of them with a single ability. It lives up to RWBY combat for the most part. However, I never liked fully upgrading abilities. Fully upgraded abilities take two resources (called "special", which is gained back by getting combos on enemies) instead of costing one, like it did prior to fully upgrading. It just feels better to spam it twice as often rather than have the abilities do more damage with the additional effects.
Leveling:
Something to keep in mind is that you don't keep your levels from each game. The only thing that carries over from each game is your progress towards completing challenges. When you complete a challenge, it unlocks an ability that you can then choose when you level up. Each character has an unlockable ability when they reach level 10, which all have something to do with making it easier to get special with combos.
Speaking of reaching level ten, it's not paticularily easy. Experience is given to the player that kills the grimm, which kind of creates a competitive aspect to a co-op, which can either be fun or frustrating depending on your outlook. I always felt kinda guilty killing more grimm than my friends, since I could end up a level and a half ahead.
Multiplayer:
Players can drop in anytime through the first chapter, and you can join a friend currently playing regardless of what chapter they are in. Everyone can play as any off the four huntresses avalible. Want a team of four Ruby's? Go for it. On one hand it's nice, since it means that your waifu isn't always taken, but it's weird, cause there can be three other people playing as your waifu right in front of you. As for balance, the most powerful team seems to be one of each huntress. However, since certain characters are more AoE damage orintied, while others are more ulility based, the AoE damage dealer tends to get more kills, getting more levels, which gets them more kills... it's a vicious cycle.
Music/sound:
Jeff Williams is a God. However, some fine tuning on the transitions between tracks/dialouge could go a long way. Voice acting was solid, though I personally thought there were a few lines specefically from Blake that sounded off. Sometimes enviroment sounds would make it difficult to hear the dialouge. Sometimes in combat I got tired off hearing the same grunts over and over again.
Enviroment:
I love the level design. There are collectiable artifacts scattered throughout each level, which grants everyone on the team 100 exp. It's always fun to find one down a little corner you never saw before. There's two to three on each level,There's some pretty bad geometry. I don't apreciate having to jump over a street curb. Also, running down the stairs and inclines is... interesting.
Graphics:
Beautiful, even on potato.
Conclusion:
This game has a lot of potential. However, potential doesn't make for a good game. It's in early access for a reason. It needs a lot of polishing, and a lot more content. If you're on the edge for buying the game after reading those giant blocks of text, then wait until the full release. Early access is not meant to be the full experience of a game, it's more of an open beta to help the game get to where it needs to be for the full release.
TL;DR:
If you're not a fan of the series, wait until the full release.
If you're looking for a full and satisfying game, wait until the full release.
If you're willing to put up with a lot of bugs and want to support the game, buy it right now.

Sniper Elite 3 is a solid, if more accessible, entry to the Sniper Elite series, the quintessential Sniper series out today.
I still own Sniper Elite 1 for the PS2 and I still believe that it is one of the most difficult game experiences ever made, even compared to Soulsborne, Ninja Gaiden, and DMC 3. It featured intentionally limited HUD, limited saves, limited ammunition, and sprawling maps with hidden enemies that instakill you, leading to an immersive, oppressively difficult but rewarding experience.
In comparison, Sniper Elite 3 has objective markers, aim assist, enemies marked on maps, regenerating health, light RPG elements, quicksaves, and the levels, while still quite open, are laid out in long stretches like most games. Sniper Elite 3 still maintains a certain level of difficulty, but is much more friendly to a casual game player, which is definitely a plus for many, but I still want to point it out.
You play as a covert assassin in WW2 taking on axis powers in Africa, which gives the game a much more colorful and visually interesting setting than the perennial war-torn Europe. You are given a host of different weapons and explosives, but your bread and butter is, of course, your sniper rifle. The game allows you to hold your breath and shows you the true reticle, adjusted for wind and bullet fall. This, while much easier, takes a lot out of the challenge of sniping, but it is balanced by only being accessible while holding your breath.
The most enjoyable aspect of the game are the slo-mo x-ray bullet kills that are triggered by a well-placed shot, which organically incentivize effective sniping.
For the most part, the game levels feature multiple buildings, vehicles, and cover that lend themselves to stalking around and stealth killing your way through the level, with multiple options for carrying out each objective. There are also optional side objectives and collectibles. However, out of nowhere the game throws escort missions and sniper protection missions that throws all your stealth and planning out the window. I found them contrived and stupid, and they marred what was otherwise satisfactory game play.
However, there is a lot to recommend and it is an overall solid experience that is much more friendly to the newcomer than the previous entries and features a large variety of gameplay options that lend themselves to multiple play-throughs.

I'll start with the negative first:
This game gets tedious. There's been a handful of times where I'm stuck looking for the portal to the next world, or for a specific ore for more than a couple minutes. I get it-- it adds longevity. But why would I want to explore a specific randomly generated dungeon if the only difference between this world and the world before it are that this one spawns a crystal ore instead of metal?
Further still the inventory management is the games most severe problem currently. With this type of game, it's expected I'd have to dump my inventory in a chest or two periodically... But this is bad. I often found myself every ten minutes or so having to revisit my homeworld just to make another chest or dump my inventory into a pre-existing one. This begged the question- did I really need some of this stuff? Should I even be keeping it?
My last negative point is the bugs- which I've already seen improvements on through updates so I'm really not too worried. Things such as disconnects when playing with friends, the game freezing, etc. Rest assured, they're becoming far less common, but still happen.
Positives:
Combat is tight. It may be simple... but very tight, and there's something endearing about it. You can make the odd spell, even as a typical warrior-class to help with combat, and on occasions the game can be a potion-guzzler that harkens me back to Diablo in a strange way. But the responsiveness of your weapon swinging, the knockback your weapon causes feels snappy and precise.
The crafting system has plenty of potential. It may be derivative and a tad lacking at the moment. But you can easily sink an extra couple hours into getting that next set of armor, and it's a tried and true formula.
Aesthetically, the game really shines. It may be a bit on the cuter side, but the amount of moving grass or trees on-screen are really pleasing to the eye.
Other comments:
Optimization is interesting. I'm operating on a 4790k and one and only one of my cores are maxed out. Share the load!
And secondly, variety is kind of "middle of the road" at the moment like I mentioned in cons prior. There is SOME variety between worlds... but this is just akin to biomes in other creative-exploration-style games. You may come across 3 worlds in a row all incredibly similar. But there IS a good sense of variety between different biomes. The desert feels distinct to swamps and forests, it's when you compare your 3rd forest in a row that I find unflattering to the game.
Worth a buy in any case. There's plenty of potential here.

While I'm still feeling neutral towards recommending this game, I'd say this game is decent enough to get a thumbs up
(+):
* Combat is decent enough, I personally liked the combat mechanics of some mobs and bosses
Equipments (although some are class locked and is pretty annoying, but I suppose that's to balance things) have decent variety, with various stats, in a way it motivates the player to mix and match (there's no set bonus in the game) and use what they think is good.
* Overall quality (texture, lighting, etc) is good and the view is pretty sometimes.
* Multiplayer makes it more fun (just like most coop game), and now with the new update players can go to different islands separately (although needs stronger host to compensate for loading multiple islands at once obviously)
* Replaying the game might be boring (islands aren't 100% the same but they are generally similar if they are the same island number), but there's 3 class that's pretty different from eachother that you can choose when creating new character, so there's a bit replayability.
* There's random events that happens periodically. Seasonal events, too.
(-):
* For a sandbox, it feels 'empty'. There's only like 60 types of blocks in the game (excluding furnitures, but including unobtainable blocks, and blocks that're pretty much just a recolor of other blocks)
* Obtaining materials for crafting better equipment early on is easy, but later on it gets *ridiculously* expensive (e.g. 3 copper ore = 1 bar, and 1 copper pickaxe = 1 copper bar. Endgame? 10 ores = 1 bar, and a pickaxe is 8 bars.), and of course the endgame materials aren't easier to get than early game.
* Some decorative/vanity items are too expensive, limiting your (already) choice of blocks to build with even more.
* The gameplay is pretty short (I have 70ish hours put in and already at late game of my 2nd gameplay), but I suppose worth the money (esp on sale)
* Most events are imbalanced to me. It's either trash event (no decent loot whatsoever, or good loot extremely rare) or op event (literally gives me 1k+ of high tier ores in one run)
(?):
* The game itself is fairly casual (excluding anything past the hollow king), pretty good game to chill on
* Inventory might be annoying to some players, but I am fine with it (chests NEED metals to craft, which means higher tier chest is also affected by that increased crafting cost i put in (-) part of my review, but you can always spam copper chests).

No, just no.
Okay it's a shoot'em up, obviously.  Tiresome Japanese style story spam before you get into the action.
But seriously, it's not for PC.  It runs in windowed mode, you can't even go to fullscreen, you have absolutely zero control over the graphics configuration.
Gameplay is the same as any other (but better) shoot'em up.  If you like shootemups, this is still not the game for you, because it's worse than all the other ones.

POSITIVES
-----------
• Optimized Good Graphics:
Runs easily on high graphics, looks great, and the art style matches with the graphic quality.
• Personality:
Each character has a unique and wacky personality that matches their design, the game feels full of life with the intro cutscenes, campaign, and character customization that makes each character highly changeable which allows each player to give themselves a name and custom look for the character they chose to play.
• Many characters:
There are 30+ characters each with their own moves, personality, look, movement, and rage mode. This creates countless combinations of battles and fights that you may have.
• Multiplayer:
It's in the game. More on that in the negatives.
• Fair:
This game is free of unfair advantages, no purchasable upgrades, and the in-game fight tokens you earn for playing matches are used for cosmetics and not a replacement for skill.
NEGATIVES
------------
• Multiplayer is bad:
The multiplayer is rough and doesn't work well, either there aren't many players searching for the same match as you due to matchmaking standards, IE: players both need to be similar skill level, experience and in quick match. You get disconnected from roughly 50% of the matches it finds, and when you find a match sudden disconnects in game happen often. If you are looking to play multiplayer competitively in this game, I would hold off for buying it until it gets fixed.

Shmup Love Boom is a vertical bullet hell in where you play as some anime teenager who is the last hope to fight off the aliens. Your character has no name and you will be able to give him a name after completing the first mission. You will be accompanied by one of the two AI women of your choice and together you will fight your way through hordes of enemies. Your first choice is a purple haired girl that gives your ship missiles that fire randomly and the second is a brown haired girl that fires laser beams randomly. Each are dressed differently and will strip off more of their clothes each time you lose a life. True to the visual novel genre there is a lot of talking, mostly about uninteresting stuff like how you were the ace pilot of Earth even though you appear to be a 13 year old emo looking kid. There are tons of spelling mistakes in the game and is a rather uninteresting tale from what I have seen so far. I have not finished this game or played more than an hour for reasons I will state throughout the “review”.
To start off there is no full screen and when you try to alt+enter into it you will only see the upper left of the game. That means you will have to play on a tiny window. Okay, fine, I could live with that but you will soon discover that you control this game solely with the mouse. That is already a big mark against the game as most prefer using a controller or an arcade stick for this genre but due having to play on a tiny window with your ship being at the bottom, your mouse cursor will frequently go outside of the bounds of that window, causing you to lose control of your ship. In a genre where the slightest distraction will spell your doom that is a fatal flaw. Even if that were not a problem the controls feel floaty and delayed, it feels like you are dragging your ship around instead of being in full control. Your ship will automatically fire when you move around and it does remind you of a phone game though done much worse. Enemies are bullet spongey as well so there is no real sense of impact when you shoot them.
That lack of impact is also due to there being no sound effects. From you dying to projectiles being fired there are no sound effects to be found anywhere making the game feel drowned out by the music. Unfortunately the music is not all that great and gets old fast. So far we have terrible controls, no sound effects and are forced to play in a tiny window. Surely it can't get worse right? Wrong. Once you lose all of your 5 lives you will be thrown all the way back to the start of the game. While not uncommon for bullet hells (even though most feature continues) that is a terrible idea for visual novels as you have to go through all the text again and again. There is nothing interesting to be read the first time around so you can imagine how tiresome that would get. While fighting enemies they drop blue items that when enough are collected will upgrade your firing speed as well as other benefits. Sadly even collecting them is a pain, the range that you have to be to attract them is very low and even when you are in range it takes a long time for them to zoom into you which means a lot of them will be dropped as you are forced to dodge projectiles.
There is so very much wrong with this title. It may actually be less time consuming to list the positives of the game. The graphics are okay. That's pretty much it. Though they do not do a good job at distinguishing the projectiles and often times found myself killed by something I didn't see coming. At this point it really does feel like I am just picking on the title but it is not beyond redemption if more work is put into it. Fullscreen, savepoints, controller support and some other tweaks may make this title worth a play-through at such a low price. As it is right now there is no way I can suggest this title to anybody, it feels like a prototype of a game by people that don't understand how to make a bullet hell. I truly can't speak of it's worth as a Visual Novel given the low amount of time I put into this title but given it's uninteresting opening and common grammatical errors, it wasn't a compelling reason to force yourself to start from the very beginning every time you fail at the terrible bullet hell sections. The bullet hell sections add nothing to the visual novel and the visual novel adds nothing to the bullet hell gameplay. It is a Frankenstein of a game that will appeal to neither of the genre's fans.

It has potential, but it misses the mark in a lot of really important ways. With some tweaks from the dev I could see this being a great game, but as it is right now (v1.2), it's just not there.
I really didn't like the way most of the upgrades worked. The first damage upgrade is just a flat 40% bonus, but the second two upgrades in the tree either increase the damage again at the cost one of your three health bars, or cut the original bonus in half to get a fourth health bar. After you go a few nodes down any branch of the tree, it felt like I was more focused on mitigating all of the penalties I had accrued rather than actually improving my ship.
The game balance feels a bit off. I spent all of my upgrades increasing my damage at the expense of everything else. Even with that, everything still takes what feels like ages to die. I'm constantly having to deal with multiple waves at once because I can't clear them fast enough, and the screen is just blanketed with enemies and bullets. When I respecced for health instead of damage, it was even worse, and I couldn't even kill the first enemy before I blew the time goal.
It also baffles me how a developer can put in the really nice option of restarting just the boss fight and not the entire level before it, but have that skip bring you right up to an unskippable cutscene. The restart boss option is great, I wish more games had it, but even skipping the dialog portions it's a full 20 seconds from hitting restart to actually engaging the boss.
The last issue I have with it is that it frequently wants you to make really precise, minor adjustments to your positioning, but it doesn't really give you the tools to do so in a way that feels good. Some of the boss patterns, and the ring sections at the end of each level, expect you to navigate very tight spaces, but you ship only has one speed, and that speed is tuned for dodging the bullet hell parts of the levels. There is no button you can hold to slow your movement speed, so you have to quickly tap back and forth to keep from drifting into things, and try and tap for a few frames longer in one direction so when you balance out you're a bit more to one side.
For $10 there are much better games in this genre out there, and even on sale it's probably not worth it unless you've tried everything else.

This is an interesting parody of Fallout in a rogue-like format, which on the surface is an interesting concept.
However... If you like exploring, gathering gear, and just taking your time to enjoy things, then this game isn't for you. You see, while the game is interesting, it's strongly tied to a mechanic that forces you to rush through the game. The game developer himself has declared that this is a core aspect of the game (and while it can be modded out, the game becomes trivial that way, and you never have to make certain difficult choices).
This means you have the option of playing the game at a rush, unless you want to get stuck in a fight with a cheap, uninteresting bullet sponge *or* modding the game to take away the need to rush, and revealing that the game is ultimately pretty shallow (as well as removing some 'story' elements).
Is the game fun? It depends on if you really mind being rushed through a game. If so, then I guess my recommendation might be a 'yes'. If not, well, if you disable the 'hunter', it could be for a while.
Either way, I wouldn't recommend the game at full price, and I am definitely not a fan of a developer who reacts to fans asking for more options with what is basically an eye-roll in text form and dismissing their desire for options. For that alone, I wouldn't recommend buying this game at all.

I have read some reviews that say the game is extremely difficult, but fair. The first part is true, it can be extremely difficult. The latter part is a lie, it's not at all fair. Probably 1/4 of the times you die will be things you have no control over. Examples, you say? All of these are things that have happened to me while playing:
1. You find the exit to the level only to discover it is completely enclosed. You need a bomb to get in, but you're out of bombs.
2. A spider is hanging on the ceiling but you can't see it because your "score" card covers it up, so it drops on your head.
3. The exit is below you and the drop is far enough for you to take damage. You don't have a cape, parachute, jet pack, or rope (God help you if you get to the ice level without these items and/or a compass).
4. An explosive frog not even on screen gets hit by a Tiki spike trap, explodes in a shop, and that sets of all shopkeepers to immediately attack you.
5. A spitting cobra spits on a shop keeper.
And so on...the game is *really* stacked against you. Luck plays a big part. If you don't get certain items, the game becomes a LOT more difficult. That having been said, it's extremely fun and addictive. I just wish it were a little more "fair".

Well, given that this is an early access version of the game, it naturally has some issues...some greater, some smaller (looking at you there "running animation"). So let's get right into it.
Pros:
-It's fun (smashing buttons and kicking a Grimms butt with a scythe/rapier/double-sword/YANG is just entertainig as f*ck)
-Great athmosphere (charakters look like in the show, and also sound like it...for the most part...Blake sounds kinda off. Enviroment is in-tone with the style of graphics, so that's good)
-The Bomb-mission (ok, I'll admit, it isn't much of a challenge with 3 other guys, but if your teammates pass out during this one, it's gonna be a hard one. Still the best part of the objectives in the game so far.)
-The humor (Potato-Graphis, "That was AWESOME", and so forth and so on. The humor of the game [though rarely encountered as there isn't that much talking] is great and very much like the show).
Cons:
-It's repetetive (Uh, big suprise I know. Given the approximatly 30 minutes of existing gameplay, and the three objectives "kill that", "protect that" and "power that" it's not much of a suprise, that so far it's just doing the same thing over and over and over again [yes, I know, I played it for several hours so far...])
-The walking/running animation (Whenever you start walking or stop walking or stop attacking, it plays a "walking" animation for a splitsecond, where the model barely moves, but slides across the ground at maximum speed, before changing to the "running" animation. And the running animation only ever stops about a second after the player has stopped moving. This isn't that much of a problem...but, you know...)
-Going up/down cliffs (here the model bumps and looks really bad. But once again, not much of an issue.
-There are several types of enemies ("creeps", "Big Creeps", "Beowolves", "Big Beowolves", "Boartusks", "Ursa", "Big Ursa" and the "KABOOOM-Creep". So it's not that much of a variety, but the real thing is...there is no BOSS feeling in any of these opponents. Sure, the Big Ursa tanks a lot, and deals♥♥♥♥♥♥tons of damage, but the moment you can freeze the grimmidimmi he's as dead as Yangs puns. That said, the only "challenging" opponent in the game is the friggin Boartusk, and even that thing isn't scary after you get the drill of dodging [such dodge much wow].)
-The experience (Ok, to be honest. All of the above listet cons are...things, the developers are most vertainly working on, but I really do hope they change this **** level-experience system. So here is the thing: You get experience based on the amount of grimm you killed. Sounds fair...NAAAAAAY, because if you are the unlucky one of the team, you will end up being level 6 in the fourth chapter, while that arrogant Schnee heiress crops around level 9 laughing at your underleveld face. Experience should either be given to all players equally or not per grimm but per objective cleared.
-The leveling...skills...and stuff (I enjoy a MOBA just like the next forever-alone-guy, but this might not be the right system for a 4 player survival game...given that the purchased skills do not change THAT much of the game. You will still do approximatly the same amount of damage [slight improvement], and you won't unlock new moves [and no, even the challenge-skills are no real new moves]. You can upgrade your tankiness [healing and "hitpoints"] but neither your damgae, your attack speed, nor your "special"-creation-rate [12 hits is easy to get against most of the grimm, but those friggin ursine break my combo every time, when they gank me as a pack]. It would be really nice to have upgradeable stats like "melee-dmg" or "ranged-dmg" or "hitpoints" or even "special per sec" things. Sounds conventional, but still better than those challenge "upgrades". Speaking of those...
-The challenge-skills (so yeah, there are a few moves [I think it's 5 per charakter or something like that] that can only be unlocked for purchase, after fulfilling a certain objective in the game [or possily more games]. They go from simple tasks [like Yangs special] to almost impossible ones [FREAKING GET LEVEL 10!!! HOW?!??!?!!]. And some just take so much time, it's not worth getting them [like the "Dust shadow" unlockables]. And it's not just that. The third upgrade of an ability makes it cost 2 points of "special", BUT it does NOT hit twice as hard. The only skill so far, that really pays of for spending 2 points of "special" for it's effect, is Weiss' FREEZE, for it makes even the hardest enemies look like punching-bags)
So much for the gameplay, now the UI and the menu:
Pros:
-The potato-graphic option (hahhahahaha, I'm still laughing at that one)
-That's about it.
Cons:
-Almost not customizable (you cannot adjust the controlls, the sounds, the mouse speed, the brightness, and all these things, every game has an "adjust"-option for.)
-Title Menu (The Title Menu shows a part of the "Emerald Forest"-Map [obviously, since it is already in the game] but I must say, I expected something like Beacon-Akademy or a World Map of Vale, or the Kingdom, with a marker at each chapters location. It kinda feels wrong there).
-Charakter selection (There is only text at the selection. Certainly would look cooler if an image [or the model] of the charakter would show, with a short description, or even the difference in their gameplay explained).
The Charakters:
-Ruby Rose
Ruby is a lot of fun to play. She has by far the most enjoyable commentary, and just hacks through oppoents while looking all kawaii-cute and♥♥♥♥♥♥[WEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEEH]. Her basic attacks and "Special" abilities are hard hitting and AOE + her ranged shots and the 3rd-special ability have extreme range, so she is the perfect charakter for the newbies. Aaaaaaaaaaaaaand she has a scythe, which is also a sniper-rifle. Now what have you got?
-Weiss Schnee
In my opinion (and I played her the least to be honest) Weiss is the weakest charakter in the game, and rather little fun to play, mostly because she has mimimum range, and dies at the mere sight of an enemy. This is UNTIL you unlock her freeze abilities. From that point on, Weiss quickly turns into the strongest charakter in the game, and makes her allies appear useless, as she can easily deal with every enemy wave on her own. She is SO damn strong it really hurts to play her, and I felt really bad for all those grimm. Honestly, playing her is a bit of a crime, and should be punishable (talking to those XP stealers out there).
-Blake Belladonna
The faunus-girl (that's a secret) feels somewhat different. Her combo attacks hit very hard, and can be upgraded to hit even harder (even so far as to generate an additional hit [special-incoming]) BUT her abilities don't deal as much damage compared to the rest of the team. The first and second one see to be dedicated to movement an deal rather little to no damage (but you got the combo attacks for that, so it's actually rather cool), and the third is a somewhat-ranged slice, that somewhat-hits-the-enemy from time to time and acutally can deal a♥♥♥♥♥♥TON OF DAMGE. In my opinion the most fun to play tied with Ruby.
-Yang Xiao Long
She always starts out HER mission with the "Yang"...get it?...because...ah...nevermind. Yang has the shortest range of all the 4 charakters, but feels the smoothest when fighting against single opponents, with the animation being the least stiffy. Her abilities are versatile and deal good damge + her ranged attack is a short-ranged shotgun pump. BUT as much fun to play she is, Yang friggin Xiao Long attacks incredibly fast with her ranged attacks and is ths perfectly able to steal you every piece of experience on the map (even unintentional). +While her "special" makes you gain full"special"-bar with depleated aura, she gains NO bonus damge on her combo hits, and doesn't change her eye colour to red (as in the series). This would have been a cool looking feature (probably still gonna be).

Abalone is a strategy game with very simple rules (the tutorial will take about a minute of your time), but is pretty tricky to play.  I've never played the physical boardgame before, but this digital version seems solid enough, and in addition to the requisite multiplayer options, has many single-player scenarios to teach you the basics and progressively tougher strategies (I've only played SP so far).
See those screenshots on the store page? That's exactly what the game looks like--no bells and whistles here.  I've encountered only one music track so far, and it loops pretty fast, but I just turn it off and play my own music... or have silence if I need to concentrate, which is most of the time ;) The controls are very simple, and there are easy ways to backtrack if you accidentally click on the wrong piece. However, you can really tell this is a port of a game that had touch controls; small things like having to move your cursor all the way to the bottom right corner to finish your turn could have been a bit more streamlined for the PC version.
The big question for single players is: is the AI good?  As of now, I'm working through the scenarios to learn the game and the AI is still at the Easy level, but as a complete newbie I find there's still a fair amount of challenge to be had and I'm improving and making steady progress. I have very mixed feelings writing this. The game itself was a lot of fun, and I really enjoyed the unique way of controlling both characters at once. The puzzles were mostly easy to solve, but I like that. It allows me to enjoy the experience without getting frustrated and still concentrate on the story being told.
Which brings me to the story. Tragedy and sorrow can be powerful and valuable things to explore through a story. I've read plenty of sad stories before that left me feeling sad but uplifted. You just have to be careful about how you present it and make sure you show the little rays of light that give value to the struggles the characters are going through.
This game does none of that. The closing scene is the most depressing and worthless end to any story I've ever read before. There ARE good things they could have shown to help bring a feeling of worth to everything you went through in the game, but instead they just depress the heck out of you and leave it there.
If you're ok overlooking that, the game itself is a LOT of fun. Controlling both brothers to solve the challenges they face is both challenging and rewarding, and I honestly enjoyed that part of the game.

A great and fairly detailed game were you start of with choosing  your backstory, effecting your starting stats, and then you can do pretty much what ever your want from being a leader of hundreds of low costing peseants to a powerful ally of the kings or even a mercant buying and selling goods.
There is a fairly large map full of differant kingdoms and alliences fighting and teaming up to take castles and raid villages, each with differant troops and thus having differant stregths and weaknesses.
You will start of your journey in one of the kingdoms and have to start low with hireing cheap workers from the villages that you sill train over many battles to one day even make your own kingdom.

How to cheat:
However it can feel a little grindy at times with having to hire men and train so you can easily cheat to have even more fun and options if you want just by going into configue in the launcher, then when in game go to your characters page and click statistics then export character, once you have done this alt tab to your desktop then go into your documents and find mount and blade then find characters then choose that character you want to have the cheats. This will open up a file containing your characters stats money etc just ajust the numbers to your likeing then save the folder (only chage the numbers). Go back onto the game then click import character next to the export you used earlier and you will have the adjustments you made. You can also ctrl click on the map ith cheats to teleport and ctrl x on a troop selected in your party to give them xp
Multiplayer:
You can join a quite large amout of people in duals, battles, and sieges (sieges are sort of like capturing the base with you being able to break doors, climb ladders, and puch a tower to the walls and climb up) which are all great fun with the fighting being realy cool and enjoyable with directional attacks and trowing wepions etc
Bonus Custom battles:
Although they are not the focus of the game at all, i find my self experimenting with things like 200 archers vs 25 cavalry just for fun and it is just a nice little extra to the game!

NEGATIVES
