Spelunky is a Adventure Game were you explore randomly generated caves that extend far beneath the surface of the earth. While you search for treasure, you'll also encounter several different areas in the depths of the cave, such as an abandonned mine shaft, a subterranean jungle, an alien infested ice cavern, amongst others. The goal of the game is to reach the bottom of the cave you entered and claim the ultimate treasure, but that is easier said than done. You only have four hit points to begin with, and most enemies do more than one hit point, and some traps can one-shot you. And, if you die at any point in the game, you have to start all over. They're ways around this, like buying special items like shotguns and jetpacks to help you avoid danger, or you can build special shortcuts using specific items. If you were planning to buy Spelunky just for single player, I would recommend it, but prepare to have your patience tested.
Spelunky also features two competetive modes: The Daily Challange and Arena Mode. In the Daily Challenge, you get one shot to get as far down in the cave and collect as much treasure as you can before you die. When you die, you have to wait another day to try again. In Arena Mode, you fight against your friends in a, you guessed it, Arena-isk scenario. Both of these modes are a lot of fun and worth chenking out if you had beaten to game before hand.

I made a firm decision to never buy anything in early access after getting burned one too many times. However, I've been a long-time fan of Roosterteeth and I follow RWBY with a passion. I also played the original fan-made version and the pre-alpha on the Roosterteeth site. So boy howdy did I buy this as soon as it went up.
The first thing I should point is that I'm obviously going to be biased towards the game, but I'll try to point out some of the flaws. Bearing in mind this is the first version of Early Access, so I bet in a few weeks this review will be entirely outdated.
Pros:
- Combat: Solid hack and slash combat. Each character has three unique skills as well as a general skills that are shared between the characters. Weiss for example, has a lunge attack, an AoE and a long range barrage attack. Special attacks use up segments of your special bar, which can be refilled by chainging combos on enemies. Enemies are reasonably varied and require different tactics, although once you've played through a few runs you begin to determine the best ways to beat them, so it's a case of memorisation e.g. Beowolves can be killed with a single combo, Ursas take multiple and you should avoid their ground pound etc.
- Upgrade trees: Characters can level up their skills over the course of a campaign. You get 9 points (assuming you reach level 10) to invest however you want, and at the end of the campaign your character is reset. This MOBA style leveling allows you to play different roles each time. Using our Weiss example, one playthrough I might max out her Nova AoE attack, allowing me to freeze enemies and control the crowd. Another run I might max her lunge, letting me quickly dispatch high health enemies. Challenges that let you unlock special skills are persistant though, so once you unlock them you never have to again. This rewards people that play the game with special upgrades as time goes by.
-Voice acting: Since the game is made by Roosterteeth, all the characters have the same voice actors as the show, which really puts you in the world. Ruby and Yang especially make you feel like you're taking part in an episode.
Character variation: Each character has a distinct style of combat, so it's really refreshing to switch between them. Yang is very much an in your face brawler, Blake excels at moving around the battlefield picking off targets quickly, Weiss can provide incredibly useful support in the form of freezing, Ruby has superb long range attacks and varied skills for any situation. Additionally, the unique passive skills you can unlock feel perfectly suited for each character, tied to their history and styles.
Cons:
- Bugs: To be expected for Early Access, but surprisingly minor bugs so far. Characters suck at going down slopes, their animations freeze or stutter until they get onto level ground. If using a controller, moving at low speeds causes your character to glide. Blake has a weird period of glide if you move immediately after firing her gun. Ruby's ranged attack propels her backwards, so sustained firing can cause you to sort of merge into walls, although I've not gotten stuck from this yet. However, the combat is absolutely solid. I've heard that two characters that are downed next to each other can revive each other but I've not experienced this myself.
-Jumping: To be honest, the jumping feels kind of pointless so far. Most enemies are low enough to the ground that jump attacks just miss, and the ones that you can hit (like Ursa) you're better off getting a ground combo off for full damage.
-Short: While the character leveling and variation lends itself nicely to multiple playthroughs, at the moment there's only one campaign, spanning four 'stages'. It can quickly get repetitive, but there are a planned 3 total campaigns. That's probably around 3-4 hours content if you play multiplayer, more in singleplayer. But, the real appeal is in the character development so this should balance out fine.
Overall, if you're a fan of Roosterteeth, RWBY or solid hack and slash games I highly recommend Grimm Eclipse. It's a small team of 4 developers, but since they're not on a schedule and this is basically a side project for RT they can take their time and make exactly the game they want to make. Very fun, High replayability, Great matchmaking/co-op and less buggy than Assassins Creed.

When you require a walkthrough within the first few minutes of the game because the game designer hides a key object behind your character, you know something is going to be wrong.
This isn't a game with multiple solutions to the puzzles. The cryptic game design wants to you figure things out in a very specifically scripted way with zero clue as to what the hell the game designer was thinking. There's no internal puzzle logic within the context of the design. No clues, just snarky commentary as you try to do something that might make sense, only be to told you're wrong (and sometimes, only barely, like needing to use a blowdart on a window, rather than the target, in order to use the necessary blowdart on the target).
Hours of aimlessly frustrated wandering around, and soon you'll be wondering why you're still playing.
When "puzzles" (more like cryptically hidden scripted events) absolutely REQUIRE a walkthrough to complete, and, upon looking up the solutions, the player can't help but think "AW COME ON!" or "WHAT THE HELL I TRIED THAT ALREADY DIDN'T I?!" you know you have a problem with your game design.
Thus, I give up by the time I reached the junk yard area, where apparently I'm missing an item (even after interacting with every known object in the vicinity and consulting a walkthrough). You can try to get further than I, but you won't have fun doing so.
What you'll have is boredom or a headache. That's all this game has to give. Hard to enjoy it's laughs with such stonewalled pacing.

This is just a quick review of the first play through. I only have about 4 hour of play time in Portal Knights so I will update as I log more hours.
First off this game is amazingly pretty. When I got into the first world I was amazed at how pretty everything looked.
The tutorial is decently helpful but I wish it was a bit more in depth on a few things.
From what I've seen you don't even have to build a house to live in since there are already dwellings built. You just have to fix them up.
Everything you need to build and craft items is scattered across all of the worlds. So if you don't have coal then you'll need to travel to a world that has coal. Luckily when you go to the world map and click on the world you want to travel to it will tell you what resources are located there. So that’s kind of a plus.
The combat is a nice feature. Something I've noticed is with the right kind of weapon you will do extra damage to an enemy depending on what it is.
There is an RPG fact to this game that I adore simply because I love RPGs. There are different weapons you can craft as well as armor. your workbench, furnace, anvil, and everything you use to craft different items can be upgraded. You also have different traits and attributes that you can upgrade to increase your character.
Leveling is a process. If you are constantly killing enemies then you will level pretty quickly (I only got to level 8 in the first four hours) but if you are like me and want to explore and see what all you can find, do and craft then it will more than likely take a little bit.
For now, the only thing that bugs me on this game is the fact that I have to go to different worlds to find different resources but I'll get over that pretty quickly as I progress through it.
Updates to follow as I log more hours.

Mankind Divided is a triumph in every aspect (well,almost). The game improve every aspect of the original, but not the history, the weak point of this one, and not the missions, here's only a few missions in other places (low variety). But about the gameplay itself where Human Revolution was perfect Mankind Divided are perfect too, and where Humans Revolutions has its flaws (very few, but still), Mankind Divided are perfect. There no need to talk a lot about the game, everyone here know what will find: a deep action-rpg, a complex and incredible well writting plot, a impresive cyberpunk world, a complex gameplay with multiple paths, multiple ways to do the same things, choices that matters... so if you like Deus Ex this is a must have, right now. If you like semi open worlds games with actions and stuff, this is a great option and if you look only for a shooter... hey, maybe is not the best option (the gunplay is something heavy sometimes like in its predecesor) but still a great fps (but isn't its main focus).
With all this in mind, I must say that Human Revolutions was a better game, the history was more complex and way better, and the variety of missions and scenarios was greater.
Overall Human Revolution it's a better game than this. And one thing I really hate on this one, they broke the tradition of various cities... there's only one city to explore (and not very bigger)
The ambient, the enviroment, the multiples secrets, the lore, paths, the verticality of the scenarios, the choices, the graphics... everything in here are perfect. The game adds many things like crafting, weapons, abilities and movements. There's a lot to do, to discover and find.
The history and its context is very current, so much, scary.
Special mention (like with Human Revolution) to Michael Mccann, his music is incredible, perfect and grants the game a greatness even greater.
About the performance, Nixxes talks about it and said that the "very high" and "ultra" options are for a top equipment (above the recommended spec) so maybe there's many people who want to play on ultra settings without a top gpu or processors, and they are complaining for reasons like that. I don't know, but I have a system very similar to the recommended specs and I currently playing with all the options activated, all in very high and with MSAA x2 and I haven't any problem, the game run smooth, 60fps and no crashes or weird things. Sometime a puntual fps drop and things like that, but they fix it in the future with a patch.
And about the microtransactions... after 7 hours I discovered there was microtransactions when reading reviews on Steam lol... so I don't care to much about it. Is it ugly? Yes. But unfortunately is a common practice nowadays (looks Phantom Pain for example), but well if someone want to buy an augmentation with real money rather than explore the game to find it, well, the free will and stuff, you know? It's a single player game, noone gets hurts.
The first DLC is just a cut part from the main game (well, they launch it one month after the main game so...) and it's overpriced (only adds 2-3 hours of gameplay). And that thing about play it from the menu, it's like meeh, it's feels like a fragmented experience without sense, your decisions has no impact it's only a mission out of the game.

That being said, the introduction to this game is phenomenal. It looks gorgeous and the refinied mechanics from previous titles stand well on their own here. Incredible cinemtography in cutscenes alongside seamless transitions to gameplay have (so far) made for an incredible begininning.
Hub gameplay is flawless. Open areas with incredibly detailed side-missions are engrossing. Managing augmentations, customizing weapons and taking care of your loadout is fun and complex. There are not enough good things I can say about Mankind Divided.
Story is an incredible letdown, which causes me some pause when recommending this title. Should you get it running, the game is a mechanical masterpiece. But the story is depressingly short-lived and the ending is abysmal. Tread carefully if you are expecting a detailed story.
In the end, it's a great game mechanically.

As of now, the game is unplayable. Crash to desktop at start.  Will change review when this is resolved.
-edit-
Day 2 patch fixed CTD issues. Super fast response time on the part of devs which should be applauded. Since I was reading up on it, they put together a response team that was ready to go when the game launched to troubleshoot.  Approach to releasing a game that should be emulated by others.
Overall impressions in the first parts of the game is that it feels like Deus Ex but I can see why more than a few reviewers gave it 80-90 ratings.  The control scheme still feels a bit clunky, there are some odd narrative choices that don't mesh, and they continue to use the same button for leathal and non-lethal takedowns (Can't even change in settings? Really?).  If you are a fan of the series, this is most certainly a must buy.
-edit2-
Yet another CTD issue that is preventing me from finishing the game. Literaly on the last mission and unable to complete because it crashes.  The reason why I am switching this back to a negative is because I honestly have no interest in completing the game.  I suppose we could forgive the abundant bugs and other technical issues, but in terms of a game its rather... meh?
Gameplay-wise it seemed combat was the most tedious way to proceed.  It got to the point where I'd rather just cloak, sprint past guards, and multi-tool through all the doors. Combat just feels clunky and not worth the extra time. I ran into constant issues such as invisible walls, objects with too large of a hitbox, AI detecting me through walls, and the autosave kicking in while I was in cover resulting in me running out into the open when I loaded back in.  Gave up on the iron man approach after that one.
Story-wise it just feels like they tried "enough".  There were a few arbritary moral decisions that just bugged me.  Do you pursue this one lead or another? Its not like you work for Interpol with a few field agents a block away that could lend a hand. Those sorts of plot devices worked in the previous game as you were truetly operating alone and off the books.  Likewise Prague or Golum never really felt "alive", they just felt small and almost on the rails.
You should get the game, but for maybe $40. I don't regret getting the game but I would not recommend buying it right now.

This game is amazing. It is quite possibly the best rougelike game ever made, and boasts an excellent time as you learn how to beat the game one area at a time. Now, there are only four areas, plus an optional and somewhat secret fifth and some special levels, so you may be tempted to think that it will be easy to get each area down. It's not.
The allure of this game, is that every single time you die you know that it's 100% your fault, not because of a lack of balance or a bug (with extremely rare exception: maybe 1 in 100 runs that you lose will be due to a game design flaw, if that). And so the journey as you go from dying in the tutorial to doing speedruns and robbing shopkeepers as you go to hell is one of the best ones in gaming.
I will say though, do not buy this game if you dislike difficulty: there is no easy mode. In fact, there is not even any progress that will be saved from game to game besides purely aesthetic character skin changes. Everything is dependent on your skill.

I took note of the negative reviews and almost didn't buy this, but I'm glad that I did. It's a nice little adventure game treading the same ground as old Lucas Arts games. I didn't find it hugely funny, but it was entertaining enough with a couple of real laugh out loud moments.
I didn't find the main character as obnoxious as many people seem to have done. I never got the impression that the writers were trying to portray Rufus in a particularly sympathetic light. He was supposed to be pathetic and anti-social, with a huge chip on his shoulder originating from his early abandonment. I don't think you are supposed to actively like him.
The puzzles are pretty decent and have some logic to them (I mean, adventure game logic, but better than many adventure games that I've played). It looks good and the only bug I encountered was that the inventory button would occasionally disappear, but that was easily remedied by exiting to the main menu and then resuming the game again.
All in all, this wasn't an adventure game that I'll think of in the coming days. It didn't move me, it won't haunt me, and it hasn't taught me anything new. So, nothing special, but still a competent little game. I'd happily play the sequels if I can pick them up cheaply.

First off, this is early access. It's unfinished. The idea is that if you believe this game has potential, you pay the developers in advance and help them as the game grows. So there are a lot of bugs. That's the point. I won't bother mentioning the bugs here.
This is, essentially, a co-op hybrid of Devil May Cry and Dynasty Warriors. You fight a lot of enemies, and the fighting is very fast paced and has a focus on combos. It's also RWBY, which is a series that screamed "MAKE ME INTO A VIDEO GAME" from the first teaser trailer.
You play as one of the 4 main cast through a series of levels, one after the other. Each level is akin to a typical DMC map. It's a linear progression from enemy encounter to enemy encounter, with some nooks and crannies for collectibles. There is variation from encounter to encounter, some are simple "kill a mob" encounters, others have objectives like protect a structure.
The skill progression system needs work. Currently, as you level up you can spend points to buy upgrades to special attacks or passive buffs. But to do this, you need to pull down a menu and look through the skill trees. This of course doesn't pause the game as it's co-op, so it means you have to stand still out of combat to do this. No one wants to stand still in this game, it's very design focuses on keeping the fight going. Health recharges quickly and your special resource recharges from fighting, so when you pop open your skill menu to pick skills, you will probably find yourself left behind by your teammates.
If you are a fan of the series, and are ok with the either of the games I compared this to, this game is up your alley. It's well worth the $15 to get it at a discount and help it grow into a proper game.
If you aren't familiar with the series, wait until a little further in the development to buy in. Or go to youtube and get familiar with it first.
The potential is there.

This is just a quick review of the first play through. I only have about 4 hour of play time in Portal Knights so I will update as I log more hours.
First off this game is amazingly pretty. When I got into the first world I was amazed at how pretty everything looked.
The tutorial is decently helpful but I wish it was a bit more in depth on a few things.
From what I've seen you don't even have to build a house to live in since there are already dwellings built. You just have to fix them up.
Everything you need to build and craft items is scattered across all of the worlds. So if you don't have coal then you'll need to travel to a world that has coal. Luckily when you go to the world map and click on the world you want to travel to it will tell you what resources are located there. So that’s kind of a plus.
The combat is a nice feature. Something I've noticed is with the right kind of weapon you will do extra damage to an enemy depending on what it is.
There is an RPG fact to this game that I adore simply because I love RPGs. There are different weapons you can craft as well as armor. your workbench, furnace, anvil, and everything you use to craft different items can be upgraded. You also have different traits and attributes that you can upgrade to increase your character.
Leveling is a process. If you are constantly killing enemies then you will level pretty quickly (I only got to level 8 in the first four hours) but if you are like me and want to explore and see what all you can find, do and craft then it will more than likely take a little bit.
For now, the only thing that bugs me on this game is the fact that I have to go to different worlds to find different resources but I'll get over that pretty quickly as I progress through it.
Updates to follow as I log more hours.

Gameplay:
Gameplay is a step above Human Revolution in most cases but a step below in a handful of other cases. Guns feel good in your hands. The Active Augmentation abilities are a bit weird to use. I found it easiest to just have my toggle augmentations on f1 to f4 and any weapon augmentations on my quick augmentation button which I bound to Mouse4. I would switch from quick augmentation from tesla to typhoon to peps whenever I needed to by using the Augmentation Wheel. In the other hand you can peek out of cover by press WASD anymore. You have to press RMB to peek out of cover now. Currently Iron Sights are not togglable and have to be held.
When doing a lethal I found the game to be to easy. Even on "Give Me Deus Ex" All you need is a 10mm with a Silencer to 1 tap heads on regular enemies and a Revolver for Stronger Enemies such as Sentry Bots.
Story/Setting:
The Story is shorter than Human Revolution. I don't believe all those people that say they spent 60 hrs to beat the game by exploring every corner of the game. An average person will spend about 20-30 hrs to beat the game. You can beat it faster by not doing all the side missions, but heavily advise against it.
The setting is amazing. Prague is sprawling with life. There is so many stores to visit and people to talk to. The world is painted with so many details. That being said the story feels a bit imcomplete at the end. The whole segregation theme isn't wrapped up by the end of the game and this leads to the question of the sequel which they are obviously planning for. I don't see myself wanting another Deus Ex game focusing on the mechanical apartheid. This game beats you over the head with it's segregation theme and it's enjoyable, but I can't do another full of game of it.
Graphics/ANimations:
Graphically it is definitely a step up from Human Revolution. It's prettier than HR and it doesn't have the infamous yellow tint that HR did. Animations in the other hand are a bit hit or miss. Some animations look a bit less impressive than their HR counterparts. Animations such as the "Punch through Wall" animation or the "Typhoon Animation" looks a bit stiff. In the other hand the Icarus Landing animation is fast and flashy.  The Takedowns are in my opinion better. Human Revolution had a problem where the takedowns were too intricate. It became a problem when players saw it again and again throughout the game. It broke immersion to see enemies do the exact same attack and Adam counterattacking the exact same way multiple times through the game. It was also immersion breaking to see civilians trying to attack Adam during a double takedown animation. The Takedown animations in Mankind Divided are better in my opinion because they are more generic. Adam stabs the guy twice and is done.
Another complaint  I had with Human Revolution is more or less fixed in Mankind Divided. There were only about 10 different faces for civilians in HR making it so players would run into the same faces multiple times through the game. This is basically fixed in MD with more variety in civilian NPC faces.
Performance / Bugs:
There has been many complaints on performance issues for this. I can't speak for everyone so I'll just give you my experience.
Specs :
i5-6600k
Gigabyte GTX 970
16 GB DDR4 RAM
250 GB SSD
ON very High to High Settings. No Tesselation and no MSAA. Average 50-65fps.

If you save while in cover. When you load the save and press Space you will come out of cover and either vault over it or start running in the direction you are looking. You can fixed this by hold Space instead of pressing space when you are loading your save.

I got this game for just over £1 in the sale and for that price is was absolutely worth it.
It presents itself as a game that is very short and very sweet. I finished it in just under 4 hours with all the achievements. Asuming there is no sale, you will have to question whether you are willing to spend £11 on a very short game. The story and graphics are beautiful and the only other thing that has stuck me emotionally in a game is the Walking Dead. Prepare to pay for quality (in abundance) and not quantity.
I loved every second of the game. The camera angle was always focused on the boys one way or another ; you knew what was happening at every second. It suprised me how such simple controls (1 stick big bro, 1 stick lil bro-1 trigger big bro, 1 trigger lil bro) could actually be used in a range of puzzles and multiple scenarios.
There isn't too much in the scheme of negatives, but heres a few:
-Missable achievements. I HATE them.
-The game displays itself as a sort of puzzler. I found the 'thinking' part of the game far too easy and I never got stuck on anything (not to toot my own horn). The average person will not have to think much. It seems the game wants to show off visuals rather than give us puzzles.
-In a few instances the boys interacting with some objects was glitched (not holding handles in the hand properly) but that is minor.
-Too short (obviously)
-You need a controller to play which is fine and works but you are limiting your market audience. Just introduce big bro as WASD and little bro as arrow keys with the mouse to turn the camera. Its suprising how many people don't have a controller.
In conclusion-if you are looking for a lot of content and lots of replay value, spend your £10 on Borderlands 2 and put in 100s of hrs. If you looking for a memorable, mesmerising gaming experience with beautiful visuals and you have a controller then buy it and put in 3-5 hours. I VERY MUCH RECOMMEND you do not rush the game. Take every second in and experience at the game. I've finished and I don't intend to play it again for a long, long time because I know the story. I don't see why I would want to restart.

WASTED presents itself like a parody of the Fallout universe. It takes Fallout's quirkiness and brings it to comedic levels. What if the apocalypse happened in the 80s? This game answers that question. Big hair and fanny packs dominate the wastes. WASTED plays like any dungeon crawler. Dive into WASTED's version of vault's called "Coolers" in search of loot and "booze" (radioactive cocktails that give permanent bonuses to your character.) WASTED's light hearted and childish sense of humor help it stand out from other dungeon crawlers. I found myself falling in love with this game in the first 15 minutes.
Positives:
+Sense of humor
+80s Style
+Fast paced combat
+Crafting System (Fallout 3 Style)
+Quests
+Memorable Characters
+Lite RPG elements
+Various playstyles
Negatives:
-Extremely loud default volume
-Repetitive dungeons
-Combat seems very easy
-Little enemy variety
So far, WASTED's charm has me hooked. I would recommend this game to my friends, because it is a refreshing change from other dungeon crawlers I have played. WASTED does nothing new, but it combines elements from other games into an interesting formula.

I took note of the negative reviews and almost didn't buy this, but I'm glad that I did. It's a nice little adventure game treading the same ground as old Lucas Arts games. I didn't find it hugely funny, but it was entertaining enough with a couple of real laugh out loud moments.
I didn't find the main character as obnoxious as many people seem to have done. I never got the impression that the writers were trying to portray Rufus in a particularly sympathetic light. He was supposed to be pathetic and anti-social, with a huge chip on his shoulder originating from his early abandonment. I don't think you are supposed to actively like him.
The puzzles are pretty decent and have some logic to them (I mean, adventure game logic, but better than many adventure games that I've played). It looks good and the only bug I encountered was that the inventory button would occasionally disappear, but that was easily remedied by exiting to the main menu and then resuming the game again.
All in all, this wasn't an adventure game that I'll think of in the coming days. It didn't move me, it won't haunt me, and it hasn't taught me anything new. So, nothing special, but still a competent little game. I'd happily play the sequels if I can pick them up cheaply.

Full voice-acting, funny humour, an attractive art style, and puzzles that really make you have to think. Deponia is almost like a guilty pleasure for me. The protagonist is the definition of an anti-hero who's seriously hard to like, but that doesn't prevent the world of Deponia from being lovable and hilarious. The puzzles are a bit hit-or-miss and you'll probably be looking up a guide at some point, but don't let that deter you; The satisfaction and surprising sense of making a cup of espresso using post-apocalypse garbage and a chili pepper makes the endless stewing worth it.
The voice acting and music are truly immersive and the world is genius! I've never been so inspired by a singular dystopia as I have ths one. The art style is charming and allows for very fluid and frequent animations. Everything about the game is indescribably satisfying and detailed. All the puzzles are tough but will have you smacking your forehead in realization when you've finally nailed them. The minigames are very difficult as well but all of them are skippable right off the bat (I believe) with no punishment.
Some jokes could be considered in poor taste but they're not upsetting, perhaps just a bit uncomfortable if you really think about them. Even so, they're rare, and the most pressing trope of "horrible jerk getting the girl in the end just cause he's the protagonist" doesn't feel nearly as insulting when you've put so much work into getting him there - ESPECIALLY if you've played the full series.

Депония - несмотря на положительные отзывы оказалась весьма посредственным поинт-клик квестом. Паззлы нелогичные, довольно глупо и топорно исполненные, типа как есть две палки в инвентаре на вид одинаковые, но сахарную вату можно только на определённую из них намотать. Или когда надо привлечь внимание кита приманкой, но он её не видит - игра не даст просто осветить её имеющимся в инвентаре фонариком, а будет ждать когда вы догадаетесь использовать фосфоресцентную массу (которая возбуждается от света того же фонарика, и как следствие по оперделению светится хуже). Многие нелогичные дествия можно с натяжкой объяснить тем, что это логика протагониста, который откровенный идиот. Но далеко не все. Лично мне пришлось раза три с досадой заглядывать в прохождение, чтобы намертво не застрять. Многие так и не понял в чём был смысл, почему медитирующий Руфус должен называть себя именно "Папап" например, а никак не иначе.

Okay so now that the full game is out I can give my thoughts on it. I may do a video review at some point but I'll sum up my thoughts here for now XD
Graphics/Sound -
The game looks pretty good, as good as can be expected for a first game especially. The world of remnant really comes alive here and is a joy to behold. The only level I thought looked dull was Mountain Glenn but how do you make a crumbling city look "good", it still made me feel like I was exploring Mountain Glenn so job well done there. The voice work and sound effects are really well done and will immediately pull you in especially if you are a fan of the show. The music is mostly music from the show which is amazing so I am perfectly okay with that.
Story/Characters -
The game pretty much requires you be a fan of the show to even remotely get into the characters. The characterization is bare bones and you would only be able to enjoy the interactions between our four girls if you already know them from the show. As for the characters that contact the girls over their scrolls throughout the game, you pretty much get what their saying since they don't really reference plot elements from the show and stay grounded in what is happening here and now BUT much like with our four girls if you don't know the show their isn't much reason given to care about them either. Just being honest here but all that being said this game was more or less made for the fans so that is forgivable for the most part.
As a fan of the show though I didn't really care for the story. The story much like the characterization is pretty bare bones but unlike the characters it isn't salvaged by knowing about the show because this story has pretty much nothing to do with the show (taking place between volumes 2 & 3 I believe). Its not a terrible story but it isn't very engrossing and feels extremely short and rushed (which ties into one of my gameplay complaints.)
All in all the characterization isn't very good but if you love the show you will enjoy hearing the dialouge and interactions between the characters however the story isn't great show or no show.
Gameplay -
Okay lets get the bad stuff out of the way first with this one because I only really have a few complaints. First the hack'n slash gameplay gets a tiny bit repetitive after awhile. Second some enemies especially towards the end felt a bit cheap. Third and this is the biggest problem for me personally the game is VERY short. Remember how I said the story felt rushed, well that is likely partially because the game itself isn't long at all I think I managed to beat it in like 3-4 hours.
Now with that out of the way what was good about it? Well despite getting a little repetitive after awhile running around as one of team RWBY and hacking Grimm to bits is actually really fun. I genuinely felt like a badass tearing through Grimm especially since taking them out efficiently definetly requires a bit of skill. I like leveling up each of the girls because they all play well and have some cool attacks to pull off. They don't feel like carbon copies of eachother they genuinely feel different to play as. I like looking around for the hidden relics. It especially gets fun if you join up with some friends.
I can't comment on performance because any slow down I experienced could just be because my PC is underpowered.
Verdict -
This is definetly a flawed game. The story is meh, the characterization pretty much relies on you knowing the show, the game is very short and it has a minor issue with becoming repetitive after awhile BUT the game looks nice, sounds great, if you do the know the show you'll love the character interactions, and the despite some little issues here and there the game is genuinely fun to play. For a first effort from Roosterteeth Games it's not bad at all and I do recommend it to everyone, if you are a fan of the show then this is a must play! 8/10

After sinking about 40 hours over 3 I'm still in a bit of a stupor over this game; this feels like a little jewel found on a beach, a pleasant surprise at first, then you realize is not a jewel, just a really shiny bead;
On the pros - Solid building system, allows the creativity to really run amok and the scenarios can be very intriguing, if you, like me always wanted a fort floating on a island amidst clouds, the combat feels very impactful and mix-mashes the dodgy-rolly Dark Souls-esque that still feels rewarding and the diversity of possible builds puts an extra touch on customization; that is until you inevitably float towards the most-effective-possible and make the build that everyone else does. The UI is tightly woven and the music has heart, altough can get quite repetitive; and the game just looks ♥♥♥♥ing adorable.
On the cons - It gets very grindy and repetitive. A bit too fast even. With 3 bosses and 40 worlds, that sound like much in theory, until you realize that they're pretty 6~7 biomes, and 8~9 worlds on the same biome gives you the "haven't I've been here before 7 time?" feeling. Not much in the way of quests, always some variation of "get/kill X for cockhead Z to get money/xp" but, then again, all quests EVER boil down to some form of this, so not really an issue. End-game feels a bit rushed, as if it's not really end-game *wink-wink* and the grind can get REALLY frustrating on the non-rewarding side, with the need of 20 ores to make a single a bar of Y-type metal and the boss giving measly 5 ores and a bar every full moon if you're lucky will get tiring really fast and you'll get too tired to keep grinding and will leave that "I wanted to deck myself out but I just can't bring myself to have the patience to keep on" aftertaste that turned sour and unpleasant instantly. Oh, and have I mentioned it gets really grindy?
OVERALL
I like it, hope the devs keep at it and improve; for an early acess it feels very wholesome; I'd givit and 6.5/10

Also there a few major bugs (at the time of writing) that almost break the game. In more than a couple combat encounters the AI would not progress its turn for minutes at a time; at other times the rumble on the controller seemed to turn on and not turn off for equally long amounts.
Exploration wise, traveling around the town is tedious, with one of the worst fast travel implementations I’ve encountered. You may only fast travel from a fast travel location to another fast travel location. While this speeds up travel mediocre amount, a better system would have been to allow fast travel from any location.
The town itself is a clone of Stick of Truth for the most part, those familiar with the first game will be, for the most part, unexcited by exploring locations. Beyond the story there’s not much excitement except for the rabid completionist searching for all the collectables and selfies.
I’d recommend this game to fans if it’s on sale and they have patched some of the major bugs.

To clarify, I've played a tiny bit of Tekken 4 on PS2 and Tekken 6 on PS Vita, but that's the extent of my previous experience. I barely played either of these and I just button mashed, so I'll call myself a Tekken noob and say that this game is my first 'real experience' in playing a Tekken game. I pre-ordered this game without knowing how well it will be optimized on PC, if the online servers will work, if it supports controllers, etc. To my amazement, Tekken 7 on day 1 tackled all of these.
Constant 60 fps is vital in this game as framerate drops will affect button inputs. This game is extremely smooth to run on ultra settings whilst maintaining constant 60 fps (at 1920x1080 on a GTX 1060) though borderless windowed settings forces me to run at 3840x2160 for some reason, but this does not seem to affect system performance at all. Only drops you will see are the loading cutscenes where it will run at 30 fps, but who cares about that?
Amazing. Simply amazing. Day 1 release gives you a whopping 37 characters to choose from (38 if you got Eliza as a pre-order bonus) with 10 of them being new characters. The characters all speak in their native language, so I found myself very confused when they all seemed to understand what each other was saying during the story (a great example of this is the dialogue between Nina, Heihachi and Claudio). However, this is by no means a downside as we don't have to hear horrible dubbed voices of foreign characters, but instead it feels more natural and fitting.
Not only are there a wide selection of characters, but there are also 20 stages to choose from. The stages have different layouts so it doesn't feel repetitive. You'll have stages with and without walls, some which are octagonal shaped, others which are square shaped and even stages with multiple platforms that can be broken through by using certain moves. Each stage has it's own music piece composed to it and gives it a sense of uniqueness. Oh, and they all look great too.
I found the story to be very interesting and gripping at times, but I also found it to be quite short. For the most part it's spending 5 minutes watching a cutscene, fighting someone and then rinse and repeat. Though I guess for a fighting game not much else can be done. I completed the story in a couple of hours in a single sitting along with the extra character episodes unlocked after completing the main story. I found myself hysterically laughing at certain character episodes (Paul vs. Panda and Lucky Chloe vs. Eddy are the two that come to mind) and it was just really fun overall. But as I previously mentioned it is VERY short.
I gotta say, the gameplay is near-flawless. For a fighting game noob, I was able to quickly pick up characters I have never even played before and within an hour or so I would come to grips with their playstyle and how to use them. Blocking is done simply by holding back for mid and air attacks and down-back for low attacks, there is no button input required and it is as simple as that. Most characters have very easy 3 or 4 hit combos which is helpful when starting out with a new character. One thing I am not too impressed with however is the inclusion of 'rage arts'. I understand that it is included to help give players an edge when they have low hp, but it honestly just feels cheap. Not to mention that Akuma's rage art can not be blocked, but only evaded by sidestepping or jumping at the right time.
Because who would ever dare to play a fighting game with keyboard and mouse? I play this game using my PS4 controller and seems to work flawlessly. The button layout however still shows the Xbox controller button layout, but this isn't an issue at all. I really appreciate the inclusion of custom controller input bindings so I can easily bind multiple buttons to a single button (LP+RP to L1 for example).
The soundtrack is quite possibly the best soundtrack of any game I have ever played. There isn't a single track that I have disliked and I have found myself sitting in the character select screen and certain maps in practice whilst I do other tasks just so I can listen to the soundtrack in the background. Honestly even if you don't like fighting games, at least listen to the soundtrack and you will not be disappointed.
It's honestly hard to fault this game, it is quite possibly the best fighting game of all time. I love every aspect of this game from the characters to the soundtrack. The game runs very smoothly so I have no issues with input lag and I just find myself falling in love with this game more and more each day. The only issue I have found is that you will sometimes lose connection to a host before you have even joined them, but otherwise online also works flawlessly with no noticable lag.

I've been playing the Tekken series since the very first one was released.  I can say that Tekken 7 is one of the best in the series.  Great graphics, Great tekken humor, and great online play. The king of fighting games has now made it's way to the PC MASTER RACE!
10/10

Online matches are great. Matchmaking is fast and I didn't experience any lag at all. In general it feels like a good PC port.
Practice mode is one of the most important features in fighting games.
In Tekken7, this mode is well thought out. It offers a lot of different settings and makes it fun to learn new moves and combos.
There is also plenty of singleplayer content for a fighting game. You can choose from different modes like Story Mode, Arcade Mode and Treasure Mode (for unlocking new items that can be used to customize the looks of your characters).
All items that can be used for customizing the outfits of your characters must be earned through playing the game. There are no microtransactions. Also, these items don't provide any  gameplay advantage.
Controller support is also fine. All of my controllers worked without any problems.
The last Tekken game I've played was Tekken3 and this game made it easy for me to come back to the series. If you've ever played a Tekken game it should be easy for you to get into this game again.
But also for people who are new to fighting games or the Tekken series, Tekken7 is a great choice. It's one of these games that are easy to play, but hard to master.
As long as you like fighting games, I would totally recommend this game to you. Whether you prefer playing competitively in online ranked games, casually with some friends or even some singleplayer matches, this game offers it all.

This is my intro into any fighter game except for super smash bros, which is so differnt than this that I don't even count it. With it being my first experience, it has been very pleasant. Game runs perfectly smooth on my I5 4690k @ 4.6 Ghz and my GTX 1070. Many people complain about there being no tutorials in game, but that's fine with me with this game. Besides, there are plenty of good videos online. I did watch a few tutorials, but I mostly just found it easy to learn myself. The reason why I like this game more than street fighter is because the moves are easier to perform for the most part, not giving you a huge disadvantage if you can't enter the inputs in correctly. I usually take a character into practice and just start pressing buttons and looking at their moves list. Doing this I find it's actually pretty easy to get an ok combo going. I find a good one for most characters is usually up 4, forward 1, forward 1, and then maybe a down 4 or a down 2. Pretty decently simple stuff if you actually put the effort into the game. Now of course, this is just a beginner's perspective, so I didn't cover anything advanced, so if I were a more advanced player then the review may change.
This game is a fresh breath of air for fighting game enthusiasts. The best Tekken in the series, and I dare say the best fighting game EVER.

Not sure what it is about the kinesthetics of this series that made me adore number 5 and despise number 6. If anything, the last numbered sequel showed just how wrong this series can get simple controllability and overall feel so I was sceptical.
So of course the mechanical core of this thing ended up being the best since Tekken 3 and I made myself look a♥♥♥♥♥for doubting it.
That said, the game modes are anemic, in terms of single player there are two (not counting story mode), the arcade mode is half the length it used to be with no cinematic endings and the trasure mode is a poor replacement of ghost battles. It is the only real single player option in the game but the stages only change every 5 or so matches and you can't even switch up the rules (you know, I really would enjoy 3-round figts with no time limit. Also, can we talk about adding the option to turn off custom outfits for NPC opponents?).
So the game gives you one of the best fighting game combat systems on the market and then doesn't really let you have any fun with it. It's kind of frustrating.
The systems, aesthetic and kinesthetics carry it well enough for me to recommend it but god damn it the game needs some updates.
Also the thing runs on my 3-year old i5+GTX770 rig on ultra and rock solid 60FPS. I'm not entirely sure how they pulled that one off.

I honestly liked this game. I did not mind the lowpoly look, liked the humor, the setting and the idea of a random generated fps crawler. But i cant recommend it in its current state for a simple reason.
You never die in a fight. Honestly, not even once. The AI is absolutely ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ and easily outmanouvered because its whole strategy involves walking towards and shooting while strafing to either side every now and then.
There are only 2 situations in this game where you die:
1. You find yourself completely overwhelmed with dumb enemies that you simply dont have enough ammo to kill, especially later in the first dungeon/cooler when the big guys show up. And when you run out of ammo you cant really fight anymore.
2. You get ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥tted to death. This involves opening a door and looking right at a trap that shoots you. Opening doors from an angle is A. difficult when most of the maps consist of tight corridors and B. the trap on the other side can also sit at an angle to the door. So again, you cant fight that.
There is also the mechanic of the S.O.B Purifier. When you take too long crawling through a dungeon, a knight with a minigun spawns at the start and slowly moves towards you. Now, this guy is killable if you have the right stuff and a bit of time to prepare and you can grab his armor, but he forces you to rush things and run into dangerous situations where you will take damage until you know how to handle him. And when you look at the threads in the forum you can see that even people who played this game longer than me hate this guy.
The next problem that arises is that the game becomes extremely repetitive. The first dungeon involves the same equipment, enemies and design every time and because of point 1. and 2. you need to get lucky to finish it and see the rest of the game. But you wont get lucky. You will ram your head agains a wall until you stop and come back some other time. Again, check the threads and see what im talking about. At some point, you will even try not playing smart and act like one the enemies and get the some non-result as to when you acutally tried. You will feel betrayed at said point.
I like a challenge and i will also continue playing this game because i spent money on it, but it lost its fun months ago and just feels like a cheap exercise in futility unless you become one of the lucky ones to see more than the first dungeon.

I can say, despite this game being as...unpolished as it is, there's just something about it I love.

An enjoyably brainless button-masher, and I mean that literally as there is only one combo: press attack five times, whilst occasionally dodging attacks. But there is surprising depth there, as you can change individual attacks in that five-button sequence, and switch between three sets of sequences on the fly, unlocking new attacks as you progress through the game. This opens up the game to a ridiculous amount of experimentation: maybe the third attack knocks enemies out of the reach of your fourth, or maybe a sequence that works really well against regular enemies keeps being interrupted by enemies with projectiles, and before you know it you're legitimately thinking about whether an uppercut would be a better finish than a bazooka. Along with moves there are also other characters, weapons, challenges (which are REALLY challenging), accessories and colours to unlock, so there's plenty to do and it doesn't actually feel that repetitive to do it, as you're always compelled to experiment with attack sequences as you fight through mercifully short levels.
I'll also give Soda Girls praise for this: it lets you upgrade individual enemies as well, which is a really creative take on difficulty levels, and one I now find myself wishing more beat-em-ups did. Levelling up the cannon fodder enemies doesn't make the bigger bosses any harder, so you can find a nice difficulty balance that works for you instead of a binary easy-normal-hard.
There's an element of grind - as there always is when there's so much to unlock - but Soda Girls is really enjoyable to play; it's one of the better brawlers to just idly beat up bad guys in, and the attacks are suitably over the top that changing up your combo sequence is surprisingly fun. The translation is really bad though, personally that doesn't bother me but if it bothers you, well, bear that in mind. Other than that, don't be put off by the Early Access stigma, Soda Girls is really polished and there's a solid game here, and beat-em-up fans will find much to keep them punching in it.

Remember as kids we would usually choose a mainstream cartoon to watch religously yet there would always be a "close 2nd" as near and dear to our hearts that simply wasn't quite as "well known"? In other words, there is G.I. Joe then there's M.A.S.K.. There's Transformers then there's Go-bots.  There's Thunder-cats then there's Silver-hawks. There's TMNT but then there's Street-sharks. There's Batman The Animated series then there's Disney's Gargoyles. Er,you get my point!
Soda-Girls embodies the above conundrum. With iconic characters that look like they're the "cousins" of all-time-great gaming Divas like Tron Boone(with assisting mech),Samus Aran,Nightshade, and Jill Valentine it's obvious the developers are pretty honest about wearing their inspirations on their sleeves. Furthermore, the graphic style bears more than a slight semblance to Skull-girls.Viewtiful Joe, and some of our nostagic favorite kids shows from Cartoon-Network. None of this feels sloppy though as the little details and in-jokes show how much the developers cared when making this game. There's a difference between "entirely ripping off" an idea as opposed to being inspired by an idea and putting one's own twist/embelishment on it. Soda Girls fortunately does more of the later than the former.
On the surface some might mistake Soda Girls to be a "mindless brawler" with some platforming segments in which you must navigate police-woman Jacey (Your first character in story-mode before you help to liberate Jacey's friends) thru small contained 2D danger zones of falling debris, electric panels,sinking foot-steps,and various exploding propane cannisters. Luckily these same hazards can be used againt the enemies too forcing you to strategize. Unlike other brawlers, enemies in Soda Girls come at you in smaller numbers though they tend to be a lot more formible. Aka a couple of zombie hippy girls or zombie weiner dogs can still ♥♥♥♥ your♥♥♥♥♥♥up if you go into a fight with bad timing. (Sorry I failed to mention there's a zombie apocolypse going on but now you know!)
Bosses start off easy peasy but by the time I got to "The Cess-poll" there was a Junk-rat looking psychopath giving me issues as he eventually eats the huge mutton chop he's beating you with (restoring his health) THEN he brandishes a friggin shotgun that can fire in three directions. This means yeah,you'll probably have to grind to level up whilst farming for better weapons, farming more bottle caps to purchase additional perk-items (Or level them up as well), and pick up more attacks to mix and match in your various combo strings. I can see how some might get frustrated by this but for me it's just a chance to improve and loot which appeals a bit to my OCD-laden tendencies!
Oddly enough, one character can even improve the performance of enemies. I'd advise against this until you're very skilled and prepared but if you want greater risks and greater rewards the oppertunity is definitely there.
Furthermore, reviewers that complain there's only one attack button miss the point. Aka the whole appeal of soda-girls is unlocking "new attacks" that you can place in any sequential order on one of three equipped plan sheets. Yes, you are pressing one button rapidly to do combos but those attacks are ones you can put into any order you want. This once again plays into the strategy of the game as you'll need to experiment with the sequential order of different moves to get the best and flashiest results. I feel as if people out there read a few bad reviews about Soda Girls being a "mindless button masher" and never bothered to clarify whether that was true or not. It's really not and the challenge always feels "just right" though if you're in a jam all the characters can be "leveled up" and also be equipped with additional charms and ornaments that can increase strength,speed,immunity to certain kind of attacks,and even the rate at which you attain bottle caps (currency) or experience points.
The only qualm I can level against Soda Girls is it's still an early acess game though in its' defense it seems to be an early acess game that's "almost" done. Aka, there's already a lot there but the developers have talked about adding more characters and more stages. I'm hoping they do just that though I understand how it can be discouraging to put together such a good game only to have it be a "flash in the pan" as far as its' public impact is concerned. Aka, I feel with the right marketing and the right e-celebs doing let's plays Soda-Girls would have really "taken off" as it taps into that same nostalgia as Skull girls,Viewtiful Joe, and Senran Kagura.
Pros
+Good cast of unique characters
+ Nice colorful and outlandish "punk noir" enemy designs
+ You get to custom create your own combos
+ Levels tend to be well designed with a decent balance of enemies and environmental hazards. (Which if you're smart enough can be used to your own advantage. Kicking a propane tank into a pile of slumbering zombies is always fun!)
+ Appealing art style
+ Is deeper and more layered in complexity than it initially seems
+ Injected "something new" into the beat-em-up genre which is not something I see done too often
Cons
-It can be easy to get caught up in "cheap juggles" from multiple foes.
- Some bugs remain. In one area I could literally "walk on air" and I'm sure that was not intended.
- Still "early acess". We can only hope the developers are stalwart enough to see this one through and finish their work.
- Soda Girls had a "flash in the pan effect" which may have discouraged its' creators even more. Still, a somewhat recent update suggests not all hope is lost!

The patch did nothing for me in terms of performance.  Still playing it just fine but wherever stutters and such happened before the patch, still happen after the patch.  While it improved for some people, many were also actually negatively effected by it.  It didn't fix online at all, the krypt levers are still broken for those who messed that puzzle up, the memory leak still causes your CPU usage to go higher and higher until the game eventually crashes or freezes.  This patch, according to Ed Boon was supposed to bring the PC version to "parity with consoles".  Since that didn't happen I guess we wait for the next patch.
The game itself is great, it really is.  But the performance, memory leak and online issues make this a hard recommendation.  Once they address and actually fix those issues, then I'd definitely recommend picking this up on PC.  The game is worth every penny, but in it's current state, I really can't encourage anyone to pay full price for it.
Update: So it's not as fixed as I'd like it to be after this patch.  It does run better and they did improve it, but after further playing it since the last update, there are still glaring optimization issues.  The game is a resource hog.  While the memory leak is gone for the most part, it still uses a crazy amount of memory to run.  I guess I'll have to update this again once a new patch or patches release.  As of now I still recommend the game and will leave my review at a thumbs up but it's a hesitant recommendation in it's current state.  I'll further recommend the game if the patches optimize the game properly.

There were a lot of people claiming it was people's "potato" PCs and such which is why we couldn't run the game smoothly.  This last patch just proved that incorrect.  As for online, that's still not quite up to par, so if you're in it for mainly the single player modes, then I highly recommend this game.

After countless ours of fun and having personally recomended this game to all my friends, I think the least I could do is leave a positive review for it online as well :)
Before I start, I would like to point out that although the game is marked Windows-only, I also runs fine on Linux under Wine. Just make sure to disable the ingame Steam overlay.
Spelunky is one of those rare games that just feel "perfect" and I can't really think of anything what I would change in it if I could. Everything from the controls to the cost of the items in the shop feels perfectly balanced and its clear that the developers really thought about everything. Spelunky is a gem of game design that should not be missed!
Compared to other "roguelike" games I have played, Spelunky deserves a special place in how well it makes use of the randomization and "permadeath" mechanics. The randomization combined with the emergent platforming gameplay ensure that every new play session feels fresh and challenging. At the same time, the game still manages to feel very fair. When you win or lose it feels as if it was due do your skill (or lack thereof) and not because you just happened to get a random seed that was too easy or too challenging.
All that said, you do need to know that Spelunky is a very challenging game; I've only been able to reach the "true ending" a handful of times and have yet to unlock some of the achievements (beating the game without picking up any gold is reeeealy hard). However, as explorer Yang would say, "the journey is its own reward and mastery is the greatest treasure of the all!".

I sat here for a good while in a poor attempt to conjure up some eloquent, semi-professional review of my favorite game. I'll just say this: when I hear "platformer", the first title to come to mind is Spelunky.
I had followed the later parts of development for the original Game Maker version for some time before its release. I'll never forget my first adventure ending with Spelunky Guy swiftly attaching himself to some spikes in the first level of the mines. Thousands of attempted runs (literally), several killed Olmecs, and hundreds of hours later, here I am still enjoying this masterpiece in 2016. Props to Derek Yu and all the developers of Spelunky in all its forms--you've given me a truly unforgettable experience.
PS: the only reason I don't have more hours on Steam is because I play the game more on PS3

So Deponia....
Let's take two people. One is a guy who's trying to be a master pirate, and the other is a guy who wants to leave a dying world to go to a better world.  Which of these guys would be more likable?
Well the first is Guybrush Threepwood of Monkey's Island,. and the second is Rufus of Deponia, and surprisingly Rufus is the unlikable character, but I'm getting ahead of myself.
Rufus stars in Deponia, a technically proficient and beautiful game.  Deponia is about a world called Deponia, and Rufus, a man who wants to go to a magical place called Elysium, and no it's not the afterlife, and no it's not based off that film Elysium in 2013, though kind of the same plot.
The difference between Elysium the movie and Deponia, is Rufus is unlikable and Matt Damon is one of the most charismatic actors out there.   Oh we're back to that again.  Well let's deal with it.
You see, the problem with Deponia is that the comedy kind of centers around Rufus being well... I think any word I used about him would be censored.  At the beginning of the game, you see him make some poor judgements and you think he's a dope.  He's a bit of an jerk to the person he's living with but she's a bit of a jerk back so maybe it's just a situation of a roommate you don't like.
But from there on... well Rufus just doesn't seem to get along with anyone.  It's not that he's a troublemaker, or at least it's not only that, he just seems to constantly be snarky with everyone to the point where he's a ... another name for a donkey.
You see in games like this such as Monkey's Island, the main character works in a morally grey area, usually picking up everything they can and using it together to accomplish a goal.  Quite often the game shows that the player's actions can be seen as deviant or criminal, but they're necessary to proceed, they work towards a goal.
On the other hand Rufus delights in all the misery he causes.  He laughs at times when he's doing awful actions, he directly hurts people, and snickers about it.  This isn't a "I have to do this" but rather a "I enjoy doing this" moment, and it's not exactly actions the player enjoys either so... Rufus comes off as unlikable.  Others have pointed out misogynistic tones in the character or game, and they exist, but the way Rufus treats everyone is just poor.
Now that the main character is out of the way, what about the game itself.
Well it's a point and click adventure, and I have to admit there's some clever moments in the game, but quite often you have a huge inventory of items, and no hint on what's the next thing to do.  There's points where you have a drill, a knife, a syringe and more, and often times you need to use a specific item to complete a task, but which item?  The game rarely gives you a hint.  Sadly there's a lot of trial and error required with this game and oftentimes that means use every item with every item and one will hopefully click.
On the other hand if you miss something, well you're going to be out of luck.  There's very little hinting on the item.  For the first hour of the game, the game keeps the locations you need to visit to a minimum, but then once you meet the girl in the game (called Goal... yeah maybe there's something to the idea the game is misogynist) the game opens up and now there's tens of locations.
The good news is there's a button that shows you all the interactable items on a screen, but again.  Use all your items on all the other items and hope you hit on the right combo quickly.    Or use a guide.
And eventually you're probably going to have to use a guide or try entirely too many wrong combinations.
The other issue I have with the game is the walk speed in the game is slow.   You can warp between rooms but just watching the main character walk between point a and point b is kind of a drag.  In other games the player might not move when an incorrect selection was made and just drop a clever quip or just "I can't do that" In this game, the character walks between the two points to even just look at an object, and this is a slow process.
I mentioned before the game is beautiful and technically impressive, and it is, but the walk cycle could have been quicker.  A beautiful game will get duller the more times you have to look at the same location or object, and Deponia doesn't do enough to keep that beauty from being dulled by the main character, the slow walk speed, or just the obtuse puzzles.
So I wouldn't recommend Deponia, I won't be picking up the sequels, but I can recommend some good point and click games to also consider.  Grim Fandango, Day of the Tentacle, Secret of Monkey's Island and machinarium are all rather good point and click games.  Deponia isn't a horrible game, but it's just that I have trouble recommending it because I just don't like it... but that's the thing, with Rufus as a main character, I'm not sure I'm supposed to like it.

I'm going to start with the biggest issue i had with this game right off the bat. The characters, namely the protagonist. I actually took a liking to Rufus at the beginning of the story, they had given him some poor, yet relatable qualities like being messy and carless, yet ambitious. That ended very quickly. It didnt take long for me to realise how utterly infuriating his whole charater was, in fact i didnt even leave the house before realising.
But not only is he completely irredeemable, he continues to have everything go right for him in a way that feels almost like some sort of fever dream. Everyone in the town dislikes him, if not hates him, and yet they just let it slide. I understand the angle that they were going for was a loveable prankster who dreams of a better life, but it really just comes across as an entitled deadbeat who has no empathy for anyone around him and is only interested in his own wellbeing. Maybe a bit harsh, but i was happy to let that slide for a while. besides, the best part of an story driven game is the growth of the characters in better or stronger people. NOPE. Rufus remains insufferable through many great potential points of growth, in fact he almost seems to acknowledge that he should have developed from some situations but then just brushes it off with some flatline quip. But enough about Rufus, i think i've painted a vivid picture of him. The rest of the cast in this game are actually pretty good, I enjoyed the fact that most people felt the same about Rufus as i did and they did feel reasonably immersive for the world that they lived in. It was a pity that most of them were only there for Rufus to pester occasionally with his rudeness.
Now, appart from the above mentioned, i really liked the world design and the voice acting, but it was not enough to make me stay for long. The puzzles and the minigames always felt extremely convoluted and i spent most of my time walking back and fourth trying everything on everything just to look up on a walkthrough that there was 6 more steps that wasn't even really necessary.
This review quickly turned into a rant, but it pains me to see such a great game be ruined by the simple pitfalls.
TL;DR
The protagonist will probably make you want to jump off a cliff. but if not, you might enjoy this game

Summer Sale is a game developed around the idea of Steam's famed Summer Sale. The sole objective of the game being that you buy everything you can from the Steam Store at the cheapest prices. From the first look at the game, it appears filled with unfunny jokes, memes and other pointless things that were funny 2-3 years ago.
Upon loading the game, you're met with a 3 options. Play, Settings and Exit. Having looked into the settings menu, you're able to change a lot of settings to suit your personal needs right down to the colours it displays on the screen. This is a great addition but I feel there should be a colour blind mode for those with poor sight.
Once you're finally into the game, you're given $30 to buy as much content as you can from the Steam Store before you need to play the Mini Games to amass an amount of coins to buy the rest. This is where the game falls flat for me personally. The mini game choices you have to choose between are; Dragon Erol, a game which doesn't actually work nor does it allow you to collect coins with much ease; Glorious Cannon which premises you of essentially defending some black squares with meme names. It's also the easiest to get coins on if you do not own an auto clicker; Finally we have Coin Train which will delight the players who enjoy using an auto clicker. There really isn't much choice between the games and after a while, you'll get bored rather quickly. It doesn't help matters when you need $150 roughly to complete the game.
The positive side of the game is that isn't expensive. It's currently just 79p on the Steam Store and comes with 6 rather quick and easy achievements which offers you around 90 minutes of gameplay. If you're just after the quick completion, this game will fill your needs but ultimately it's another Indie game that shouldn't of passed Steam Quality Control.

I've gotta say, I thought I was going to enjoy Portal Knights a lot more than I have been for the first several hours.  I'm usually a big fan of the open-world, survival, and voxel-based genres.  Especially when they incorporate free-style building like in Minecraft (not so much the modular building, like in Rust or Ark).  But playing this game feels similar to when you cook-up a dish that contains all your favorite ingredients and spices, but when you actually sit down to try it, it just tastes awful.
One of my favorite parts of these types of games is the element of exploration, but here I consistently feel like my roaming and poking around isn't really rewarded.  If you do end up finding some items for your troubles, they're usually just more of the same resources that are already all over the island.  And when you do find some interesting or rare resources, it's almost maddening due to your limited inventory space.  Especially due to the fact that more often then not you'll have to wait until you travel to a few more realms before you find the rest of the components you need to eventually craft the item that the rarer resource is required to make.  This means you'll just end up squirreling away all these odds and ends in a very limited inventory or within an ever increasing pile of chests that become more and more of a chore to move if decide to change your home realm.
The realms are interesting, but small, even on their largest setting which limits the exploration as you can see most everything once you climb a dozen or so blocks high.  I'm enjoying the unique islands, but if you get the notion to build yourself a base in a new realm, you'll have to grapple with the fact that you'll be shuttling all your chests-worth of things back with you (while sitting through two load screens on every trip).  I almost feel punished for wanting to build a new base each couple realms because you need most of your resource stockpile that came from looting older islands because those resources are limited to only a few realms.  If you don't bring them along, you'll be forced to return to older realms just to gather up some more to begin yet another stockpile for crafting in your new base.
I like the inclusion of RPG elements and a class system, but the talent tree seems pretty uninteresting overall (at least for the warrior class I've been playing anyhow).  You can also change your talents at any time for no penalty, which just feels a little "easy-mode" for any RPG.  This leads me to the combat system, which to be fair is better than many voxel-based games (it's similar to the ill-fated Cube World), but at least in the case of the warrior, it gets extremely dull and repetitive very quickly.   Slash, slash, roll, repeat.  And the death "penalty" is a very small loss of just a handful of gold (whose use seems pretty limited anyway), so really the worst part about dying is an additional load screen and starting back at the portal.  Weak.
I like the inclusion of temporary quests that draw you back to previous islands to slay monsters to gain unique resources for crafting an item you wouldn't normally be able to attain.  But again this ends up feeling pretty "meh" when you realize the item's use is menial such as giving you a boost to mining speed for a couple minutes (and also adds to the stockpile of semi-useful items you'll be quickly accruing).
And possibly the most personally disappointing thing for me are the NPCs.  Every NPC I've seen so far just stands there and either stares off into the middle-space or does a simple looping animation over and over (sometimes at a ludicrous speed).  This would be OK if they actually served some sort of function, but the vast majority just spout a couple lines of unhelpful/vague dialogue and nothing else (and the gibberish sounds they assault you with are truly horrible).  I've only found two NPCs so far that have actually been helpful, a merchant for specific types of items (which weren't meant for my warrior... *sigh*) and an NPC that told me where I could look for some extra items.  Not "useful" items, just "extra".  Also, many of the buildings and other points of interest on a single island have identical copies located not too far away, with their only distinguishing feature being a different looking, but equally useless NPC housed within.
I'm hoping the game will be adjusted to mitigate some of these things in the future so that I can actually enjoy playing it on a level like I do other games that hit these genres, but for now (and for the price), I would say stay away.  There are less frustrating/more rewarding ways to explore a voxel-based world.
