This review is based off of around an hour and a half of gameplay; which, for this sort of hack n' slash combined with the content currently existent in the game, is enough time to properly evaluate my opinion. Do take note, however, that I am a HUGE fan of RWBY, which may have influenced my review a little, but I will try to avoid bias as much as possible.
I'll split this review into multiple sections to help narrow it down, while also allowing me to be more specific about what I'm talking about, so, lets get started.
In terms of fun factor, this game has it. It's effectively a hack n' slash in the vein of Dynasty Warriors, so if you are into that sort of combat, you'll likely enjoy what Grimm Eclipse has to offer. However, combat is all it has; there are no bonus modes (as of yet), side objectives or unique approaches to situations; it's all run in and kill X amount of Grimm before they kill you. In terms of the enemy variety, I have only seen 7; You have your standard "Creep" & "Creep Alpha", the "Beowolf" & "Alpha Beowolf", and finally your "Ursa" & "Ursa Major". There may be more enemies later down the line, but I have yet to see them. I hope there's a Nevermore.
The levels, unfortunately, are very "Defend the X" focused. Need to open a door? Defend it for 4 waves to proceed. Need to stop Grimm destroying a Command Center? Spend 4 waves doing so. as more things are added, I hope that RoosterTeeth Games adds more modes to play around in, as well as more varied objectives to pruce things up rather than having to do the same thing almost every level, it gets repetitive.
I know I mentioned earlier about the combat being fun; and it is. However, Each character (Ruby, Weiss, Blake & Yang) Don't have enough to differentiate them, apart from appearance of course. They each have unique animations and abilities, but thats where it stops; the attack speeds are mostly the same, the damage values are mostly the same, and the general tactic for everyone is literally "Mash buttons until dead". I'd like to see more done with each character's speciality; Make Yang a heavy hitting tank who not only does more damage than the others; but increases in power as she gets hit (As per her semblance) at the cost of maybe her speed or even her aura regeneration, as an example.
Attack variety is something else that needs working on; I feel like I see the same animations all of the time. And while this game is animated excellently; it could really do with some extra attention in future patches.
Enemies could definitely do with having a lower health bar, too. I often find myself surrounded and getting absolutely wrecked because their health just doesn't seem to decrease unless I focus a combo on one at a time; which gets very tedious. There is also no incentive to revive others if they are down, either; 50xp does nothing for you really, and you only put yourself at risk by trying.
Not much to say here; it's very underwhelming.
I'm not talking about appearance customization, though; I'm talking about the upgrade system. As of now, it is completely pointless to upgrade any character; your progress doesn't carry over into other games, so you would lose all of your gained levels and abilities upon joining a friend from a public lobby. What IS there to upgrade is disappointing, too; the trees mostly center around each character's special abilities, of which there are only three, and the tree itself is extremely small with around 3-4 upgrades on each.
Saying this; I love the idea of having your upgrades and XP only apply to each character individually; it encourages you to try everyone out just to see how they are animated and how they play, so make sure you expand on this, RT.
RWBY: Grimm Eclipse follows an alternate story to the one in the show currently, but there isn't much to say about it as of right now, since it isn't presented to you all that much really. However, I like the idea of having a seperate story, as it allows RTG to have huge creative freedom with it; which is always a good thing.
For a game made in Unity (I believe), the visuals are very stunning on Ultra, and stay true to the show in every possible way. Combat looks flashy thanks to all of the attack FX, and the lighting is very well done. All in all, it doesn't need an in-depth analysis. I would say however that advanced options need to be implemented ASAP: I like to customize all of the graphics settings individually to my liking.
Now, something to remember is that this game is in Early Access. And while many would say this is no excuse to have such little content and variety, you have to remember that RoosterTeeth hasn't made a single game before; it's a first experience for them, and they could do with all the constructive feedback that you can possibly throw at them. With this in mind, I'm willing to let it slip and stick by this game; as I believe it has the potential to grow into something epic should the developers listen to the fans.
I recommend this game to both fans of RWBY, and those looking for a good stress buster/hack n' slasher.

Portal Knights is a beautiful game that makes excellent use of Depth of Field. As any of the 3 classes, you explore island by island, gathering materials and fighting monsters. It's a bit simplistic on its RPG side, but sufficient enough when there is much more to do than the quests you sometimes find hidden away on the floating islands. The combat is enjoyable as well, as you can roll away from enemy attacks to avoid damage.
Often games will have resources that you gather in order to craft whatever, but lack variety and scaling. That isn't the case with Portal Knights. Each island has its own types of materials. As you progress, the materials do too. It gives you as the player more things to find, rather than hording on just one thing. So there is incentive to explore.
The major downside that I can say is that since you keep needing new materials, you have to either maintain a home base or bring all your upgraded crafting stations with you. And without any upgrade to your inventory, you're going to be lacking on space. Even across multiple people, if you have friends with you.
The experience is much better with at least one other person to play with by the way.

Beyond the absurdity and the humor, Surgeon Simulator can only offer frustration. Poor controls are taken as a core design philosophy and buttressed with any restrictive obstacle that came to mind. This is not the hilarious but humbling exercise of realizing how difficult complicated basic movement really is, this is a constant fight against a game that not only has to struggle to understand what the player wants it to do but also has trouble preventing objects from phasing in and out of each other. The lesson this game has to teach, what it demands of its players, is that they put aside the anger born of uncooperative controls to practice patience and precision in a world that has none. It's quite clever really. Shame all that's left to look back on is annoyance after annoyance, which increases level by level in the name of some sense of progression.

What happens if you take away the wastelands and reduce Fallout to its vaults? You get a rogue-lite RPG dungeon crawler called Wasted, a cel-shaded FPS heavily influenced by Bethesda’s most beloved franchise. A lot of the mechanics and gameplay will be very familiar if you played the post-apocalyptic roleplaying game, but it’s not just a shameless copy, it’s a game that stands on its own and doesn’t hide its influences.
The story is a negative of its role model. Instead of being a survivor of a vault, you are a waster of the surface, while everyone in the coolers, this game’s vaults, have died due to malfunction. The coolers were supposed to keep the smartest minds of the world alive in cryogenic chambers to rebuild everything after the radiation has settled. Instead only the dumbest specimens have remained and raid the coolers for their radioactive booze, which grant powerful hangovers and you are out to get them as well!
The gameplay is really solid and can be challenging when you don’t play the game as intended, but from all the FPS rogue-lites and -likes I have played, Wasted seems to nail the mechanics perfectly. Alas, once you obtain the required skill to progress, the game becomes too easy - an extreme contrast for a game that felt too hard at first. And even though the gameplay mechanics are really good, the enemies don’t offer much variety, meaning that you must have a high tolerance for repetition. Same goes for the dungeons themselves. They all have the same layout, the same rooms and beside some visual changes there is nothing fundamentally different. It’s the same thing over and over.
But if you are like me, you love hoarding and grinding for gear, which this game let’s you do. Inbetween runs you can go back to your home and hoard all the loot you collected to prepare yourself for other raids as well as visiting the Ony Express, a small town you can go to to receive quests, buy gear from the TP you got (yes, the currency is toilet paper) or just get hammered - not really, you get a buff that will last for a run though.
The quests are what make the game more interesting, they connect each cooler run and give them a purpose. The writing is hilarious and the voice acting suprisingly good. The last hours of the game felt exhausting, but the story was so rewarding I didn’t mind all the repeptitive, time-consuming dungeons.
If you are the Diablo grinding, farming, looting type and have a high tolerance for frustration and repetition you will have a good time with this game. I certainly did.

WASTED is a Semi decent permadeath FPS "dungeon" crawler, parodying Fallout, the 80's, with a dash of the graphical style from borderlands. Now, The person who made this game, Mr Podunkian, is known for STREEMERZ, of the Action 52 owns project, which was actually a very good retraux game (playable on a NES, no less).
While my computer is a semi potato, I experienced extreme lag on the Limited overworld areas, and such. This is pretty consistent with what other people said, so I assume its not just me.
The music, which is again, Limited, is actually very 80's esque, and would definitely fit right in. Of course, you only get to hear the actual songs if a boom box is nearby, or you get an item that allows you to listen to it.
One of the main problems of this game is the LIMITS. right from the getgo, you start out with 10 inventory spaces. and from there, you can get 3 fanny packs (bum, sideslung, and regular) to increase that to 16, which is not enough for the stuff you'll have. not to mention, you can't have multiples of some items, because why the **** not. that means you have to desprately rotate your stock of healing items, pizzas, liquified bread, and taters to make sure you don't die.
and all for a good bottle of beer to drink. Now, the perks on the beers are pretty cool (except for the starter ones, which are basically Get the heck outta heres)... except that once you die, you have to reobtain them all over again.
you can store goods in your house, but you can only store what you have on you, plus up to 6 (later 8) items you put in a box. Most of the time, most of the stuff you have on you is pretty much required for surviving in floors 7-10 in EVERY cooler you face.
Thats what makes it so difficult and unfair. the game throws so much cheap shots at you, that its difficult to get an actual foothold, unless you intentionally farm out multiple characters. from zombie machinegunners that can easily stunlock you, to landmines that blend in well with the ground, to traps that can One Hit Kill WITHOUT NOTICE, and you have an unfair and difficult game.
Oh, that character you named at the beginning? he gets replaced with RANDOM ones. that you can't rename unless you get a perk from defeating one of the coolers.
So yeah, All in all, I would say pass on this, unless you're wanting a challenge.

With the overwhelming amount of reviews geared towards Take-Two's attack on the modding community, it feels as if we are ignoring the things that really make GTA V a bad game.
I've been a fan of the GTA series since the beginning and with a few minor exceptions have played through the singleplayer missions of all of them. GTA V as a standalone, is multi-player focused. The meta-game of online is pretty standard, grind money and rp while unlocking perks by finishing certain missions. And just like any other MMO, online cheating is a huge issue with cheaters who not only have the ability to gain unlimited money and rp but also the ability to use god-mode to terrorize players in a lobby. It is almost impossible to get into a lobby without a hacker in the PC version of the game. When you are lucky enough to find a server that you aren't being constantly teleported and insta-killed, a neo-nazi will be spewing racist rants on voice/text-chat.
I have played GTA V and GTA V Online since it first came out, these problems have existed since. What has Rockstar done to address these issues? They ban players who recieve money drops (willing or not) because it hinders their Sharkcard (pay-to-play in-game currency) business. Anyone who played GTA online knows that money is only useful up to a very low threshold and does very little to unbalance online play. It is only useful for aesthetic mods. But having no money at all in the game makes it VERY difficult to enjoy because you will miss out on content that allows you to make money in the first place. If you want to make money legitimately in this game, you have to play heists using Rockstars awful matchmaking systems on missions that require collaboration between every member of the team. You don't have four friends that play GTAV on voice-chat? You're SOIL. So maybe this is a real-life simulator...I can live with that.
So what about the cheaters that terrorize players in lobby with god-mode and the bigots who harass players in game-chat? These people don't seem to be on Rockstar's radar at all. They've significantly INCREASED since I started playing this game! It makes GTA V online unplayable most of the time but it doesn't hurt Rockstar's Sharkcard sales. In fact, I suspect it increases Sharkcard sales because players don't even want to play the game legtimately anymore, they rather pay for a big sharkcard so they can play current meta-content or choose the easy way and cheat. Playing GTA V online without cheating is waste of your time and effort.
R.I.P. GTA modding community

This game just has too many issues and things to dislike.
On the plus side, the music, visuals, and voice acting are all quite good. The spacebar also highlights selectable items in the world, which makes things a bit easier.
I had/noticed some technical issues where the mouse would register the wrong click or not register at all. The subtitles are full of typos, despite being translated by a London based group and being voice acted. Those are small issues and easy to overlook, but the story and characters are not.
The story is barebones as can possibly be, and is still not explained much. You get the what, but not the who or why. It makes it just feel like a super generic bad guy and you really just don't care. It's pretty evident that they expected to make a series, further reinforced by the cheesy question mark after the end. I'd like to give a synopsis, but it would take about 2 sentences and cover the entire story. [spoileri]You play Rufus, an unlikeable character who just wants to get off his trash heap planet to a floating space station named Elysium. During his failed attempt he knocks a girl off a vessel... thing, who turns out to be the fiance of the main bad guy who wants to blow up the planet.[/spoileri] There's literally no explanation at all, and the villian is just about the same level as Dr. Robotnik, not even close to Bowser.
There's also a third group of... androids?... Maybe? They're called metal beards at one point and seem to be magnetic, but this is just something else with zero explanation.
None of the characters are flushed out enough to care about any of them, much less the one character you're stuck with the whole game.  Rufus is terrible. He makes a few quips that can be humurous, but for the most part just cries and whines about having to do literally anything. The entire game, along with other characters constantly shove it in your face about how much you don't care about his whiny self centered personality, but only seems to idolize it and makes no attempts to change it. [spoileri]He has no redeeming qualities throughout the game, his only motivation is leaving the planet and banging the unconcious engaged girl. At the end he takes the place of her fiance as she has lost her memory but instead decides to tell her the truth. I suppose this could be his redeeming quality moment, but when it's literally an entire planet vs. your chub I just don't find it that redeeming.[/spoileri] He's not dislikeable in a good way like a well made villian, he's just flat out that annoying person that no one likes, and lucky you get to spend about 8 hours with him.
All the other characters may as well be nonexistant, but not mentioning the apparently hot piece of Ginger Elysian Goal would be a mistake, as she's the driving "plot" device. She's unconcious for 96% of the game, in which time Rufus constantly calls her "babe" and his girlfriend, despite never actually talking to her aside from when she told you to call her fiance. When she finally actually wakes up by the end, she initially tells Rufus to not call her babe, then about 30 seconds later she apparently loves him.. I guess... for some reason... I'm actually not really sure. The whole thing is just kind of creepy and weird.
The last complaint is the super obtuse puzzles. Maybe it's just because I don't play much adventure/point'n'click games, but I just don't understand the type of mental connections you'd have to have for these puzzles to make sense. One involves a parrot and a couple kittens, which goes through a rather ridiculous process, and one involves a skeletons leg to meditate. Or rather, not involve it? Just for spoilers sake, here's the explanation of these puzzles:
Parrot:
[spoileri] In order to get to a radio, you need to stop the post office from functioning. The radio also requires headphones found on an operator near some carrier pigeons. So what you need to do is make a drugged blowdart to take out your ex girlfriend and steal some vouchers. Then you get a magnetic field tablet thing, switch some lights around which switch the pigeons to the wrong hole. You then need to drug one cat, give "espresso" to another, and give the post man robot a stolen voucher, which then sends a package to nowhere. The postage is incorrect and the postbot has to rebox the package with bubble wrap, which you then need to walk over to distract postbot. You then grab some spare kittens and a cypher to decode the lock to the radio room where you get a nodding bird. You place one kitten on a button and the nodding bird on the other.
You still with me so far? Good, because that's the part that made sense. The parrot follows.
From here you then need to go to a completely different area. This alone I just don't find good. The whole point is there's 3 lines of communication you need to block, the kitten and bird taking care of two, You once again to reiterate go to a completely different area and I don't understand how this logic is supposed to work. Just even guessing that you need the parrot is a hell of a stretch.
You fill a balloon with laughing gas and knock out the parrot, shove it in your coat and then inexplicably give it to your ex. You have to leave and come backto find out she's apparently been telling it of all your crimes (again to reinforce that you're a ♥♥♥♥♥♥ character.) Steal the parrot and put it on the phone with the police guy.
Huzzah! Headphones are now yours to steal. By comparison, you also needed a microphone, which was down the hall and you just pick it up. [/spoileri]
It's a bit ridiculous, but the skeleton leg is worse.
[spoileri] At one point you need to operate a crane, but apparently you're too nervous... for some reason, which results in dropping chubbait Goal about 25 feet directly onto her spine. You talk to a man who teaches you how to meditate, followed by taking a swig of alcohol. You then need to do the meditation thing again (because now you know you need his alcohol) and siphon some of his drink into your own empty bottle. This part's fine, but what follows angered me probably a lot too much. While I'm undeniably a fan of the show, I'll try my best not to let my bias effect my review
While certainly still a work in progress, RWBY: Grimm Eclipse shows a lot of promise to be a very fun game, and defiantly worth the $15 spent on it for anyone, but especially for fans of the show. The game is fun but not without its faults, which as of 5 hours into single player, seem to largely be restricted to needing a bit of polish and a few tweeks to the mechanics.
Combat System
While the combo system is a bit simplistic at the moment and I would love to see it expanded upon with branching combos, what's there now is pretty solid, with a few VERY necessary tweeks needing to be made. First is the lock-on system, which while pretty tight and accurate, is largely out of the players control. The game could benifit GREATLY from a lock on btton with target toggle and target reticule ala devil may cry, but if that would either be too much of a copy or too difficult to employment, then the lockon system needs to be more responsive to directional input from the player, as wading into thick clusters of enemies currently results in a crapshoot as to which direction you'll be focusing your attacks, which can end up with some very bad results, I.E. wading into a group of small enemies with a large, powerfull one near the center, pushing a weaker enemy away from the group and suddenly donig a 180 mid combo/aerial combo and heading back toward the large enemy right as it's attacking. SPEAKING of attacking enemies.
Enemy invulnerability animations
Okay, I have to admit, this is a pretty big point of contention. Several enemies gain complete invulnerability during many of their attacks. This isn't really a problem in some cases, and can even be an interesting mechanic for some heavier monsters like the Ursa or Boarbatusk while they're using their combo breaker, but it's pretty ridiculous when you have a pack of 4+ Beowolf rotating their frenzy slash in cycles, where they should clearly be susceptible to ranged attacks at the least. And while we're on the subject of ranged attaks
Long distance combat
While I can't really speak for all characters yet, as I've primarily played as Blake thus far, I feel that the ranged aspect of combat really suffers from the current lock-on system, far more even than the melee system as there have actually been situations where I was firing my weapon and ccompletely missing unobstructed targets heading right at me. Without a targeting reticule, the player generally has absolutely no idea what enemy they'll be shooting at with the exception that you will, of course, shoot in the general direction of your directional input. While I realize that this game was compared more to Dynasty Warriors than Devil May Cry, I can't help but make the comparison again and think that this game would benefit greatly from a similar targeting system, though I believe this largely won't be an issue while playing as Weiss, as her shots seem to have a fairly accurate homing system.
Camera system
While it's not the WORST camera system i've seen, it's hard not to say that this game suffers from poor camera controls. While the default sensitivity with an Xbox 360 controller allows for pretty quick turn around, the game has absolutely no auto centering, either by input or lack their of, and with both horizontal and vertical panning, this can make keeping a good eye on your enemies while ssimultaneously fighting them rather annoying. Personally I think the best solution for this is an auto-center button, which I would recommend be mapped to clicking in the right analog stick by default, and maybe a tolerable force centering option.
Control Remapping
Not much to say here other than that the game doesn't currently have a way by which to remap the controls, which is pretty disappointing.
Graphics
While not the most beautiful work of 3D art to ever grace a PC, RWBY is by no means an ugly game for being a hoard hack and slash still in early access. There are a few animation issues that should be ironed out, such as the characters sliding across the ground without animation if moving at the lowest possible speed or after firing their weapon and while traversing some slopes, but this is largely a polish issue, and being in early access at the time I'm completely confident things will be ironed out by full release.
Clarity of mechanics
With no tutorial or guide to speak of at this point, I feel that the game could do a better job of explaining a few of its mechanics, such as canceling a melee combo into a special attack by pressing the ranged attack button mid combo, or that upgrading skills in a certain way forfeits access to other variants of the skill that, in the beginning, you'll have to wait extra time beyond simply acquiring the skill points to buy them due to having to complete particular challenges (usually kill monsters with said skill [x] times) to unlock being able to buy them.
Overall
In closing, I would give this game in it's current state with absolutely NO changes a 5/10. The gameplay is fun and fluid if perhaps a bit annoying while playing solo due to a few quirks like the camera control and lock-on targeting. HOWEVER, given the love I expect this game will be treated with by it's makers, and how far it's come from the pre-alpha stand alone program and the alpha (beta?) that was playable to members on the RT site, I feel prospects for raising that rating up to a potential 8/10 are good. While there's nothing super ground breaking going on here, it's got fun factor and potential, and it's only just come to early access.
TL;DR
If you love the show or just enjoy a good hack n' slash, and have a few bucks to spare, pick this game up. It's fun, it's got potential to grow, and for $15 the price is most defiantly right.
EDIT: It seems that progress towards challenges does not yet save when the program is closed. This is a must fix, as the time it takes to finish these challenges vs. their reward (unlocking of skills in skill trees) is WAY out of balance to have to re-do them every time you launch the game

Very challenging game.
Pros:
For a roguelike, this game is very skill based.  Most of the time when you die, it's because you weren't paying close enough attention.  In my opinion, this is good design.  The game plays smooth, quick, and is mostly enjoyable as long as you're focused.  Very good for speedrunning, and with a pretty complex physics engine.
The story is enjoyable.  I haven't finished the game yet, but wanting to know what actually happens is enough to keep me going.  The tutorial was a nice introduction, too.
Good atmosphere:  The areas feel like they should, and have nice touches, such as little crawlers unique to each area which won't hurt you.  Kind of cute.  Each area has its own natives and traps, which will take time and patience to learn in order to succeed.
The whip and Indiana Jones references are also a nice touch, while the infamous ghost is also a very cool creepy compliment to the game, something I haven't seen in other roguelikes.
The music is also catchy and atmospheric.  Some of the songs are sure to stick in your head.  The game is a pleasant experience when it comes to visuals and audio.
Cons:
Offscreen arrow traps:  There are several occasions where, no matter how much strategy you use, or how slow you play, you will be nailed by an arrow trap while scrolling the screen horizontally.  This is just plain unfair and is a design flaw no matter how you spin it.  Fix this.
Lights out:  This takes away greatly from the skill based portion of the game.  I guess luck SHOULD be a thing in a roguelike, and that's fine for many players.  In my opinion, having a good run ruined by falling on spikes you can't see is kind of offputting.
Tunnel guy shotgun:  The way casual players progress through the game on a grand scheme is through the tunnel guy.  He has usually reasonable requests; a few rope, or a few bombs in exchange for a checkpoint, if you do it enough times.  Having him request a shotgun is not reasonable compared to the other things he asks for.
No swap system:  I'm sure we can all agree that it's pretty annoying having to crouch-drop your item before you can pick up the chick or use your whip.  A simple swap system would've made this a lot less tedious.
All characters are the same:  I might be wrong on this, since i've only used a few, but it seems all characters start with the same stuff.  In a game like this, you would expect each to have their own advantages and disadvantages.  Again, i've only used a few characters, but the system on the whole seems to be redundant.
All things considered, i'd definitely recommend this game, IF you're up for a challenge.  It's definitely above average.

All of these factions are competing for full control over Calradia. Politics, war, and crime pollute this crowded melting pot of a world... You play as a traveller who is not Calradian-born, you create your character's backstory and starting skills and attributes (also facial appearance). You will start off small, and you are given a choice to help a merchant find his brother and bring "justice" to a city, but you do not have to do this quest.
Now for gameplay, the combat system in this game is in a way, button-mashing proof. It is supposed to represent a more realistic fighting system in which defence and timing are more important, and reaction time is a very significant feature. You are given the choice of close range combat (one-handed & shield, polearm, two-handed, poolearm & shield,), long range combat (bow & arrow, crossbow, projectiles,), and you are allowed to ride on horseback. The armor and weapons in this game aren't like games like WoW, or Warhammer, or any usual Fantasy games in general because the armor and weapons are very practical and adhere to real history, nothing really ridiculous or impractical (unless you use mods),
This game has a GREAT modding community with MANY mods usually consisting of Full Conversions, or Multiplayer Maps. You should definitely check out ModDB, or the Steam Workshop for this game...

Suffers from the exact same problems as all your classic adventure games of old: from the very first room onwards you'll be looking for small objects that are easy to miss on the screen, trying your inventory items on everything in search for a solution, using game logic to accomplish things that make no sense in the real world and getting stuck without any sort of a hint system for help. It's very sad to see a game released in 2012 hasn't learned anything from its many predecessors.
Admittedly, it seems to be lighter on these elements than most old point-and-click games so if you're an old Sierra or Lucas Arts adventure fan this most likely will be a treat, with funny writing, good voice acting, a pleasant art style and an interesting setting. If you don't mind using an external guide (cheating) to get unstuck, I'd also recommend this from my first impression. Myself though, not being a huge adventure fan and only coming in because of a 90% discount,I'm pulling out at the first glance of every single bad design that better modern adventure games try so hard to stay away from.

I am such a huge South Park fan that it kills me to leave a negitive review. But the combat system in this game is just so horrible I think people need to know.
The writing is still there, there are more good jokes than ones that fall flat. The social commentary is as witty and well done as ever.
But the combat is so annoying I just can’t enjoy it. I know that any minute all this fun is going to go away and I’ll be in another fight. Combat in the last game was nothing special but it was effective. It did what it needed and added just enough to the old turn based formula to keep it interesting.
In this game the combat is based more on chess, but somehow worse and more annoying. So many turns go wasted as the selected character simply can’t reach anyone. Each character only has three moves and each move only effects a set number of tiles it’s so easy to find yourself stuck.
There are loads of status changes but they all seem pointless, gross out and bleeding the main two seem functionally identical. And again because everything depends on how the game board is on your turn, the idea that you can plan tactically is nonsense. The only tactic worth following is just try to get the combat over this as quickly as possible.
If you're a massive South Park fan like me than i still recommend it but just stick the combat on easy and just think of it as a commercial break you have to put up with to get back to the story.

Look, I like this game very much, but the learning curve is way too poor. Everyone gets thrown into the top matchmaking group, where everyone has everything, yet you having nothing -- nothing at all. No weapons, no vehicles, no classes, and -- most importantly -- no money to buy any of that.
So, right now, until that changes, I can't recommend the game. Having that said, I will elaborate a little, why the game in current state is impossible to enjoy.
I will not cover graphics, sound, UI or anything like that, because you probably already saw the screenshots -- game looks and sounds wonderful. The most con of this game is matchmaking, and I must say -- it's neither fair nor any good. Might be the worst matchmaking I ever say.
Now, the game has 4 game modes: Encounter (1), Skirmish (2), Assault (3), War (4). The most important difference in those game modes are the availability of the classes/vehicles.
(1) is the most basic. You've got only infantry class available, no vehicles, basic weapons. You'll start with this one, consider it a tutorial to basic game mechanics. Really small maps (currently, there's only 1 map, though), so no snipers or anything. You can't enjoy it this game mode, because it gets boring really fast. Playing it for more than 20-30 minutes is impossible.
(2) is your average modern shooter experience. A few classes, some vehicles, nothing too special. A variety of maps (around 5 available, I think). This was the most enjoyable game mode for me -- it offered a certain difficulties, but it wasn't too frustrating. There were no tanks or snipers shooting through the whole damn map. So yeah, I did enjoy playing this one.
(3) is your most popular mode (I presume). Tanks and aircrafts are introduced, as well as huge open spaces, where snipers dominate the field. My KD ratio in (1) and (2) was around 1.0, or even higher (depending on the matchmaking group, but more on that later). In this mode, however, I was around 2-16, 4-20, something like that. This is really frustrating, since I couldn't afford anything, so I was playing basic infantry class, with no auto rifle even -- I was using a mere default rifle, having no chance against snipers and machine gunners. My gameplay in this game mode was "deploy, run for 2-3 minutes, die while not seeing an enemy, respawn, repeat". Very frustrating, and mildly infuriating even.
(4) is the most ambitious game mode. Alas, I didn't climb up my XP ladder to get into there yet. Might update this review in a couple of days, when I'll reach level 10.
Now, there's one more thing: matchmaking group, and this is currently the weakest ♥♥♥♥♥iest matchmaking I've seen in my life. There are three groups: Bronze, Silver and Gold.
You're starting off in Bronze, like everybody else. You play for about an hour, reach level 5, and then your difficulty jumps up drastically, since you reach Silver. In Bronze, I was dominating my enemy team -- when all of us were in the same starting conditions (no superior weapons, no superior classes), but at level 5 game has changed. People at this level are already using guns that you don't have money for. They play Recon (sniper class), they use auto-rifles. But okay, it's still bearable.
What really sucks is when you hit level 7. At this point, you reach Gold and game really starts to infuriate you. Every single match you have people with superior equipment, superior classes and hundreds of hours in-game. You simply can't match them. I have to repeat -- you're going to reach this cluster♥♥♥♥ at level 7, which gonna take you 2-3 hours from the start. Great, isn't it? No, it isn't.
Why do I keep saying that you'll have no weapons? Well, simply because in this game, you have to play matches, to earn in-game currency to buy yourself anything. Literally, everything in this game costs money -- weapons, vehicles, new classes, repairs (yeah, you need to repair your♥♥♥♥♥♥ constantly), boost-ups to your levels.
Or you can just pay to get your♥♥♥♥♥♥unlocked for you. I believe, this is the only choice for a new player. Well, this choice doesn't suit me.
I will give this game a chance, in order to reach level 10 and see what's that final game mode is. Alas, my hopes aren't too high on it either.

At its best this can be both high octane fast paced action with many twists or slow and methodical experience. Whatever suits you. At its worst it is a futile grindfest with cheap and undeserved setbacks.
The problems with this game (in my opinion) are permanent death, purifier mechanic and repetitive content:
1) permanent death - When you die, you lose almost everything your character could have had on them. Most of your gear gone (solve it by collecting the same useful items over and over) and all your bonuses (booze hangovers). Now here is the thing. One dungeon run = plus one booze hangover. So imagine raising your character from blank sheet of paper into a mutant god of violence in the course of few hours only to lose them to random level layout that just happened to be in configuration to your disadvantage or something like that. I think the developer has quite different view of difficulty versus unfairness than I have.
2) purifier mechanic - If you take too much time exploring any one floor, this dude will spawn. Every. Single. Floor. It is a 600 HP (quite a lot) slow moving p.... with a minigun. First he will be terrifying hunting you through the dungeon. Then infuriating, not letting you explore enough. Then you learn how to deal with him a start to farm them. Later still, his gear will be abundant and he will become a chore you have to do, if you want to go at your own pace. The problem with this is his weapon. The knockback is quite insane, pinning you to a wall a pummeling you until you die. His magazine is 200 bullets so if you are unlucky (or too cocky - I am both) you will get caught and then just murdered. Other rapid fire enemies can do something similar (but they sure af do not have 200 bullet magazine). You can learn to kill him, yes. I have killed about 100+ of them. And yet, even with good gear and plenty of mutations, he can still kill me. Not by being difficult (the game has enemies that dodge, heal themselves, have multiple kinds of attack etc.) but by stunlocking you. He is best dealt from afar (if you do not like running in circles), making short range and close quarters combat ineffective due to knockback of his weapon.
3) repetitive content - What are you here for? After losing your progress (see 1) to for example Purifier (see 2), you can enjoy the same room/floor layouts. Different "dungeons" have different music and some specific enemies etc. but are all based on some basic principles. I am not saying here is not enough, I am saying that due to you going through it over and over it is spread too thin.
Despite thisI like the game. I like the world, the humour, the gradual improvement of yourself and your character (of course until you lose it all...), daily leaderboards runs and other features. Still, and maybe because I like it enough to sit through a night going over and over into a dungeon, I hate this three aspects very intensely. I suppose the game would be over in 20+ hours (maybe less) if it did not have them. If it was difficult in the sense of learning curve and content variety, fine. But this game doesn´t deserve the time it took. It bought it through cheap deaths and punishing setbacks rather than anything else. Also, I know this is a small game but... BUT... I still think there are some very rough edges.
So I hoped to come back here and say how I completed it and all is good, but... The RPG element screwed me. The game story can be influenced by your actions, stats, gear etc. And well it did not work for me. I got the achievement for acquiring the thing. If the idea of a Fallout rouge-like with the humor and art style of borderlands sounds good, then chances are you'll like this game.  I usually don't like rouge-likes but there's something about this one that makes it work.  The gameplay is really fun once you get into it (especially the courier's runs).
The gunplay is where this game really shines.  There's a good variety of guns and most are fun to use.  The melee is also pretty decent, though from what I can tell it's a bit limited after the beginning.  There's really only one thing I, and a lot of other people, don't like.  The S.O.B. Purifier.  This is a rather tough enemy that will spawn at the beginning of a floor when you've taken too long on a floor.  This is a terrible system for a rouge-like, especially one with a sneaking and trapping system in place.  It makes it so that sneaking and traps aren't really viable choices.  It also discourages you from exploring a floor too much, as if you stray off the main path too much you might be screwed.  This is the type of game I want to take my time with but the game discourages that approach.  The dev seems to love this system though, so I don't think it will be going anywhere.
The only other thing I don't like was how it lets you customize your own character, but 99 times out of 100 your first character will die and be replaced with a random character you have no way to customize.  I get this is just how rouge-like games are, but it just seems a bit strange.
Other than what I mentioned, the game's great.  I recommend picking it up and doing the daily courier runs, as it lets you play around with late game things early on as a separate character, though you can only keep 1 item for your main character.

This a nice photo editor... but not a photo shop like program. It will edit photos quite well but if you are looking for a interface like photo shop I would look else where. Now if you need a powerfull photo editor and are willing to look past the interface it really is a very good editor just didn't meet my needs in the end.

Who needs this software?
Anyone who is like me and let their mobile phone/tablet upload every picture ever taken to a cloud drive.
Seriously, my photo collection is a mess. I always intend to sort through it later and to arrange things.
Friends and family await the photos I took from that one event long ago where they want that cool picture from.
You get a really good interface to tag photos by category (red, blue, etc.) or rate them on a scale 1-5 or simply just tag them Flagged/Rejected.
For the sorting possibilities you can either create one big project containing all of your images and tag photos to export them to their own directories (this is what I do), or you can create many small projects by event/date and hand pick the photos that belong to this event and leave the original images in the same folder they were. You can then go on and export your project to Facebook or mail after you finish your edits.
Since I became a father I have not gotten a real chance to take my system camera out for a spin so I have not tried the lens correction. But I guess one can assume it is working as advertised. Perhaps I can update my review later when I get a chance. For now I bring the camera that fits in my pocket and is less expensive to replace if an accident happens, my phone.
While my own use case is mostly sorting and arranging images into albums there are some(quite many actually) features to enhance images.
I do not really approve of altering images after they have been taken (I prefer to shoot as many images as needed to get the one that is good) but sometimes there really is no other option.
For example you can build a panorama from multiple images or run face detection (and enhancing) on images.
One seemingly useful feature is the possibility to take several photos in a row when doing group portraits and then merge them to select the best face of each person and merge that into a final image and presto.. No more closed eyes!
One of those really cool features I found and tried out was content aware removal.
I tried it on an image of a guy sitting on a lawn and it took me about five seconds to highlight him and his shadow with the marker tool and then to press apply and see him and his shadow gone and replaced by grass. Although the grass was very flat and you could tell (if you look closely) that the image had been edited I figured, hey.. lets try to remove that flat grass as well and so I marked it and press the apply button. The results was scary good because now the flat grass was removed and replaced by taller grass just like the rest of the image had. I couldn't even see it had been edited even when I knew where the guy had been sitting and was looking for signs of edit in that region. I am truly amazed at how good these software tools have gotten over time. I think it will be a winner for those times when you want to take a photo of an object in a semi crowded area and you just can't get a break without a person walking into the shot. Well, now I can easily edit them out at home!
There are many more features to try out but this is a review, not a tutorial, so I will just post this already and say that I think this program has way more features than I think I will be able to take advantage of for my daily sorting and editing. That is a good thing cause it means I can grow into the program instead of outgrowing it! Definitely a thumbs up from me.
PS. At the time of writing this I have like 3-4 hours of using the program but the time reported by Steam is way less. There seems to be a bug with the time reported but that does not affect anything else than the "time spent in program" timer.
On a scale where Photoshop is 9 and Paint is 5 this would barely score 2.

If you are a fan of crafting and exploring with a touch of RPG elements Portal Knights is worth checking out!

Hopefully it gets fixed in the future, but don't waste your money on this port for now.

So yeah, this game is definitely early access, and has cracks and highly, highly visible seams in need of a good few months of straight polish on top of the content that's in development for it. But fortunately most of it is visual fidelity, audio issues, and missing or non-functional options. The gameplay feels good, and nothing's crashed. This early access experience is better than I expected.
Alright, so I'm gonna rattle off some things, what they did well, what they need to improve that they definitely can improve for the for-realsies actual release. To whoever this information concerns, and anyone who wants to know what they're getting into if they want in on this right this second (and obviously as of the time I write this, 2nd December 2015, etc.).
- No keybinding/controller button mapping options
- Shortage on options in general but it's not been a
problem so far
- Walking animation when going down a slope is super jank but I think they're aware of that
- Audio levels are a mess while in action. Voice lines in battle are drowned out by fighting SFX and aura refilling is insanely loud
- Extra variety in sound effects would be nice. Even if it's slight random pitchshifting of the blade sound effect, it goes a long way
- Ultimately not of priority but I'd like to know the composition of the team I'm quick joining, even if it's because I want to not have duplicates as a picky flair thing
- That one Grimm enemy with the invincible slashing attack could use some tweaking. Slowing down start-up to keep it in line with all the other telegraphs (which I'll discuss later) because wow a group of 3 really trips you up with that in an annoying way.
- Subtitles during particularly long mission briefing lines straight up get cut off out of the screen and the rest is just missing.
- Some very arbitrary invisible walls that don't feel natural with the environment. In most cases it'd have been more appropriate to just put something that's actually there in the way so I don't feel like I should try and walk through to a place I can't.
- This is basically a multiplayer character action game (ala Platinum Games brawlers, etc.) when you think about it, that's nuts. Way to take a stab at that idea.
- It's not terrible brawler gameplay either. Combo variety isn't the greatest but you've got just enough at your fingertips to keep you figuring things out for a few hours, specials in particular, even before the skill trees come into it.
- You can dodge cancel. That's good, someone somewhere knows what's up. There's certain things you can't do that with and all but one of them are invincible anyway. And it's a pretty good invincible dodge, though it's got an invisible single second or so cooldown that nothing in the game, HUD or otherwise, expresses. I'll let the devs figure out how they want to balance it for this co-op game and if they want to keep it that way or make it as responsive and as whenever-you-need-it as a Bayonetta dodge because that's the maximum level you would want.
- Isolated progression and skill upgrades confined to a single run of a mission are a nifty idea to keep the game unique and it's not handled badly either. Leveling up seems to be just for skill points for ability upgrades and passives which can get really good without buffing damage and health numbers, which means a player dropping in closer to the end isn't too behind the curve, they can still brawl with the same bread and butter damage output and health pool.
- Very respectful enemy attack telegraphs, you've got the lesser Arkham-like red sparks above the head for a regular attack, and then flashing white for an attack that's invincible and that you should just dodge. They even did a good job telegraphing that flashing white = invincibility without explaining it. Your character also gets that effect during specials and dodges, so you should be able to pick it up right away.
- We've only got the one level but it's still got replay value right there and then as you go back with different characters. Not even that though, it's enough that you might go back with the same character as before just to do it again with a different build. Does that AoE spec work the best in general? Will it be fun to do it again with single target damage maximization? How about I take all the support passives for when I'm with my friends and use abilities with crowd control like knockback? They lock some skill tree stuff behind challenges which carry over across all runs, which might be a little dastardly but not an offensive strategy all in all to promote replay value.
I recommend this game, eventually, based on good faith and the fact that right now there's something here that's worth coming into fruition. If it's got the polish and features it needs and has a good chunk of levels for a worthy playtime it'll be worth the price tag, maybe even more depending on how big the game gets, but I'll reserve judgement. I'm not keeping up with what's expected or planned to be in the game.

Let us first have a look at the state of this game before the release, so have a look at my previous review of it (which was also positive) and written just a month or so before the official release (shortened version):
The game had an incredible change since I touched it for my first review in the beginning of December (note: day after the release of the early access version) and improved a lot.
In any way this game became so much better paced, both in terms of mission design as well as in terms of combat and I'm looking forward to review this again after the next few big updates.
I can now completely recommend getting this game, if you are unsure feel free to wait for a sale or consider trying it out and if you don't agree with my opinion you can still refund it.
And now... what I would LOVE to see in the future:
- Difficulty options
- more characters
- unlockable cosmetics (for example some different outfits like the one from the dance night)
[END OF OLD REVIEW]
As you can see it already improved quite a lot over the EA release state back then.
But was it able to keep this rate of improvement?
I would say, yes, it did.
Now let us look at the features added since my last review:
- Team JNPR (paid DLC):
To be honest I hoped for a free additional team, but the price tag of 5 € is reasonable if you consider how much effort each character needs. I haven't tried out any of them yet (bought the pack though), but considering they are on they same level as the regular characters I think this price is justified. Now all I can hope for are new teams in upcoming releases, including SNNN and CFVY.
- Horde mode:
A kind of wave defense / survival mode. Not tried yet, but it sounds promising and feels like something this game could benefit from.
- saved character progression:
Before only the unlocked skills were saved, but not the level of your characters, now that this is saved, too you don't need to unlock it all over again. Previously unlocked skills, including the mastery were kept unlocked for those who managed to unlock it previously.
- upgraded HUD:
While the old HUD was functional, it was exactly that and nothing more. The new HUD includes a character portrait and feels very sleek in its design.
So aside of the (unlockable?) cosmetics/alternate outfits (maybe also as DLCs? I would PAY for Weiss' alternate outfit she wore during one of the last few episodes of vol 2. HEARD THAT DEVS?).
The game overall still shows a steady self improvement, which makes me keep my review on RECOMMENDED. I hope they keep this up even now that it was officially released.

Buy this game only if you really like the series and really desperate for more RWBY because at this current state, this game is lacking in everything. Thats my short review of RWBY. now for the longer review..
First thing first, since this is a hack and slash action game the combat need to be really good. Soo, how is RWBY: Grimm Eclipse combat ? It got a lot of potential, but right now there isn't anything that you can do when encountering enemies except to press the dodge button when they about to attack and then press the attack button 8 times to do that 8 hit combo. There isn't any combining 2 to 3 of different attack button to combo your attack, just 1 button for attack, one button for dodge, and occasionally use the skill button to do 1 of the 3 skill available, long range skill, AoE skill to hit all the enemies around you, and another AoE skill that hit all the enemies in front of you. I have to admit its pretty awesome  when you keep the combo going by keep hitting the enemies, but the overall combat mechanic at this current state ? Its not really that great.
The leveling system in this game is per match basis, so you didn't carry your level when you change the map, kinda like DotA 2 as the developer said. But, how is the leveling so far ? There isn't anything interesting in it, you didn't even feel that great when you level up since you didn't earn a new combo or anything, you only can choose what essentially a damage buff to all your existing skill, a health buff, a regeneration buff, and all other sort of other buff. That didn't make you feel more powerful then before. They really need to improve this if they want to make a great game, make it so that you learn new combo or add a new skill that you can use or something.
The graphics itself its really good, it really capture the series aesthetic even though its natural for them to do that since the company that make the cartoon animation is the same as the company that make the game, they could just pulled the guy/gal that draw and make the cartoon animation to make the game animation. Well i have to point out that i have suffer a one second random freeze during my playthrough, even though my laptop isn't that great but it can run both Fallout 4 and GTA V, i'm sure it should be able to run this without any hiccup.
The plot and the story of this............. Its kinda been told just from the voice acting of the teacher to tell you to do stuff and tell you whats going on, like "what is the boxes doing here i wonder, ohh ! It was from *this* company ! Why they would do such a thing !" there isn't any cutscene at this current state. The main characters also said something sometimes, like Ruby said "Yay ! More Grimm to kill !" or something like that. Truth to be told, as long as the combat is good, we don't need a story.
In the end, just like what i was said in the first paragraph of this review, if you are not a desperate hardcore fans that need more RWBY or a really supportive person that likes to support the series that you loved. Wait until they perfected the game before you buy it.
Now i will list all the lack of content and bug that i see in this game:
-Lack of animation in a lot of thing like going downward from a ramp, or walking reallly slow using a controller.
-In one of my playthrough, i get stuck in the terrain and cannot get out, game breaking bug.
-Only have one campaign which took about an hour to complete.
-Cannot change mouse and analog sensitivity in game.
-Cannot change the control.
-You could walk through some of the terrain.
-The running animation feels a bit, floaty.
-One second freeze and fps drop which a bit annoying.
But !!! You might be asking to yourself, why you thumb this up if nearly all that you said in the review are a bad thing ?? Because this is a RWBY games and i'm a huge fan of it, and also i have trust in Rooster Teeth to delivered a great product. Please don't let me down Rooster Teeth.

Heyo folks, End World Gaming here to share an excerpt from my review for Figment by Bedtime Digital Games.
Figment is an audio-visual themed puzzle game that puts you in the role of Dusty, the mind’s courage. The entire game takes place within the mind and it’s world’s and characters use this theme throughout.
Dusty sets out on his journey with his overly optimistic companion, piper, after his scrapbook is stolen. Dusty’s journey takes him to various parts of the mind. The right side of the brain, where creativity is controlled. The left side of the brain, where logic comes into play. Finally, the conscious mind, where you’ll find a harsh and ever changing landscape.
In each area you’ll be tasked with defeating nightmares. These nightmares sing while battling them and each song is excellently done. The songs vary depending on the nightmare as well so it’s varied in genre. I personally liked the fear of death’s songs the most, since his were rock/metal based. They all were excellent though and very catchy. The ambient music was also very good. There are often instruments as trees and hearing them was also enjoyable. All in all, the music mixed with the ambient sounds was quite eargasmic.
The game’s gameplay mostly revolves around solving various types of puzzles. These puzzles are very well designed and are the perfect mix between easy and challenging. The game definitely makes your brain work and the puzzles are often very fun to solve as well.
I also really liked the colorful artwork that was used throughout. Each area you visit is well designed and you could feel that a lot of work went into making them unique. The game often felt like playing a fairy tale in truth. It was a mixture between lighthearted and dark and it was highly entertaining.
The game does feature some combat and it often kicked in at perfect moments. This way the puzzles never become monotonous or repetitive. I will admit that the combat system isn’t the game’s focus so it’s a bit on the basic side. It does it’s job well in the end though.
Overall, Figment is an amazing audio-visual experience. It’s gorgeous art style mixed with the excellent music throughout creates a torrent of enjoyment. Listening to everything on a surround sound system was pretty amazing and I highly recommend it with headphones. The game’s story was pretty good too but it’s world, mixed with the music and art is really what makes it worth playing. I highly recommend this one folks, it’s pretty epic.

This is my new favorite indie game. You can tell that a lot of love and care has gone into the development of this game and playing it feels like being introduced to someone's favorite childhood sock monkey. The story has elements of Pixar's Inside Out with its own lovely humor and quirkiness and I found myself humming to the music long after playing the game. It's a southpark game. Played through the entire game, did all the sidequests and all but one collectable, so these are fairly informed opinions I have here.
You might wonder why, as generally the second game in a franchise sees what could use improving and attempts to do that. Well, this is a different kind of game. The combat and leveling system here is....bad, from an RPG standpoint. As is the equipment and gear you get. I'll get into that in a moment.
Combat.The tactical elements are awesome. Each attack hits a specific number of tiles, ranging from a 1-square distance punch, to a straight line laser blast, to more exotic moves. But you only ever have 4 moves, one of which is a charged 'ultimate'. As you progress, you get more classes and can hot-swap abilities when out of combat. But really, you could go the entire game with the same abilities you started with and do just fine. Plus, these abilities never power up or do different things, and you'll likely find you stick with the same set of powers most of the game, since few of them seem much different or appreciably better than others. And combat is generally easy, even on the higher difficulty settings, other than a few boss battles which seem cheap and overpowered.
Leveling and equipment. Max level is 15. You won't reach it without grinding a lot, and there's no reason to do so. You unlock slots for artifacts as you progress, but by 10 or 12 you have them all. Since level doesn't affects stats at all, it's pointless to level further. Stats and overall power level is determined entirely by the artifacts you have equipped. And my god, do they ever rain artifacts down on you.  Usually one per EVERY SINGLE STORY BATTLE. And sometimes one for every random encounter like Chaos Minions or Raisins Girls. Because of that they all sort of blend together and most of them are not much better than any other of the same might level. Oh, and artifacts (and dna) are the only gear in the game you can equip. No weapons, no armor. Everything else is cosmetic changes or costumes. I really didn't like these aspects at all, not a welcome change.
Story. Without spoilers, it's both pretty good and extremely upsetting. Some later story choices you have to make.....and I thought climbing up a gay mans ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to disarm a s-nuke was bad. And bad as in distasteful, even for southpark. I won't go into that further, as some people may not mind it. It's also quite a hand-holder of a game, you always have a quest marker telling you where to go.
Overall: Good game. Not worth full retail launch price, not as good as the Stick of Truth. Certainly 'mostly' enjoyable and worth playing.

I've always been a fan of Mortal Kombat. I grew up with the series, and though I see its flaws nowadays, I still love it and consider myself a loyal fan to the series. With the reboot of the series in the previous title, I never imagined there would be good storytelling in story mode, it was always just background on characters and people starting up rumors on what is happening with which character and whatnot, With the latest titles, I'm actually glad I can enjoy a cinematic experience, even if it is not that entertaining to some.
Combat (That is how it is spelled -.-) has improved significantly since the last title and X-Ray moves have been "nerfed" so as to not let the player depend on them. There are also Easy Fatalities and Skip fight bonuses claimed during story mode and versus or online. The Krypt is much more entertaining than the last one. It feels like an Adventure game although it gets boring at times. All in all the game ran smoothly.
However, it didn't run that smoothly as a PC version. There are way too many issues that it pains me to not recommend this port for simple reasons. While I was halfway through story mode my save has been deleted because the game updated itself, to my knowledge. Sure enough, I threw my frustration aside and decided to beat story mode again, this time skipping all the cutscenes till I reached 80% of the story mode. After finishing story mode, it happens again. Fool me once shame on you, Fool me twice, Shame on me. Shame on me for not having a backup file, sure. But the fact of the matter is that it shouldn't' have happened in the first place and I'm sure if it was on a console, I would have uploaded my save and just downloaded it again. This is not a matter of preference in consoles, it's just from what I've experienced is this port is the least functional one. Hopefully it gets fixed in the future, but don't waste your money on this port for now.

It's a southpark game. Played through the entire game, did all the sidequests and all but one collectable, so these are fairly informed opinions I have here.
You might wonder why, as generally the second game in a franchise sees what could use improving and attempts to do that. Well, this is a different kind of game. The combat and leveling system here is....bad, from an RPG standpoint. As is the equipment and gear you get. I'll get into that in a moment.
Combat.The tactical elements are awesome. Each attack hits a specific number of tiles, ranging from a 1-square distance punch, to a straight line laser blast, to more exotic moves. But you only ever have 4 moves, one of which is a charged 'ultimate'. As you progress, you get more classes and can hot-swap abilities when out of combat. But really, you could go the entire game with the same abilities you started with and do just fine. Plus, these abilities never power up or do different things, and you'll likely find you stick with the same set of powers most of the game, since few of them seem much different or appreciably better than others. And combat is generally easy, even on the higher difficulty settings, other than a few boss battles which seem cheap and overpowered.
Leveling and equipment. Max level is 15. You won't reach it without grinding a lot, and there's no reason to do so. You unlock slots for artifacts as you progress, but by 10 or 12 you have them all. Since level doesn't affects stats at all, it's pointless to level further. Stats and overall power level is determined entirely by the artifacts you have equipped. And my god, do they ever rain artifacts down on you.  Usually one per EVERY SINGLE STORY BATTLE. And sometimes one for every random encounter like Chaos Minions or Raisins Girls. Because of that they all sort of blend together and most of them are not much better than any other of the same might level. Oh, and artifacts (and dna) are the only gear in the game you can equip. No weapons, no armor. Everything else is cosmetic changes or costumes. I really didn't like these aspects at all, not a welcome change.
Story. Without spoilers, it's both pretty good and extremely upsetting. Some later story choices you have to make.....and I thought climbing up a gay mans ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ to disarm a s-nuke was bad. And bad as in distasteful, even for southpark. I won't go into that further, as some people may not mind it. It's also quite a hand-holder of a game, you always have a quest marker telling you where to go.
Overall: Good game. Not worth full retail launch price, not as good as the Stick of Truth. Certainly 'mostly' enjoyable and worth playing.

Figment: Quirky, entertaining, actually kinda emotional and all around feel-good-game of the year.
Figment was an enjoyable play, with a wonderful surrealist-characteristic style, a fun duo consisting of an hopeful lil' bird named Piper and an old reclusive rabbit-racoon hero who was and you'll come to find still is; The mind's courage. Together they will face the fears that have been ruining the mind.
Now since this is a puzzle-adventure, puzzles and combat are first.
Puzzles: Okay, MOST of these puzzles were actually really thought out well however some were a little bit too easy (for me at least.) I was playing it with a friend and she had no trouble getting through most of them. Also can I just say how much I love the recycling idea? Anyway, some there are some puzzles here that some might find simply simple. All in all puzzles could have been harder.
Combat: Alright, but was it really needed? While of course Dusty is the mind's courage and needs this sword to y'know? Be courageous but maybe a good substitute would be narrow and witty escapes? I know it does not sound too "courageous" but there were not enough combat moves. Though, it is good in the character sense at the very best.
So those were just two basic aspects of the game but what really snagged me was the. freaking. sound. track. IT IS A BEAUTIFUL MONSTER! I loved all the effort into the music from the villain songs to just the freaking backgrounds. It made me want to stay around the map a little bit longer which is just too good! Please everyone! You should really consider purchasing the sound track!
Now after that huge  fan-girl fest it's time we get to the characters and the story.
Story: It passes well. It has a few cliches but I do think it's all in good fun. So it starts off with a family in their car, Father, mother and the daughter. The parents come off as stern and noble as they have already decided on the daughter's career which to me adds a neat contrast compared to the real wold and figment's. The father did was not seeming to pay attention to the road he crashes and both him and his wife seem to be left unconscious leaving the little girl alone. Now this is where it begins and we enter in on a transition to the little girl's voice to piper saying "Wake up!" then we pan to dusty who is then told he needs to stop being a bum and rid the mind of these nightmares once and for all...in the most charming way possible. The story is well written though not too original however the stuff around is what comes to make it so immersive.
Characters:
Antagonists - NOT ENOUGH OF THEM, DANGGITT I love all of there designs but I do think it need more diverse henchmen! As for the main villains, amazing with some awesome metal, show tune, Disney villain vibes! They are amazing!
Protagonists: FAN-FREAKING-TASTIC. I am a huge sucker for the optimist and the witty grump duo. Dusty and Piper are a really cute representation of a father-daughter type of relationship. For the inhabitants worth, They can be really funny from the accents to math puns they can be really cute to listen to!
Figment is a dangerously-underrated game made by a very talented danish studio. The team really deserves the credit but I fear that this may end being a lost gem. Seriously show this to your friends or maybe even get the attention of some youtubers! Figment is truly a wonderful game with a few bumps and bruises but the journey you'll have with Dusty and Piper is full of so much more. (In the good sense.)
Happy gameplay everyone!

Figment:
~~~~~~~

The mind is one of the most important functions of each individual. Everything is happening up there for every one of us.  It allows you to daydream, to enter endless conversations about anything and everything. It’s a huge memory box between a pair of ears where all knowledge is stored. Some information can create fear, anxiety or nightmares and needs to be washed away. That’s when you need to call on Dusty, the chaser of bad dreams, to eliminate them once and for all. Let’s enter the world of Figment!
Figment is an adventure/ puzzle / action game where you take control of a charming creature; a sort of rabbit named Dusty.
At the start of the game, you’ll hear a conversation between a child and her parents in a car. Then you’ll hear a big boom! From here, you’ll enter the charming world of Figment. Your character will be relaxing on a rocking chair (sleeping) holding onto his scrapbook, and will be woken up by his friend, Piper the bird. A drink will be located on a nearby table, but Dusty will want some ice to make it fresh. This first quest is basically a small tutorial. As soon as you get back, you’ll discover that your scrapbook was taken by a strange black and purple creature – which is called a nightmare - and you want to take it back.  It won’t be easy, though.
Dusty will have to solve puzzles, eliminate enemies with his wooden sword and defeat a few bosses to reach the ultimate nightmare. The puzzles are fairly simple and involve picking up coloured batteries, metal discs, gears, levers, moving squares, as well as reproducing sequences. In battles, Dusty will have only two forms of attacks; the normal attack (single sword swing) and the power up attack (hold the button on your mouse or gamepad for a few seconds to inflict more damage to your enemies). They are a few types of opponents in this game and each time Dusty eliminates one of them a few white spheres will appeared at that spot. They’ll go towards the white gauge and as soon as the gauge is filled it will give you additional health, which is represented by a green gauge. Dusty can also find green spheres within the world to regenerate his health. There are memories to collect within the mind, represented by pink spheres.
What I really like is the artwork. The world is beautiful, full of colours, and each area of the mind looks different. Guitars and trumpets are lying on the path playing music. The soundtrack is great, too, and you’ll be entertained with a few songs before entering into battle with bosses. Control-wise, they are responsive either with the mouse and keyboard or gamepad.
Positives:
~~~~~~~
-	Beautiful artwork
-	Interesting concept
-	Nice soundtrack
-	Easy to play
-	Achievements and trading cards
Negatives:
~~~~~~~~
-	Too few enemies
-	Puzzles could have been harder
Figment is an interesting concept setup in a beautiful mind world.
7/10

Time Rifters is a fun and enjoable little indie game.
The basic objective is to destoy all the cubes in a level in a limited time. There are too many cubes to destroy in one go. This is where Time Rifters shine. After your first playthough of a level you control a second charecter. Your first still remains and does the exact thing you did with your first try. This repeats until you play a level with a fourth time. This makes for some chalanging gameplay, as you have to think ahead and plan. It can also be very chaotic to see four charecters run around in a room, shooting everywhere.
There are three chapters, each containing five arenas. There are a variety of weapons each character can pick at the start of each chapter. Each gun can be upgraded between rounds with gold. Gold are found be destroying th cubes. The challange is to destroy all the cubes.
The biggest problem with Time Rifters is the lack of official content. There are only 3 episodes, each only containing 5 arenas. Each arena takes 4 minuts (one minute per charecter). Thats a hour to play everything the game has. The replay value is high if you care about getting good times, but otherwise the game is short. Thankfully the devs decided to add a level editor with workshop support. This adds a lot of content, but I haven`t found anything nearly as good as the oficcial levels.
Time Rifters is a great game with a unique idea. It`s defnitley worth a try.

With the overwhelming amount of reviews geared towards Take-Two's attack on the modding community, it feels as if we are ignoring the things that really make GTA V a bad game.
I've been a fan of the GTA series since the beginning and with a few minor exceptions have played through the singleplayer missions of all of them. GTA V as a standalone, is multi-player focused. The meta-game of online is pretty standard, grind money and rp while unlocking perks by finishing certain missions. And just like any other MMO, online cheating is a huge issue with cheaters who not only have the ability to gain unlimited money and rp but also the ability to use god-mode to terrorize players in a lobby. It is almost impossible to get into a lobby without a hacker in the PC version of the game. When you are lucky enough to find a server that you aren't being constantly teleported and insta-killed, a neo-nazi will be spewing racist rants on voice/text-chat.
I have played GTA V and GTA V Online since it first came out, these problems have existed since. What has Rockstar done to address these issues? They ban players who recieve money drops (willing or not) because it hinders their Sharkcard (pay-to-play in-game currency) business. Anyone who played GTA online knows that money is only useful up to a very low threshold and does very little to unbalance online play. It is only useful for aesthetic mods. But having no money at all in the game makes it VERY difficult to enjoy because you will miss out on content that allows you to make money in the first place. If you want to make money legitimately in this game, you have to play heists using Rockstars awful matchmaking systems on missions that require collaboration between every member of the team. You don't have four friends that play GTAV on voice-chat? You're SOIL. So maybe this is a real-life simulator...I can live with that.
So what about the cheaters that terrorize players in lobby with god-mode and the bigots who harass players in game-chat? These people don't seem to be on Rockstar's radar at all. They've significantly INCREASED since I started playing this game! It makes GTA V online unplayable most of the time but it doesn't hurt Rockstar's Sharkcard sales. In fact, I suspect it increases Sharkcard sales because players don't even want to play the game legtimately anymore, they rather pay for a big sharkcard so they can play current meta-content or choose the easy way and cheat. Playing GTA V online without cheating is waste of your time and effort.
R.I.P. GTA modding community
