SNOW is getting a lot of flak at the moment, as the devs have changed the way that the game works somewhat (from a totally free to play game with optional paid cosmetic upgrades, to one which requires some funds to access certain parts of it). However, I still recommend this game without any reservations. For an indie game developed by a small team, it really exceeds all expectations. Graphically it's very attractive, the physics are entertaining (and occasionally hilarious), and the amount of customisation available is utterly overwhelming, both with real-world brands and SNOW's own labels.
There are, at present, two ways to play the game:
- Free. Completely and utterly free. This gets you all the functional aspects of the game - ability to use skiier or snowboarder plus drone - and access to two maps. One of these is the basic tutorial map, which has plenty to explore off-piste, and which the devs have stated they will be expanding in the future. The other map is different every week, taken from the pool of existing maps developed for SNOW, most of which are facsimiles of existing competitions (X-games and the like), but with substantial surroundings which reward a bit of exploring away from the jumps.
- Paid. Buy credits in game using real money, pay for any clothing or skis which tickle your pickle, and buy "lift passes" to access any of the available maps at any time. At present, the lift passes are for relatively short time periods (between one day and one month, essentially) - but again, the devs have stated that in the near future you'll be able to purchase the entire game, with access to all current and future maps. All the clothing and gear options are purely cosmetic, and don't affect your performance.
Gameplay is fun (definitely best with a gamepad, keyboard/mouse users will struggle); either free-ride down the mountain doing as you please, or take part in time trials, slopestyle, big air, or halfpipe contests. Each mountain has a series of challenges which can be performed whilst free-riding, too, so there's plenty to do - as well as just exploring. The landscapes are gorgeous, and riding a perfect groomer as dawn peeks through the pine trees almost captures the feeling of being the first one up on the lifts in the morning.
Give SNOW a chance - play the free game, see if you like it. If you enjoy it, pay a bit more to access more content. Seems like a no-brainer to me. I'd happily pay full price for the game and have access to all of it, forever. If you don't want to spend money to change the way your avatar looks, then don't - it's all cosmetic anyway, and no-one will care. For me, it's a perfect game to relieve the stress of a hard day at work, and I don't begrudge the dev team for trying to make a game which actually turns a profit.

With the overwhelming amount of reviews geared towards Take-Two's attack on the modding community, it feels as if we are ignoring the things that really make GTA V a bad game.
I've been a fan of the GTA series since the beginning and with a few minor exceptions have played through the singleplayer missions of all of them. GTA V as a standalone, is multi-player focused. The meta-game of online is pretty standard, grind money and rp while unlocking perks by finishing certain missions. And just like any other MMO, online cheating is a huge issue with cheaters who not only have the ability to gain unlimited money and rp but also the ability to use god-mode to terrorize players in a lobby. It is almost impossible to get into a lobby without a hacker in the PC version of the game. When you are lucky enough to find a server that you aren't being constantly teleported and insta-killed, a neo-nazi will be spewing racist rants on voice/text-chat.
I have played GTA V and GTA V Online since it first came out, these problems have existed since. What has Rockstar done to address these issues? They ban players who recieve money drops (willing or not) because it hinders their Sharkcard (pay-to-play in-game currency) business. Anyone who played GTA online knows that money is only useful up to a very low threshold and does very little to unbalance online play. It is only useful for aesthetic mods. But having no money at all in the game makes it VERY difficult to enjoy because you will miss out on content that allows you to make money in the first place. If you want to make money legitimately in this game, you have to play heists using Rockstars awful matchmaking systems on missions that require collaboration between every member of the team. You don't have four friends that play GTAV on voice-chat? You're SOIL. So maybe this is a real-life simulator...I can live with that.
So what about the cheaters that terrorize players in lobby with god-mode and the bigots who harass players in game-chat? These people don't seem to be on Rockstar's radar at all. They've significantly INCREASED since I started playing this game! It makes GTA V online unplayable most of the time but it doesn't hurt Rockstar's Sharkcard sales. In fact, I suspect it increases Sharkcard sales because players don't even want to play the game legtimately anymore, they rather pay for a big sharkcard so they can play current meta-content or choose the easy way and cheat. Playing GTA V online without cheating is waste of your time and effort.
R.I.P. GTA modding community

As this game is in Day 1 Early Access, take this review more as feedback and less of a...well...review.
So to start things off with the good stuff, I was pleasantly surprised that the game was able to quickly get to the gameplay.  Joining and hosting lobbies is quick and easy.  Depending on the host, connections were varying but still very much playable.
The characters look good, although there are particular moments where the animation gets a little goofy (i.e. decending down an incline).  Combat animations seem very fluid mirroring the source material of the show.  Firing a shot from Ruby's scyth or lunging from a rune with Weiss seems one to one with what you'd expect.
Some things I'd hope to come with changes down the line is ways to vary up the combos.  Other than what seems to be a universal 3 melee dodge cancel into another 3 melee and maybe eventually into a special, there doesn't seem to be too much room for doing anything deeply creative.  Perhaps making certain windows within the standard melee string jump cancelable and/or add a way to follow up an aerial rave could solve this, although I can't say whether or not this is possible or the goal of the combat.  Regardless the hack and slash mechanics are solid.

If you're looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.

Check out this game, guy. A pretty solid sequel to The Stick of Truth.
PROS:
- Improved combat system. The "tactics" style grid adds another strategic element to the RPG turn-based combat system, and has been fairly enjoyable.
- Social commentary. Southpark does what Southpark does best - the social commentary is par excellence. Just enough satire without feeling moralizing or propagandizing, a dash of humor, a prophetic mirror at all of culture.
- Intruiging story.
- Southpark Superheroes! It's just ___fun___ to play alongside Coon and Mysterion from the Coon Trilogy eps, and even more fun to see new characters that I won't spoil here. The meta aspect of playing a game of kids playing a game of superheroes is also done really really well, with occasional allusions and references (like stopping a fight in the street so a car can drive past).
CONS:
- Somewhat buggy. Some of these issues may be caused by me having a 2-core processor, although I also have two R9 280s crossfired. This setup let me play graphic-heavy games like Tomb Raider or Skyrim on Ultra without any significant issues, but I suspect they "optimized" this game to run more on the CPU than GPU as a way of allowing more people to play. Great for anyone with a quad-core. Bad for me. Still, it's possible these problems are unrelated to this, so it's worth mentioning them anyway.
1) NPCs often don't load into the scene until a minute or two. This creates some awkward popup, where (for example) I'll assume a living room is empty, only to discover that if I would have waited longer, 2 NPCs would load onto the couch. A few scripted events have messed up because I could walk past the trigger point because the NPCs didn't load in time.
2) Battles are extremely delayed in starting. I have to frequently wait upwards of 30seconds to 1minute while the tactics battle system loads.
3) I could never get Steam to stream it from my PC to my laptop without messing up the resolution.
4) Occasionally boots to a black screen.
Killstreaks everywhere

An overlooked and clever game who's elegance belies it's simplicity.  It's Diablo, made to play like Fallout 3 with perma-death, and has Diablo chasing you down rather than waiting for you at the bottom.  You, the player, are tasked with racing as deep into the dungeon as you can to drink as much radiation-infused booze as possible before dying.
The graphics and effects are all great and run smoothly on my pc.  The voice acting, characters, sound effects, and writing are all extremely good and humorous.  The soundtrack is fantastic, with one of the best original game songs I've heard in ages.
Overall, I'd rate this a 9/10.  I'm really enjoying this title.  FPS dungeon-delving goodness with none of the mess or fuss, sign up.

WASTED is set after the Cold War between the USSR and the United States came to fruition in a barrage of nuclear fire. You play as a waster, one of many foolish enough to travel to the western wastes aka California to acquire the mystical, rare, and extremely irradiated booze. It isn't an easy jog through the park though, as our protagonist must travel deep into the depths of coolers, or vaults meant to house the greatest scientific minds safely until after the nuclear fallout. Sadly, due to the companies that built these bunkers cheaping on materials most of the inhabitants are dead or mutated beyond recognition. In this game you will glady battle other wasters and the mutant products of radiation, all for the ambrosia that is a good scotch.
The gameplay of the game is quite fun and the best way I can describe this game to others is if you mutated Fallout 3 into more of a rougelike instead of an open world exploration game. You have stereotypical quests, shooting baddies in the face, and the rougelike staple of more loot than you know what to do with. Speaking of shooting, the gunplay is more complex than one would think initially. Instead of your usual FPS bullet sponges, these adversaries pack a punch and also get debuffed in shot in a specific part of the body. For example if one shoots an antagonist in the leg, their movement speed will be slowed. If you shoot enemies in their enormously grotesque heads then you have a higher change to get a critical hit. Finally, if you shoot an enemy in the groin, they take a guarenteed +100% critical hit damage. This leads to enjoyable firefights where you must think on your feet to achieve the best end result.
There isn't only gunplay though, there is also melee and explosives. I haven't spent much time using explosives since it doesn't really fit my playstyle but you can expect big booms that do a satisfying amount of damage. The melee is my only real gripe with the combat system. The melee at times feels laggy, especially when you use charged attacks. Another issue I had with melee is because melee weapons are held so close to your characters body in first person view, it is very hard to deiscern what your melee hitbox is.
What is gameplay without good enemy AI though. This game has some of the best AI I have ever had the pleasure of playing against. They use strategy which is first of all astonishing such as hiding when reloading and they actively dodge bullets. Considering this is more of an indie title, I was thoroughly impressed. Sadly nothing can be perfect though. Whether is due to the radiations brain damage or a lack of dangerous object avoidance, but enemies will often walk, or even run, into killer traps such as gun tripwires, bear traps, and toxic waste and will die. I wish that they would be a bit smarter so that I didn't feel like I was cheesing the system by jumping over toxic waste and a group of melee wasters would charge after me and quickly die to the poison. I would be fine if they were knocked back into these environmental hazards, and it would make melee a bit more rewarding of a gameplay style. All in all, this AI still makes for a great Wild West shootout game that is challenging, but is also rewarding such as learning how the different enemy types will react to your presence.
Speaking of presence, the game also has a bare bones stealth system which works for melee and guns. If you are crouched you are considered in stealth form and can critical hit anyone not aware of you. While this is a fun addtion, I found that with a high enough sneak rating on my armor bonuses enemies would sometimes walk right past me when I was crouched but not hiding while other times enemies would spot me across the room, so I'm not quite sure what I'm doing wrong.
The story is enjoyable and silly, but don't think silly to mean childish. The jokes are spot on with their comedic timing and sometimes take a good knowledge of raunchy innuendo to understand complete. With memerable characters which are all fully voice acted I can't help but enjoy what I have played of the story so far.

There are things to like about WASTED. I have a soft spot for first person roguelikes and this game scratches many of those itches. Running through corridors shooting people and creatures with the available guns can be satisfying.
What the game doesn't really prepare you for at all is the fact that you have a very limited time to make it through the stage before a nearly invincible enemy with a minigun that stunlocks you if it hits spawns at the entrance of the level. Stealth seems useless as it always knows where you are and constantly moves towards you.
With the way the game generates its levels this can mean that there can be multiple diverging paths that lead to dead ends, and with the time constraint the ridiculous enemy can basically trap you through no fault of your own. To succeed you need to memorize the limited number of room types so you can go through grabbing everything as quickly as possible on the way to the next floor while hoping that you don't get unlucky and get trapped. It's almost never worthwhile to bother opening the locked doors because they can't lead to the end of the level.
Honestly I think WASTED shows a good amount of potential, but to me it feels more like it should still be in early access. There are a lot of rough edges that could use polishing and more content is never a bad thing. I wouldn't recommend it right now but I can see it becoming worthwhile in the future.
Post beating-game edit (11/2/2016):
After beating the game I can confirm that the content for the game feels anemic. There might be some slight differences in rooms from the first and second cooler, but afterwards those same rooms are pretty much endlessly recycled with only the placement of items/traps/enemies changing. There are pretty much no new guns after the first 3 coolers, and I spent the entire game playing through mainly with the guns that I had picked up in the very first cooler.
Some of the gun categories are disappointing. As far as I played, I only ever found 2 different types of shotgun and maybe 3 different types of revolvers.There are plenty of pistols though a lot of them are very similar, a decent spread of rifles, and a pretty good variety of energy weapons. I picked up some rockets but only found a rocket launcher in the daily seeded run that you can bring an item back from to your main character.
It didn't take me long to get used to just rushing through the levels, after a while I pretty much never saw the ridiculous enemy. It's easier when you realize that there just isn't much there that you don't see past the first or second time you go through the cooler and all the rooms blend together.

Update 6/30/2015
After a patch or two later and playing more I have had a successful online experience, finished story mode, and now I have a few extra things to mention.  The memory leak "seems" fixed for the moment and the game appears to be much more stable.
+ I only did a couple of online bouts and the experience was surprisingly smooth compared to initial release.
+ Living Towers offer a good alternative to the classic arcade tower with a ton of modifiers and challenges along the way.  It still feels a little tedious after a few, but definitely an improvement on the idea.
+ Being able to overlay combos / specials / finishers on the screen while you fight was extermely helpful at times especially in story mode when you are switching characters every few fights.
-  Between mobile and console/PC versions the developer makes too many attempts to reach into my wallet.  It is extremely tacky and distracts from the game.  The focus that was placed on this should have been spent on making the game a better experience, but that would've cost money instead of made it so what motivation did they have.  On day one this was a $30 game at best considering how much money would be made on DLC / microtransactions.  Develeoper greed is definitely out of control at the cost of quality making us quite literally pay more for less.
-  Loss of tag modes... why?  It was so much fun and when I could actually convince someone to play with me locally it kept their interest longer since they could essentially test out two characters in a single match.
-  No stage fatalities which have been a staple of the series throughout and a few of the backgrounds seemed well suited for a good set up.
-  Too few background stages that become repetitive and worn out quickly.
- Story mode, for me, seemed far too short or at least much shorter than MK9.  I was both surprised and a bit disappointed it was over so quickly.  Too many playable characters had a miniscule / meaningless role in the story such as Baraka, Reptile, Jax, Kitana, Kung Lao, etc. - Erron Black and Ferra/Torr were completely disposable and had zero explanation or back story.  Lots of fleshing out could've been done, but this game was clearly rushed out the door.  Major plot events such as Scorpion being released from Quan Chi's power and his humanity restored went by so quick I didn't even notice when it happened.  Suddenly he was human and I was like ... okay, that's cool, but when did that happen?  I had to go back and then noticed it happened when Sub-Zero and Jax were released as well.  If your audience can so easily miss such a pivotal plot point you've not done your job correctly.  And the glowy green power Johnny / Cassie absorb and display prior to giving Shinnok a royal beatdown ... was that ever explained?  Also, the vintage character's overwhelming trust in the new recruits to perform tasks far outside their abilities and confidence level seems horribly naive and misplaced.  And then trusting them to defeat Shinnok seems unbelievable if not utterly ludicrous.  The ending, regardless of how short and full of missteps the ride there ended up being, was satisfying and the potential set up for a sequel was interesting.  Also, I hope Rain becomes a playable character at some point since his fighting style seemed pretty reasonably fleshed out in the story.
-  Speaking of the new recruits, I don't think Neatherealm did nearly enough with them to make them interesting as fighters or for the player to have much if any investment in them in story mode.  Takeda and Kung Jin's move sets were okay, Cassie's was decent, but just felt like regurgitated ideas from Johnny Cage and Sonya which was intentional, and Jacqui Briggs seemed completely uninspired.  As for other new characters D'Vorah was interesting, Erron Black was kinda fun, but Ferra/Torr was just weird and as a fighter did not interest me at all.
-  The new crypt design is a pain in the ***.  It is nearly impossible to follow what you have and have not opened.  It's no wonder they offered the abillity to pay and unlock it all because going through and trying to do it manually, even if you had infinite coins to start with, would be an exercise in frustration.  Whoever designed this needs to be punched in the jeans.
In summation, my review is still negative and I deem its predecesser MK9 a far better overall game that Neatherealm seemed to really pour their heart and soul into so if you don't have it go pick it up.  This game needed a more fleshed out story with less day one DLC and preferably zero microtransactions, less disposable characters, more stages, a more logically designed crypt, and without tag modes and stage fatalities completely missing.

This is one of the best "value for your money" games I've ever bought.
I played the original Mount & Blade, back when it was in beta, and Warband certainly only improved things.
Firstly: The graphics look downright ancient. For a game that is older than Half-Life 2, expect worse graphics, by far, don't let that get to you though, read on instead.
This game dumps you into the intrigue of the war of rule in a land called calradia. There's no magic, and no focus on religion, just politics and war. And you get to do, essentially, whatever you want. Ride around the land, and gather your own company of men; let them evolve into battlehardened veterans that can take out any army, or just gather a horde so great you can overrun anyone, or perhaps you even like to keep your group small and nimble across distances?
It's really up to you how you play that part out. Then there's picking weapons for your character, there are a lot to choose from including throwing weapons like javelins and axes, ranged like crossbow and bow, and almost everything you could possibly imagine for the melee. You can even choose whether to slay enemies, or just knock them out and sell them into slavery.
Finally, you'll choose whether to support a king in their claim for ruling Calradia, or perhaps breakout and make your own attempt at it.
Also: This game runs great on Linux.

Forget Minecraft, this game is everything you love about that blocktastic game, but fixed everything wrong about it.
+ You get a character you can customize (they look like MySims characters), not bad cusomizing options either. More than I expected, at least.
+ You can pick a class which is hella fun. My sister and I play as a Ranger and a Warrior, so I can nab flying things while she tackles ground enemies. Makes for fun teamwork.
+ Combat is super fun. I suggest turning on the option in your settings that turns fights automatically into third person. It's so much easier. I find exploring = first person, fighting = third person to be best.
+ No fall damage! NO FALL DAMAGE. DO YOU HEAR ME. (Except falling off the edge of the world. I've done that so many times. Don't do that.)
+ When you die you lose gold, not items. Which makes it way more appealing to adventure and explore with rare things on you. I don't think they lose durability either.
+ BUT IF THEY DO THEY DON'T BREAK. You can keep that janky stone pickaxe for eternity if you want without fixing it. Broken stuff just works less, but totally still usable. Hella nice!
+ Armour and stuff looks hella freaking cool. Also, dig your hair but want your helmet stats? You can toggle your helmet visibility! Awwyiss aesthetic.
+ Like your armour stats but you hella hate how it looks and wanna wear that sweet♥♥♥♥♥sombrero? There's separate slots for "Armour" and "Vanity". AESTHETIC x2. I LOOK FABULOUS.
+ You can jump up more blocks than you can in Minecraft
+ There's cool freaking portals where you can get other materials and explore more.
+ THERE'S GODDAMN NPCs. WITH QUESTS. OR STUFF TO SELL. Not like ♥♥♥♥♥♥ villagers, I mean they're actually doing something. Some just chat with you or tell you where some♥♥♥♥♥♥is. It's so much fun to find them. Quest rewards are awesome also.
+ WORLD EVENTS. YOU GUESSED IT. I dunno how often they are, but it's really fun. So far I've gotten about one a day and get rare♥♥♥♥♥♥from it.
+ There's so many extra awesome stuff that's just little things to make the game better. You can run with a torch if it's dark and it'll still light up the whole place instead of having to set them down everywhere. You can still set them down, but sometimes it's super easy to just have someone running beside you holding one while you fight.
+ Also it still has the same blocky look, just smooth and not 'gritty' (?) looking. The colours are really saturated which in my opinion just makes it so much more pretty and appealing. It's like a texture pack already installed!
- The only thing I wish they would fix, is maybe letting people change their look (face, hair, etc.) later in case they don't like it? I don't know if I'm just missing that option or haven't found it yet. If so, my bad! Ignore this.
- When you go through portals to other worlds, it takes EVERYONE with you. You all always have to be in the same world. So ask people if they're done what they're doing first before you run through a portal to go get that copper you wanted. I'd love to be able to stay back and build the home base while people go hunt for items in other worlds, but alas I cannot. Hopefully in the future!
But seriously. TLDR; if you like Minecraft, ♥♥♥♥ that game. This game is everything but better.

Pros:
I really enjoyed playing Figment. The idea of making the mind a world where the various emotions, quirks, fears etc. are portrayed as characters or the scenery, is great in my opinion! If you enjoy quirky music, beautiful illustrations, humorous dialogue, heartfelt moments, puzzle solving, and insightful thoughts, then I would definitely recommend this little gem of a game to you.
Playthrough will take somewhere between 5-8 hours, dependent on how quickly you solve the puzzles and whether you hunt for the Remembranes - memories of the person whose mind we are introduced to in Figment.
It might not be the longest game in the world, but it is definitely memorable for what it is and is worth filling a weekend afternoon with.
Cons:
I have to note that I did run into some problems with the game, where during my first attempt at playing, I ended up facing a bug that stopped me from continuing the game. Since the game works on autosaves and you can only return to your last saved location, then that meant I had to start over again.
A couple of hours later, I ran into a similar issue in another place and couldn't progress. Gave up for the night and discovered the next morning that the game itself had vanished from my PC and I was unable to reinstall Figment. After some digging around in Steam's Support topics and cleaning the download cache, I was able to once again install the game. Started playing again and was finally able to do a complete playthrough without any other glitches or bugs.

You play as Dusty, a cynical, slightly grumpy character with funny ears who is never much impressed by anything and is always keen to skip the nonsense and get on with his quest. He's accompanied by his female sidekick Piper, a colourful bird of some kind, always cheery and optimistic, following Dusty around and offering advice but never actually doing anything.
Our intrepid duo journey through various towns chasing the Nightmares from one place to another and occasionally doing battle with them. The Figment world is chock full with all manner of interesting characters and puzzles. The world overview has a distinct Dr Seuss quality to it, with whimsical objects leaning at funny angles and curly things galore.
In each area you usually have to find items to use on other items to make them work, and unlock the path to the next area. Fairly standard stuff. There are a lot of handles to be fitted to windmill operators to turn them in the right direction to blow the cloud blockages out of the way, and colour-coded batteries to be discovered and fitted to the mechanisms to make them blow. As you progress the puzzling becomes slightly more complex and you have to fight off spiders, sewer rats, snakey things and other miscellaneous monsters now and then.
There are many houses where anonymous characters live. If you knock on their doors they all have quirky comments to make in a multitude of voices and accents, often bemoaning the latest happenings in their town brought by the Nightmares. None of them ever open their doors but the voices alone really bring life to the whole environment.
The artwork is colourful and imaginative, there's always something fresh to enjoy, but for me what makes the game really stand out is the music and voice acting. There's a wide variety of original music throughout the game, and none of your synthesised garbage either, it's proper brass, drums, guitar and ukelele. The instruments within the game emit the music as you pass, so for example you have a guitar bush and the music gets louder and softer as you pass. The instruments are like the local vegetation, growing wild. You can give them a whack with your sword and they'll produce little bursts of sound. Brilliant! Sometimes I would hang around in an area just to listen to the music for a bit longer, it really is that good. The final boss deserves a special mention though, that song is so awesome, if someone told me it was the latest Metallica release I wouldn't be surprised!
I don't know how many voice actors were used in this game, but it seems like a lot of them. The variety and quality is staggering. Each vividly-drawn character has its own unique voice, making them all so memorable, like in a big budget cartoon movie. The main characters, not content with just having great voices, use rhyming poetry when they talk. There were definitely some professional musicians and poets involved in the development of this game, not just programmers.
If you're looking for a tough challenge you might want to give this a miss. The puzzles are interesting and keep you busy, but they couldn't be described as difficult by any stretch. You may get held up a little now and then but you won't be needing an online guide for this one. It's about the adventure, storyline and enjoyment of the environment rather than the challenge. There is combat and you will die now and then, but you respawn and try again, and after a few attempts you'll succeed.
Most of the latter achievements are for finding all the houses and special items in all the areas. I've completed the game and then gone back to have a look for the ones I missed and I must say some of them are well hidden because I haven't found them yet, so there's some challenge for you if you need it.
All items present and correct: Achievements - half of them for normal progression, half for post-completion searching for more obscure items; Trading Cards (x7); fully cross-platform and Cloud Sync for us dual-booters.
There's about 8 hours worth for a normal playthrough, plus extra for completion. It's not the longest game ever, but the quality packed into it makes it well worth full price in my opinion. I loved every minute of it.
Sometimes games in this genre become a chore for me towards the end and I have to force myself to continue. This one kept me glued to the screen from start to finish. There's so much great content packed into it that it's constantly fresh and you want to discover the next wonderful puzzle, tune or character in the story.
The only small thing I would mention is that it would be suitable for family consumption if not for the occasional bloody buggers and ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥s.

Full review:
What a beautiful little puzzle-adventure this game was. Figment is definitely one of the better-looking games released recently, with the art and music creating this wonderful atmosphere that I found myself easily immersed in.
Pros:
Absolutely beautiful art style and music. Figment is a beautiful game. Both the art and the music are top-notch. The backgrounds, levels, characters, everything is just designed so well. The music matched this outstanding quality as well. In fact, the bosses would actually sing while in battle, which sounds dumb, but was actually rather refreshing and really fit with the game’s atmosphere. There were numerous little things that would just bring a smile to my face, such as the dialogue from certain residents or the fact that the flora (in the shape of instruments) actually plays music when interacted with. All of this made Figment a fun, immersive experience.
Great puzzle and level design. Figment’s puzzles were pretty well designed throughout. In general, they were not too difficult to complete, steadily increasing in difficulty over the course of the game, with only a few towards the end taking any significant effort to complete. This lends well to the game’s aesthetic, maintaining the immersion while still being fun to complete. The levels are equally well designed, maintaining a mostly linear path, yet leaving just enough room to explore and find all of the little extras scattered throughout the game’s world. There are collectibles to find, residents to meet, and a entire world to be immersed into. Overall, the level and puzzle design meshed quite well with the game’s aesthetic and really helped to better the experience.
Cons:
Movement can be awkward at times. I ran into some minor issues with the game’s movement. I would sometimes get teleported back when rolling through tight corners or up staircases and there were also numerous instances in which it looks like I should be able to move across something, but was not able to. This mostly was due to how the game is played, or rather the perspective that the game is played at. Many of the bridges, stairs, etc. have tight invisible walls surrounding them, forcing me to realign myself in order to cross. This is very noticeable when crossing certain bridges. Although it did not inhibit gameplay, it was rather annoying at times.
Long loading times. Figment has several loading screens, all in-between each level. Normally this would not be a problem, but these loading screens can last quite some time. While recording my playthrough of this game, I mentioned the long loading screens several times, with the longest one lasting 18 seconds. I did not have the game installed on an SSD, but I do have Skyrim installed on the same drive and the loading times there definitely do not last anywhere near 18 seconds (not even 10!). This is especially annoying when having to traverse through multiple levels just to get somewhere. Missed a secret in an earlier level? Have fun backtracking through all those loading screens.
Overall, Figment really is a good game with a beautifully drawn world and a great soundtrack to go with it. The puzzle and level design was solid throughout, even if said levels are separated by such long loading screens. The movement may be awkward at times and may take some time to get used to, but it is worth it.

It's just about 3 hours long, maybe 4 if you decide to stop and smell the roses once in a while, and it's one of the most focused, coherent narratives told in gaming. Its story is old and has been told before, but Brothers tells it well. Its gameplay mechanics add to the story in subtle, yet deeply satisfying ways.
You control two brothers who are on a quest to retrieve medicine from a tree nestled far from home, before their father dies of an illness. Using both brothers at once, you will guide them through puzzles, dangerous enemies and uncertain situations. The game is best played on a controller - on a pad, the right stick + trigger control the younger brother, and the left stick + trigger control the older brother. The younger brother can't always do what the older brother can, and vice versa - big brother can swim, but little brother has to hold on to bro while they cross the stream.
It's well worth whatever price you can snag it for.

I don't care who you are. I don't care what kind of games you usually play. Drop everything you're doing, pony up whatever Steam is charging this week, and play through "Brothers." It'll take you 4 hours tops, and it's worth every second.
I have rarely encountered a game that is so close to perfect, by which I mean it integrates story, mechanics, graphics, and overall execution to create something that is far greater than the sum of its parts. Don't let the bright and cheery aesthetic fool you: "Brothers" will drag you to some dark places, and boomerangs from fun, engaging puzzles and sumptuous visuals to deeply distressing scenarios with a willful abandon. "Brothers" is a story about family, dedication, and mortality, and it succeeds magnificently at just about everything it sets out to do. If you're looking for a solid puzzle platformer that'll punch you squarely in the feels (and maybe even freak you out a little), this is not to be missed.
I was incredibly impressed by how thoughtfully the gameplay mechanics themselves were integrated into the storyline, and how much weight they ultimately had on the relationship between the two brothers. The gameplay forces each brother to rely on the other, which is not just inventive and rewarding to play, but actually adds a huge amount to the game's emotional impact. I've never played anything that used mechanics to enhance a story so clearly, and without being heavy-handed or gimmicky--my hat's off to the developers in that regard.
The other aspect of "Brothers" that I loved was the fact that the puzzles were all super intuitive. I'm sure there are many reviewers out there who'd rather have a game that was far more challenging, but nothing frustrates me more than trying to beat a puzzle and having no clue what my next step should be. The puzzles in "Brothers" are all fun and satisfying to figure out, which I appreciate. It's important to keep in mind, as well, that the point of this game is to tell a story, not break your brain, so I feel the difficulty level of the puzzles is warranted.
Spoilers and more nit-picky critique follow, so I'd suggest reading on only AFTER beating the game.
As I was playing this on a PC without a controller, I found that my biggest gripe with the game was how difficult the keyboard controls could sometimes be. While I didn't have too much trouble with the controls, a few of the game's most charming sequences (the goat riding and the hang glider come to mind) were spoiled by how awkward the controls were. There's an easy fix: make the "grab" mechanic click-hold click-release, instead of having to hold it down and simultaneously manipulate two characters. Here's to hoping the devs revamp the controls at some point in the future.
My other HUGE gripe is with the game's story (spoilers for the end of the game follow). I get that this is a story about two brothers, but did they really have to rely on the tired old "bros before hos" trope for the story's climax? It's boring, it's been done, and it's pretty misogynistic sterotype to play into. C'mon writers, for a story with so much nuance and heart, did you literally have to kill Older Brother with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ "Black Widow" trope? This game deserved so much better.
Even with those critiques, though, "Brothers" is an outstanding game, and one I'd highly recommend.

NOTE: This is the same review for the other two games in the original Deponia trillogy aswell. I thought that as they are a continuation of the same story that they should stay together.
The
trillogy is a classic point and click game on a wold filled with garbage. In the trillogy, you assist the, at first forgettable/dislikeable, protagonist Rufus try to reach the floating paradise of Elysium. Over time, the originally forgettable Rufus uses his witty dialog to slowly get you on his side rooting for him on his quest.
+Amazing story
The story, although only really played out during cut scenes to new areas, is deep in detail. It pulls you in, really pulling you into the world.
+Funny
Not many games have blaitently funny dialog, but these games definatly do. Rufus has funny responses to other characters, his own acvtions, and stuff you try to have him do.
+Characters
All the characters seem fleshed out quite well. Each has a uniques personallity, displayes different emotions, and just act different. The variety is also pretty good.
+Enviroments
Most enviroments are well detailed with other people and objects to bring the scene alive. In some cases, youll get people who are from other games showing up in the envirments aswell.
+Music
The music worked well with each area you would be exploring. Although mostly being simmilar themed, it all was different and interesting.
-Animations/Movement
The walking animation on Rufus, for me was a bit weird. He didnt really face where he was going and took odd paths to where he needed to go.
-Duration
Some areas seemed too short, while others were too long. It was an odd thing and may have just been the way I solved the puzzles in each area, but it struck me as odd how I could clear one area in ~30 min and another in 2+ hours.
The
trillogy is an amazing set of games that brought back tthe nastolga of point and the point and click style. The quirky dialog was fun to hear and laugh at resonces. The story makes the narcissistic Rufus someone whos actions have you rooting
for the duration of his adventure. If you have some time free I can highly reccomend all the games in the
trillogy and
.

What can you say about Mortal Kombat X?  It's a Mortal Kombat game not unlike every other release on PC, but, and it's a big but, It's no longer supported on the PC platform.  From day 1 it was a poor release, that's somewhat understandable as it's the norm these days to release games before they are ready.  However, Netherrealms really never lived up to fixing the largest flaws the PC port had.  Multiplayer support was weak at best.  The game lacks even a decent level of optimizations for the PC.  Personally I have never cared for online gameplay, I much rather have a friend sitting right next to me playing the same game.  Regardless, it has issues on the PC but it's not a game killer.  The game is actually pretty fun.  The story mode is ho-hum, pretty short, not terribly difficult.  You could probably finish it in about 7 hours.  Clearly a game like this has a nice level of replay-ability.  But that being said, multiplayer will clearly die out and with support being dropped as of January 2015 anything that is not single player will most likely be unplayable before too long.  Overall, while I've had fun playing this game, it comes off as nothing more than a cash grab release from WB and Netherrealms.  It is what it is, and since they've cut support for PC less than 1 year from it's initial release I have a feeling this will be something that haunts those companies for the years to come.
Would I recommend this game, probably not.  Mortal Kombat 9 has more than enough to offer and at a much more decent price.  If you are interested in this game I wouldn't say don't get it, just wait until it's less than $10 because that's about all it's worth.

6/10 - Definitely worse than MK9. Despite nice graphics and more brutal X-Rays and fatalities (and brutalities <3) this seems like a step backward from the point that Mortal Kombat (MK9) defined.
Yes, there is more interaction with stage itself (as in Injustice) but there are no stage fatalities.
There is less warriors (yes, there are various styles but some of them are too weak and some are OP. Additionally there are too many members of Cage/Brigs family). On the plus side however some new/returning heroes are great (D'Vorah, Ferra/Torr. Erron Black or Takeda). Sad thing is that there are some warriors like Barraka, Shindel or Rain that are in the game but are not available in other modes (they are probably comming as DLC).
Storymode seems like a joke in comparison to its predecessor. Its shorter (only 4h long) and really boring. There is nothing that makes you want to know whats going to happen next. Quan-Chi and Shinok seem very week (in comparison to Shao Khan from MK9). New "youngsters" seem boring and
feels just sad).  Id say that only scorpion and sub-zero part was interesting. I was also wondering why can't we get story which would focus on "bad" characters and let us play as Ermac, Reptile in story-mode?
Another sad part is PC port... and this is what I hate about modern gaming. Developers are releasing unfinished games. We have 3rd of may today. Game is out for over two weeks and it still has some serious issues (fps drops on good rigs - for me its visible on Sky Temple, bad Netcode and memory leaks). I hope that this will be fixed soon.
Do I recommend this game? I have mixed feelings. If devs will fix these serious issues then it will be a very solid title, however there are still things that are worse than they were in MK9. I'd say - play MK9 for now (if you have it - if you dont then get it!), wait till MKX is fixed and released with more warriors (possibly longer story) in GOTY edition.
P.S - I'd love if devs would make more X-Rays that correspond to characters playstyle. Currently each playstyle has the same animation.

Im not gonna write a review on the story or series. I enjoy watching RWBY & basing a game on its universe is a great idea, we could all see that, I want to talk more engine and build quality. Now this is written 2nd December 2015 a day after release on Early Access. so expect alot to change in the game.
The game is a basic 4 player co-op hack and slasher with a simple bold colour scheem based off the western anime (it is anime, anime is a style of art not animation from Japan you racists). The game plays along the same lines of Left4Dead crossed with Dynasty Warriors with players choosing a short campaign made up of several areas & killing masses of grimm in each area.
Im running the game on a mid range laptop simular to what the masses would be using, and i'm aware that an i7 is advised. But I feel that the engine should be better utilised to include lower processors. I had complete frame loss when 20+ grimm spawned in the area which with the games simple design beggers the question what drains the processors so badly.
A simple fix to this would be to allow (or include) more graphics & refresh rate settings, just so players could better setup for there systems. Also more volume options would help. Combat is very loud & it completely covers the musical score, which has always been one of the franchies strongest points, & voice acting from the RT crew.
Speaking of combat the moves and combos are very basic right now, its also very simular across all 4 charaters. Each member of team RWBY has 3 bonus attacks each which to be honest felt underpowered, even with any leveling bonuses. In fact it felt like none of the additional buffs & perks really did anything. But these only got used in the mist of combat when the frame rate was suffering badly, so maybe I missed any real effect on screen.
To be fully honest the games needs alot of work, we know that it's why it's called Early Access, but it does show alot of promise. I would advise spending any earned resorces on dev of the engine. Get it to span more varaity of machines & make it more stable. Also look into introducing more setup options so users can adjust to fit their build.
Once done then look into including more campaigns, charaters, weapons or even a make your own team mode (a build your own team with loads of customisation options, hell you could introduce cosmetic paid dlc down the way to continue funding the titles developement). But please only start adding stuff when the build is solid.
If your a fan of RWBY you've already brought the game, but if you have no interest in the show but after a solid hack & slash FOR NOW look at other titles. BUT keep an eye on the updates page as features get added & the build gets better. Jump in when you belive the title holds up for you.

I had some issues with stuttering in this game when I first upgraded my computer. It was running at 120-140 fps at all times, but had issues with freezing fully for half a second or so 15-20 times a minute.
My specs:
Overclocked GTX 1060
8gb ddr4 @2400mhz
i5-7600k
700w PSU
(windows 10 also too as well)
If you have a setup like mine you will probably face these same issues. I was able to find a fix however. Using MSI Afterburner and RivaTuner I locked my framerate to 60. Then I disabled the in game V-Sync, and forced V-Sync on inside of the NVIDIA control panel. This stopped my stuttering issues, and the game now runs perfectly.

I have to give it a 'no' for a review because there are a few aspect that totally killed it for me - and not in a good way.
1) If you spend too much time in the cooler a hunter comes with crazy high HP and a rapid firing gun and basically insta kills you. This wouldn't be quite so bad if it weren't for #2.
2) When you die, your character isn't regenerated back at a safe point minus their gear or anything, a completely new character is randomly generated and put into it's place.
That did it for me, I can handle dying and repeating a level until I beat it, even if it involves a stupidly hard boss fight, but I HATE that it wipes your character, what is the point of customizing your character's features and name if it's just going to be replaced anyways?
If these things were changed, I would recomend it, but for now, it's not worth the frustration.

Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is a story about love, family, and courage. It is a visual masterpiece. This, for me, is the best example of a visual novel. Playing the game was like reading a book without words. Have you ever felt like you were in the book you are reading-- that you were in the story itself-- playing this game is like that.
---
The visual art is like a painting. You do not need mods to beautify the environment or your screenshots, it is a masterpiece in itself. The story and lore is loveable. The puzzles are well thought of.
Controls are a bit hard or challenging, especially if you're using the keyboard as in my case-- it sometimes gets frustrating because you are controlling two characters at once. It's also hard to take screenshots especially in interactions because I think Steam prevents the user from pressing to many buttons at once.
Although the game is short, linear, and that there is little replayability (except maybe twice or thrice or until you complete the achievements), I personally recommend that you get and play this game yourself.

6/10 - Definitely worse than MK9. Despite nice graphics and more brutal X-Rays and fatalities (and brutalities <3) this seems like a step backward from the point that Mortal Kombat (MK9) defined.
Yes, there is more interaction with stage itself (as in Injustice) but there are no stage fatalities.
There is less warriors (yes, there are various styles but some of them are too weak and some are OP. Additionally there are too many members of Cage/Brigs family). On the plus side however some new/returning heroes are great (D'Vorah, Ferra/Torr. Erron Black or Takeda). Sad thing is that there are some warriors like Barraka, Shindel or Rain that are in the game but are not available in other modes (they are probably comming as DLC).
Storymode seems like a joke in comparison to its predecessor. Its shorter (only 4h long) and really boring. There is nothing that makes you want to know whats going to happen next. Quan-Chi and Shinok seem very week (in comparison to Shao Khan from MK9). New "youngsters" seem boring and
feels just sad).  Id say that only scorpion and sub-zero part was interesting. I was also wondering why can't we get story which would focus on "bad" characters and let us play as Ermac, Reptile in story-mode?
Another sad part is PC port... and this is what I hate about modern gaming. Developers are releasing unfinished games. We have 3rd of may today. Game is out for over two weeks and it still has some serious issues (fps drops on good rigs - for me its visible on Sky Temple, bad Netcode and memory leaks). I hope that this will be fixed soon.
Do I recommend this game? I have mixed feelings. If devs will fix these serious issues then it will be a very solid title, however there are still things that are worse than they were in MK9. I'd say - play MK9 for now (if you have it - if you dont then get it!), wait till MKX is fixed and released with more warriors (possibly longer story) in GOTY edition.
P.S - I'd love if devs would make more X-Rays that correspond to characters playstyle. Currently each playstyle has the same animation.

Remember people this is Early Access, so the game isn't finished, so don't go judging it on lack of stuff because it's not all there.
So after seeing this advertised for finally going to Early Access, I thought I'd give it a go, I don't usually buy early access games, but I love RWBY so much I thought I'd give the game a go. After following this game every now and again I have to say that I was fairly impressed with the state of the game (for Early Access), now there are bugs here and there and certain wall textures were missing (Mainly on Mt Glenn in the boss arena) but overall there isn't anything game breaking, which is more than can be said for most Early Access titles. The graphics are very nice and fit well with the style of RWBY, I had a look at Ruby's face (The character I played throughout the levels) and it looked very well done and looked almost exactly like the shows version.
The animations (mainly running animations) aren't the best however, possibly because they may placeholder animationswhile they work on the actual animations or whatever, the movement is the main problem, but the fighting animations are much better, I felt pretty awesome as I pulled off Ruby's charged Reap attack as I span the Crescent Rose slicing enemies as I went, it felt all very satisfying watching at and actually doing it. The enemies animations look ok but there's nothing to scream about and for Early Access, it looks ok.
The amount you're getting for £11 (I don't know the dollars amount for the game) isn't that great in my opinion, if you're buying it to help the development, that's fine, however I feel at this stage the game itself with all that's available doesn't feel like £11. The characters do feel similar, I feel Yang should have more heavier attacks, but she feels very similar in speed to the others, and there are only 4 levels (for the time being) although there will be more down the line obviously. There are no cutscenes in the game (yet) however there is dialogue fully voiced by the voice actors and not all the sound has been put in yet.
That all being said I still enjoyed the game, it's not done, yes, but I had fun slicing, punching and shooting through Grimm, there were always new types of Grimm being introduced each level which added a new layer of play and looking around and seeing the world of Remnant was a feeling that I have wanted to experience for a while. People who're complaining about Customisation are obviously either not seeing this as an Early access game and only made by 4 people or are expecting too much from a game that isn't really about that. I throughly enjoyed my time playing this game and am excited to see the finished product. I'd recommend it for anyone looking for an RWBY game or just to hack and slash their way through enemies as each member of RWBY. I'd love to see more characters being playable down the line as DLC or content patches but in it's current state it's an enjoyable, fun and well done game.
Overall rating 7/10
Recommend (Early Access Version): Yes

I'd like to start by saying that I only recommend the game, as it is now, to die hard fans and people looking to test it. As a fan, I absolutely love it. The visuals are great, the animations are amazing, and the entire game looks like it came right out of RWBY itself. The voice actors are as is in the show: Lindsey voices Ruby, Barbara voices Yang, etc. Honestly, to me, it felt like I was in RWBY.
Now, if you are not a fan of the show and looking for a fun game, come back when the game is more developed. Right now, it is only worth the $15 price tag to those who love the show. The story is OK but a bit confusing and not to far along. Took me about an hour and a half to beat the story so far with two characters, the long time mostly due to people quitting in the middle. The combat is still pretty basic, and the ranged attacks are incredibly difficult to aim. Your normal melee attack will be your main source of damage and you'll most likely be mashing that button into oblivion. There is also no tutorial or menu to show keybindings, so you're going to have to figure it out on your own. The special attacks are cool, and make sense with the character, but you aren't going to need to rely on them to often. The music is pretty quiet and can be hard to impossible to hear, along with the lines from your character. The upgrade sytstem is very limited in what you can do. Either you upgrade your special attacks or increase your Special bar or health, but it's a linear path for the Special upgrades. More of a variety would be nice. There are also these boxes around that you can break to find objects that give you experience, and I found a few that, once broken, lock the object behind an invisible wall, keeping you from getting it.
Right now, that is all I have noticed during the game. I got a lot of lag problems, but I'm going to chalk that up as computer issues, not game issues. Overall, it is a promising game, and I am excited to see what Roosterteeth improves on. If you love the RWBY series, want to seem like you're in Remnant, and have $15 to spare, I say get the game and help Roosterteeth improve it. If not, wait a while but keep your eyes on the game. I can see it being a very good, well put together game in the future.

To start, I normally don't play primarily single player games.
NOTE: The game is advertised as 'multiplayer', however you do need Steam friends (Which I don't have any :( ) to play Multiplayer, OR you can play on LAN.
Pros:
-Visually Stunning
The bloom effect is a very nice touch, I love the character modeling, I like the variety of gear.
-Tutorial
The tutorial is laid out very simply, and if you could imagine the controls of your standard MMORPG smacked with Minecraft, Portal Knights is the result (NOT hard to understand at all!)
-Character and Game Progression
This is both a Pro and a Con, I'll touch more on the Con of this later; I enjoy the simplicity of the overall character building and also how clear the objective is.
-Dainty Maps
By this I mean the maps do have a lot to explore, however they are just perfectly sized to where you can explore each individual map in a timely fashion while also taking in the visuals around you.
-Variety
Each area you are faced with has really stunning visuals with themed blocks that fit that specific biome. Unlike Minecraft (I use Minecraft because it's something we can all relate to), where you can leave one biome and enter another, in Portal Knights, you take a portal and enter a new island with a biome/theme.
-Combat
HONESTLY, going into this I thought I'd hate the combat, yes it does involve a lot of clicking, however each monster has its own little special ability (Yes, sometimes they hurt, a lot) and you can dodge/roll with your character in attempt to avoid their attacks; after awhile it gets really fun to engage a few monsters at once.
-STUNNING VISUALS
I really have to say it again, this game IS FREAKING BEAUTIFUL, and honestly it doesn't lagg, at all, the framerate is GREAT, and the game looks ohh so divine, I just want to eat the berries right off of the bushes.
-Building
The building system is great, there's a huge variety of blocks offered to build with and you can really design your house how you want, and you can even set an island as your home and get back to it any time (And use it as a base of operations). I look forward to building more in the future, and I hope they add more ores/block types.
-Villages/Doodads
This really goes hand in hand with the visuals, but there's little dungeons scattered around above and underground that you can go into and get loot or find rare ores/items, you can also harvest blocks to add to your house.
-Crafting
The crafting system is actually pretty straightforward, it's really simple to discard items, and the material requirements are laid out really easily, and crafting an item is as simple as the click of a button, it's also really visually appealing as well.
These are a few things of many that this game will offer you, I highly recommend it and it's completely worth your dime, as well as your time.
Cons:
Honestly I'm really grasping for straws here to think of anything really negative that I would have to say. It's HARD with this game, I really have thoroughly enjoyed my time playing it.
-Character/Game Progression
As stated above in the Pros segment, I'd touch on the Cons a little down here. My only (Very small) complaint is that the gameplay can get a tad repetative and grindy, however I stand by the fact that the game enables you to create your own adventure, and there's plenty to do, so it really isn't too bad.
-Ore Variety
I would like to see a little more variety in ores, there's plenty as-is, but you can never really have enough in my opinion, so this is something I'd like to see personally. It's not really a con, either, just a suggestion.
-Actual Online Multiplayer
This isn't really a big issue, but I'd really love a server finder option to make it easier. I don't necessarily mind visiting forums or online communities to find people, but it really is more of a hassle to do it that way, many people including myself prefer to have a server finder within arms reach, by arms reach I mean 'just click here, click the server you want, click join'. I totally understand WHY they haven't implemented this, because I know it's supposed to be more of a social thing; but I think it would really benefit the developers to reconsider this, by adding a server finder or allowing individuals to easily host an online server for random people to join, this allows people to network and find friends even easier than how you currently are doing this. I would also recommend allowing people the ability to password lock servers, in case they just want to allow certain people to join. This really is my one and only true complaint that I do have, really everything else is pretty great, and unless you hate RPG games, and you hate Minecraft, you'll really love Portal Knights.

Spelunky is one of the few games I own that I had never heard of before watching the trailer on steam.  The combination of game footage and story telling evoked distant memories of playing Nethack.  An amalgamation of the roguelike and platformer genres? Yes please.
It certainly delivers everything the trailer promises.  Spelunky is a whole lot of fun, though I can imagine some people may take issue with the difficulty level.  It is challenging, but it is very fair.  When you die it is fairly easy to figure out what went wrong.  The controls are very responsive and when you die it is almost always due to a clearly avoidable mistake.  I played through on an Xbox One controller and I loved the controller support.
Much like many roguelikes, the dungeon in Spelunky is procedurally generated.  You could easily spend hundreds of hours playing and mastering the game.  Although I moved on to other games after winning, it is something I can see myself revisiting.  This game is definitely something fans of challenging platformers and roguelikes will appreciate.

Perfect game.
I enjoyed every minute of this. I was drawn into the world and the story completely while I played. I felt like I was on an epic adventure, and I was truly invested into the 3 main characters. Now that I'm finished I can appreciate things in finer detail.
Gameplay is certainly unique, but that's not the main take-away here. I think -everything- comes together to make a truly memorable experience.
The unique gameplay mechanic (driving both brothers with one controller) is certainly notable and memorable by itself, and something else will use this mechanic in the future and I'll think of this game. But that doesn't give the full picture. The atmosphere created by the design and the music and the story all- is a new benchmark for me. I'm sure I'll think of it often.
You can run through this world, taking the shortest path to your goal, and enjoy yourself thoroughly I think. But you don't have to. Despite the epic adventure vibe, you're not at all rushed, and you can stop to smell the roses of this wonderful environment (and you get an achievement for doing so). There are other characters in the world that you pass in your travels, and you can often play some part in their lives. Looking at the achievments screen now that I'm done reveals that I missed some of this myself, but I don't feel like I missed anything really.
I was emotionally spent after completing this game. I took a lot from the experience and that might stick with me longest. As an experience, I think it rates with the best movies I've ever seen. I don't usually get this quality from games, and that probably intensified it for me, but it's excellent to be sure. I took some minutes to bask in it after I was done.
It's not a difficult game, although the very first time you come across a new puzzle aspect (particularly at the start of the game) you will be confused until you get it, I think that as a whole, that aspect was good for the game. It doesn't take long to pick up really.
Find some quiet hours and throw yourself into this game completely and you ought to get twice as much out of it.

Wasted is an analog of Fallout 3 Vault gameplay with some open-air rpg elements.  The look of the game is lifted straight from FO3 + big bobbleheads.  The gameplay is exactly like FO3 with its shooting/looting.  The humor is lighthearted which fits the artstyle.  And as a randomly generated experience using ready-made prefabs, it's also got some unique and controversial elements.
I'm a fairly big completist and I think the systems are fine as is.  The game is paused in inventory.  You don't need every piece of junk in there and more to the point you don't have room for it.  Just loot fast and get out.  The SOB purifier is also not an issue with the quest reward you get early on provided you save up the ammo.  All the tools for success are there, it's about building up the courage to stand your ground and fight really.  So basically it comes down to changing the playstyle to fit the game - a staple of any hardcore roughlike/soulslike titles.
I like this game a lot.  The price is on the low end for games of this type, the fact that it's stylish and humorous is a priceless bonus.

I dont reccomend using pistols/shotguns to kill him, unless they are throwaways that you've picked up off other enemies on the floor and you just use the ammunition thats left over in the clip/magazine.
All In all this is a great game, Its got many mechanics that remind me of the fallout series, and it doesnt cost nearly as much. Its great fun watching yourself as a player improve and learn the different strengths and weaknesses of various builds and strategies.

Before the most recent update, SNOW was a phenomenal game (considering it was in the alpha stage of its release). It was a unique experience that invited exploration in a one-of-a-kind free roam skiing/snowboarding game. The graphics and physics of the game were a little questionable, but it was an overall enjoyable experience that kept bringing me back to it.
Then, the beta was released.
In the beta version, they added ski passes. They wanted to find a way to drain as much money out of their players as possible, and placed a time limit on how much they could have access to any given mountain other than the tutorial. Before, we could find ourselves searching the deep corners of Sialia or trying our best on Suzuki Nine Knights, but now we have resorted to trying to get up that slide at the bottom of the tutorial. (Or at least I have)
If SNOW wants to succeed, they should highly consider removing the ski passes and making the game back to its charm of being a free-to-play explorer that changed the way many people felt about skiing games. If this isn't possible, they could maybe change it so there is instead a standalone price to purchase the game beforehand, rather than forcing people to gain currency to spend 24 hours in one place.
I hope this suggestion helps you choose whether or not you shall want to play SNOW.

Mount & Blade: Warband is without a doubt one of the best RPGs ever made if not the best. This game should honestly not be as good as it is. The graphics are ugly and the animations are strange and stiff yet it owns it. What do you do in this game you might ask? Anything. What do you mean by anything you may ask? ANYTHING! Do you want to be an infamous raider who enslaves villagers and sells them into slavery? You can. Do you want to be a merchant who travels from one place to another selling goods in an everchanging amazing economy system? You can. Do you want to be a King who destroys all other competetion and controls everything? You can. This game's freedom is what makes it truely amazing. This game's lack of story is it's story. Every playthrough is like an entirely different game, not one playthrough or experience will be the same. The combat is great, the mix between action and strategy is genius, the economy system is realistic and can be changed and influenced dynamically by the player or NPCs, the character creation is great. This game is truely a treat for any RPG fan, especially those who love to roleplay and immerse themselves into a world. You can be anything and do anything. And with the abundance of mods for this game that is especially true. Conversion mods such as the Lord of The Rings ones, Game of Thrones, Warhammer. Even people with a new and original world such as Perisno and Pendor are all great. And the game's expansions are amazing, Viking Conquest adding a new humongous map that takes place in our world during the Viking age, Viking Conquest adds so much and is an impressive and great expansion. Napoleonic Wars adding a new multiplayer module that is extremely fun and expansive. This game is a must have for any RPG fan or any gamer in general, get it now.

I had some issues with stuttering in this game when I first upgraded my computer. It was running at 120-140 fps at all times, but had issues with freezing fully for half a second or so 15-20 times a minute.
My specs:
Overclocked GTX 1060
8gb ddr4 @2400mhz
i5-7600k
700w PSU
(windows 10 also too as well)
If you have a setup like mine you will probably face these same issues. I was able to find a fix however. Using MSI Afterburner and RivaTuner I locked my framerate to 60. Then I disabled the in game V-Sync, and forced V-Sync on inside of the NVIDIA control panel. This stopped my stuttering issues, and the game now runs perfectly.

I went in not expecting to like the game at all. The style is just not my cup of tea. It's online only? Yuck.
My expectations were wiped away almost immediately.
There was virtually no wait to get into a match that already had 3 others in it and playing with other people was not the pain it can be in other games. I had no connection issues. When someone dropped out, a replacement was added almost immediately. I ended up playing through the existing game twice. The first time round, a beta veteran showed us some tricks and in the second I passed them on. I know this community will be good for that in the future. My only complaint was that when downed, players are often abandoned (more later).
I'm still not a big fan of the game style, but unlike in any other Dynasty Warriors-type game, I actually enjoyed it. In other words, way better than expected. The combat was simple enough to figure out without any tutorial, and though I'm pretty awful, someone good would probably be able to do complex and amazing things.
I played as Ruby and Weiss. Both characters have very unique styles and definitely require different approaches. Given how well I scored compared to the others (we had the whole team!) I think Weiss may be a bit OP, even is she struggles with crowds as compared to Ruby. I felt like Ruby's projectile attacks were a bit lacking but the melee combat was powerful and downright fun to see.
Combat could be a bit repetitive but the variation in enemies added some flavor. For most of it, the objectives were a bit bland but at the end there was an interesting set-piece (I won't spoil it). If I had to describe the combat simply, I'd call it beautiful chaos.
Now for the issues.
I don't think the game is very well optimized. It might just be my comp, but I was getting some stuttering during particularly chaotic encounters. My system plays Far Cry 4 on High with no problems, so I'd surmise the issue is with the game. It's something I've seen from a few small developers so I'm not too surprised or disappointed.
I feel like the special system needs some balancing. At times it's almost automatic to fill up the meter and max out the charges. At others it can be nearly impossible. That wouldn't be so bad but in difficult situations where getting specials is difficult, they don't have the punch to really reward you for your hard work. If they were easier to get or more powerful once you did, it would be fine. Maybe I just suck though.
I wasn't really a fan of the revival system either. It takes a very long time to revive a downed teammate. Unless you've got some space-creating specials to burn, reviving someone during combat is a real chore. As a better system, I'd recommend removing the timer, make the revive instant, but leave both parties involved with no aura, as if the person doing the revive gave their aura to the one being revived. Reviving in the midst of battle would still be risky, but it would make it less likely that your teammates would just abandon you when you're down.
Conclusion
After almost two hours of playing non-stop, my arms are pretty tired. I've never experienced that from playing a game with a controller. It feels like I just lifted weights. Now I can say I got some exercise!
Overall I really like what I've seen so far. It's a very promising start and I think RT has a real winner here. Some balance and optimization issues need working out but it doesn't ruin the experience. I think the best indication of the quality is that it left me smiling and wanting more.
I give this game 7 swords that are also guns out of 10 with the expectation that the final version will be higher.

Oh my Lord. I have a good processor on my laptop, an i7-4700HQ CPU @ 2.40GHz. I cannot play this game unless I shrink the resolution down to about the size of a youtube video thumbnail. I do not understand why I would need that much more GHz just to run this game on the "potato" setting without framerate drops. at max resolution the game is running at about 2 fps and is damn near unplayable. I hope to God this is more well optimized in future updates, because if I can't actually play the game or see anything in it, I cant write a meaningful review.

What I like:
The controls, while nothing helped me to figure them out, were still very straightforward and easy to learn. I don't really remap controls, so not having that feature didn't really affect me.
The graphics are very nice despite some of the animations breaking as you go down a hill.
Voices are lacking a bit, but it's expected that they'll improve over time and add in more dialog. I wouldn't mind hearing Ruby scream out Weiss's name when she's downed though like in the second season.
What I didn't like:
Gameplay. I know it's an early access game and that it has as much fat as an Ethiopian kid, but I can't stand playing a game where the missions are exactly identical. See Metroid Prime Hunters for example. Leveling up is also kind of strange.
Music. There's music in this game?
Interface. Kind of clunky and a little hard to work with, but will get the job done.
All in all, it's a pretty faithful recreation of the show. I'm sure that once more mission and character varieties come out, then it'll really flesh out the game and make it 15 USD worthwhile. For now, unless you're a hardcore fan of the show, I wouldn't recommend the game. It's just too new and needs a bit more content.
