For me personally I enjoy getting my money's worth when it comes to video games and usually ensure no corner or aspect of a game is left unexplored, therefore I've only explored 3 islands in Portal Knights in the 5 hours that I've played it, 2 islands i explored for 4 hours and I only spent 30 minutes with the 3rd island as i wanted to spend some time building, and improving my home.
The game comes with a very basic leveling and class system that currently has 3 classes to choose from, warrior, ranger and mage, as you level up you are given attribute points which can be allocated to certain atrributes for example, strength, dexterity and intelligence. Beyond this each class has various "Talents" which you unlock as you level up in the game. For example the talent "Aggressive mind" is unlocked at level 5 and if selected, gives the wizard 30% added damage to spells. This system is very basic however it works perfectly, and makes the game that much more fun in my opinion.
As of right now there arent that many building blocks in the game that can be used for any structures you wish to build, however with just a little creativity and imagination you can undoubtedly still build amazing structures. I perosnally have many ideas which i've conjured up in just a few minutes, and plan to cover the first island in a multitude of various buildings.
Portal Knights visuals really pop, and remind me greatly of Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts & Bolts. If played on max settings rest assured you'll have some great eye candy. Getting to the aspects of video games i know nothing about such as optimisation and game physics. As far as i can see the game runs perfectly fine on max settings with around 40fps on my ancient PC. The games combat is simple and easy to get used to. The movement of the camera whilst in combat is perfect aswell allowing for enjoyable, "smooth" combat.
As of right now the only problem I've come across in the game which isn't really a problem but a visual glitch is some of the water visuals, mostly water which is supposed to be falling or flooding an area. Water that is moving downslope or falling from a fountain or waterfall looks very strange to say the least O.o. However this is expected as water was just added to the game.
In conclusion i applogise for this somewhat messy and unorganised review, i dont usually do these, and last of all I would say that without a shadow of a doubt Portal Nights is to be a truly awe-inspiring game upon completion.

I had high hopes, but this game is extremely basic for it's cost. I was brainwashed by the hype emanating from other reviews.
It's a 'dungeon' platformer with few mechanics to it and overall with very limited depth. It's most prized virtue - its replayability - comes down to the common game feature of 'procedurally generated' levels - which honesty can cause some of the levels to lazily pan out, unfairly and as a cumbersome mess - but mainy you'll find yourself replaying for the same reason you'd keep plugging away at slots in a casino, with the fun of it ebbing away before you're consciously aware.
The whole premise of the game is to get to each level's exit, and if you're trying to get your money's worth you'll inevitably go through at least 100-200 attempts.
What was initially interesting were the few dozen items (not a lot) you may find, but most are next-to-useless (a camera that dazes enemies, a web-gun that slows their advance) since you need your hands free for more important things. Many others are awkward to use in a game which already has clunky controls. The items which ARE of use you quickly tire of (equivalent to about 10 items).
Visually it is unimpressive: apparently designed for children but unforgivingly difficult enough and requiring enough patience to only be playable by adults.
Finally, of course, there's next to no narrative or story, nothing to drive you to play on except perhaps to reach a more stimulating environment in the next chapter. For example, I learned that there's an Egyptian themed stage but this can't be accessed without necessarily replaying the 3 previous sets of levels (cave, jungle, ice-cave) at least 3 times over, each, without failure. Grinding! In a game like this? And on the note of underground jungles...really?
In short, Spelunky is an uninspired, higher-than-average quality flash game but at a price of £11. Arguably it's worth getting at a discount of 75%.

Seemed like the kind of game I would enjoy, and I did, for about 2 hours, until I started noticing all the terrible things about the game.
The game is mostly luck based rather than skill.  There are plenty of things you learn and get better at, but most of your deaths are going to come as a result of unavoidable events.  The game is designed to ♥♥♥♥ you over and kill you as much as possible, and not in a fun way,  You'll be amused at the start, but eventually grow increasingly annoyed as the nonsense never ceases.

What really sours the game though is that you'll eventually figure out that most of the game is pointless.  The best strategy is to run straight to the exit as quickly as you can and ignore most of the things you see.  The more you explore and collect things, the greater the chance that the game will ♥♥♥♥ you over and you'll die.  By running straight to the exit, you minimize the number of times the game can ♥♥♥♥ you.  The other reason why it's the best strategy is due to the progression system in the game.
There are 4 zones with 4 stages each.  When you finish the fourth stage of a zone, you'll run into the Tunnel Man, who will create a shortcut for you to the next zone so that you can start there instead of zone 1 after you die.  The problem... he'll require you to give him 3 different items before he'll make the shortcut, and you must give him these items in seperate runs.  So collecting a lot of items in one run is pointless.  What you want to do is immediately kill yourself as soon as you give him the first item, start a new run and give him the second item, then kill yourself again and get him the third item.  Sounds fun right, well it gets even better.  The third item that the tunnel guy wants at the end of the second zone is a shotgun, which may or may not appear in your current run.  Have fun waiting for that to randomly generate and not getting screwed over trying to deliver it.  Even more fun is that the third item that the tunnel man at the end of zone 3 wants is a key from zone 1.  So you have to carry this damn thing through at least 10 stages and hope the game doesn't randomly ♥♥♥♥ you over while trying to deliver it.  FUN!!!!!
Spelunky has a clinging mechanic, but the randomized landscapes make it a hinderance as you'll often cling to things you don't mean to, which gets you killed by monsters and traps.  Zones 2 & 4 have Tiki traps that you'll often accidentally cling to resulting in your immediate death.  It's especially fun when 2 of them are next to the exit for the stage and instead of falling in between them, Spelunky decides he'd rather give one a hug.
Also fun is that Spelunky can only carry one thing at a time.  Until you figure out it's pointless, you'll waste a lot of time trying to get a weapon, a damsel, and a golden idol to the end of a stage.  It gets tiresome pretty quickly.  I'll save you some time... Don't bother doing it.
I could go on and on about the problems in this game.  It's initially enjoyable, but quickly becomes tedious and frustrating due to artificial difficulty, by 3 hours in I hated it.  I'm still not sure why I bothered finishing it.

The game is mostly good but after 14 hours of play I'm getting bored with the broken AI. I've been playing and replaying certain missions trying to get all of the extra objectives and items and there are definitely quite a few things to do in this game. My time has been almost entirely in Sniper Elite difficulty and the missions are set up well. There's usually one main goal that is obvious, but if you travel around the area you can usually find other objectives to finish.
The main issue I've had, so far, is that the AI is broken by giving them omniscience instead of some other method to increase difficulty. Once the AI determines you are in the area, they generally point directly at you and will fire blindly at your location even when they have never seen you and shouldn't have any idea of your exact location. In nearly every level I've tested this and most times enemies that have no possibility of knowing my location will track me through walls. The worst was at the airfield, where simply walking alerted enemies 30 feet above my head, (with metal, dirt and concrete between us), and I watched them on the mini-map turning to point directly at me. I get that this game is about stealth, but when you do break stealth, (whether on purpose or due to enemies hiding inside rocks/ground), the game becomes a joke at times.
Luckily, and the reason I can still give it a thumbs up, is that the game has a decent auto-save feature after objectives so these types of AI issues aren't catastrophic as long as you aren't on Authentic difficulty. I originally tried this game on the highest difficulty and the lack of saves made it unplayable in my opinion. Around the third mission I kept running into enemies inside walls and rocks that would negate the last thirty minutes of my time and it felt more like a roll of the dice rather than anything skill based.
If you have patience and like sniper games, I would definitely recommend this!

I thought long and hard as to whether I'd recommend this, and ultimately I think I still do. Albeit with a gigantic asterisk.
See, this game is fun. Really fun. You've got to go down what amounts to fallout vaults, you get to read interesting snippets of the old world (as seen by rich people), you're constantly on the edge of your seat wondering if the next door will kill you - or more to the point, planning your escape. It's a game that punishes stupidity and meandering while rewarding skilled shooting, fast reaction times, fast planning, and speedy exploration.
Of course, there's my first complaint: speedy exploration. SPEEDY. Because the SOB is a Son of a B. I got used to him - or more to the point, I got used to going through each level fast enough that I could escape him before he arrived - but on my first few runs he mowed me down, or I died panicking running away from him. If you don't hurry it up and just skip exploring, it's almost a game over. Sure, you can kill him if you know how, but in the beginning, when you're getting the hang of things, you won't know how. This game rushes you.
That said, I dig it, and when I got used to it I had a blast. Then came the second cooler, and it was amazing! Even more frustrating than the last, mind, but that's the point - it introduced new mechanics, new things to keep track of! Enemies on the ceilings and flying machines! I had to become even more situationally aware than I'd already been in the first cooler! So by the time I got to the next cooler, I was really roused up! What, I wondered, would I have to learn to deal with next?
And here's why I almost couldn't recommend this game: every single cooler after the second one is basically the first cooler. Again and again. Sure, there are slightly different enemies, some new environmental hazards (ice-barrels instead of fire barrels), even some new weapons (flamethrowers anyone?), but there's nothing new to learn. The learning curve had petered way out, and the game becomes routine waaay too quickly.
What I love about playing games like Spelunky (not on my steam library, but I do have it) is that each new area has entirely new themes and hazards in them. I have to worry about completely different things for every new level. Each new area is actually new and fresh! Sadly, this game was clearly rushed, and the developer could only add more varied content to one level, which isn't even the climax!
I had over 14 hours on record before I beat the second area, though. And even if I cannot recommend anything afterwards (it's still fun, just really repetitive), the first two coolers are already basically worth the price. This has my approval, albeit only barely. Definitely has my interest and keeps me addicted, if nothing else.

A surprisingly delightful game, in this day an age! Deponia is well made (seemingly with lots of love) and I have honestly not seen anything quite like it since the late Monkey Island series. I did buy it on sale though, so I might have a more positively biased view than those who bought it at full price.
The voice acting is fantastic, the art style is lovely and the many jokes are actually really funny - I even found myself laughing out loud from time to time!
I've seen several other reviews here complaining about the puzzles, but to the contrary I thought the puzzles where very clever, non-repetitive, logical and made perfect sense in the story line. Only once or twice was I really stumped, but I eventually pulled through without any help or walkthrough. Also, the game is actually really long - yay for lots of content!
I've also seen people complaining about game instability - perhaps they have fixed the issues, or perhaps I've just been lucky, but I've had virtually no problems at all, running it on a Windows 10 machine. The overall quality is great, though on very rare occations the voice acting has been cut sub-optimally. Also, the scripting engine still has some rough edges concerning animation timing and voice playback, making it feel "not quite as polished" as the old Lucas Arts classics. This is easily overlookable, though.
The only large flaw with Deponia, as many others too have pointed out, lies in the personality of the main character: Rufus. Yes, he is funny. Yes, he is witty. Yes, he is *supposed* to be a "likable scoundrel." But I just cannot make myself "like" him. Rufus seems to lack that important "heart of gold" behind all the outwardly obnoxiuos narcissism, which means I just can't identify with him, and consequently I don't really care about what happens to him. And that's a bad thing for any protagonist, anti-hero or not.
Still, the game (and Rufus too) is funny enough to be very enjoyable, all the way to the end, and I highly recommend it to any fan of the old Lucas Arts classics!

I'm going to compress this review into three categories: Visuals, Sounds, and Gameplay.
Note that these are my opinions, which may be biased. Please formulate your own after purchasing the game, it might be
leaving you wanting more.
Visuals: 5/5
It looks great on my TV connected from Steam Link; ~50-58 fps and I'm running with a low-mid range graphics card GTX 750Ti, and there's no lag at all except when fighting bears, their models slow the framerate quite a bit. Each stage has dynamic lighting so it falls onto the character models making them look amazing during battle. I really dislike the Arctic Glacier stage, but maybe it's just me. The best stage would have to be Infinite Azure so far, it's great when your character looks sweaty by the final round surrounded by all that water; a minor complaint would be that the clouds in the sky looks like a static image, not modeled. Then you have all the flashiness from combos (hit-FX), the slow-mo when attacking with low health (at the same time as the enemy), and Rage Art animations. Every model looks fantastic. Hair looks somewhat like plastic, but only in certain stages.
Sounds: 4.5/5
I came in expecting a lot of ~step music (electic-step?) since I've been following the release of the soundtrack since it's Arcade release. It's appropriate given the genre, fantasy-tech fighting game with robots, corporations, etc. It reminds me of the Tag 2 soundtrack, but of course Tekken 7's is much better due to the final round tracks adding hype for the final round. The only gripe I have is that the PS4 version gets Tekken Tunes, and PC does not (maybe future DLC?). No complaints about the soundtrack, it's solid electronic music energizing and adrenaline building.
Gameplay: 4.5/5
I have to say that the gameplay rivals Virtua Fighter 5 FS in so many ways, but Tekken 7 is not only flashier, but just as complicated, and better. You got frame openings, counter hit combos, mix-ups, wall splats, stun combos, super-armour atacks, and there are more. Each character plays their own way; obviously, there are going to those with better stances and/or frames and even those that do 10-50 more damage than your main. Rage Drive, and Art depthen the gameplay so that comebacks happen way more often than you think. The balance is there, you have to outsmart the opponent, keep them guessing, and find their string openings. Fighting a skilled opponent feels very dynamic.
I've played online, reached mentor/greatmaster, and just thinking about this game wants me to pick up the controller and go to practice mode. I like finding the enemies opening, or when they start to go for low sweeps rather than strings, and then counter hit combos begin. If you like 8-directional fighters, there's no reason not to pick this up. I'd even say it's better than SFV (though 2-D fighters are very different), which I've poured about two times as much hours in it than T7. The Online however, lacks Replays and Crossplay support (so sad). I want to watch replays of mine, or mainly those who are in the top 100 leaderboard like you can in SFV. I'm hopeful it will come as DLC...
The Story mode was amazing ONLY in terms of presentation. I played and finished it during release on easy mode, which took about 3-5 hours. You see the perspective of a reporter analyzing the Mishima events outside of the main characters (the Mishimas + everyone hovering around them) so it adds some understanding to the scattered story that is Tekken.
TLDR; Other than that, the game is basically Story mode for some wow-factor, Arcade mode for practicing combos on bots, hunting/grinding chests to make your main your own with the (almost bare) customization, and then wreck some scrubs online. Very rewarding if you ask me, just as the previous versions. It'll last 3-6 months, maybe more if you have people to play with, or even choose to attend some tourneys. Don't forget the DLC; Eliza and Akuma add in some jumping heavy combo characters (definitely a homage to Capcom IP's who can start combos with jumping heavy punch/kick, a string followed by stun, and end with an EX attack). Eliza fights similarly to Morrigan (has an uppercut, projectile, and flies breifly). I hope to see Anna and Lei sooner or later.
Get the game, enjoy it while it's online is thriving then 6 months later, play something else after being burned out from seeing too many Akumas, or whoever is top-tier online.

Portal Knights is a cute light RPG sandbox, with building and crafting.
It's playable alone or in co-op.
You explore islands procedurally generated (44 of them, a bit more with events), with different biomes, random dungeons, random quests (mostly to get more xp or unique furniture) and random events, gather new ressources to craft better armor or weapons, but also furniture for your home.
You don't "need" to build a home base but you'll quickly want to do it to gather more ressources. And also for the sake of building, it's fun, that's all.
Controls are easy and pleasant to use (some won't like the auto target thing, but you can disable it in the options).
The game is early access but is very playable, no game breaking bugs (I rarely encounter bugs.. and they are hotfixed quickly anyway). There is enough content to keep you on the game at  least 30h. Way more if you really dig the genre.
The devs team is doing an awesome job so far.
Regular quality updates, with lots of content, and quick hotfixes when needed.
You can safely buy the game for what it is right now, it's really worth the price asked.
But, don't buy this game if:
- you want an openworld game. It's not.
- you want a dedicated server to play on with lots of friends. It hasn't been announced by the devs for the moment. So don't buy an early access for what it could be, but for what it is. And atm it's Steam friend list for 4 player co-op or single player.
- you want a strong RPG game. You'll find only 3 classes to choose from. They don't make a lot of  difference, the RPG  features are very light and won't appeal to someone looking for a deep combat or customisation system.
- you want a very difficult game. There is some end game stuff (hard mode bosses), but it's mainly a casual game (casual can be fun too!).
If those 4 points don't turn you away, the game is just a gem, buy it.

I don't generally like games that use the same block world as Minecraft, but I am thoroughly pleased with how this game turned out. I had high hopes, but this game is extremely basic for it's cost. I was brainwashed by the hype emanating from other reviews.
It's a 'dungeon' platformer with few mechanics to it and overall with very limited depth. It's most prized virtue - its replayability - comes down to the common game feature of 'procedurally generated' levels - which honesty can cause some of the levels to lazily pan out, unfairly and as a cumbersome mess - but mainy you'll find yourself replaying for the same reason you'd keep plugging away at slots in a casino, with the fun of it ebbing away before you're consciously aware.
The whole premise of the game is to get to each level's exit, and if you're trying to get your money's worth you'll inevitably go through at least 100-200 attempts.
What was initially interesting were the few dozen items (not a lot) you may find, but most are next-to-useless (a camera that dazes enemies, a web-gun that slows their advance) since you need your hands free for more important things. Many others are awkward to use in a game which already has clunky controls. The items which ARE of use you quickly tire of (equivalent to about 10 items).
Visually it is unimpressive: apparently designed for children but unforgivingly difficult enough and requiring enough patience to only be playable by adults.
Finally, of course, there's next to no narrative or story, nothing to drive you to play on except perhaps to reach a more stimulating environment in the next chapter. For example, I learned that there's an Egyptian themed stage but this can't be accessed without necessarily replaying the 3 previous sets of levels (cave, jungle, ice-cave) at least 3 times over, each, without failure. Grinding! In a game like this? And on the note of underground jungles...really?
In short, Spelunky is an uninspired, higher-than-average quality flash game but at a price of £11. Arguably it's worth getting at a discount of 75%.

Seemed like the kind of game I would enjoy, and I did, for about 2 hours, until I started noticing all the terrible things about the game.
The game is mostly luck based rather than skill.  There are plenty of things you learn and get better at, but most of your deaths are going to come as a result of unavoidable events.  The game is designed to ♥♥♥♥ you over and kill you as much as possible, and not in a fun way,  You'll be amused at the start, but eventually grow increasingly annoyed as the nonsense never ceases.

What really sours the game though is that you'll eventually figure out that most of the game is pointless.  The best strategy is to run straight to the exit as quickly as you can and ignore most of the things you see.  The more you explore and collect things, the greater the chance that the game will ♥♥♥♥ you over and you'll die.  By running straight to the exit, you minimize the number of times the game can ♥♥♥♥ you.  The other reason why it's the best strategy is due to the progression system in the game.
There are 4 zones with 4 stages each.  When you finish the fourth stage of a zone, you'll run into the Tunnel Man, who will create a shortcut for you to the next zone so that you can start there instead of zone 1 after you die.  The problem... he'll require you to give him 3 different items before he'll make the shortcut, and you must give him these items in seperate runs.  So collecting a lot of items in one run is pointless.  What you want to do is immediately kill yourself as soon as you give him the first item, start a new run and give him the second item, then kill yourself again and get him the third item.  Sounds fun right, well it gets even better.  The third item that the tunnel guy wants at the end of the second zone is a shotgun, which may or may not appear in your current run.  Have fun waiting for that to randomly generate and not getting screwed over trying to deliver it.  Even more fun is that the third item that the tunnel man at the end of zone 3 wants is a key from zone 1.  So you have to carry this damn thing through at least 10 stages and hope the game doesn't randomly ♥♥♥♥ you over while trying to deliver it.  FUN!!!!!
Spelunky has a clinging mechanic, but the randomized landscapes make it a hinderance as you'll often cling to things you don't mean to, which gets you killed by monsters and traps.  Zones 2 & 4 have Tiki traps that you'll often accidentally cling to resulting in your immediate death.  It's especially fun when 2 of them are next to the exit for the stage and instead of falling in between them, Spelunky decides he'd rather give one a hug.
Also fun is that Spelunky can only carry one thing at a time.  Until you figure out it's pointless, you'll waste a lot of time trying to get a weapon, a damsel, and a golden idol to the end of a stage.  It gets tiresome pretty quickly.  I'll save you some time... Don't bother doing it.
I could go on and on about the problems in this game.  It's initially enjoyable, but quickly becomes tedious and frustrating due to artificial difficulty, by 3 hours in I hated it.  I'm still not sure why I bothered finishing it.

Brutally difficult hilarity and mayhem.
You will die. Alot. And often before getting past floor 4, too. But that's the beauty of it. With every game, you build your skills and learn to avoid the arrow traps, the spikes, whatever the RNG god throws at you. And eventually, you break through into the next level, only to be killed by a frog. And the cycle repeats.
This game is all about skill and luck. Any floor layout can be cleared perfectly, but it's up to your skills to pull it off. And none of us are perfect, so it then comes down to luck. Did you get an early jetpack? Did you find an altar on floor 2? Life is harder, but not impossible. Press on; maybe the jetpack will come to you floor 3.
Get this game; while it will eaet up your life it is one of the best ways to waste it.

Gameplay. I know it's an early access game and that it has as much fat as an Ethiopian kid, but I can't stand playing a game where the missions are exactly identical. See Metroid Prime Hunters for example. Leveling up is also kind of strange.
Music. There's music in this game?
Interface. Kind of clunky and a little hard to work with, but will get the job done.

As we all understand this game is in its early stages I will be highlighting my experience, some pros and cons and finally my input on what should be updated.
My Experience
----
Took 60 mins to play through with 1 friend as Ruby and Yang. Was fun for the time being and a little challenging with some of the zerg rush moments. Its definately worth the money as I am happy to help back this game and hope that the finished product is something solid and enjoyable with some sort of replayability.
Pros
----
Voice acting is 100% spot on
Fun Hack n Slash
Leveling system (bare bones of course)
Possibility of having slightly different playstyles per each character
Cons
----
Sounds overlap (very loud sound with the recharging Aura)
Animations are very slidy and fast
Gravity seems to be cranked up as physics on the boxes make it seem we are in some sort of tiny world
Characters feel the same with just spamming left click and dodging when needed
UI could be better even this early on in development
What I would like to see changed
----
Sound overlapping: Simply add a queue to the sounds so that if one is already playing then dont overlap.
Balance sounds too. Aura noise obviously way too loud in relation to everything else.
Targeting system: As Ruby I find myself trying to snipe an enemy and it chooses one at random even further away or misses completly.
Some kind of class system: The characters can all fight in a big horde as individuals. Having some sort of speciality per character would be great at making each character even more unique.
PvP lobbies: This game would be great for PvP in the same setting as the battle arena from the recent episodes of the show. The combat system would need to be refined a lot however and hopefully some more characters from other teams can be playable. I want to be able to bonk someone as Nora :3
Overall the game lacks the feel of a co-op game even when playing with others. I first expected less of a Hack n Slash due to the initial fan trailer and would like to see a more technical combo system in the attacks as its all really just left click, left click, left click at the moment.
Attack modifier buttons and blocking would be great. It all feels a little too fast for me at the moment and wouldnt mind a more toned back approach to the combat system while still living up the the fighting style of the anime.
This game is everything i wanted it to be, for only £10 i would defiantly suggest it, if you are a RWBY or a fan of hack and slash games

*Optimization is better than it was but still not great

In spite of all its problems, however, I really did enjoy playing this, both during Early Access and the full release. The game has improved a lot since the initial EA launch, the devs have done a great job for such a small team, and they engage well with the community. The price is a
high, perhaps, so I'd say wait until it's on sale tbh (I got it in Early Access so I didn't pay as much anyway).

If you're a true south park fan, it's worth it even at such a high price. It's basically the play-in-your-own-south-park episode, version 2.0, with a ton of the main TV characters as well as recurring themes getting screen time, even more than in the Stick of Truth. The references to the TV show episodes are great and easy to notice. Fights are fun, especially with the banter between the superheroes. (Mosquito is my favourite in this) Thankfully, the game does not try to outdo the Stick of Truth in terms of outrageousness, instead refining the combat, exploration and levelling system as well as the jokes. The humor overshadows the storyline a bit, but thats not a problem for a comedy/satire-based action game. The story itself seems generic at first (evil villian vs superheroes), but it quickly gets more complicated than that and splits into multiple subplots as well as the relationships (read: jokes) between the 4th graders and the new kid/protagonist. Coupled with the new kid's super smelly "superpower", the story is funny enough to keep you interested for the most part. Plot twists included. If this game was a little bit less expensive, I'd give it a 9/10. Farts not included.
EDIT: Regarding other opions on this game, rember, this is based on a 2D CARTOON SHOW from the 1990's. Don't expect the size, depth and customization of Skyrim or the combat system of Metal Gear Solid. Don't expect character stories as important as Mass Effect or a storyline as compelling as The Last of Us. It's based on a cartoon show for crying out loud. There is beauty in simple but funny things. Such as farts.
Also, the last boss fight isn't at the end of the main storyline. It's someone much more powerful.

I recommend South Park: The Fractured But Whole to anyone who is a fan of south park and enjoyed the stick of truth, but with the added warning that I think Stick of truth is the superior south park game. If you don’t like South Park or the previous game, I doubt this one will win you over.
So many fart jokes… Now, I know that South Park loves fart jokes, and I am okay with that, but I tend to find them to be the weaker south park jokes. (Except maybe in the queef episode.) Plus it is used so much in this game that it completely loses its comedic effect pretty early, kinda how in “It Hits the Fan” the sh-word loses what little shocking/gross out power it had because of how much it is used. (Luckily there was other fun parts of that episode) but that was just one 22minutes episode… This took me 22 hours to play through with the main joke being not all that funny just getting less and less funny…
Repeating some of the more mediocre jokes really does hurt this game a bit for me.
Generally the game has a lot of less memorable scenes compared to the first one… And I felt it missed one opportunity, since I chose to play as a girl, I was hoping for a massive Cartman freak-out once he discovered he had been playing with a girl this whole time (and a girl had ended up as his boss in stick of truth).
Let us be honest, I think the most memorable south park style joke is the skin-color difficulty slider.
The skin-color difficulty slider was a fun character-customization detail.
I think the combat has improved, still sticking with a turn-based style, it now allows you to move around to position yourself and your fighting companions.
The voices are still the ones you know and love from South Park.
Seeing some of your favorite characters in their superhero outfits. Personally, Professor Chaos is my favorite one of the “superhero/supervillain” characters.
It is still very much South Park, even though there are less really memorable and great moments compared to Stick of Truth, it still very much has the south Park feel and love to it, which is why I recommended it to fans. Just don’t expect it to top stick of truth in terms of comedy.
Being able to pick gender, sexuality, and race for your character was fun, even if it led to a missed joke in a Cartman style freak-out. I would have preferred a shorter game, where the choices led to a few more scenes based on genders.
Most of the dialogue between Cartman and Wendy, and when Cartman and Kyle are mad at each other is great.

I'll keep this brief: The game itself is fun.  There is a wealth of worthwhile single player and multiplayer content.  The mechanical changes such as interactive environments and alternate character variations add plenty to the game.  If it gets patched into a more functional state, I'll say go for it.  If.
You see, the PC version of MKX is a car wreck.  It runs poorly, with frequent frame rate drops.  The netcode is gag-inducing, and has all but pushed away much of the community of online players.  Glitches abound, including everyone's favorite, the classic save data eraser!  Yep, after 15 hours of play, I booted up the game this afternoon to find that all of my data had been wiped for no reason.  Similar reports have been popping up for weeks, with some people experiencing this glitch on multiple occasions.  Oh well.  I'll write this one off as a lesson learned, at least until (IF) High Voltage patches it up.  Until such time, don't make the same mistake I did.
5/5 Edit: So I come home from work today, cautiously excited to see if the new patch had improved the game.  LOL nope, there was no patch.  Why?  Because after being rolled out, it was pulled back because it deleted all players' save data.  All of it.  Everywhere.  Permanently, unless you had the foresight to back your stuff up.  This is the world we live in, ladies and gentlemen.  I weep for our children, and the world they will inherit from us.

As someone who has never played any of the Diablo games, on which Torchlight II and its first iteration are based, I had no taste of the top-down hack and slash action RPG. The comparisons to Diablo are commonplace, especially since Torchlight was developed by some of the original team from Diablo II. My lack of previous experience with the genre enabled me to adopt a more impartial and first-hand opinion, and I can say with confidence that this is a game I can certainly recommend. The crux of Torchlight is the hunt for better and better loot, which provides a lot of replayability if you're into the addictive nature of farming for gear. Graphically, the game has something of a cartoon look with its art direction which sets a much lighter tone than the Diablo series.
If you're into the RPG genre and want to try something different, you can't go wrong with Torchlight II. Now to see what this little known game called Diablo is all about.

Gameplay & review:
The video above says it all. I start playing it full of optimism but slowly I get worn down. I'm a little confused but that's probably because I don't know the backstory of the game.. like it was probably one of those games made in 24hrs for a jam right?
The visuals aren't the best and something just doesn't feel right about how rapidly the goblins move. I understand that there's no point in making them move slower 'cos there's nothing you can do once you've pressed "R" but still, it just feels unnatural and at times you can't pay attention to all of the goblins at once to see if all your traps worked.
The trap menu *is* translucent but you're still not able to see fully through it and preview the up-and-coming level meaning that you have to guess which traps you may need. This also means that a life of a poor little kitty has to be sacrificed for you to even see the next level! (There may be a way to remove the menu briefly so you can see the level and I missed that in the tutorial, in which case I apologise!)
Also this whole idea seems surreal.. goblins killing kittens.. what?
I do like the idea of mixing the tower defense and puzzle genres, it just could've been pulled off much better I feel. The game feels like it's still in alpha (it may well be and I didn't realise, if so then I apologise!) and possibly untested. I mean I'm sure each of the levels were tested but the glitches when the demon smashes the kitten got through QA apparently? Or maybe they were left in 'cos it was funny to see the kitten model stretch and mangle itself across the scenery?
Overall I wouldn't recommend this game if you're looking for a polished experience but if you're the kind of person who adores glitchy games with bizarre premises then Bomb Defense is perfect for you!

It's basically a first person shooting gallery. There are no "enemies" to speak of, no way to loose except failing to take out enough targets. Yet it is still incredibly fun.
If you are like me and enjoy FPS games as a fun and relaxing experience shooting stuff, and wish you could play a multiplayer game with yourself instead of a stoner, an 11 year old, and one guy who is afk, this is the game for you.
10 out of 10 for the concept of 4 player coop with yourself. If they don't add more features to the existing game, I certainly hope there is a more fleshed out game as a sequal. A full FPS campaign, with enemies that shoot back, and a story, built around this awesome mechanic, could be one of the best games of all time.
That said, it IS a pretty basic game. Some arcade like shooting gallery levels, and user generated content for longevity. You will inevitably find yourself competing with yourself for a better score on past levels after the first few hours. For the price point though, 4-5 hours of great fun is totally worth it. And I would say it is a very replayable game.

Despite this game being Early Access, and even though I am biased toward RWBY, however, I will try to make this as unbiased as possible.
RWBY : Grimm Eclipse - Story :
The Story as i can tell is virtuallly non existant at this point, except it seems to be the missions that the Teams of Beacon would take on as training, such as traversing a forest to find an abandoned control point for the betterment of humanity.
The Gameplay :
If you can to this game for Trailer like combat, or sick fights against giant Mechas on a highway, then you came to the wrong place. You exclussively fight Grimm as of now, however the variety is pretty good. You have your basic grunt-like Grimm, your sizeable increase Grimm, and a few "mini-boss" Grimm, such as the roly poly that Weiss fought, and the huge bears the Juane fought, but no giant scorpions or bird monsters. when you press shift, you dodge, and unless you have Sticky Keys off, you will get destroyed... alot. Whenever you kill Grimm, YOU kill Grimm, you get a bit of xp toward your next level up. Once you have filled the xp bar and leveled up, you get 1 point to spend on increasing the damage f your specials, or increasing the amount of life you have. Your life, or "Aura", is shown in the bottom right of the screen. You probably won't notice it at first, because it takes a little while before you actually start taking damage. You also have 5 different attacks for each character, Melee, Ranged, AOE, Large Projectile, and "Move or you get destroyed". The Melee attack is the left-click, and Ranged is Right-Click. I have found the ranged attacks for Blake, Weiss and Ruby are pretty good, but Yang's could use a little work. However, Blakes is by FAR the best. It doesn't push you back, it almost ALWAYS hits, and you can just keep shooting. I was able to get to a 50-hit combo before a guy snuck up behind me and ended my combo. The Melee attack is the most reliable, and basically makes this game "Prepare to buy a new mouse" type of thing. The AOE, Large Projectile, and "Move or you get destroyed" attacks are all 3 of your specials. The AOE is probably the most useful of the 3, as it is, well, and AOE attack, or Area Of Effect. When upgraded, it can Do mass amounts of damage to the hundreds on Grimm around you at the same time, and if Weiss' if upgraded twice, it heals 25% of allies Aura when near it. The Large Projectile attack is the second most useful special, as it hits multiple enemies from far away. And the "Move or you get destroyed" special is the one I found almost COMPLETELY useless. It pushed you forward, doing a bit of damage to the enemy in front of you, but other then that, I almost exclusevly used it as a better form of dodging, as the AOE attack would do the same, if not more, amount of damage, while stunning, pushing back, and/or killing any Grimm near you, giving you time to dodge and get away if need be. Also when you have leveled up, you can put points into increasing amount of Aura, how long before your Aura recovers, the amount of special you can have at one time, and more. You also have to get a certain amount of kills with the specific special to unlock a "Ultimate Skill", as I would put it. I have yet to see what these are, but you need absurd amounts of kills with a single special to even unlock it, if you havn't gotten to the end by then. Another way to get xp is from finding Artifacts. Hidden around the levels are little Rook pieces from Chess, like the ones used to pick the teams in the anime, and they reward everyone with 100 xp each. Another thing about leveling, I havn't made it past level 9, but I assume it stops at 10 because one skill is only unlocked at level 10, and the way leveling works is it doesn't carry with your character. So if you play as Ruby for half an hour, and are at level 5, get off, come back, and start game again, you wont be the same level. The level you have when joining a game is determined by what level you are in, so if you play through every level and get to level 10 as Yang, and start a new game as Yang, you will be level 1 again, and your skills at default again.
The Characters :
If you are a fan of the anime, which you must be if you found this game on Day 1, then you will be happy to hear that the characters have their respective voices from the anime. Ruby, Weiss, Blake, Yang, and the disimbodied voices, Professor  Peter Port and Professor Bartholomew Oobleck are all voiced by their respective actors. Just as a side note, I think it will be cool if and when they add Characters packs, send $5 or something for Team JNPR. I think its a cool concept
The Sounds :
The sound can be worked on, even at really low music volume, everything is still too loud. There is only a setting for Music and voice volume, no SFX. I have to play with 1 earbud in so I can still hear my favorite characters, but not go deaf in the process.
The Multiplayer :
First off, the video settings of the game are EXTREMELY lack luster. There is Potato, the lowest, Sandard, and Insane. With my potato of a computer, I can barely run on Standard, and probably cant run on Insane, although it would look beautiful. However, when you change the video settings to Potato, this also seems to be true for Standard, the text in game is almost completely unledgable. I had actually stop playing, and TRY to read what other people said. That being said, there is no voice chat in Multiplayer, so with the poor pixilization of the text, Cooperation was almost impossible, almost, I was still able to perform some coop. When you start, you can either start a new game in the first level, Emerald Forest, or join an existing game, hence the "level is based on what level you are playing" thing. You can then pick any of the 4 characters from team RWBY at that point. All 4 people can be Ruby. All 4 people can be Yang. Everyone can be a different character. This is a good, and a bad thing in my eyes. For a team to BE a team, diversity is a must. If you had 4 Blakes running around all using their ranged attacks, it wouldn't be too much fun. And also a roleplaying type of thing is nice too, like if who plays as Ruby stays near Yang alot, and Weiss stays away from Ruby. When you die in multiplayer, your teammates have 45 seconds to revive you until you respawn anyway. You can still fight while reviving, but you have to be really clsoe to the person. Some of my multiplayer experiences were a person playing as Ruby going down, and when they were revived, they said in chat, "Don't worry, I've got milk." Another one is I was playing as Weiss, and there were 3 Rubys. I said in chat, "Man, if there were this many Rubys, Weiss would probably kill herself." -Disclaimer Suicide isn't funny- And also, in the final level, there are a TON of "Mini-boss" Grimm that spawn, the first time through, we got destroyed, but the second time, I initiated teamwork. I said to stick together. We stuck together, and had little problem beating it.
The Graphics :
Despite it being early access, and the limited video settings you can change, the artstyle is beautiful. It looks as if its straight from the anime itself. The characters look really well done, and the Grimm look scary AF.
The Conclusion :
The Pros :                                               The Cons :
- Amazing visuals                                   - Terrible Video Settings
- RWBY Voice actors                             - Atrosious Sound Settings
- Amazing potential                               - No Voice Chat
- Hard to read Text chat on lower settings
- Can't remap controls

Being a Rooster Teeth fan for 6 years now I have been incredibly biased on what they produce... Until now.
I played the fan game and the version they had for people to play at RTX and I don't see much improvement in this version of the game, the combat is super simple: spam left click, right click every once in a while, use your special moves when you are surrounded or you're attacking a tough enemy, and dash away when you're low on health. It would be fun to put on while you marathon a podcast, cartoon, etc in the background but it has incredibly frustrating aspects to the game like how teamwork is non existent and is actually more competitive in a bad way, the objective besides getting to the end of the level is to level up your character from last hitting an enemy, I repeat LAST HITTING an enemy so everyone attacking a powerful enemy to cooperatively kill it doesn't happen except when all other enemies are dead what normally happens is everyone separates and gets hordes of their own to kill and then try to get the final blow on the tough enemies that that poor sucker was attacking the whole time. There are no two person combos like in the show besides multiple people flaying their weapon at the enemies to hopefully get the last hit, also multiple people can play the same character when the lobby caps at 4 people so I kid not every 4 man lobby I've been in consisted of Ruby, Yang, Weiss, and Weiss. It just doesn't look or feel right. Other problems, all character progression go away once you leave a game which is fine but you can't leave and pick up where you last left off, the levels are all very repetitive, enter an area kill monster, enter another kill monsters, enter an area protect a stationary object from monsters, rinse and repeat, the enemy's are all so similar with slight differences in health and looks with one exception of the boar looking ones who role and have armor In certain spots so as far as I can tell no big bosses like the giant bird they fought in season one, I wouldn't know if there is because I can't make it 20 minutes without getting bored and quitting. You can't customize the resolution because wouldn't change to 1920x1080 it would just revert to 720 after trying to change it, the sound options are a joke, you have voice volume and music volume so I can't turn down anything else so I can't hear anything the characters are saying half the time because so much is going on. The game drops frame rate way to often on my computer that can run Battlefield 3 on full ultra graphics settings and Skyrim with all of the best graphics enhancements mods I could find. So overall the game is really boring and frustrating because of cooperative gameplay turning into competitive gameplay with a story that I don't know because i can't hear what they are saying and putting on subtitles and looking at the subtitles takes me away from the action, I have drop into a quick match in the middle of the game because their is no solo mode and none of my friends own the game. I realize the game is in early access but this is what is what Is wrong with its current state and I do realize that fan boys are going to down vote this because the game is 10/10 perfect no flaws in there eyes but I payed $15 wanting to like it and couldn't bring myself to play it for 20 full minutes.
EDIT: After playing for a little while more I felt like I should add somethings that I like about this game to my otherwise fully negative review, I figured out how to play solo, you have to start a new game which puts you in a lobby and you have to do nothing until everyone else in the lobby gets tired of waiting for you then leaves then put the lobby to friends only, it is really mean to do but I really wanted to play solo and playing through the game I found it to be more enjoyable than a lobby full of people because it brings an actual challenge to the game, also the voice acting is pretty good and the graphics are pretty impressive. The only negative things that weren't mentioned above were that the running animation is not good at all the characters often start floating going up and down stairs and such but this isn't a big problem at all. Another problem is that there are invisible borders everywhere which didn't bother me much. It still is ironic that a RWBY game is more enjoyable solo than Co-op

I played TEKKEN as a kid through to Tekken Tag, and then picked it back up for Tekken Tag 2. I think the easiest way to detail how this game plays (since it is very similar to Tekken Tag 2) is just to compare the two, so here goes:
PROS:
-Easier to Acquire money. No more endless grinding,  you can deck out a custom character in no time, and you earn money and items just by playing the game naturally. No need to go do something unfun just to earn $$$
-Better AI scaling. Whether you're a novice or a semi-pro, you can fight opponents that are fun. Treasure battle's ranking system in particular gives you some fun AI to knock around, and if you're pro...
-Online. Online works perfect so far. Only gripe is the tournament mode which should be avoided atm due to a host's ability to kick anyone (yes including people that just beat them)
-More diverse character roster. More characters.
-Story, well there is one. I guess that makes it a pro compared to the old game. It includes cutscenes and all that, but it's not the most engaging IMO
CONS:
-Inability to switch out. It's not a tag game so that should be no surprise.
-Music. Music in the old game was better. Heck, even some of the old old titles had more memorable music. It's soft though so it should at the least not be a distraction.
-Less interesting costumes. By a hair, I thought Tag 2's were better. But the difference is you can actually buy one from time to time in this game compared to the old, so the overall edge of costumes I'm giving to Tekken 7
If you've never played Tag 2, or a Tekken game in general. Idk what to tell you, it's a fighting game, and some people like it. There are cute girls.

WASTED: A Post Apocalyptic Pub Crawler is a first-person dungeon crawler with some rogue-lite elements with a comedic flair. The main goal of the game is to venture into dungeons known as "Coolers" (basically vaults from Fallout)  to find booze that, once drunk, will give your character a permanent buff or debuff, and if your character dies, they are gone forever. Outside of dungeon crawling, there is also a small amount of side content including a fair amount of genuinely funny and well written dialogue with, for the most part, fairly competent voice acting, some sidequests, a daily dungeon challenge that can yield rare loot, and a few little quests.
Gameplay, for it's genre, is nothing short of superb. The guns all feel nice and responsive. Enemies can have limbs crippled which will produce various debuffs for them. There's a decent amount of enemy variety, however, you can end up in a situation where you'll get stuck repeating old content for a frustrating amount of time, but I'll get to that later. There are enough ways to approach a situation to make the game feel fun, even after investing a fair amount of time into it. And the quests, while extremely simple, give you a little something more to do while playing instead of the mindless, repetetive slog that can sometimes be dungeon crawling. And how could I possibly forget about the writing of the game?! This is where the game truly shines. The basic premise of the game is that the world was destroyed by a massive nuclear war, and the only people who survived did so by going into great hidden undergroun...oh wait no. Those guys all died, the only ones that actually lived were a bunch of idiotic, tough as nails, boozehounds. It's absolutely hilarious whenever you find a new, wacky character.
However, despite all of the positive things about, the game, it does fall apart a little 'bit in respects to it's balancing. If you manage to make a really good character with a bunch of really rare weapons and armor and a lot of good buffs, losing them can be quite traumatic to your overall progress. You'll have to go back through old dungeons, fight what are now boring and repetetive enemies, and build your character almost all the way back up from scratch. The game tries to mitigate the losses by letting you store away valuable loot at your house which you will go back to whenever you drink booze or finish a dungeon, and by letting you buy back items from dead characters, but it's the buffs that you lose that hurt the most. You can get buffs that will completely change how you play the game, then when you lose them because you walked into a randomly generated room that happened to have a shotgun trap aiming right at your face that goes off...well, it can be frustrating (I do have to say that I've never had this specifically happen to me because I use a very cautious playstyle where I always keep my health at basically max no matter the cost, but this has happened to a lot of people who played the game other than myself). The game also has some odd performance issues where whenever you go to a more open section (anywhere other than a cooler), your framerate will drop from 60, to just around 30. It's not gamebreaking as there's nothing in any of these places that would call for the need of a higher framerate, but it can be quite jarring. The game has also suffered from quite a few bugs, however, the developer of the game has been doing his absolute damndest to get rid of all the bugs.
Overall, I have to say that the game is great if you're into dungeon crawlers, FPS, or games with hilarious writing, as this game executes all of these things very well. Of course there are a few things I didn't cover, both on the negative and the positive side, like the SOB who still need a little 'bit of balancing (my suggestion would be to set the timer until he shows up to be about 5-10% longer), and the awesome soundtrack, but if I keep talking about this game I'm gonna end up writing a friggin' novel. If I had to say whether or not you should buy it regardless of whether or not you like first person dungeon crawlers, I'd say HELL YES! It's a great game with just a few rough edges, but the developer of the game is and has been phenomenally dedicated to making sure that a lot of the issues that the community has had with the game are fixed.

This is NOT your typical Tower Defense game.  It does have a couple of gun turrets that can be placed in the level, but It is more of a a puzzle/defense game.
It's different than most games of it's genre. It is a thinking man's game with different ways to pass a level.  You first select a level, then decide what kind of traps, blockades, guns, bombs and other devices you want to bring into the level to beat it.  You do have a budget, so you must choose wisely from a list and cannot take too much into the levels with you. This game is one of the better multiplayer co-op FPS shooters out there. Me and some friends managed to form a great team together, and got through most of the arenas okay.
I was Blue. I was the weakest; I admit. Always behind in upgrades. When I entered the arena, I never knew what to do like everyone else. I would shoot at whatever I saw, but the others looked at me like I could never see the bigger picture, and I always felt like my efforts were pointless against the massive cube army we were up against.
Then there was Purple. He had better reflexes, better skills, better gear... he would pick out groups and take them on, trusting his teammates to take on the rest, and keeping a level head. He was a better fighter than I.
After him, there was Yellow. He and Purple made a great team, and were closer than any other two team members. He always seemed to know where the enemies would come from, how to take advantage of the arena... like he'd done this before. They would split up and take on different groups, laughing at me for flailing around so helplessly.
Then, Green. He was a bit odd, didn't talk much. He'd watch the rest of us, maybe help us out, but seemed content to let us handle most of the work. And yet, whenever we missed a cube, he was there, destroying it the minute it slipped past us. Without him, who knows how many more cubes would have gotten past our lines.
All in all, we somehow managed to take out wave after wave. I'll never know where the others got their training, or what secrets they had. Ah well.
(But seriously, it's a cool game with a cool concept. Get it.)

Wish I hadn't bought this game. While the graphics are nice, and the combat is much better than a game like minecraft, it has so many negatives that they swamp out any benefits.
The first and largest problem is that the islands are tiny, and resources are specific to each island, so you'll be constantly hopping around trying to find the materials you need. Run out of coal while crafting? Time to jump back 3 islands to the last place that had any.
This brings me to a second problem which is that island jumping is done as a group. If one person goes, you all go. It makes me think they're using the Unity networking system that loads levels as a whole. Same reason world sizes are so small, and biomes can't be mixed.
Aside from this, there isn't very much to do in the world, and mining is tedious because the blocks are so small - making it difficult to properly hit what you're aiming at. Inventory space is so limited that you can't even carry the materials you need... and you'll spend a ton of the space you have on weapons, spells (those are items), and all the workshops you need to carry from island to island just to keep crafting.
It's like carrying your house on your back, with an inventory smaller than minecraft.
Another annoying thing is that the chat isn't saved in multiplayer. If you didn't see someone say something within 30 seconds, you won't ever see it. It's gone.

Game is great and you can really enjoy it. But I want to tell you about things what makes this game a "NO-game" for me (and therefore I can't recommend it), it's less than a year on the market, so expect things to change and this review too.
Biggest problem: no motivation to play it. Events are nice addition (though 200 events achievement is a big crap imho), but end-game currently is all about digging titanium.. alot of titanium (to upgrade all your chests so that micromanagement become lesser burden) and that's all. There are 3 nearly identical classes (I am leveling my warrior with BOW atm) and "some" randomness, but leveling one character to lvl 30, killing last boss is around ~8 hours max and then there is nothing to do, except ocasional events.
You can build, but there is no necessity to do so, purely cosmetic thing. A flat place with teleporter, vendor nearby, all craft stations and lots of chest is basically all you need. Build is important part of such sandbox games, remove it and there is nothing to do...
Bigger map means only one thing: more of boredome. "More exploring" you say? Well, with compas you go "straight" to be portal and I mean it (go up, dig, no exploration anymore). Dungeons are ALL THE SAME, combination of same rooms, crappy mobs AI and no joy in exploring.. compared to many other Minercraft-like game this aspect is very poor in this game. Not talking about loading time (rougly 30~ seconds map changing on my quite TOP system)..
Water is latest adition, but there is no swimming nor anything to let us swim (aka boats or waterwalking). So prepare to suffer on the bottom of lake. Once I jumped into huge lake of huge world to reach bottom in like 20 seconds.. imagine now the way up.. pressing space makes a JUMP in the water.. higher than normal, but a JUMP......... I personally hate water as it is. I'd turn it off if I could.
Second bigger problem is the light. This game suffer from light implementation, where torch does so little light. It's not minecraft way of mining, where you put torches and they are working. It's some crappy system with potions what last few minutes (requiring more time to collect reagents) or constant switching between torch and pickaxe... yes, you light up to target something to dig and then dig it in absolute darkness.. lots of fun!
Third is inventory.. this game hates PC users (me, you, all of us).. small inventory, lots of chest, constant micro-management.. prepare to do mule-trips after every world (to unload precious and you_dont_know_if_it_is_precious_or_not stuff) to home world.. oh, yeah with ~1 min of seeing nice loading animation which makes me sick and my friend wants to vomit..
Cooperative: makes things double- (tripple-/quadro-) easier. Game is easy enough, but... all difficulty mostly come due to camera, AI and the way of how you deal with stuff: arrows hits other objects (e.g. doors), spell does too litlle damage to be even considered to use (healing spell and some buffs are good), and melee... OMG MELEE.. Are you ready to suffer? Take melee class and get hit by everything..
There are more problems (I'd say much more), but this is already long enough I think. You were warned!

I remember playing the old fan based Grimm Eclipse back when it emerged from the depths of the internet, and thinking to myself ... "Wow for a fan game this is really good! I wonder if RT will ever make an official version of this?" Little did I know at the time that would be a reality.
Ok, so trying my best not to be biased by my fandom, here's my take on the new Grimm Eclipse. It is clearly an early access game. Bits of it are a little rough around the edges, particuarly in the early levels, but that's to be expected. The important detail here is that it doesn't stop the game from being fun ... which it is very.
There were a few issues I noticed early on, such as the absence of a tutorial. Most of the controls are straightforward enough so it isnt too much of an issue, but it did mean that it took some awkward practice before I got the hang of it. In addition, one of Blakes lines in the first level sounds a bit odd, but she evens out later on. Ruby handles quite nicely and for the most part so do the other girls, but they could use a bit of tuning, particuarly Weiss. Her skills are expensive compared to Ruby's and not equivillantly powerful at low levels. That said, the melee combat is very fast paced and exciting once you get used to it. When it comes to ranged combat, you can tell it's definitely meant to be secondary. It can be somewhat difficult to aim from longer ranges, but that could easily be fixed with a small reticule or dot.
I was a little worried about how RT was going to add elements of Left 4 Dead with characters as powerful as team RWBY since in L4D a lot of the fun comes from that feeling of being overwhelmed. However, i'm pleased to say they pulled it off, because team RWBY isnt up agaist just a few grimm, or even a bunch of grimm. Grimm eclipse boasts legitimate hoards of monsters while still maintaining a sense of sheer power with weapons like crescent rose.
So far the game looks great, in my opinion is reasonably priced (with the assumption that more content will be added later on kept in mind), and as an added bonus it ports fairly easily with wineskin, if you want to run it on a Mac. The game requires no additional tweaks to run. RT did a good job coding it. I look forward to seeing where they go with it.

- Funny!! Not just fart jokes and political incorrectness for the whole game as one would (fairly) expect, but genuinely humorous human interaction between the kids as well as some other actually funny recurring jokes that mean you can expect to have a smile on your face for the majority of the game
- Combat system is miles ahead of Stick of Truth, allows for much more planning and strategy with picking your team members + skills. Playing through the game on the hardest combat difficulty is difficult but never feels like it is unfair, as far as I experienced there was no RNG whatsoever
- The characters are very well balanced. No kid is a direct upgrade of another kid, and they all have trade-offs + different moves that make two kids of the same class have their own place in a battle
- Lots of avenues to go down with your character, you start off quite limited but as the game progresses you can morph your character to be whatever you want them to be in terms of both appearance and combat
- None of the kids feel like "Clones" of the others, which is a problem present in a lot of games with many characters to choose from. Their combat abilities + stats vary in usefulness in different scenarios which means that you will probably find yourself using every character at least once in a playthrough
- Sidequests aren't just fetch quests, and battles aren't always just "kill all the enemies". The missions + battles vary greatly throughout the game so you don't have to worry about getting sick and tired of doing the same thing over and over again.
- Visuals look just as true to the show as Stick of Truth, and the menus + attacks as well as all of the other little miscellaneous things that aren't part of the TV show look much cleaner and nicer.
- Took me a decent amount of time to complete just the main story without doing any sidequests. (16 hours on a single playthrough) Not an extremely long game, but much better length than I was expecting from what is basically an interactive South Park episode.

Some good, some bad, but overall a great game.
South Park: The Fractured But Whole is much like The Stick of Truth.  The main differences are a longer story, new jokes, and a revamped combat system.  Gone are the clothing based stats, which I prefer for greater freedom of characters appearance.  Now bonuses come from Artifacts which are equiped to slots that become availible as you gain levels.  The new combat system is fun, but has a few drawbacks.
No game is perfect, but I feel these issues shouldn't exist in a sequel.
First is the fast travel, the distance between these felt great in Stick of Truth.  In The Fractured But Whole however, the fast travel points seem to be clustered on the left and right of the map.  They serve so little over the course of the game, that you hardly notice when they are taken away at one point in the games story.  The new combat system is also not without some issues.  Now you can no longer use an item and attack in the same turn, while some attackers can kill you in 2 attacks and we're not talking about bosses.  The removal of any and all defense options (other than a shield buff), the react system seems to be replaced by a power charge meter buff that's as simple as mashing the key or button.  There's also almost a complete lack of aoe buffs and heals.  However my biggest complaint about combat is that nearly all the Allies have either 1 range left or right, or 4-5 range or both.  This usually ends with Allies or your main character not being able to get into position to attack.  Why can't you attack in any of the 4 directions, idk, but it was a poor choice in my humble opinion.
The last thing I want to say is the game is not very difficult, it's really very casual.  I was able to beat the game on the most difficult settings on the first go, and I only remember dying once during the entire game (in a battle).  Also I rarely used items outside a few of the boss fights. (money was also not an issue, just fight everyone)
While I did have more negative than positive to say, the game was quite fun and entertaining.  While the negatives were more of a minor nuisance.

Explore dungeons, pick fights with well-armed paramilitary organizations, and get plastered all along the way in this classy, less pretentious Fallout 3 spoof!
WASTED is a fun, abide occasionally stupid, FPS dungeon crawler with RPG elements. In a world where only the biggest, dumbest morons survived Reagan's nuclear annihilation of the world, you, the player character (Either your own custom starting character, or a random waster who has "commandeered" your previous character's shack and possessions) are on a quest to get plastered with irradiated alcohol, which will give you a mutation (Perk), or "Hangover" which may or may not be positive. To get the booze, you have to dive into a dungeon, or "Cooler" to get that sweet booze, fighting raiders, angry mutants and, again, Paramilitary organizations who have every reason to kill you. You need to reach the floor exit as fast as possible, because if you take too long, a Purifier (a 600 health, power armor clad murder machine with a minigun) will spawn to murder you, and everyone/thing else on the floor.
The game has randomly generated dungeons, with random routes, enemies, and item spawns. However, because each floor coincides with a specific area of the cooler (living quarters, storage, evacuation area, ect.) those floors will draw from the same level assets. This can make multiple dungeon runs quite repetitive, as there is a real incentive to cut short cooler runs to store particularly valuable loot, or because you found a hangover that is particularly good, or fits well into your character build (which sends you back home, where you then start over again from the first floor on your next run).
There are also random "buzzes" (temporary buffs/debuffs) which can be obtained prior to, or during a cooler run, and can be anything from stat boosts to having your cross-hair hidden. The unmarked flasks inside the dungeon are a particular source of rage in WASTED, as it's safer to ignore the flasks then to risk getting a crippling debuff, particularly on a character you like. This is on top of the already difficult game, where enemies, despite intentionally being stupid for your own entertainment, can do some smart-ish stuff that might kill you (like swarming you with suicide raiders).
The story is charming, in a stupid way, and the combat is fun, but the repetitive nature of the dungeons and the frustration that can result from a crippling debuff or sudden death can act as a serious turnoff for some players, but if you don't mind either of the above issues, WASTED is a fun dungeon crawler with a charming take on nuclear annihilation.

Big online, "Battlefield -type" battles. It feels almost as if Battlefield 2 and Red Orchestra had a baby. Here is some stuff I like about it:
-Stamina meter, no unlimited sprint. Increases the tactical aspect of the game slightly, have to think when and here to use it.
-No zooming when aiming down sights (counting out sniper-rifles and scoped weaponry)
-No regenerating health. Health can be replenished form first-aid crates scattered around bases/capture points
-Different map sizes; small for infantry only combat, medium for infantry + vehicular combat and large for infantry + vehicle + aircraft combat. (Vehicular combat does include armored vehicles such as halftracks and tanks)
-No global chat, you can only use chat within your team and not the opposing team (io. the enemy) This was a surprising move, and eliminated the verbal griefing and
-You earn little bit of gold (purchaseable ingame currency) every day, after your first battle. It's not much, but overtime you can afford small stuff like weapon skins or something.
-You can purchase ANYTHING without using the gold currency, by earning ingame credits. It's a grind, but hey, part of the charm!
-Tanks actually feel dangerous! You can find AT-rocket launchers at captured bases, so unless you earned yourself some credits and purchased one for your class, tanks feel really really scary.
-While tanks are very powerful, they arent impossible to kill. 2-rockets destroy a lighter tank, incapacitate a heavier tank and third one finishes it off.
-As you begin, you have to choose which faction to join: Germany, Soviets or USA. After that, you can't create a new character without spending lots of credits. Makes you care more about your character!
And here comes the bad:
-Some large scale battles last way too long. If teams are too even, prepare to spend the next 2 or 3-hours fighting! You can always drop out and find a new battle, but if you finish it only means more XP and Credits in your pocket.
-Some of the sniper-rifles feel little overpowered. Scoped sniper-rifles can kill you with one shot, despite being the same caliber as a non-scoped rifle of the same faction, which takes between 2-4 rounds to kill. It feels very silly and unrealistic but doesn't ruin the game. Each faction has a 'one-shot-kill-sniper-rfile' so no need to feel jealous there!
-Little difficult to get into; it takes some time to learn how the gamemodes work. To be frank, I'm not totally sure about this myself at this point!
-Baseraping. Now this doesnt happen very often, but sometimes you have a player proning in your spawning area, picking off freshly spawned players of your team.
-Aircraft don't take damage from rifles and assault rifles. When the enemy team has three planes on the air, bombing everything and your team has none, you might have bad time. There stationary AA-guns scattered across the maps, but no indicators to help find them.
-No quick-voice commands. This would be soooo helpful! Easier and faster than typing on the text chat!
SHORT VERSION
