This is the major example of a wasted potential in AAA game. Don't get me wrong - the singleplayer is one of the most intense ones I have ever played. However, the decisions made for the online mode are the prime examples of what not to do with a great product - and how to drive your creation straight to the trash can. Here are the biggest cons that were not present at the release of the game, but are now a thing due to the most mindboggling decisions made by Rockstar Games and Take-Two:
- The studio only supports online mode, and any new DLC vehicles since the beggining of 2016 are not being released to the singleplayer, therefore players which want to test new vehicles before buying them have to mod single player - which Take-Two just made almost impossible by shutting down OpenIV, a modding tool used to mod GTA games since 2009.
- Even with the shift to online, singleplayer is still a lot more immersing. Rockstar encourages players to only play online by releasing free DLC's only to that mode - but online still feels like a cheaper version of the singleplayer experience. Even the simple things, like animals not being present in online since 2013, make online appear much less polished than the singleplayer.
- Another big problem are the Shark Cards - the prices of them are just plain stupid. Overall, the pricing of vehicles shifted a lot after the heist update in 2015. The prices of Shark Cards did not change since 2013. Before the heist update, the biggest 8MLN in-game dollars Megalodon Shark Card could buy you almost all of the in-game content for 100$. All of the content from the newest DLC, Gunrunning, costs around 40MLN in-game dollars - which translates roughly to 500$. We have to remember that all of the DLC's since the release of the game are free - that "unfortunately" does not justify the content hiding behind a 500$ paywall.
- If you are one of those people that do not want to spend any money via microtransactions, turn away from this title. Everything is hiding behind a neverending grind. In-game jobs pay nothing, and still, after 2 years, the best way to make money is by grinding heists - which released in 2015. The community is so upset at this fact that every two online lobbies, you will see people begging modders to drop them money.
- Adding to the topic of modders - online mode is filled with them. I, personally, have a mixed opinion about them. Rockstar can't control them since the release for PC. Modders can create the most hilarious and fun moments of online - or they can simply wipe your account and even steal your IP adress - as you can see, they are totally out of Rockstar's control.
- Last thing I am going to write about is purely subjective, and is about the content added in the new DLC's. I am one of those "rare" casual players that would like to drive vehicles into the back of the Titan (which is not possible since the release of the game) or go offroading and hunting in the countryside with a couple of friends (as I said before, hunting is not possible due to animals not being present in the online mode). Instead, we get new super cars added in almost every DLC. For me, GTA has always been about having fun - not grinding missions to unlock the "fun" content. Even simple things like custom lobbies with police, player icons or friendly fire disabled - which were present in GTA IV - are not possible in GTA Online.
Thank you for reading my review. As I said, in my opinion, GTA V is the best example of a wasted potential I have ever seen in a video game. This game released in 2013 and with the right development could still be one of the top contenders for the best sandbox, best racing game and even the best fps (because of the next gen option of first person camera mode). Unfortunately, in my opinion, it will not be any of those any soon. Also, adding more context to my review - I have been playing this game since the release, both on Xbox 360 and PC. I think that with the recent shutdown of OpenIV, it is the highest time the community should speak up and protest against the greed of Rockstar and Take-Two.
Sincerely, a disappointed GTA fan.

I played this game on a PC with a usual monitor, without DK2. This game is good for VR but bad for a desktop PC. As a non-DK2 owner I can only give it a thumbs down. Maybe the devs should have just waited for the Oculus Rift to come out and publish the game then. On Steam and desktop this game is somewhat out of place.
It's like a shooting range, where you shoot at moving cubes and run around a small area for a better shot angle. The innovative part is that you do this 4 times per level, and each time you do this you are recorded, so next time you will see your own copies doing what you did last time. With the efforts of all your doubles combined, it plays like a co-op game. Sounds fun, right? Well, it is for a short time, just don't expect too much.
Usually you will shoot a portion of the enemies in one run, another portion in the second run etc. Or, since it's all pretty casual and you won't plan much, you will just shoot what you can in the first run, then, recalling what you had difficulties with (like the tough yellow cubes), you focus on those in the next runs, maybe also guessing which weapon will be best for the situation. You also run around collecting loot (small dots which make a typical "score" sound reminding Mario-like 2D platformers). For the coins you buy straightforward upgrades for the weapons (more damage, faster firing, more spread, faster rockets etc). The game feels like an attraction in a theme park where you compete with other visitors to win a teddy bear for your girlfriend.
There is even a level designer but it's awkward to use on a PC since it's obviously made for people wearing a VR headset and struggling with its limitations. The graphics are bright and feel casual. The music is disco-style; it's good but somehow it adds to the game's shallow feel. The levels are pretty varied, struggling to postpone the rising boredom. You may want to play it 15-20 minutes in a session when you are waiting for something - much like a mobile/flash game.
The feels though.... Buy the game.

This game is sheer brilliance, and I really mean it. It's not often I say that about any game at all. At the time of writing this review, I realise that I only have a little over an hour in it, but that's all I need to know that this game is amazing, and the hours will for sure be racking up in this game. Don't let the screenshots determine what this game is, this game cannot be described in a single screenshot. This game either requires you to play it for yourself and learn every little minor and major detail to help you win the game. Let's get down to the basics of what this game really is, and how it is absolute brilliance in a single game.
Before we get into what the game really is and how you play, I think it's important that I bring this up; this is something that I love in games. As you open the game, you aren't greeted by the usual, boring, same-old menus. No, you are greeted by.. Well, the game! That's right, you play straight from there. There is an amazingly simple but somewhat flabberghasting easter egg in this "hub" if you want to call it that. It's not my place to spoil it here, that's something you'll have to find.
To start playing, all you have to do is hit a big, floating "play" button. That's it. You're then welcomed by 3 seperate menus.
Campaign; your basic campaign, where you fight the evil cubes and try to emerge victorious.
Daily Challenge; community designed challenges which you can play every day.
And for those of you who have a more creative side, you can also create a custom arena. You can choose to play others custom levels or you can create your own. That's something you'll have to find out yourself, I haven't even tried to do anything with that yet.
If you are wondering, "are the enemies.. really just cubes?". Yes, the enemies are basic cubes which follow a simple principal.
- Red Cubes are the WEAKEST cubes with the lowest HP.
- White Cubes are the NORMAL cubes with normal HP.
- Yellow Cubes are the BEEFY cubes with high amounts of HP.
Each cube will reward you with a yellow or white smaller cube. All you need to know about that is, those are your score.
A white, small cube is equal to 1 gold, whereas the yellow, smaller cubes are equal to 10 gold.
So, enough about just the menus, I think it's time we talked about the game. The game has a dubstep soundtrack, and before any of you run away due to the fact that you hate dubstep, you have to understand this games theme. It's fast paced, high-octane action. The dubstep, if doing nothing else, will just hype you up and make you ready for the next spawn of enemies. The dubstep soundtrack, as someone who despises dubstep, actually really fits the games feel. I mean, the only music genre that pops to mind when you think high paced action with badass explosions, it's got to be dubstep, right?
Aesthetically, this game is gorgeous. No, I really mean it is GORGEOUS. The thought cubes to some people will probably make you think that this game is some Minecraft clone, and I am included in that general consensus. But when I started to play, I realise that this game is way more than that. It's nothing like Minecraft at all. This game has so much potential to be one of the best games out there, I just hope that the devs can do something about how short this game is. I mean, 3 areas each with 5 levels is only a total of 15 levels. Whilst that isn't that bad, it's not exactly great. And that's actually my biggest flaw with this game. Sure, it has tonnes of replayability, but it will only last for so long. If the devs can add more things to the game to keep people playing and gaining the game more publicity, then it's their choice to realise that that's what they need to do.
So, the basics of this game then.
- Fast paced, cube killin' action.
- Dubstep which fits the games theme.
- Amazing amounts of replayability.
- 6 great and very differing weapons to choose from.
- Tonnes of fun.
Although this game would be an instant GOTY for me if it was just slightly longer!! Just even 3 or 4 more chapters added on to increase the level of content and playtime that I can get out of this game. I want to play it for so much longer, but I don't know how long my willpower will stick out with no new Missions in sight. Great game, very short though.
(Great price, too.)
So, final conclusion, get this game if you want to have a true gem in your Steam library. One of the best games out there at the minute and I cannot wait to play tonnes more!
Have a great day/night everyone!

This game is what Diablo 3 should have been. Torchlight 2 is really the penultimate ARPG. Hundreds of hours of engaging gameplay, addicting combat that has weight to it unlike PoE or Diablo, and a huge world littered with interesting storylines and tough dungeons. Abilities are plentiful and well varied, most including a flashy animation that brings life to the game. The visuals are well polished, however they are not straining to your hardware. Torchlight 2 and the first game which I also recommend will run on pretty much any computer so specs will not be an issue. There is lots of color in the game, and different environments really feel distinct and unique. Co-op is one of the best parts of the game, as the game only gets more fun as you add more people. There is a large active community around this game and the Workshop has tons of awesome mods that make the replayability of Torchlight 2 just utterly insane. You can have dozens of classes installed with the right mods, each with their own seperate abilities and skill trees. This is a very well made game and there is content constantly being added, you can tell the developers at Runic set out to make the ARPG they and many others always wanted, and they couldn't have accomplished that task more. The only gripes I have with this game are the music, which is bland and boring, and the fact that there were no respec potions in the game, which were present in Torchlight 1, however a simple mod puts them in the game and fixes that right up so I have no quarrel there anymore. I wish the graphics of Torchlight 2 would have been of higher quality, but even so I still find it looks better than most other ARPG's, except for maybe Path of Exile. Maybe that's just an issue with this genre as a whole. All in all definitely pick up this game, it's well worth it and I can see it being a full $60 and I would still have no problem with the price, as there's just so much content in this game. If you like any game similar to Diablo or RPG's in general, this game is for you.

There are many ARPGs on the market. Like Diablo, Titan Quest, Sacred, Van Helsing or Divine Divinity but how does Torchlight 2 hold up compared to other titles in the genre?
Pretty damn well I would say. Torchlight 2 is an excellent game that does many things right and some things wrong. Simply the low price is already an huge incentive to buy the game if you like the genre.
The things that make Torchlight 2 so great are the solid and polished gameplay, tons of loot, unique art style and cooperative multiplayer. The game feels really nicely designed and the gameplay is fast and frantic, the interface provides every information that you need in an instant and the controls work like a charm. It's really rewarding to smash through massive amounts of enemies with your skills and check the loot that you obtained. The basic premise works flawless, killing monsters, getting loot and leveling up. The game doesn't look all that great but the artstyle is cohesive and pleasing to the eye, there is a lot of variation in terms of armor, weapons, locations and enemies. Furthermore the multiplayer is really great, playing with some friends is a terrific experience. Each class feels individual and plays differently, personally I don't like them as much but they're more refreshing than the standard classes from other titles. The skill tree isn't that amazing and a lot of skills are just standard rpg stuff, nevertheless there are some really satisfying abilities available.
The downside of Torchlight 2 is that it can be quite repetitive, especially in the singleplayer. There are huge maps and dungeons filled with monsters. After a while it's pretty much the same. Each area has their own enemy types that you will be fighting for a long while. The game immediately throws everything at you, so there isn't much to discover or explore. You will usually find some dungeons with typical fetchquests that aren't that interesting. The story is pretty boring and uninteresting, it's all about the gameplay. So there aren't any surprises or epic adventures, the basic formula is to go into a dungeon. Kill everything and then vanquish the final boss.
Nevertheless this game absolutely enjoyable and offers a lot of content. Especially the multiplayer which is a blast to play with buddies.. I definitely recommend this game, furthermore there are multiple difficulties available and randomly generated maps.

There is a good variety of items which have a small effect with a lot of impact, also the choice between an item and bombs is sometimes really hard, both are really important, without bombs you'll have a hard time getting through the enemies (bombs help avoiding and killing them) but items will save you a lot of health and will often help you with the later levels. Also, if you purchase anything in the early levels it'll be hard or even impossible to go through the hard route, however, the items will cost more the further you progress.
Overall it's a terrifyingly hard game, but even so a great timekiller. Has tons of replayability value and is definitely worth the money.

My evaluation is based on standard level playing.  Therefore higher difficulties may cause different gameplays or even some of the situation below to change or stop from happening.
Good parts
- great graphics (scenary wise, buildings, ...)
- playing campain up to mission #8 should give you aprox 16 hours of play (if like me you like to kill every single ennemies)
- destroying ground vehicles with a snipping gun (I know it does not make sense)
Bad parts
- soldiers animations have not been quality tested, sometimes they will make a 90 degree turn instantly, sometimes they will walk a bit crouchy (knee bended) for no reasons, animations in general is smooth but sometimes you definitively see when it changes from one animation cycle to another
- key scenes are automatically played as soon as you reached the icon destination no matter what was going on at the time (ex: you being chased and shot at). As soon as animation is stopped, its like nothing was going on before
- soliders are the dumbest ones I have ever seen. You kill soldier-a standing next to soldier-b. Soldier-b raise alarm. Alarm goes off 2 min after. Soldier-b goes back to his spot next to the dead soldier-a as if nothing ever happened. Therefore you can just kill them one by one, stay hidden, wait for the alerts to stop and then kill the next one
- if you cause an alert where they see you, they will stop looking for you after 5-10 min if you manage to hide away or run away (really would an amy stop looking for someone they had a spotting confirmation and had solidiers killed by that ennemy ?)
- interration is extreamly limited to picking ammo, health kit, letters, maps, playing cards, climing up to get to a 2-4 feet of the next flat surface (you cannot climb hills or mountains unless there is a flat root to it), the only way to turn off an oil lamp is to shoot at it
- sometimes ennemy dont seam to see you when you are expecting to see you (not often)
- when you want to start running right away from a crouching position you have to hitt sprint and standing up twice or it will just start moving semi crouch at normal speed (not good when you have been spotted)
- night time is almost as illuminated as morning time, it is not really night time, game dev did not do a proper illumination compilation so everything is visible, there are no dark areas
- coop games on server list is almost non existing, its just about player vs player, other kinds of game are almost non present (at least the few times I checked)
Overall game is kinda dumb but at least you get the satisfaction of head snipping.  But honnestly with this game now being at version-5, I was expecting v3 to be a bit more realistic.  It will give you a good idea of what this series look like.  Other then graphic wise, game feels like it was rushed to production without proper quality testing.

Review Revision 7/5/16 - Forever Fall Update
Cons/Issues(and fixes) as of 6/5/16:
- NO kill assists, aka no EXP if you help kill an enemy, last person to hit an enemy gets all the sweet EXP which is really annoying and unbalanced. Like, I'd wail on an Alpha Beowulf for Minutes and then all of a sudden Yang kills it with a special and I don't get♥♥♥♥♥♥for it.
- Lack of Lock on and no centered-behind character-camera: When shooting enemies you are never sure which one you are shooting at since your character just chooses the furthest one away, but you cannot decide which one it will target
- Can't select Forever Fall as a Starting Area (aka skip First Campaign)
- No Leveling past Lvl 10 even though you continue straight into Forever Fall after the First Campaign
Minor Issues:
- Subtitles often appear in huge chunks of text, making it hard to read
- Subtitles sometimes don't "scroll", aka get cut off
-  (Personal Issue) I can't seem to be able to adjust audio in Level (aka after using the sliders it didn't change anything)
- Not many objectives so far, mainly just "Protect X from 4 Waves of Grimm"
- Invisible Walls, SO MANY INVISIBLE WALLS, it breaks immersion and lowers exploration
- Mini Map is... not really a MiniMap, just a radar
Pros:
- Very pretty, especially love the new Visuals of Forever Fall!
- Runs smoothly on my PC (Win 8.1, GeForce GTX750Ti, 8GB Ram)
- Interesting Story so far, Introducing new thing sto the Lore.
- New and interesting Grimm!
- Replay Value to some extend (Playing as all 4 characters / using different Builds)
- Definitely fun to play
- Combat improved a lot since the Combat Beta. It is not fun and not just "button mashing" !
- The new Style of the models is something I personally really like. It looks more like its own Style instead of an MMD Ripoff.
- Forever Fall Campaign adds new mechanics (Keys)
- Added Team attacks, which is a nice way to explore the idea of Shared XP !
- Well balanced Counter attacks ! (even tho Grimm still block a tiny bit too much ? )
- Game adjusts difficulty based on the amount of players !
Sugggestions:
- Remove Invisible Walls and switch them out with maybe Trees, high ledges or Buildings to indicate: "You're not supposed to go there"
- Add more secret areas in which you can fight. Before the update you could jump through a mountain to get to an extra area, after the patch said mountain was removed and it's now main part of the map

- Alternate Outfits maybe one day? Like, if all of us played the same character? Or at least different colour scheme (similar to the Alpha on the RT site way back).

Below are reviews of all the updates. In order of most recent to when it released. Please realize that this game may have issues all games do. Needs more butter upd8: The charecters look better now than they ever have. Yea the first models were more direct copies from the show, the second style was more like a realistic doll that i saw alot of potential in. This third instalment of *sprites* is a sweet middle ground between the two. OTher people see this as a sin (becuase its not whats exactly in the show) However what is saying that as a company you cant go a diffrent route with a game then is in the base its off of. The removal of forced ssao and lighting effects should be a whole lot better for anyone running the game on a non-beast of a computer. Forever Fall update: I enjoy the new look of the charecters, It is much more refined, and from a game astetic pleases the eye more with the refinement of the stages. Yea the faces are dead and lifeless like a sharks eyes, but they said they are gonna fix it. I have not had a problem with framerate, cliping, or anything else. A large protion of the negatives come from people who didnt opt into combat revision, and combat revision fixed the game imo. Team attacks can be chained to finish large portion of grim, and clear a wave faster than a charectert can turn to dust. :) The new stage looks amazing and shows a good direction for the game to go. I wish their was more than one puzzle to complete but the one was super fun and i loved that the charecters in game voiced to acknoledge the goal. For someone who has played this ithin 40 min of it releasing. and unlocked everything, its still fun and something that can become a great game. Combat revision update: In short the new update has made this game a thousand times better. IT not only improved on everything they had going for it, but made this game a hell of a lot more easeir to play and more enjoyable.
Original Review: So after playing this game a bit. and now with the improvemnt on combat, scratch that the MASSIVE IMRPOVEMENT on combat. this game is just all the better. For anyone who played it pre update 3, its gonna take a learning curve. I will say that there needs to be a way to look up combos, or see moves well. It just kinda has you figure them out yourself. Not that i hate that, but i can see casual gamers have a whiney time trying to fiure it out. (HINT: on a xbox controller x is light y is heavy, and you can charge up y BOOM! mind blown) Team attacks are pretty fun but not very smooth right now(not a big worry cause they are cool to see.) The counter system is probably the BEST! thing in the game now, cause it can really help you do things that were hard for a solo player, or small group. Which is keep up with the beowolfs. The new camera system rocks. You can now see a close up of all the 4 charecters and it really shows the detail that was put into them. Also the fight camera contol and lock on are supreme. Like a chelupa supreme. To stray away from the one armed jokes there is a glitch where yang isn't a whiney mope for a good portion of the game. Even if you dont watch the show, or care about it. This game is fun, and for an early acess is pretty well done with a team of under 20 people working on it. PROPS!

I was both amused and somewhat disappointed with Deponia. The characters are amusing, the humor appropriate, and the plot is something of a nostalgic classic with a sarcastic twist.
The disappointment stems mostly from the game adhering a bit too much to the classic pixel hunt gameplay, with the twisted puzzle logic that point and click adventures are notorious for: solving puzzles can sometimes be a matter of just trying every possible permutation of solution until you figure out what unique (read: ridiculous) logic the creator was using to imagine a solution. I would have hoped that a modern point and click adventure might improve upon this shortcoming somewhat from where it existed at the genre's height. On the plus side, at least we don't need to call a hotline for tips anymore... help is just a google search away.
That being said, if you're a fan of point and click adventures, and interested in buying another, then you're no doubt comfortable with this shortcoming, and that's why I recommend it.

I'm going to start by saying something that seems contradictory to the totality of this review: I LOVE this game. It's such a great, simple concept. It's fast-paced arena action that would keep you entertained for hours. That is, if it weren't for the constant crashes. Apparently the engine the game runs on is not too compatible with Windows 8. And EVERY FIVE MINUTES the game crashes, and I lose progress. That is not a good thing for this kind of game, which should be one I can sit down in my addiction and enjoy it for hours. And it doesn't seem like the devs have any plans to fix this anytime soon, which is the cruelest shame. I don't know what percentage of PC users use Windows 8. But for those who do, I cannot recommend this game. At least on Steam. My suggestion: go download the game directly from the website. It doesn't crash every five minutes for no reason there. The only crashes I've found so far happen for specific reasons: like blasting more than two enemies with the flamethrower or cracking a shotgun in the big guy's face. Either way, this game would be so much more satisfying and probably one of the most popular and critically acclaimed F2P games on Steam if not for these major issues that only serve to frustrate and negate the fun from this would-be amazing game. In conclusion I don't recommend you download this from Steam, but from their website. It's much more stable, and you don't lose nearly as much progress when you crash from a stray bullet.

This is the major example of a wasted potential in AAA game. Don't get me wrong - the singleplayer is one of the most intense ones I have ever played. However, the decisions made for the online mode are the prime examples of what not to do with a great product - and how to drive your creation straight to the trash can. Here are the biggest cons that were not present at the release of the game, but are now a thing due to the most mindboggling decisions made by Rockstar Games and Take-Two:
- The studio only supports online mode, and any new DLC vehicles since the beggining of 2016 are not being released to the singleplayer, therefore players which want to test new vehicles before buying them have to mod single player - which Take-Two just made almost impossible by shutting down OpenIV, a modding tool used to mod GTA games since 2009.
- Even with the shift to online, singleplayer is still a lot more immersing. Rockstar encourages players to only play online by releasing free DLC's only to that mode - but online still feels like a cheaper version of the singleplayer experience. Even the simple things, like animals not being present in online since 2013, make online appear much less polished than the singleplayer.
- Another big problem are the Shark Cards - the prices of them are just plain stupid. Overall, the pricing of vehicles shifted a lot after the heist update in 2015. The prices of Shark Cards did not change since 2013. Before the heist update, the biggest 8MLN in-game dollars Megalodon Shark Card could buy you almost all of the in-game content for 100$. All of the content from the newest DLC, Gunrunning, costs around 40MLN in-game dollars - which translates roughly to 500$. We have to remember that all of the DLC's since the release of the game are free - that "unfortunately" does not justify the content hiding behind a 500$ paywall.
- If you are one of those people that do not want to spend any money via microtransactions, turn away from this title. Everything is hiding behind a neverending grind. In-game jobs pay nothing, and still, after 2 years, the best way to make money is by grinding heists - which released in 2015. The community is so upset at this fact that every two online lobbies, you will see people begging modders to drop them money.
- Adding to the topic of modders - online mode is filled with them. I, personally, have a mixed opinion about them. Rockstar can't control them since the release for PC. Modders can create the most hilarious and fun moments of online - or they can simply wipe your account and even steal your IP adress - as you can see, they are totally out of Rockstar's control.
- Last thing I am going to write about is purely subjective, and is about the content added in the new DLC's. I am one of those "rare" casual players that would like to drive vehicles into the back of the Titan (which is not possible since the release of the game) or go offroading and hunting in the countryside with a couple of friends (as I said before, hunting is not possible due to animals not being present in the online mode). Instead, we get new super cars added in almost every DLC. For me, GTA has always been about having fun - not grinding missions to unlock the "fun" content. Even simple things like custom lobbies with police, player icons or friendly fire disabled - which were present in GTA IV - are not possible in GTA Online.
Thank you for reading my review. As I said, in my opinion, GTA V is the best example of a wasted potential I have ever seen in a video game. This game released in 2013 and with the right development could still be one of the top contenders for the best sandbox, best racing game and even the best fps (because of the next gen option of first person camera mode). Unfortunately, in my opinion, it will not be any of those any soon. Also, adding more context to my review - I have been playing this game since the release, both on Xbox 360 and PC. I think that with the recent shutdown of OpenIV, it is the highest time the community should speak up and protest against the greed of Rockstar and Take-Two.
Sincerely, a disappointed GTA fan.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

This is the major example of a wasted potential in AAA game. Don't get me wrong - the singleplayer is one of the most intense ones I have ever played. However, the decisions made for the online mode are the prime examples of what not to do with a great product - and how to drive your creation straight to the trash can. Here are the biggest cons that were not present at the release of the game, but are now a thing due to the most mindboggling decisions made by Rockstar Games and Take-Two:
- The studio only supports online mode, and any new DLC vehicles since the beggining of 2016 are not being released to the singleplayer, therefore players which want to test new vehicles before buying them have to mod single player - which Take-Two just made almost impossible by shutting down OpenIV, a modding tool used to mod GTA games since 2009.
- Even with the shift to online, singleplayer is still a lot more immersing. Rockstar encourages players to only play online by releasing free DLC's only to that mode - but online still feels like a cheaper version of the singleplayer experience. Even the simple things, like animals not being present in online since 2013, make online appear much less polished than the singleplayer.
- Another big problem are the Shark Cards - the prices of them are just plain stupid. Overall, the pricing of vehicles shifted a lot after the heist update in 2015. The prices of Shark Cards did not change since 2013. Before the heist update, the biggest 8MLN in-game dollars Megalodon Shark Card could buy you almost all of the in-game content for 100$. All of the content from the newest DLC, Gunrunning, costs around 40MLN in-game dollars - which translates roughly to 500$. We have to remember that all of the DLC's since the release of the game are free - that "unfortunately" does not justify the content hiding behind a 500$ paywall.
- If you are one of those people that do not want to spend any money via microtransactions, turn away from this title. Everything is hiding behind a neverending grind. In-game jobs pay nothing, and still, after 2 years, the best way to make money is by grinding heists - which released in 2015. The community is so upset at this fact that every two online lobbies, you will see people begging modders to drop them money.
- Adding to the topic of modders - online mode is filled with them. I, personally, have a mixed opinion about them. Rockstar can't control them since the release for PC. Modders can create the most hilarious and fun moments of online - or they can simply wipe your account and even steal your IP adress - as you can see, they are totally out of Rockstar's control.
- Last thing I am going to write about is purely subjective, and is about the content added in the new DLC's. I am one of those "rare" casual players that would like to drive vehicles into the back of the Titan (which is not possible since the release of the game) or go offroading and hunting in the countryside with a couple of friends (as I said before, hunting is not possible due to animals not being present in the online mode). Instead, we get new super cars added in almost every DLC. For me, GTA has always been about having fun - not grinding missions to unlock the "fun" content. Even simple things like custom lobbies with police, player icons or friendly fire disabled - which were present in GTA IV - are not possible in GTA Online.
Thank you for reading my review. As I said, in my opinion, GTA V is the best example of a wasted potential I have ever seen in a video game. This game released in 2013 and with the right development could still be one of the top contenders for the best sandbox, best racing game and even the best fps (because of the next gen option of first person camera mode). Unfortunately, in my opinion, it will not be any of those any soon. Also, adding more context to my review - I have been playing this game since the release, both on Xbox 360 and PC. I think that with the recent shutdown of OpenIV, it is the highest time the community should speak up and protest against the greed of Rockstar and Take-Two.
Sincerely, a disappointed GTA fan.

First of all, I have to admit that I bought this game solely because I am a fan of RWBY series. The game in current state already shown a great deal of potentials despite it being an early access game. The graphic is very similar to Yandere Simulator and the vocal is minimum but on point.
The control is fairly simple and, personally, I would like to see it being developed into something similar to Mortal Kombat. With that being said, I cannot get my Steam Controller to work with the game yet and that's pretty much my only complain.

While the game is early access, so some flaws are expected, overall I felt like it was a pretty solid game.  I only played as Blake and Ruby, so I can't speak for the other characters, but I felt for the most part they were the same, but they did differ at key points, as in their specials.  While Blake was more hit and run with focused damage, Ruby had more of an AOE feel to her.  The potential for the game to be a fun hack and slash game is there, and I am interested to see it evolve as time goes by.  As the game stands this moment, I do not believe it is worth the $15.  With only four levels of content, no real plot line behind it, and the minor bugs here and there.  For the bugs I have found most of them have been graphical: characters not running correctly, subtitles only showing the beginning of the dialog, and things like that.  However, I did notice a hit box error as well, it was small only with the beginning of the weapon arc not registering me hitting a crate.  All in all, I will be keeping an eye on this game to see how it changes in the coming weeks, but unless you are looking to play this with friends, or are interested in another round of beta testing I would not recommend buying this game in its current state.  I will also be updating my review to reflect the game's state in the future.

Amazing game for what it is. Yes it does lack content, which is a major problem i see on the review board, but that's to be expected from Early Access. They have already said that they will add more content so no need to worry there.
Combat is extremely fluid and feels amazing. True to the hack n slash style. The dodge mechanic seems to work well for the most part, can also use it to reset your combo so you can keep hitting enemies.
Story is obviously lacking but i played over a good hour with 2 other people through all the missions/areas. The game seems to lean towards fighting waves of enemies while defending something but then changes that up with a more objective based mission for the last one.
The skill system is one of my favorite parts and i cant wait to see it expanded upon. They do a kind of trinity mastery system kind of like WoW used to do except focusing on your three main skills, upgrading them and even being able to unlock new a new skill upgrade through killing enemies with that skill which is really cool. There are also passive upgrades like health (aura) or special and can unlock further tiers of this as well. Lots of choices for each character and lots of variations for different builds.
Also co-op with friends is so much fun. Gives me a L4D vibe with the lobby system and character selection and all, being 4 characters of course :)
Overall i highly recommend this game right now if you are a huge fan and want to see the combat system. If you are looking for a more full game with a large amount of content, something over 5 hours or so then its probably not for you YET.

Portal Knights, at first glance, looks like a pretty remake of Minecraft. It has the same blocky, cartoony charm, and does have exploring, fighting, mining and building as its main features. The game is, in some ways remarkably similar, but in other ways, remarkably different.
I'll be using spoiler tags to hide both challenge-reducing tactics as well as actual game spoilers (for those who want to experience the game with zero advance knowledge, which can actualy provide a lot more fun to the game for first playthrough).
The class and leveling systems offer some options for how you'd like to experience the game.  Warrior focuses on melee damage, Ranger focuses on bows and evasion tactics, and Mage focuses on spells and elemental weaknesses. All classes (as of this post) can use all armors, have a mana bar, and can use all skills, though due to primary stat gains on levelup, all classes will perform their niche better than the others, as expected. That said, you can totally hand a warrior a magic staff or a ranger a battleaxe and theyll use it no problem.
Combat in general is loads of fun and, when you're progressing normally, a decent challenge. The dodging mechanic brings some fun to it, and the game will punish you pretty harshly for not avoiding damage, which in some regards is really refreshing. I got some Ocarina of Time flashbacks with the dodging and lockon systems, doding and then striking my foe, then blindsided by another random foe that just showed up, or dodging across the landscape because it's far faster than any movement speed bonus ever is. Most enemies have some kind of ranged magic attack
.
Magic follows an "opposing elements" theme
, fire and ice are weak to each other, electro and nature are weak to each other, and light(holy) and dark(astral) are weak to each other. Mage needs to focus on exploiting these weaknesses. At endgame stats, the difference in damage between the early nature staff and the later game
staff is not much after weakness bonus is applied, so
simply due to weapon power rating, which is a very nice thing to see. The spells, while only one spell (with varying ranks) exists per element, have specific uses, and are good in some despite the enemy you face.
Levelups yield some customizable stat points as well as a few instant primary stat allocations. You gain talents at specific levels (2, 5, and then every 5th) and they all lend something to the class or something generally useful to the game (except that level 10 talent for all classes
). All talents can be hot-swapped without having to be anyplace specicif or spending something. You can open the menu and change your build whenever you like, but you only get one talent per tier, but there's no pressure to really specialize your talent build. There is an item in game that will allow you to reset your stat allocations, so if you screw up, you can redo it.
The islands are undeniably beautiful and fun. Each Island has a biome, and its own list of spawns, plants, and resources, and are plainly shown to the player on selection from the world map. It's easy to know where to go for a specific resource or enemy, and that is glorious. It definately aids in the building and equipment progression aspects of the game, and is a very welcome feature. The game is further enhanced by the ability to simply "step" up one full block without jumping.
One thing about PKs that im conflicted on is the separation of Worlds and Characters. On one hand, it's nice to take my fully leveled character to a new world
and just have fun tearing through it or mine more resources that my already mined world lacks, and on the other hand, the first time I brought a new character to a completed world with full
gear and went straight to the final areas and leveled to 30 in under an hour. I feel this really diminishes the replay value of the adventure since many players will want to get to level cap ASAP. While the game offers you the choice, I fear most players will take that choice, which really reduces the adventuring lifespan of the game.
Building takes a lot of keys from minecraft, and in any area that isnt a boss zone, you can build freely. Most objects, once placed, will happily hover (even furniture) until broken manually. There are a handful of objects that will break when the block theyre attached to is broken, such as plants, lights, and doors. While the game doesnt offer as much variety as Minecraft does for building blocks and decorations, there's plenty to build something interesting and unique.
The endgame of Portal Knights is literally building your house/castle/whatever, hunting recipes and vanity items, or farming
for Energy Crystals for top tier equipment, bosses, hardmode bosses (challenging even with overpowered builds), or world events. Given that only players you allow into your world will ever see your house, thats basically for showing off to your friends or amusing yourself (which in itself isn't neccesarilty bad). While not entirely surprising, how long this lasts for you depends on how much you enjoy the building aspect of the game, and combat as a whole.

I'll start this off with - it's fairly fun, and looks okay for what it is.  I find most Unity games have something odd about the way they play, look and feel.  This one is no different, but someone spent a lot of effort on it and that shows.  I enjoy the graphics even though they aren't fantastic.  The weapon variety is okay and there are a good number of different types of weapons.  Some of the bonuses on certain weapons and gear make sense and are fun.  Plus, it's like playing Escape from LA and Escape from New York - the game.  Post apoc. 1980s.
So, before you read my gripes - I'm glad I bought it and I'm glad I was able to support another decent indie dev.
I've already played it more than I thought I would, and I like it more than I thought I would.  I do have some issues with the way the game plays, the way combat works and a few other things but overall, I'd recommend this as long as you know the game's not perfect, it's quirky and it has some issues.
I find the fact that I can only hold one stack of any given type of item very annoying.  If I have a pistol, I want pistol ammo.  Multiple stacks of it.  If I have room for a stack of shotgun shells, I have room for another stack of pistol ammo instead.  If I need to collect 10 of an item for a crafting project, but can only carry 5 in a stack even if I have several open inventory spaces then I question the reasoning behind the inventory system design.  I feel it's an artificial limit to make the game "harder", but I could be wrong.
Running back and forth in the player's home to move crafting materials around is busy work and waste of time.  All items should be accessable at crafting stations if you put them in the main stash - just to save time picking up five of an item at a time and running back and forth over and over.  Fixing the previous item I mentioned would help with this a bit.
I don't enjoy that there are stat or skill boosts are on items.  I'm not sure why, but I don't like it.  I'd prefer a skill and stat system where I picked my stats and skills.  I'd be okay if they were random at the beginning so yoi'd have to adjust play style to each character's strengths.  I'd like it if I could slowly improve skills or stats through use - whether via levels, experience, stat points gained every floor or, well, anything but the way it works now.
The weapons.  Some of the early firearms are way, way too weak.  I can punch a guy out in two hits, and he's dead, but if I unload 6-10 shots into him he keeps coming like nothing happened.  The starter pistols all seem to do 1 to 2 damage, wheras basic melee weapons do a bit more, and often kill the weaker enemies in one hit if you hit them with one power attack.
The booze.  I know the whole point of the game is the booze - but the flasks that aren't marked are often terrible so I avoid 'em like the plague.  And I can't pick them up to use them later, or sell them to the bartender.  The end-level-pass-out-immediately-and-go-back-home booze is often benificial, but at least you SEE what your options are before you drink those.  But... how do you get back home?  You pass out and teleport home?  Why can't I get back to where I left off?  Gotta grind through the first chunk of the cooler every single time.  It sometimes gets a bit too grind-tastic for me.
The game menus are okay, not perfect but they work.  The interface could use some work - like if I find a bag (bags give more inventory space) then I should be able to equip it without removing another item first.  Speaking of gear - I think that I should be able to set my gear's quick number keys from the loot screen so I don't have to loot, exit, enter inventory, hit the corresponding # key then exit the screen again.  Clunky.
You can't unload firearms.  If there's a way to do it, I haven't found it.  I usually just fire all the rounds, drop the gun and equip the next one if I'm worried about ammno.  Seriously though - f I can reload it, I should be able to unload it as well and use that mag or those rounds in another firearm of the same type.
So, yeah, recommend - with the usual caveat.  Know what you're buying, get it on sale and, for goodness sakes - don't stand in the green puddles.

Anomaly Mobile Campaign is, as the name suggests, an additional campaign for Anomaly Warzone Earth, primarily designed for mobile devices, and later ported to PC.
Gameplay is the same tower offence style where you buy tanks, APCs etc and select the route they will use to travel around the map while destroying or avoiding the alien towers. The biggest difference is you don't have the commander unit running around, but you can still deploy powers like repair and air strike by just clicking where you want to use them.
The campaign is quite short at 2.5 hours, there is an extra wave based mode but except for the lack of commander, its identical to the same mode in the original game. I didn't encounter any bugs, but there's a lack of keyboard short cuts compared to the original, clearly influenced by the mobile control scheme.
Overall its worth playing if a) you enjoyed the original game and b) you pick it up on sale - I recently bought it for 90% off which seems like a fair price.

If your looking for a review on this game you've come to the wrong place, but if your looking for an outstanding pie recipe you've come to the right place.
Ingredients:
1. 6 tablespoons unsalted butter
2. 1/2 cup white sugar
3. 1/2 cup brown sugar
4. 1/4 cup water
5. 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon
6. 1 pinch salt
7. 5 apples - peeled, cored and sliced
8. 1 pastry for double-crust pie
Directions:
1. Preheat oven to 425 degrees F (220 degrees C).
2. Combine butter, white sugar, brown sugar, water, cinnamon, and salt in a saucepan over medium heat. Bring to a boil, remove from heat and set aside.
3. Roll out half the pastry to fit a 9-inch pie plate. Place bottom crust in pie plate; pour in apple slices.
4. Roll out top crust into a 10-inch circle. Cut into 8 (1-inch) wide strips with a sharp paring knife or pastry wheel. Weave the pastry strips, one at a time, into a lattice pattern. Fold the ends of the lattice strips under the edge of the bottom crust and crimp to seal.
5. Pour butter-sugar mixture over top of pie, coating the lattice, and allowing any remaining sauce to drizzle through the crust.
6. Bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes. Reduce heat to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C), and bake until the crust is golden brown, the caramel on the top crust is set, and the apple filling is bubbling, 35 to 40 more minutes. Allow to cool completely before slicing.
Eat.

Wonderful game! If you're looking for a good timesink of about 40-50 hours or so, look no further. Very much in the vein of isometric action RPGs like Diablo, but it is a powerful franchise in its own right. You'll be spending hours clicking away on monsters, picking up loot and comparing it to your own gear, and its all made incredibly simple and fun by the devs.
Major plus point for me is the steps the game devs took to extend the shelf life of this game. You'll find extensive mod support for this game, and many creations hosted through Steam Workshop. You are also given the option of purchasing (with in-game currency of course) additional maps that give you access to many randomized dungeons. Which all goes to adding towards the game's replayability.
Monsters and bosses are all beautifully animated and you will never get bored of fighting them. They all have their own little combat styles and are unique enough from one another that the game never descends into a mindless clicking exercise.
Only slight negative for me is that the exact effects of an item on your character are sometimes not always clear, and sometimes it becomes difficult to see which of your stats is boosted or otherwise affected.
Nevertheless this is a fantastic game and one definitely worth checking out.

Deponia (first in a series of four games) is at its heart, a throw-back to the early point and click adventure games first popularized by Sierra-Online in the 80's and early 90s'.
It follows the misadventures of Rufus, a self-centered, self-aggrandizing, self-destructive, yet lovable transient bum, who is trying desperately to escape the perpetual junk filled planet of Deponia for the floating paradise in the sky known as Elysium. As the opening exposition tells us on the outset of the game, he will concoct any manner of schemes or contraptions in order to achieve his goal, and Lord help anyone, or anything that stands in his way.  I just wish I had a chance to interact with them more and see them fleshed out more fully.
And speaking of goals, Rufus quickly crosses paths with Goal, a beautiful Elysium woman who is, shall we say...not right in the head.  Which as Rufus will attest, that her condition had absolutely nothing to do with knocking her off the unprotected deck of a passing cruiser deck, plummeting to the ground and damaging her brain's hardware, rendering her unconscious. Goal represents the more cultured and educated foil to Rufus's blunt and unrefined nature, but the revelation later that her memories and personality can be changed via data cartriges placed in her brain implant, seemed a little off-putting.  I realize that it was written that way for comedic effect, but it still created a few cringeworthy moments.
What follows is Rufus' travels to return Goal to Elysium and "unselfishly" earning him a complimentary admission ticket to the golden city (my words).
Deponia has a lot to like. The first thing that is apparent about Deponia, is the cartoonish art-style.  Deponia is a literal world of junk, and everything in their society is constructed out what looks like the largest garbage dump known to man. Houses, buildings, everyday objects look like they were cobbled together out of repurposed items that were thrown away.
The cartoon style also gives life to all of the characters.  Even the bit-part characters are uniquely designed and animated. Each one has their own personality, and backstory, which isn't told through a lot of needless and awkward exposition.  This also highlights the smart and clever writing. Through a few well-placed sentences, you can already grasp who the individual characters are.  I truly got the sense that this game could have been its own animated comedy series on television, and it would have held up.
While the cartoon comedy provides a lot of this games positives, there are a few downsides to this game.  Let's start with the puzzles.  The cartoonish nature of the game requires you to think as if you were in a cartoon environment. Which means that puzzles are deceptively easy, in that you have to think in very sideways terms, where most people will take a more literal approach.  For example, you are given instructions on how to assume a certain sitting pose to go into a meditative trance.  One of those instructions is to sit and place your left leg behind your head. When you get the place where you have to meditate, there is no place, or option to manipulate the character into the proper position. That is, until you take the leg from a skeleton, and place it behind you.  Many of the solutions will leave you groaning in both laughter, and frustration.
Next are the mini-games.  There are a few of these sprinkled about in the game, but they have little to no explanation as to how they work, or how to achieve a solvable state. This will leave you scratching your head for hours, while you struggle to derive some kind of meaning of the game from the few, or lack or clues as to how they work.  Fortunately, the developers left an option to skip these mini-games, if you wish.
Despite these flaws, I still think Deponia is worth its price-point.  It is funny, well-written, leaves room open for its sequels.  If you like these kinds of games, definitely give it a try. However, buy the bundle pack and stretch your money a little further.

NOTE: This review is based on the 1st day early access so this is all subjective to change.
I found the game to be well designed and thought out.  The action in my opinion makes it an interesting and fun hack and slash games and probably one of the few I have personally enjoyed.  The ranking up and skill acquisition gives the game some additional purpose.
The main pros are that it is being produced by the creators of the series, rooster teeth.  The voice actors all played their roles which gives extra credibility to the game itself.  The game is very easy to grasp hold of and I managed to competently play it within a minute.  Which is good because complex games can lose thier interest quickly.
The cons or constructive critacism lies in a few areas.  FIrstly and this has been mentioned by many others is that the voices are quite soft.  Second is an where the player stops running yet the legs keep on animating a walk or run sequence for a second or two after.  Some additional characters/teams from the series would really make this game better.  I could see it getting repetative if were just the same four main characters.  This is a general issue I have found with most hack and slash games.  Some additional combos and or animations for attacks would also be a nice addition.
I do realise that this was an early release (today) but so far I really like where this is heading.  The main menu design is set up well and easy to use and the game itself is also very quick to learn and a lot of fun.  I would recommend this to anyone who enjoys a good hack and slash game and of course fans of RWBY.

If you are a fan of RWBY and hack and slash team games you will love this.
If you are not a fan of RWBY but are a fan of hack and slash games you will enjoy this greatly!
Cons:
- Animation sometimes bugs out but not very often.
- Some of the talking is to quiet. However this seems to be because the characters VA didn't do the lines so they made them quieter as to be less noticeable.
- Performance is a issue the game has yet to be optimized as it just came out of beta today but its still playable.
- No remapping of controls.
- It has its fair share of glitches none game breaking (But some come close IE. Your chat window goes away and won't come back)
Pros:
+ Sound track! While most of the game has background music boss fights have songs from the RWBY OST.
+ Each character feels really different. I have seen people say this is not the case but I have played as all 4 that are out now and each one plays different.
Ruby plays as heavy damage and crowd control. Her abilities are tailored to be able to take on hoards head on.
Weiss plays as support. She can freeze enemies and knock them back away from her team which is helpful for reviving.
Blake is less straightforward. In the game you get special blips to use special moves. To get one blip you have to fill up the combo bar without getting hit. On her own she deals fast low damage but fills up her bar quickly. Her special attacks are pretty good ranging from crowd control to boss killing moves.
Yang plays as two ways that I have found. She is either crowd control or a tank. Her attacks and special upgrades allow her to take a lot of damage and when her Aura is depleted she gets a full special bar. This combined with high health and wide weapon spread makes her perfect to take enemies.
+ The upgrading. Each character has 3 specials and a general for upgrading. The specials vary from character to character but the general is mostly the same except for 2 upgrades special to each character.
+ Its a challenging game. Most of the Grimm are weak alone but can quickly overwhelm you. To add to that you have "Major" Grimm which are much stronger versions and can be tricky on their own.
+ A good variety of Grimm to fight.
You have 5 types to fight each with three upgrades.
Creeps
Beowulfs
Boarbatusk
Ursa
And a new mutated nameless Grimm.
In the end I would give RWBY:GE a 8/10

SNOW has always had lots of potential. For the last four years this game has remained unfinished, but as of now the game is finally heading towards completion. Seeing how SNOW had wonky and yanky controls (not to mention the physics) it would only be matter of time until the game would lose it's appeal. But, thankfully SNOW has improved lots since I last played it roughly a year ago.
They've redefined the core physics, made the controls more smoother and sharper, and generally speaking perfected it beyond it's former-self.
Sadly, as it would seem they've gone down a route which was somewhat expected. Currently SNOW has implemeted a so called "skipass". This pass is used to unlock slopes and locations which were previously completley free.
I'm honestly not sure wheter or not I support this decision going forward. I doubt new players find this feature better seeing as it restricts them from advancing. Veterans of SNOW are not happy about this implementation either.
Hopefully, the devs in charge of SNOW will remove this feature in the near future. Simply because to me and many others it makes for a less enjoyable experience.

The recipe of the game is this: Take the modern Fallout's vault exploring, gut out the VATS system, switch it's retro culture obsession from the 50s to the 80s, put in the "everyone is a stupid idiot" style of post apocalyptic humor of LISA, and then make it a roguelike. The result is hands down one of the best entries in the "FPSer Roguelike" sub genre if not THE best.
Seemingly designed by one "Mr. Podunkian" (of "Half-Life 2: Jaykin’ Bacon Source" fame), it is a surprisingly large and incredibly well designed love letter to the Fallout series. The loop is basically this: Go down into the cooler as far as you think you can before dying while collecting gear and completing the odd quest (oh yeah there's quests), until you come across radioactive beers that on consumption returns you to your base (oh yeah there's a base, and you can build on to it) and gain a new perk based on what you drank. Dump off all your extra gear for whoever takes your place when you die, keep what's handy, go to the local bar to get a buzz, and then try to explore even deeper.
There's a good balance going on in the game. Sneaking around, taking things slower, and taking your time to recover health through food is obviously safer than running headfirst into a gunfight or a trap, but there's a pressure mechanic that keeps you from making "sneaking around and looting everything" your only playstyle. There's perma-death for your character when you get got, but  there's also permanent progression that is made so every death doesn't make you don't feel you've just wasted a bunch of time and lost everything.

(Also I gotta say, calling this thing a "love letter" to Fallout is an understatement.)

WASTED is a fun game that brings some of the positives and negatives of the modern Fallout series and similar rogue-lites.
It has great combat, more akin to Fallout 4's, but I like it even better. If the developers ever make a full open world sequel, or different type of spin-off like a Doom clone, this combat would be perfect for that. One problem I have with the combat is how powerful the stunlock is. Being stunned stops you from moving or shooting, which makes it impossible to run from enemies with accurate fire and automatic weapons. It's also confusing being stunned by a smaller attack during spraying, as it makes me think my weapon magically turned empty mid-mag.
The visuals are decent, a comic-like take on a wasteland similar to Fallout. The 'vaults' or Coolers as they call them, look fair, but they get old after having to keep running through them over and over again. The Coolers are also very dark, and it can be hard to see a lot of things like traps, loot, and even the courier boxes which are kind of needed.  There's no flashlight, so It would be great if they could put some little christmas lights on those. The randomness can also come to great detriment when you have multiple choices of paths to take, with most of which leading to dead ends. You have no way of looking at the whole of the map you've uncovered, which makes getting stuck at dead ends even easier. The S.O.B. Purifier that starts chasing you after a certain amount of time during exploring can be awful to get past if you waste too much time at a dead end. You have a fair chance of getting by him or survivng being attacked by him because you will probably only take around 75 damage from his stunlock minigun before he reloads and you run off. The stunlock makes sense for this enemy, but it becomes pretty unfair on later mandatory enemies that are faster and very accurate.
You can only hold 10 looted item unless you find some of the 3 types of fanny packs you can wear to gain 3 additional slots. The devs were cheeky in making the packs take 1 of the 3 additional slots, making you only gain 2 in all actuality. I feel that having the packs not take up a slot themself, or having them give you 4 aditional spaces instead of 3 would have made more sense than capping the max inventory at 19 with much of it being taken up by the basics that you need. But there are courier boxes and other ways to load off some loot and send it back home so that you don't lose it after you die.
It also comes with a simplified S.P.E.C.I.A.L. system, but it only seems to be upgraded by the gear you wear or the booze you drink to get upgrades/downgrades. This is kind of a shame, as it makes killing the same low level enemies over and over again, and disabling all of the traps kind of pointless since you dont get anything from them except for some money and maybe some ammo to refill.
There's plenty of things in between what I've talked about, like daily special runs that let you get one nicer than average piece of loot, a buying and selling system similar to Fallout that I haven't found a use for yet, and a time & day-to-night cycle that seems kind of pointless when there's no open world to explore and you spend most of your time inside of randomly generated vault dungeons...
But overall, WASTED is a great rogue-lite for it's price. It has some things I have gripes about, but the things I don't have gripes about more than make up for it. If you can stand toilet humour, references galore, and rogue-lite games in general, then you will probably have a lot of fun with this one.

I've played puzzle platformers where you play with previous copies of yourself, but this is the first time I've seen anyone attempt an FPS with the concept. That said, this game pulls the idea beautifully. I'll start with pros, then follow with con's
Pro's:
-A simple and sqift movement system ensures that your copies will move and shoot the -exact- way you did when you recorded it, ensuring that the damage they do is reliable for ever added clone.
-A varied weapons list gives you plenty of options for unique situations; even with the same weapon, you can upgrade it differently to specialize it. (EX. My first run I take a spread pistol with scatter and acid to melt a large number of soft blocks, and my last run I take a spread pistol with maxed damage and fire rate for single block cleanup.
-Smooth gameplay and lack of danger let you really focus on efficiency. Memory, attention, and planning are rewarded: you don't need to kill the same block in a second go, the first clone will take care of it.
-Each run is color coded to let you see where and what you did before, you can even watch where your curser pointed on previous runs!
-Community built rooms and levels add a dose of the insane (Some crafters are just nuts.)
Simply put, the game is fun. Its easy to learn, fun to play, its bright, and its colorful. It has a unique concept that plays beautifully as you orchaestrate your victory.
Cons:
-The game is short. The standard "Campaign" Can be beaten in an hour. It'll take longer if you want to 100% all the levels (Which is HARD) but it won't take you too long.
-Community levels, while they add on length, are simplified; they can't have moving blocks, and they lack the elaborate setpieces found in the Campaign.
-You play the camp in sets of 5 levels, with 4 runs per level. Each run takes a solid 20 minutes, and there is no replay button. You can't replay an individual time loop, you can't even replay an individual level. You want another try, you start from literally square one. This is frustrating, especially when I missed the. Last. Block. of a level. 20 minutes of stress and effort, down the pooper.
-The upgrade system is neat, and upgrades carry between levels, but that's a mixed blesssing, because it means that once you chose with 4 weapons you want, you're stuck with that combo for the rest of that 5 level set. You can't even change up the order.
-Your first run of the first 5 level set starts you at 0 gold, and most weapons are useless at level 1. The scatter pistol, rocket launcher, and partical ball are the only ones with enough damage to actually kill blocks at lvl 1, but the rockets are slower than christmas and the partical ball has all the range of a baseball bat. In community levels, you start with enough gold for 4 upgrades, but in the camp you get zip. So, you either start with a scatter pistol or you press the escape button.
-The balancing for weapons needs work; some weapons just aren't good. The partical ball, while it has the best damage, is crippled by the short range. The rocket launcher, again, has good damage, but the rockets take so long to travel that shooting at moving targets is a waste of time. The rest of the weapons are each good in their own way, but again, only the scatter pistol is useful at level 1.
-Weapon upgrades scales unrealistically high. You will never fully upgrade a weapon in the campaign, because the costs literally become more gold than is in the entire campaign. It's an indirect cap on how many upgrades you can buy and its annoying that it's there at all, much less how sharp it is.
At the end of the day though, I very thoroughly enjoyed this game. The upgrade system is frustrating, but the gameplay itself is amazingly fun, and most of the problems become non-issues when you play Community levels. This game needs a serious patch to fix a lot of problems, but its a year old, so such an update is unlikely. Still, there's real potential here, and for a price tag of $10, I absolutely reccomend picking this game up.
If By some fluke, a developer is reading this, then start making a sequal. Give starting gold for first weapons, allow -at minimum- a restart by stage button rather than a restart campaign button. Balance the weapons a little, maybe add a few more if you can keep them unique, and if possible, take the leash off of community level creation. This is a beautiful concept and the game engine is spotless, it just needs some tweaks and some added content.

So, with Sniper Elite 3, think Wolfenstein. The level sequencing is good, the graphics are very good (for the time), the music works, the gameplay controls are some of the best in genre, and the story is generic but functional. Except, it's easy to tell that this was all done on a budget much smaller than Wolfenstein.
Sniper Elite is worth about 10.00 at the moment as of writing this review (2017). The reason for this is that it's about 7-8 hours of moderate ~ pleasant fun in single player mode. There are very few people left who are left playing multiplayer mode. Though, this is not a huge issue since multiplayer mode seems hastely thrown together with level design being slightly below marginal.
Sniper Elite suffers from 2 main drags. One:) The level design is not at all designed for a sniper scenario. I found it was much easier to go around like Alteir, Assassin Creeding it to the objective point. Two:) Objects and game play scenarios are often thrown in without making any sense. (Kill the panzer tank, rescue this person who has nothing to do with the story, etc)
HOWEVER, there are some great things to acknowledge about Sniper Elite. One:) having the original mechanics that Kojima ripped for his MGSV. Except in Sniper Elite the mechanics actually function. This game may have been on a budget, but they hit a solid run with these mechanics and their fluidity of animation. Two:) There's also something to be said about sniping two SS Troop's testicles in one shot, then putting it into slow mo. What game will ever do that? That's right Sniper Elite 3.

Spelunky is a challenging, but never tedious 2D sidescrolling game. The game is simplistic in design but has a ton of tricks up it's sleeve.
Pros:
-Challenging: This game could be equated to Dark Souls in the amount of times you will die.
-Lots of choice: How you play is it up to you. You COULD avoid everything and rush to the exit, or you COULD spend the full time looking for loot.
-Pretty Art Design- Even 2 dimensional the game is pretty.
-Tight Controls: The controls for this game are tight. All the buttons are responsive, and it almost feels like an old mario game.

Med school is arguably less of a challenge than this game.
I've been playing this game on and off for the past 3.5 years (mostly on 360/Xbone). It doesn't matter how many hundreds (thousands) of times you die, every game is a new experience and an opportunity to learn something you didn't think of before. You will get as much out of this game as you put into it. It is brutally hard but wryly grins at you with each death, giving you just enough of a nudge to force you to accept that your carelessness did you in.
And you are going to make completely preventable mistake after mistake after mistake. And you'll eventually reach a point (in a long line of points) where you start beating yourself up. Because there is no hand-holding here; Spelunky doesn't understand the meaning of the word "handicap". Making progress in this game is a victory; winning the game is a celebration of those small victories.
You'll get smarter with each run. You'll recognize certain patterns, make a mental note of your personalized gameplan that is going to get you through. You'll be making checkpoints for yourself, measuring your progress. You're going to have sessions where you say, "I'm almost there; I've figured it out this time", only to realize that once that plan inevitably fails, you're just as far from victory as the first time you picked up the controller and played this game. It is an absolute beatdown that reminds you how much you suck, in the best way possible.
