I don't do reviews often. However I'm a pretty big fan of RWBY. the show to me has always seemed perfect for a video game. Thankfully I think the basics are already there and pretty good. Let me start by saying, this is Early Access so whilst I will mention the issues, I expect them to be patched over time and if they are, then they're null and void, obviously.
So, it's an arena fighting game, sort of. If you're familiar with RWBY, then you know that the universe of the show features some pretty bombastic fights. Acrobatics, juggling, magical stuff. A gun thats also a scythe. These are all represented in the game.
The combat is however, maybe too simple for those of you expecting combos and specials. One attack key, one "Shoot" key for long range stuff. It makes things somple, but that's maybe too much. I'd have preferredmaybe a Hevy/Light attack model. so I can perform more combos and have direct control over my attacks.
Specials are activated (at least on a controller) by holding a trigger and pressing a face key. It's simple, but unlike the melee combat it works well and I like it. Each character (4 of them so far, the main RWBY cast) all have distinct aesthetics but the moves are all the same. One special is an AOE, the other is a more direct knocback and the third is a ranged ability. Some can be upgraded to be charged, or given more knockback, etc.
As Early Access, I expect the collision issues. Hits don't always register. Multiplayer desyncs badly (it's peer to peer) and the UI is simplistic and barebones.
These can be improved on. If they are, this could be a lot of fun. RWBY as a show has a ton of teams that could be added going onwards. All with unique abilities and attacks.
For now, I recommend this IF you like RWBY. There are better, more accessible games in this genre for other people. On full release, we'll see what this offers to draw in more people.

Amidst the mighty throng of dungeon crawlers, you might be wondering, "what's so special about Torchlight II?" Well, I'm here to tell you.
Torchlight II is a fun departure from the rather tedious Diablo formula. Don't get me wrong, Diablo is a good game but it tends to lose it's novelty quickly, for me anyways. One thing that I really like about Torchlight II is the pets. They're actually helpful! They don't just stand there and get in the way, they fight (even tank sometimes), they can even make runs to town for you and sell all the junk you've picked up or buy some elixirs and other helpful items. Very cool.
I haven't tried all the classes but I have leveled an engineer up to a fairly decent level. Fun times! Stomp, bash, wack, and blast your way through enemies. You can carry a giant cannon or a giant wrench or whatever catches your fancy to be the harbinger of your enemy's doom. There are three skill trees that you can go into and you're not restricted to one I don't think.
Environments are well done, armor doesn't look totally lame (well, maybe some pieces do), weapons are wicked tight, it's just fun! I'd recommend it to anyone who wants a break from the run o' the mill dungeon crawler.
**P.S. I see some people are ready to grab their torches (hehe, torches, get it?....Ahh never mind) and pitchforks and make a mad dash for Runic Studios in order to rough up the developers...ok not that extreme. I don't usually review video games because I don't usually enjoy them enough to complete them, but “South Park the Fractured But Whole” drew me in from the get-go as it is South Park through and through.
It took me about 30 hours to complete the game, from start to finish, finishing most of the side quests, so for those of you who count hours for your value proposition would equal about $2 an hour and to me, I think that value is quite Fair.
The world is rich in the story will keep you guessing and the rabbit hole of South Park is deep enough to reach terminal velocity. Players should most definitely stick to the after credits scene it almost makes me want to agree to his proposition and hope for the next game in the series..
The difficulty curve is quite Fair while pretty simple in the beginning. Battles get very brutal near the end and gives you the sense of accomplishment for taking out these Interesting bosses and varied group fights. The sense of accomplishment equally measured when finally taking out that damn Taco store owner whom beat my♥♥♥♥♥midgame.

The town is lively and crude and everything that you would expect from South Park, while that may turn a lot of people off, those who are fans (read not fanatics) would love it. I myself have not watched South Park for many years but even still have found quite a bit to enjoy in this game.
While watching some streams I've noticed that a few players are experiencing bugs, especially with the Call Girl character, I thankfully have skipped all of them. The worst I’ve had to deal with were some Hang-Ups due to the game trying to figure out turn order on newly spawned enemies and friends, but other than that, the game really ran flawlessly for me.
As of now, “South Park the Fractured But Whole” is my game of the year just because I kept wanting to come back for more, to see where everything leads, to help your friends and to overcome your enemies.
I will say that this game is a must buy to any fans of South Park or to any with a dark, cruel, or sick sense of humor and an open mind. At least get it during a sale, do not skip out on this game as it is a riot until the end.

I've been wating ages for Tekken 7 to come out, since Tekken 5 infact. Tekken 6 was ruined by Azzazel and Tekken Tag 2 was ok but I don't really like 2 on 2 unless it's porn. Anyway I digress, Firstly the technical side of stuff, I'm running this on Windows 7 ultimate which is quite an old operating system and it works perfectly so I would imagine those with 8 or 10 should have no problems. Only slight glitch I've noticed is sometimes when quitting game after a prolonged period of play I can get a black screen and have to control, alt, delete to get out of it, other than that no technical issues what so ever.
Graphically it does the job, it has the best graphics of any Tekken game but nothing spectacular.
The sound is ok, fighters talk mainly in the languages there supposed to and the effects are pretty much the same as they have been in every tekken game. The music is techno which suits the genre and the fast paced action of the game but can get repetitive after a while, fortunately  you can select the music from any of the previous games for your bouts which is a nice touch and adds some variety.
The controls are what Tekken players have come to expect and are as good as a console at least they are with a usb X box controller. prior to this game the only was to play Tekken on pc was with an emulator and they could never quite replicate some of the more fiddly combos or quarter circle moves.
Gameplay wise the core gameplay is as solid as ever although there are some significant changes. There are now rage abilities which add a new dynamic to the game play, there sort of like super moves you would find in a capcom or nethrealm beat em up, personally i'm not a fan. Experienced Tekken players will also notice some of the old characters are missing, parcticularly lei wulong and julia chang. Some other great fighters are also missing, Beak Doo San and Wang are apparantly dead and all the clone fighters have gone, Armour King, Kunimitsu, Anna Williams and a few others. Why Panda and Kuma are both in it but lei and Julia arn't I have no idea. Hopefully they wil be in future DLC. Of the roster you are given the old fighters haven't changes much and the new ones are a mixed bag, I particularly like Katarina who is like a mixture of Brian and Hwoarang, devesating power like Brian and really long kick combos like Hwaorang. I also wish I'de preorderred as Eliza looks awesome when I've come up against her online. Akuma from street fighter also seems to have transitioned over well from Street Fighter. He doesn't stick out like a saw thumb too much.
Game mode wise offline this game isn't great, arcade mode is way too short only 5 fights. treasure mode is pretty good, it's like Arcade mode in tekken 5 where you advance in rank while fighting unlimited opponents except here your rewarded with game currency and customization items. Story mode I thought was pretty meh, the cut scenes are like a really borring graphic novel, god knows who the annonymous reporter is, maybe if I can be bothered to play it to the end he'll be Paul and Anna williams love child or something but I doubt it. Practice mode is the same old practice mode and infact is probably worse than some of the older games. You can spend the game currency you get from fights to unlock videos from all the tekken games aswell as customizing your fighters appearance.
Online mode is where this game really shines, If your a half decent Tekken player there are plenty of people out there to fight most of a reasonably high standard. This is a double edged sword, great for us old hands but intimidating for new players.
Anyway to conclude this is a great old fashioned Tekken game with room for improvement. it's well worth buying in it's present state but if they would bring back, survival mode, team battle, time attack, make arcade mode longer and bring back lei and Julia this would be a game of the year contender atleast in my opinion. Namco have already stated there will be atleast 2 future DLC's containg atleast 2 guest fighters and atleast one new mode. Hopefully Tekken 7 will be like Tekken Tag 2 in that regard which had eventually 10 additional fighters added to it's original rosta. Sorry for the length of the review but a few words wouldn't do Tekken justice.

I haven't completed story mode yet but it does seem to reveal a great deal about the history of it's most notable characters.
I look forward to the season pass goodies, as this will be my main fighting game for quite a while. 5/5.

I think the term 'Playground' in this installment is an indication to the 'difficulty' of it compared to the others in the series.
Unlike the others, this game has no limit when building a bridge which I think is a good feature, as it allows you to pass some of the harder levels, which otherwise will have you frustrated and stuck. The addition of badges in this game are fantastic as it gives you 5 separate goals to complete on each bridge, that you can do individually, giving a bit of replay-ability and problem solving for each bridge.
There is also a tension/weight meter at the top that displays in real time the pressure on your bridge, which I think is a great addition as it can give you better insight on how/what needs improved on your bridge, and by how much.
Overall I think this is a nice addition to the series, albeit it seems quite shorter than the standard Bridge Constructor. If you are a fan of the series I would recommend the purchase or if you are new to it, I would suggest getting the bundle and playing this one first.

Hear me out, because this game barely has 3 hours of gameplay, and I have played it for almost 15.  You may be looking at these pretty screenshots, and hearing metacritic reviews about the heart this game has.  These are a deception. Here's why:
Starbreeze got too big for their briches one day and decided to make an artsy game just for s**ts and giggles.  So they all sat around a table and said, "What are some ingredients to make artsy games? How about a thin and short plot that you could predict before starting the game. And an underdeveloped puzzle mechanic that is unfulfilling and gets in the way of the story mentioned previously. And then, just in case the story still has any continuity or reason left in it, let's make the characters speak gibberish, and with no subtitles!"
You may have read the 10,000 reviews saying, "the babble speak proves you don't need to know what people are saying to know what they mean."  Thats bull.  It proves that nothing said in baby talk can be taken seriously, and that this game has enough gesturing to explain the actuall words. This game is poorly paced, poorly designed, incredibly short, and way too easy.  So easy you might think its for little kids, but then somebody in the background hangs himself and you say to yourself, "I can't tell if that was deep."  Because it wasn't.
This is a game that you (yes, YOU with $15 in your steam account) could probably have designed better yourself, and then paid Starbreeze to make the pretty screenshots above that you will occasionally stop and look at before saying "You can almost not tell it's a console port."
PLEASE skip on this game.  Even if you think you like these kinds of artsy games (I know I do) and EVEN if its on some huge sale price.

This is a pretty fun and addictive game. It's a rogue-like platformer that boasts some serious challenge and randomly generated levels so each playthrough is different. Armed with a whip, bombs, and rope you must traverse a trap and enemy laden dungeon while filling your pockets with treasure along the way. The gameplay is pretty standard 2D platformer fare, with the added fun of a fully destructible environment. Shops where you can buy items and hidden goodies you can find throughout your adventure helps ease the difficulty and makes the dungeon run more manageable.
The game is primarily split up into four zones, with a few hidden areas to unlock as well. Each has their own unique set of enemies and monsters, with each zone being overall more difficult than the last. I have yet to finish it myself, which is a testament to its challenge, but I keep coming back for more. The hidden items and areas give it some pretty high replayability as well. Highly recommended.

Early access Day 1 review, so lets get that out there right away. It certainly feels early access and needs to be beefed up a bit. The only bug that I've gotten so far is the characters running animation might freeze while going up/down slopes but goes back to normal no problem. This doesn't happen all the time but enough to be very noticable. There's very little story besides kill the Grimms and fix the things. I would also recommend using a gamepad over the keyboard. Tried both and found a gamepad to be way more enjoyable and easier to use. Could use a solo mode but you can do it by just setting a friends only game.
With the cons out of the way here are some pro's
Gameplay is very fluid, each character have similar attack structure but each are unique in their own way. Different characters have certain traits that fit into the show Yangs play style is vastly different from say Ruby. The look and feel of the game is very accurate to the RWBY universe. It's a decent hack and slash with moba like leveling where you have to pick your upgrades on the fly. I find it fun, which is the most important part in my opinion. I find myself wanting to jump back into it again and trying a different character. I have yet to try multiplayer but I could see myself trying it out over solo play. If you're a fan of RWBY and Rooster Teeth I would recommend this game without hesitation.

I don't usually review video games because I don't usually enjoy them enough to complete them, but “South Park the Fractured But Whole” drew me in from the get-go as it is South Park through and through.
It took me about 30 hours to complete the game, from start to finish, finishing most of the side quests, so for those of you who count hours for your value proposition would equal about $2 an hour and to me, I think that value is quite Fair.
The world is rich in the story will keep you guessing and the rabbit hole of South Park is deep enough to reach terminal velocity. Players should most definitely stick to the after credits scene it almost makes me want to agree to his proposition and hope for the next game in the series..
The difficulty curve is quite Fair while pretty simple in the beginning. Battles get very brutal near the end and gives you the sense of accomplishment for taking out these Interesting bosses and varied group fights. The sense of accomplishment equally measured when finally taking out that damn Taco store owner whom beat my♥♥♥♥♥midgame.

The town is lively and crude and everything that you would expect from South Park, while that may turn a lot of people off, those who are fans (read not fanatics) would love it. I myself have not watched South Park for many years but even still have found quite a bit to enjoy in this game.
While watching some streams I've noticed that a few players are experiencing bugs, especially with the Call Girl character, I thankfully have skipped all of them. The worst I’ve had to deal with were some Hang-Ups due to the game trying to figure out turn order on newly spawned enemies and friends, but other than that, the game really ran flawlessly for me.
As of now, “South Park the Fractured But Whole” is my game of the year just because I kept wanting to come back for more, to see where everything leads, to help your friends and to overcome your enemies.
I will say that this game is a must buy to any fans of South Park or to any with a dark, cruel, or sick sense of humor and an open mind. At least get it during a sale, do not skip out on this game as it is a riot until the end.

As far as the game goes, it's South Park. It has solid gameplay like Stick of Truth, except it's like a tactics styled game, as opposed to the JRPG styled turn based system from the previous game. I love the jokes poking fun at modern day social media, and they know no boundaries as expected. If you like South Park and Stick of Truth, I highly suggest this game. Bridge Constructor Playground is a little nice game about bridge building. It's not good like Bridge Constructor Medieval, but basically you can make the same innovations. The biggest lack: theres is not really a story. You just hop from island to island to build bridges across rivers or valleys. The variousity of landscapes is also very low.
There are three different goals: 1. build the cheapest bridge, 2. build a bridge that can handle the weight stress test at its best and 3. build a bridge with only allowed materials. Sometimes there is a limit of money or a certain number of elements you can use. Another goal is to make it safe for trucks. Btw forget about the cars. In the end just the trucks count.
So you play each level 2-3 times to fullfill all goals and then you will notice it's always the same. The bridges with less weight stress are always made out of concrete and cable. The cheapest bridges can be wooden but it mustn't be. And for the material bridges mostly steel and wood is allowed both. Yeah it's challenging but otherwise it can be boring.
Altogether playing this game was mediocre fun but it's OK. In the end there is that notorious facebook achievement which obviously doesn't work for everybody on the first try. That's a bit annoying.

I got this free from a Humble Bundle. If I had paid money for this I would be incredibly sad, especially at a $10 price point directly from Steam.
This looks like a bad iPad game written in Unity. Probably because it is.
The entire UI is clearly based around a touch screen, with the cursor acting as a glorified finger. You can't adjust sound levels in the game, I had to adjust them in Windows mixer because it screams at you. You can enable/disable the horrible music with a button on the start screen, that is the extent of the options menu. There are only a couple keybindings, and none are really useful except for undo.
So after beating the Tutoria
missions I wanted to try some of the harder ones. Nope, I have to replay the tutorial missions to get 25 "badges."
Badges are horrible. It's literally impossible to accomplish all of them in one run, and for the two budget-based ones there are one, maybe two solutions for each. It's infuriating how low the budgets are set, you genuinely do have to do it EXACTLY like it wants you to otherwise you go over budget or load.
If this was a iPad/Android Tablet game it would be subpar. On a computer this is just horrible. And it's a ripoff of
, which is vastly superior.

Upsides:
- Actual learning value in the area of bridge engineering and understanding of mechanical and physical principles. Even if the physics engine is not flawless and the means are very limited, with the basics it offers it's still a lot of fun. Physics-based puzzles are more interesting than mere logic-based ones. It's more exciting to have that connection to real-life engineering, and it's fun to watch the result play out.
- Lots of freedom. Feels like there's not one single optimum solution. Being given several approaches in which to build a bridge (cheap, sturdy, materials-limited) further increases the range of possible ways to solve the problems.
- A good bit of creative opportunity apart from the challenges given.
- No handholding. It expects you to figure out the advanced building techniques on your own, but gives you scenarios and tasks that subtly nudge you in the right direction. So it's more like the whole game itself is the tutorial.
Downsides:
- Launcher doesn't save the graphics quality level.
- Steam leaderboards advertised, but they seem to be missing.
- Advertises an extensive tutorial. As mentioned above, that's really not the case. It's at best a moderate tutorial. (The fact is OK, the false description is not.)
- One achievement requires you to share a bridge on Facebook. You can manage to get it even if it fails if you keep trying, but this was almost enough for me to not play it.
- Quite a bit of randomness regarding the results involved, sometimes especially between play sessions. That makes it closer to reality I guess.
- Not enough musical variety.
- Only one setting for music on/off, nothing else sound-wise. But, I guess playing one's own music is the best option here.
- Element highlighing not perfect. It removes the one you're pointing at, but sometimes highlights a different one.
On a more personal note: I havent's played the regular Bridge Constructor, but I think I wouldn't like it. This is called "Playground" for a good reason. Outside of the context of the challenges that give you medals, the element of scarcity (limited building resources and such) is not present in this game, and I like that a lot. People tend to live what they train/prepare for, and I enjoy living abundance.

It's a fun casual bridge builder. It's pretty simplified from the previous bridge builder games, but the challenges are a neat touch. I beat this game (except for finishing off the badges) in a few hours, so it isn't really worth the $10 - pick it up on a good sale. They added a new material, concrete, that allows building indestructable columns vertically from foundation points. It makes it trivial to solve most bridges, but you won't meet any challenges that way.
I'm not a fan. Game's more annoying than fun, you can lame your way through it and I'm not sure I've learned anything at all. Wouldn't spend money on this game, but I got it in the Humble Bundle.

Updated Review:
If you go into this game on a good Steam sale, and treat it like what it was always meant to be (a small indie fan project beat em' up) then you will enjoy yourself! There are MANY flaws with RWBY: Grimm Eclipse and the game has less content than many other fighting/coop games do for the original asking price. However, there is a lot of fun to be had smashing Grimm with your favorite characters from the RWBY-verse with your friends! Combos are limited, but all characters have their own attacks, specials, and roles to play (but often it will turn into a button mashing festival). The story is... a story by the definition of one, and the dialogue is often lacking in quality which is odd considering they had access to all the voice actors/actresses. So to put it simply, this is a dumb fun game and not worth considering for lore or anything deeper than the limited combat system. If you're a mega fan of RWBY, and use some of the wonderful community mods, then Grimm Eclipse becomes a wonderful button mashing cooperative game to kill a few hours with!
Personal Feeling:
Considering the size of the team that made this game, and the MASSIVE quality standards thrust onto them once they were acquired by Rooster Teeth Games I have to give this game a pass personally. Not a pass on the limited content, but the quality of some parts of this game.
Old Early Access Review:
In SHORT: This is a very fun beat-em-up styled 4 player co-op game! There is a TON of potential here and seeing as the game is in early access, the community will hopefully have their issues with the game addressed and fixed! If you are a fan of the show and always wanted to play out one of the many fight scenes, this is the closest you can get! If you are not a fan of the show, you can still enjoy this game, but the mechanics are SIMPLE. If you wanted a deep combo system, it will not be found in this game (yet). However, the different fighting styles and abilities of each member of the RWBY team make each playthrough interesting enough to hold your attention.  As the game is in Early Access, there is only ONE campaign that can last about 30-45 minutes, depending on the quality of cooperation between yourself and your online partners. The fact is, the game right now is 15$. There is not a lot of content as of release and therefore I cannot say that this game is worth the money as of now. But, if you are a MEGA fan and do not mind waiting patiently for updates to the Early Access version of the game, buy it now!

Alright, so let's set a premise here: RWBY: GE is a fanservice game. If you're not a fan of RWBY, I doubt you'll like this game. It's very simplistic, linear, button mashy, unbalanced, and at the moment very short and not replayable beyond trying different characters. However, if you are a fan of RWBY, this is your chance to really feel like you're part of the action. This game has the foundation it needs to become a really good fanservice game.
So I'll be writing this review as a RWBY fan.
The character cast, as it stands, is surprisingly high quality considering the studio behind it all's overall lack of experience in game development of this caliber. Meaning the combat for each member of team RWBY and the mid-game progression has a lot of unique flavor. Though Yang feels like she's lacking (she doesn't feel tanky like expected, and her gameplay is clunky), Blake is extremely fluid, fast-paced and fun to play. Weiss at the moment is a powerhouse and needs some drastic nerfing to find her niche (which I believe is supposed to be support/crowd control). Finally, Ruby has the disjointed weaponry and strong ranged play that defines her as more of a fast, squishy zoning character.
Enemy design is at a very good start. Every enemy has a clear, lore-friendly role defined for it, and they emerge through experiencing their fighting styles firsthand. Ursas are tanky with high HP, super strong slow hits; beowolves are fast, hard-hitting, and difficult to avoid, boarbatusks have their terrifying spin2win spam and hit n' run you across the battlefield, and the new mooks have an interesting swarming mechanic when they all take turns smacking you from underground. There's a definite chemistry to working against each one with each team member's niche. Of course, this is true until Weiss comes along and freeze-stunlocks everything.
The plot presented so far is an obvious set up for something bigger, with an original antagonist and many Grimm variants to come. The way the campaign progresses and enemy diversity expands gradually is well-done to integrate even those who are completely unfamiliar with button-masher hack & slash games.
The online is smooth; no complaints there. Played while streaming and experienced no lag. Co-op with friends is bound to be a fun, L4D-style RPG experience in a way.
I can't comment on optimization, but I think working on how large crowds are rendered could be beneficial. I experience frame drops during intense fights with tons of Grimm, but that might just be my PC. One way or another, all effort toward improving framerate is good effort. Most of the time the game ran smoothly and I had no issues. Some animation jank is present on downward slopes for some odd reason, though it's easily overlooked. And sound effects are way too loud with no option to fix in-game, so you'll be fiddling with your PC's volume (UPDATE: FIXED).
So in conclusion I'll repeat myself: RWBY fans, this is your game. Everyone else, wait for full release to make any potentially regrettable financial decisions. I'm happy with my investment on just day one, since I'm stupid easy to please with these types of games. Really looking forward to see where we go from here, Rooster Teeth. This is gonna be fun.

After reading all the negative reviews I didn't really want to buy this game, 30 hours max for 60 dollars? 2 dollars an hour doesnt sound that great, and thats the ideal situation right? But I wanted to play it anyways because of how much I enjoyed Stick of Truth. Because of the 30 hour thing, I made it a point to play on the hardest difficulty (Combat and Race) along with 100%ing the game.
All of that took me roughly 29 hours to do, and I've decided it is absolutely worth it; despite what anyone else has said.
Pros:
+The graphics seem a little bit more polished in this game, and personally the game ran better during cut scenes and otherwsie compared to the last game.
+The combat is totally fresh and has a lot of diversity, you can spend hours just finding fights to see what new abilities do.
+Craig and Tweek duh... Yaoi hunting added a lot more than I thought collectables ever could, beats chinpokomon any day.
+Speaking of, the characters seemed a lot more... in character, than the last game.
+Makes me laugh as hard as South Park always has, in some cases the dialogue had me put my controller down just to laugh before playing again, not something Stick of Truth had me doing- usually I was scoffing about how batshit the events were.
Cons:
-The narration and story of the game doesn't feel quite as epic and gross as before, for example in the previous game; events like the alien space ship and going inside Mr. Slave felt like south park episodes on their own, but
-I am the kind of person who likes to get as many hours in as I can for games that cost me; and there is no way you can realistically put 40+ hours into this game until real Obsidian Fallout New Vegas level dlc is released.
I absolutely recommend this game regardless and would pay the $60 for it immediately if I had to. If you enjoy south park and consider yourself a fan to the series, than you're doing a diservice to yourself by skimping out on it...
Also a quick mention to the "Uplay" complaints, there are quite a few games here on steam that require you to cross between before playing the game; while there are issues with that, none of them are major enough to bring down the actual games quality.

Beautifully drawn, funny, with actually pretty good story (and world setting) masked by simple personal quest of an egocentric protagonist. But also Deponia is a time machine with a dial set to 90's which had twofold effect on me:
First I remembered playing good old P&C adventures, warm and cosy feeling with occasional chuckle, and of course accompanied with frustrations because of illogical solutions and pixel hunting. But during those days we didn't have internet so you would be stuck on a certain puzzle for hours/days, repeating your steps making sure you didn't miss anything vital (did I mention illogical?) figuring out that you are dumb after all... Ahh *wipes the tear of reminiscence*
Second thing is that I realized why this genre has died out. I can't imagine someone who grew up with today's games enjoying this kind of experience. Nothing here is on platter, you have to figure out on your own how to solve it. Or of course go and find a walk-through online, but they you would ask yourself are you enjoying this or even if is this is for you. So you would drop it and go play something in 3D with jumping and shooting with immediate satisfaction.
If this came out in previous century it would be masterpiece worth remembering.

Deponia is a 'soft' science fiction humorous point-and-click adventure game from Daedalic Entertainment, the developers of the excellent Edna & Harvey games.
In Deponia you play Rufus, a selfish, lazy, entitled young man whose father escaped to the beautiful floating Elysium and left Rufus on the junk planet, Deponia, to fend for himself. The game begins with Rufus ready to leave his few friends behind and attempt another flight to Elysium in a craft of his own devising. In short order he encounters an Elysian woman, Goal, who becomes seriously injured. Your job is to guide Rufus through trying to heal Goal and reach Elysium.
Deponia uses the same game engine as Edna & Harvey: Harvey's New Eyes, although it seems to have had a facelift. The graphics are cartoon like and have a lot of charm. Animations are great, and there's obviously been considerable attention to detail paid to most of the scene backgrounds, which are detailed and often humorous.
The gameplay is interspersed with animated cutscenes, done in the same style as the gameplay graphics. These are also very well done.
Graphics options are few, but the game performs well on my ageing gaming laptop, so there shouldn't be any need for optimisation of settings anyway.
Music is good and fits the game world well. The narrator sings through the introduction for each chapter; he's the same performer as in Edna & Harvey: Harvey's New Eyes, and in the same way the humour in the songs occasionally falls a bit flat with rather forced rhymes, but it's still a nice touch.
Sound effects are appropriate. They're well sampled and normalised for volume, and they work well in the game, even when they're a bit over the top.
The game is fully voiced, and the voice acting is generally very good, although the default volume level is too low (hint: turn the music down). In particular, Rufus is acted well -- he sounds suitably obnoxious -- and Goal's voice is perfect. The script is a bit lacking in places, making for a few awkwardly worded lines, most likely due to translation into English, but the subtitles at least match the spoken words very closely. There are some very funny parts, too: try showing the platypus toy to Goal.
Deponia plays like any traditional point-and-click adventure game. It can be played exclusively with the mouse, using the pointer to highlight interactive objects in each scene, right mouse button to examine them (note: this sometimes also interacts with them!), and left mouse button to interact with them. The inventory, key to any traditional adventure game, can be accessed in one of two modes; I played with the mouse wheel being used to open and close the inventory panel, and this worked well.
In keeping with traditional point-and-click adventures, the story is completely linear, with dialogue choices available for flavour, and humour only, and not to allow any real freedom of choice. Puzzles mostly make sense, although the translated script makes some solutions less obvious than I feel they should have been, and I confess to having to resort to a walkthrough to complete the game. The story is interesting, too, and the characters are well realised. I'm glad that Daedalic have made sequels, and I'm looking forward to seeing what happens next.
In typical Daedalic fashion the Steam achievements are mostly unlockable through playing normally, but there a few that you'll be very unlikely to get unless you follow a guide. If you're an achievement hunter, but still wish to enjoy the game, I'd suggest playing through once normally and saving often, then using one of the many achievement guides to go back and get the achievements you missed. The Drogglejug! achievement is a right pain.
There are a few minor bugs, but I found that Deponia was more stable than either of the Edna games. Clicking on objects in the inventory often doesn't work first (or second, or third) try, but this is only a minor annoyance, and seems to be due to mouse sensitivity. Also, one of the achievements didn't unlock properly for me or many others going by the Steam discussion forum, and there were a couple of little script hiccups where a character appeared and disappeared briefly once, or text disappeared. But there were none of the non-working saves or other critical bugs from Edna & Harvey: Harvey's New Eyes.
Pros
+ Interesting story in a fun game world
+ Well-realised characters that made me care what happened next
+ Great cartoon-like graphics and animations
+ Good voice talent
+ Some funny jokes
+ Achievements
+ Trading Cards
Cons
- Occasionally inelegant translation leaves a few jokes falling flat and puzzles obfuscated
- Minor bugs in places
- The ending seemed a little bit rushed, after so much time spent in Kuvac
Deponia is another great point-and-click adventure from Daedalic, and introduces a fun and interesting game world. I wouldn't hesitate to recommend it to any adventure game fans with a sense of humour. I'm really looking forward to playing the sequels.

With Train Simulator, you'll either be playing for only 2 hours, or 200+ hours. DLC is NOT made to be purchased all at once: just pick the ones that suit you best. You have options to play in free roam, quick drive (just point A to point B), standard routes with goals and objectives, and career where you can do the same as standard but with a score which you can level up.
Routes go on sale a lot, which gives you plenty of cheap options once you have the full game. Bear in mind that this game is fairly old, and has some bugs which affect completing routes, how engines run, and how the game handles graphics. If you can get over those things, this game will bring you hours of entertainment if you happen to love trains.
PRO TIP: Shop for DLC via the store within the game! It's much easier than on the store page.

Okay, so I really enjoyed Stick of Truth. So much so that I wanted this game before I even finished SoT.  I'm still currently playing FBW, so I can't speak on the entire game. What I've played of the game though, I've formed my opinion.
The plot line is fine so far. Totally different game than SoT so if you haven't played the first one, you should be fine. The combat has changed a little bit, but it's still turn based. Character creation is different, and it's actually pretty cool. There's a lot more options, and you have the ability to look female right off the bat (which, I'll admit, I was excited about since it's nice to play as a girl haha). Same type of exploration, not really open world but you can still wander if you don't want to do the main quest just yet.
The negatives are accessability to play this game. You have to play it through Ubisoft, which sucks since you have to create a whole new account (if you don't have one already) just to play. You need to download their client. There's DLC before you even begin the game, and in-game purchases already. Everytime a combat begins, I have to wait 5 minutes or so before I can do anything while it loads. The game crashes on loading screens, and the loading screens are constant - you walk for a few seconds and there's another loading screen to get to the next part of the map. I feel like there's way more loading screens than SoT.
I'd say buy this on sale. Wait a little while for the bugs to be fixed. Wait for a few updates. The game itself is fine, but I don't think it was ready to be released yet.

TL;DR I am only recommending this for hardcore RWBY fans who want to see this game get leagues better, if that is not you, wait until it is finished.
It's enjoyable as a fan of RWBY. But it feels very unfinished, which is fine now, but hopefully will be changed later.
Voices: The voice actors are there, but the voices are terribly soft, and I've had both Port and Oobleck's dialouge cut out randomly. Also there are a lot of efforts. I understand their usefulness in show combat and what it adds, but here in the game it can be a little distracting if every time you push a button an effort is triggered.
Combat: What was the phrase used to define shooters? Ten second of fun over and over again? That's basically what it is. There are some things, like the early warning system for attacks in which red lines appear above an enemy's head. This would be useful if it would also show enemies outside your FOV which had aggro on you. It's nice to give a chance to stop enemy attacks, but with Beowulves and Boarbatusks especially there needs to be a way to interrupt their attacks once they've begun. Once a Boarbatusk charges, the ony avoidance is to dodge, no block or interrupt. Same thing with Beowulves. That slash attack is ruthless if they're in a group and there is no way to defend against it other than running away. As for combat controls, simple. A melee and a ranged attack. Combos come from spamming melee and hit secondary for a finisher at the end. Specials are "unique" to each character. I use quotes around unique because each special is very similar to another characters' with specific alterations for each character. There's an AOE special, a ranged special, and a single enemy strike special. Lock ons for ranged attacks are a bit wonky and sometimes won't work from less than a foot away but the bullseye an enemy fifty feet away.
Appearance: Visually this game is beautiful, the characters look like themselves and the landscape looks like RWBY. It would be nice to have a few more deeply rendered textures, but all in all it looks like RWBY.
Music: On point with the action, if a little bit loud when matched with voice volume. I really do like the music though, it adds to the RWBY feel.
Story: well it seemed like it was going to get better, but the my game froze in Mountain Glenn, twice. Though to be fair that appears to be an issue with my computer not with the game. Currently though you're just trying to solve what seems like a small mystery.
Other odds and ends: Upgrade system and exp is probably where this game needs more work before I'd consider it to be halfway finished. If you join a game that is further in the story a la quick game, your character will be at level one, even if you just ground out eight levels in the last game and were kicked. There is also no incentive to work as a team. Exp is only shared by finishing a round and it is only 75 per person. There is a bonus for being MVP and reviving people, so you could let everyone die kill all the remaining enemies then revive everyone for major exp. Who needs a team anyway? But yeah, there is no keeping levels or upgrades between games. That is a need to fix item. Along with more variety in combat and sound balancing.
All in all this game is fun for a RWBY fanboy like myself, but not for the casual watcher ar a hardcore gamer. If you want to buy it now just for the sake of the low price then be my guest, but if you want it to be epic from the get-go, then wait for a few updates. I am recommending this only for those who are hardcore fans and want to help this game improve.

This has got to be one of the most fun, well optimized and addictive games I've ever played! Whenever you think you've gotten bored, you're truly not!
Before reading please understand that I am a very hardcore fan of Rooster Teeth's RWBY animated series though my feedback is presented after playing the game's unfinished 1st campaign with two different playthroughs.
You see a beautiful main menu screen upon opening this game that entails the bright and graphically handsome visuals of Emerald Forest, a slowly/mildly turning camera around the mis-én-scene. You have three options (I believe); PLAY, SETTINGS and EXIT (QUIT).
Under the settings you will find that you can choose between potato (yes potato), standard (neutral graphical settings, not too high but not too potato either) :-) and lastly ultra, which maxes out everything and gives you a bloom effect. Sadly there is no advanced graphical setting at this current time however it is acceptable seeing that this is at its pre-alpha (or alpha) stage. If you are a user who owns a beast (or even fairly decent) computer, chances are you are very capable of running it at ultra, the game has little recommended requirements, I get a SOLID 60 fps (hell, it even goes to 61 at times!)
You will very rarely experience the occasional fps spike when appearing in a large crowd of Grimm, though it is expected after all! Additionally, you will also SOMETIMES see your character's running animation freeze for a few miliseconds when advancing along a steep path and/or bumpy path.
I first started this game with no other than Weiss Schnee (Yep, not Ruby! Weiss-o serious?). I got the YANG of this game after a good few minutes of gameplay and if I may say so myself, it is pretty great in comparison to other early access Steam games at a very early alpha stage.
If you are looking to buy this, please understand that the developers are doing their best so expect faults! They gave this beauty to us at an alpha stage to enjoy as they continue to create more content. I asked a game developer and he said they're hoping to update the game monthly assuming progress is going swell.
Finally, at this present time there is only one campaign and it is incomplete. You will experience around a couple hours worth of gameplay to rack up (average imo).
TL;DR -
If you want to support Roosterteeth's RWBY Game Team then please buy this game, it is HEAPS of fun with friends! Rate: 9/10 (alpha rating).
+ PROS +
+ It's A FREAKING RWBY GAME!
+ RWBY cast voice actors
+ Yang puns
+ GOOO TEAM RWBY!
+ Addictive and fun
+ Great gameplay for early alpha game
+ No bugs with monsters that I've seen (Grimm)
+ 4 player coop is well optimized
+ Performance is a solid 7-8/10
- CONS -
- Occasional momentary FPS spikes (for me it went down from 60 to 38-41 but immediately shot back up to a solid 60)
- Can't move your camera up higher than average camera height
- Not enough usage of RWBY music ( + not loud enough)
- You don't keep your level and skills after leaving your game session and going into another one
- Yang doesn't make noises when she fights (not that I can hear)
- Semblances aren't 100% complete for each character
Can't think of any more cons, though the ones I've listed already are easily fixable as the developers release updates as time goes by. :)

My friends and I have taken to calling this game "Tremor". Daedalus is Quake 3 Arena put through a blender and distilled to its core elements. It's great for quick bursts of action gaming, with games usually only lasting 5-10 minutes. Hence the moniker, as it's a mini-Quake.
It's a lot of fun, and has a map editor and various game modes to keep it interesting.
A recommendation for new players: The default control scheme is set to "FPS" mode, where the view rotates in the direction your character is facing. I found this control setup to be clunky and difficult to use. I recommend switching the control mode to "Classic" and checking the "Always face crosshair" option. This locks the view rotation, and the movement keys move you in an absolute direction, not a relative one. I.e., W will move towards the top of the screen, regardless of which way you're facing. It's much more intuitive for me. Always face crosshair allows you to more precisely control your character's facing, which is useful as you can fire faster, you move quickest when facing the same direction you are travelling in, and visibility is always a concern.
Another thing that's not made explicitly clear: Hit 'F' to turn on your flashlight. It's a bit of a double-edged sword, though. It'll illuminate darkened rooms and corridors, but it will also cause you to stand out to anybody else in the area. I recommend using it short bursts. Turn it on, survey the room, turn it off, and then immediately reposition.

Played for quite a few hours, but the lack of content and no progression between characters killed my enthusiasm for this game.
Pros:
+ Interesting Setting: Some characters interesting, and everyone is an idiot.
+ Drinking Booze: Sounds interesting as a method of getting buffs. (The booze is actually radioactive and mutates you).
+ Voice Acting: It's alright when it's there, not all of it is good though.
+ Gunplay is alright: Nothing really wrong with the gunplay besides the knockback that is.
+ Different Clothes grant different stat buffs: You can easily change up your gameplay style on the fly simply but looting the enemies.
Cons:
- Lack of weapons: You'll be seeing the same weapons, alot.
- Lack of special weapons: The only time you get special weapons is by killing a boss, or completing one of the rare quests. It's very rare to find upgrades to weapons so don't count on that either.
- Lack of variety in rooms: Seriously there's only like 20 or so different room variations before you have seen them all, and they don't change regardless of which dungeon you're in, besides the color tone.
- Small inventory limit: You can only hold 10 items, which includes ammo. So there's alot of inventory swapping. Yes you can get bumbags to increase your item carry limit but it doesn't help much it only increases the item count by 2 per bag. (The bag itself takes up 1 slot).
- Knock-back on weapons: If you get caught by surprise, you'll be sent flying back. This can get really bad if the enemy has a shotgun, or a minigun which traps you in it's line of fire.
- The random factor is bad: You can get a random buff for a dungeon run by drinking flasks of booze, though some can really kill your run if it's really bad. For example: If you are running a stealth based build, and drink some booze and all of a sudden I get - 4 to sneak. That pretty much kills that type of run, in general I got more negative effects than positive.
- Ending Runs early is just annoying: You can end runs early by drinking special bottles of booze, which you can actually see what effect they give. Though ending a run early means you'll need to redo the entire dungeon just for one buff to your character. That's up to 12 floors you have to re-run if you drink a bottle, and this can take up to 30 minutes - 1 hour to redo. You can't skip floor either.
- No progression between different characters: Did your character die? Well any buffs you got from drinking are gone, and you'll have to find all those bottles again if you want the same buffs. You also lose all the items you had on you, so if you had decent weapons and gear, all of that is gone as well.
- S.O.B. Enforcer / Time Limit is Annoying: It's a roguelike, but I have to bum-rush my way through an entire floor if I don't want to deal with an annoying guy with sponge like health and a minigun that traps me in it's line of fire. Even if you kill him on a floor, another one will show up on the next floor after so there isn't much benefit in killing him besides providing rifle ammo. At least he isn't too hard to kill since the A.I. isn't bright and he only walks.
- Bosses suck: They either change the gameplay up too much where stealth based characters iare rendered useless, or they do too much damage. Fighting a Tank after having only killed humans and basic robots for 12 floors is a big change in fighting style. While the Third Boss pretty much one shot me.
- No purpose of the Daily Run: There's not much point in doing the daily runs as you can only transfer 1 item back to your current character. Unless you really like leader-boards.
- Can't customize Characters: Yes you can customize your first character, but after that one dies, it's completely random on what you get. Plus there's no point in having unlock able hairstyles / faces if I can't actually create a character that uses it.
- Tinker Stat is pointless: Tinker is used to disable traps, or I can just shoot the trap and / or avoid the trap altogether.
Summary:
5/10
Lack of content, and alot of annoying gameplay choices does not make a good game.
If you're looking for a good rogue-like game I recommend Rogue Legacy. I preferred that game much more than this one.

Wasted is like Fallout but since the 80s is in vogue now, it's about the 80s instead of the 50s.
There's a surprising amount of depth to the combat with the hitstun system.  The game calls it knockback, because how long you're stunned and how far you're sent flying directly correlate, but the hitstun interesting part.  It works exactly the same for the player as it does for the enemy, so against the tougher enemies, you have to get into a rhythm of shooting and taking cover which ends up feeling a lot like how swinging and blocking works in other games (there is melee, but I haven't really tried it).
I'm just going to recommend that you do not think of the Booze feature in Wasted as an upgrade system.  It's really just a way to teleport out of the dungeon, and the upgrade is a little something on the side.  IMO it's more worthwhile just to get to the hard parts of the dungeon as quickly as possible in order to learn how to beat the enemies there.
An interesting design choice is that after death, you can buy back your unique items for a not so hard to acquire amount of money (as long as you remember to throw some rifle ammo into the Courier boxes).  This means that uniques end up being how Wasted does permanent upgrades.  Though really, uniques and Booze and all of that are kinda just there on the size.  The main form of choosing your character's 'build' is with common equipment; also an interesting choice.  It means you can totally change strategies with just a few kills, which I actually think is pretty fun.
Also, I only got killed by the Purifier once.  He walks after you pretty slowly and usually I never even even see him.  He's more of a vaguely scary element than anything.
I think that Wasted's biggest problem is that the early parts are too easy and too long, such that the tough (and very fun) combat gets spread a rather thin.  I think the devs tried to rectify this with the Purifier feature, which says to you "Hey, this is a randomly generated level.  There are more like this.  This is not Fallout 3.  Please move on."  I personally would rather have fewer levels and a higher difficulty for each rather than a Doom-esque maze race with monsters.  But, you know, people pay for volume, even if it's randomly generated volume.
Still, even ignoring the random generation, the amount of hand-crafted content in Wasted enormous.  It's easily worth the $13 price point (and apparently I'm nowhere close to beating it).

It is developed by Arthur Lee, who is well known in the indie game community for games like
,
, and
. These games each feature some form of spoofing and homage of other popular games, and
is no exception. The best way to describe it is a mix of
and
with a first-person roguelike flavor in the vein of
or
. Fortunately, the formula mixes up familiar mechanics in a way that creates a game that can stand on its own amongst its inspirations.
Gameplay-wise, it doesn't stray too far away from other first-person-shooters. There's not a lot to say about innovative combat other than some of the RPG-elements involved, such as crippling limbs and a certain weapon granting a huge damage bonus for shooting groins. There are even stealth elements involved. Levels are procedurally generated, with room layouts that become quickly memorized after a couple of runs. There's a good variety of items to loot and weapons to use, but you're limited by small carrying capacities to stress optimization of your loadout. Completing all 10 floors of a dungeon will unlock a new one (with 5 in total), each with its own unique classes of enemies and items.
Fans of roguelikes will be familiar with the permadeath mechanic. Upon death, you lose all of your items, money, and stats. However, this doesn't necessarily mean you have to start from scratch: you can send items back to your base during your run, and you can keep and store all of your loot after successfully leaving a dungeon. This helps the game appeal to novice and hardcore players alike by providing a sense of progression with each playthrough like in
. Plus, you can pick up positive or negative perks that permanently persist between runs on your current character, adding more variation to your playstyle, similar to
. To keep things interesting and to prevent players from straying too long, a powerful enemy, the Purifier spawns at the entrance of every level if you don't find the exit in time, like the ghost in
. As a result, the game remains fast-paced with a sense of urgency even in a genre that's known for taking time exploring every nook and cranny possible.
Unlike other roguelikes, however, there is an overarching storyline that progresses as you beat each dungeon. New mechanics also get unlocked as you beat levels. There are multiple endings and paths that can be achieved through its questlines, which warrant multiple playthroughs, adding to its replayability factor. There's even a daily challenge involved through Courier Runs, allowing you to compete online for the best score, and furthers your progression even more by giving you the opportunity to stash an item from your run if you play well enough.
Aesthetically, the game is most similar to
in its artistic renderings. The cartoony graphics may put off some people, but I personally find them charming. Its lo-fi sensibilities also let me run the game smoothly from a laptop without the need for an optimal gaming computer. Plus, it also has a cute and catchy soundtrack.
captured the dark synths of the 80's, while
embraces its pop and rock flavors. It honestly makes me question which game honored its nostalgia better! The voice-acting is also akin to both
and
, with humorous dialogue from competent voice actors.
Of course, the game isn't perfect. The difficulty may surprise some players for its surface-level cuteness. Permadeath already turns most people off, and some players feel like the Purifier can make the game too hard and doesn't let you take your time. Furthermore, the level design isn't particularly awe-inspiring either. A couple of runs in a dungeon will show you pretty much all of the room variations it has to offer, and the art assets will also become very commonplace as well. Players of other first-person roguelikes may also not see anything too unique that it has to offer from its gameplay, as others like
include arguably better mechanics.
There are also other small game design problems. For instance, you can't unload ammo from guns. According to the developer, this was done in order to balance the game properly as ammo would be too common, especially with most enemies carrying guns in later levels. Furthermore, regular players of FPS games may not like that there is no automatic reloading for guns. Also, players have had frustration dealing with knockback and hitstun, especially with the Purifier mechanic. For a good minority of players, it was an actual dealbreaker that ruined the game for them. Players who like RPGs for finding amazing loot may also be disappointed for a lack of wide variety in gear. Rather than focusing on obtaining powerful and unique items, the game is built more for using your skills as a player to make it through. There are a few bugs here and there as well, but I personally haven't experienced any gamebreakers or crashes.
All in all,
is a wonderful labor of love. There's lots of humor and meta-commentary, typical of any game published from Adult Swim. Arthur Lee has done a great job of expanding his portfolio as a flexible game designer and has definitely created a game that can appeal to a wide audience. He's also very active on the Steam forums and is willing to listen to user feedback. It's a great achievement for a game made by just one person. For $12.99, you're getting a lot of value for your money, so I hope you'll give it a chance.

I feel I should give this game a positive rating, but I do so under great conflict.
The game is good. Great, even. More than good enough to recommend to others as a good Mortal Kombat game at it's core. However there are things about this game which will leave a bad taste in your mouth, especially if you're a long time Mortal Kombat fan like myself.
If you like Mortal Kombat, and enjoyed the previous installment, then you'll enjoy this one. They've pretty much kept the core gameplay intact, tweaking and adding just enough to make it feel fresh again. Along with a roster of familiar fighters, some new and interesting faces come along. Be it the new fighting pair Ferra/Torr, or offspring of established franchise mainstays, Cassie Cage and Jacqui Briggs. The latter two are a nice touch to make the canon feel like it's actually moving forward, and that what's taking place in Mortal Kombat X is clearly some time after the events of Mortal Kombat 9.
Gameplay wise you have the usual mechanics, the super meter which can be used for an enhanced version of a Special Attack, a combo breaker or a powerful X-Ray attack, just like the previous game. New to this game is environmental hazards, but they are not obstructive or constantly interrupting hazards like you would expect. Instead these obstacles are placed strategically at certain points of the arena, and with the press of the button you can interact with them to perform a context sensitive action with them. Spots placed on the very edges of the stage will act as "walls" for you to run up and leap off of to prevent cheap cornering tactics, and everything else in between will allow you to damage your opponent. It's a pretty fun concept and it never gets old batting a metal post over the opponent's head or throwing an old lady at them when they try to approach you.
As well as the usual modes such as Tower/Ladder, the Story Mode from the previous game makes a return in this one. It works pretty much the same way, being mostly cinematic cutscenes that play out a pretty interesting story where you'll occasionally play key fights as some of the game's fighters. It's a nice way to give you a chance to try out and experiment with some fighters outside of normal matches, but it doesn't feature everybody as playable. The story mode also has occasional Quick Time Event moments, but these ultimately serve to waste your time, as you could miss every single button prompt and still be able to advance the story like there was no consequence. The story is a decent single player distraction but ultimately I found it feeling a little lacking compared to MK9, which I felt did it better overall.
That's the good. Now the bad.
The main issue is microtransactions. This game is absolutely chock-full of this type of business practice. Something that should definitely raise many an eyebrow as you would not expect such a thing to be in a game that some paid $60 for. And that's not including the optional "Kollector's Edition" or the season pass.
The most common and probably most infamous of these microtransactions comes in the form of paying for Easy Fatality Tokens. In this game, you can perform an "Easy Fatality", which is a simple two-button combination, at the cost of a Token. Outside of the few free Tokens given to you, you have to pay for more online if you wish to continue performing Easy Fatalities. This does not bother me personally as I am quite content executing Fatalities the normal way, and therefore does not directly affect my experience with the game. But it is no less a concept that the game would have been better without.
The real bone I have to pick with this game is in how it handles The Krypt content. In the last few Mortal Kombat games, The Krypt is a place where you go to spend your in-game "Koins" in order to unlock a wealth of hidden content, ranging from Fatalities/Brutalities, Concept Art, Music etc. As you play the game, you earn Koins which you can then use in The Krypt. The idea is implemented in this game, but this time around they've deliberately designed the game so that it's extremely difficult to earn Koins through conventional means. They've basically done this so that they could try to sell you the easy option of unlocking everything in The Krypt for $20. It's either that, or get ready to do a ton of dull grinding for Koins. I've played this game for over 40 hours, and more than half of that was grinding. I'm not even joking.
And finally, there's the Kombat Pack, the game's season pass equivalent. Though at the time of speaking the first wave of season pass content has yet to be released (It was actually supposed to be today, but it got pushed back a week. Go figure.), the overall season pass content feels a little, lacking. There's new alt costumes, sure, but ignoring the the fact that two of the new fighters are really neat guest characters, you only get a total of four new fighters. For $30, that's really stretching it in terms of value.
Overall, it's a good game, hence the positive rating. But the rating was barely a pass in my book. As a diehard Mortal Kombat fan I can't help but feel a bit cheated that not only is there less content in this game than there was in the last, but that the publisher thinks it's okay to ask people to fork over more money in microtransaction fees for a game that most people paid the standard RRP to play. Hopefully the next Mortal Kombat will deliver more and rip off less.

Let me get this straight, you want me to tell you a review about this game? Whoever you are, you might as well go to the curators, because if you've come for a review on this game, you've come to the wrong place. However, if you have come for an outstanding chocolate chip cookie recipe, you've come to the right place.
---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Ingredients
1/2 cup (1 stick) unsalted butter
3/4 cup packed dark brown sugar
3/4 cup sugar
2 large eggs
1 teaspoon pure vanilla extract
1 (12-ounce) bag semisweet chocolate chips, or chunks
2 1/4 cups all-purpose flour
3/4 teaspoon baking soda
1 teaspoon fine salt
Directions
1. Evenly position 2 racks in the middle of the oven and preheat to 375 degrees F. (on convection setting if you have it.) Line 2 baking sheets with parchment paper or silicone sheets. (If you only have 1 baking sheet, let it cool completely between batches.)
2. Put the butter in a microwave safe bowl, cover and microwave on medium power until melted. (Alternatively melt in a small saucepan.) Cool slightly. Whisk the sugars, eggs, butter and vanilla in a large bowl until smooth.
3. Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt in another bowl. Stir the dry ingredients into the wet ingredients with a wooden spoon; take care not to over mix. Stir in the chocolate chips or chunks.
4. Scoop heaping tablespoons of the dough onto the prepared pans. Wet hands slightly and roll the dough into balls. Space the cookies about 2-inches apart on the pans. Bake, until golden, but still soft in the center, 12 to 16 minutes, depending on how chewy or crunchy you like your cookies. Transfer hot cookies with a spatula to a rack to cool. Serve.
5. Store cookies in a tightly sealed container for up to 5 days.
For a Rocky Road Bar:
1. Lightly butter a 9 by 13-inch baking pan. Make the batter as per cookie recipe and fold in 1 cup chopped walnuts along with the chocolate chips. Spread batter in prepared pan. Bake until the edges are light brown and the batter sets, about 45 minutes. Cool slightly and cover surface with 4 cups marshmallows and 1 cup chocolate chips. Broil at least 8 inches from the heat until marshmallows turn golden brown, about 2 minutes. (Keep an eye on the marshmallows, and turn the pan frequently--they go from golden to char in a wink.) Cool, cut and serve.

Alright, a little about me and how I'll try all my might to not have this review be biased. I'm a huge fan of Roosterteeth, RWBY has been one of those series that have taken my heart and I am in love with this show, the world, the character, the concepts- everything. When I heard an official game was in the works, I swear I cried. Now that it's in my possesion, I was so excited to play this game, I expected a whole lot from a company so invested in video games, you'd think they'd get everything right.
So far, I'd say they got enough right for this game to be actually enjoyable- even if this is still a day one review.
I'm only gonna summarize the game a bit. You and your team are a four-man squadrant composed of teenage girls with powerful weapons. You can pick one of these lovely girls to be in while you battle. These characters are Ruby Rose, Yang Xiao Long, Blake Belladonna, Weiss Schnee. Not gonna go over their characters, and I'm not gonna explain what they're doing or why they're here. The combat system is basically, spam left click, press some buttons, and try to defeat all the Grimm, (the strange monsters,) in the stage at that moment. When you join a game, you are basically going through a campaign, and once the "campaign," (I'm using the term loosely, because I think this is the only thing that really decribes this progression though the game,) is over, you return to the party screen, and restart the campaign. Now, lets get on to the looks and what not. You gain experience through combat, you can unlock powerups to your existing 3 special moves, and your health bar is the Aura bar at the bottom right. It depletes, you have a few seconds to dodge hits and not get hit again before you die. If you don't recieve damage for a certain amount of time, your health fills up, and you're able to go back to hacking and slashing your way through the game.
Visually, this game is quite nice. The scenery surrounding you is wonderful, the character models are quite nicely done, and, (even if this is just the Day 1 review,) the animations are actually more glitch-free than I thought they would be. There are times where the walk cycle glitches out and the character model is stuck in the same pose as it walks down the stairs, but generally, the animations are fluid. The grim get the same issues when they are pushed against a wall, their walk cycles turn a bit wonky, but it's still nice. The GUI is lackluster, but this is early access, I wouldn't be surprised if it gets updated. The main menu GUI is simplistic, and that's totally fine, but the in-game gui is a bit confusing to get used to. I'm personally not used to looking at the bottom right corner of my games, because I usually get notifications there.
If someone logs into skype while you're playing this game, and you have notifications on- your aura bar is gone from sight and you only have some visual cues and audio cues to tell you that you need to get the hell out of there. (Added note; I would have also enjoyed being able to see the aura of my other teammates, and even their specials bar. It could make for easier coordination and teamwork, [this could also take away from the idea of a hack and slash, maybe, but coordination and teamwork are always fun.])
The BGM and voice acting are a nice touch though, I enjoy listening to all the quips and quirky one-liners characters say at the end of waves or stages. It's entertaining. I have to say though, there are instances where there were character dialog subtittled at the bottom, (because I like having subtitles on,) and their small character picture to the left was speaking, but an entirely different character's voice came through. Example; Yang's picture and subtitles were on the screen, but I heard Ruby instead.
Now, the actual "campaign," (I seriously don't know what to call this,) follows team RWBY through a forest, through some ruins, underground, and then to the location of a bomb. Seriously. I appreciate the idea of incorporating so many different meathods of playing the game. It goes from a simple, stage by stage fight, then to defending a point, back to stage by stage, then another defend the point, some more waves of Grimm, and then the last part. The bomb part. This part of the whole game is by far the hardest part to do alone. I would know, my team ditched me and I had to get the bomb to the end on my own. Did I succeed? Nope. a 85% the bomb exploded and I was a sad sally, but you know, life moves on, and I figured this game was going to be impossible to play without teammates. If you also want a four player experience throughout the campaign, I'm going to tell you now, you're not going to get it. I've never been able to finish with all 4 characters present, people drop out way too fast when things get dicey. This is also a positive thing, because the game recognizes this and changes the difficulty, which is a plus.
I quickly added this part before I posted the review, but I have to say, the combat between Ruby, Blake, and Weiss are strikingly similar and gets repetitive. While on the other hand, Yang's combat is lackluster compared to them. They all have AOE or large attacks that affect a multitude of enemies around them, while Yang has her two special punches, and a ground pound with the radius of a corn nut. It made my experience while playing Yang make me feel like I wasn't doing as much work as the rest of the team. She does make up for it by her ability to have her full specials bar come back in almost an instant, but still, her combat is the only one with slight difference in comparison to the other characters who can swoop in, use an AOE and steal
of the kills. All of 'em.
Speaking of teammates, I kind of want a single player version of this. Maybe a training mode where your teammates are really idiotic CPUs who let you have all the kills- just so someone could get used to the controls. But this is, yet again, something I want and if it doesn't get added, I won't be mad. I also won't be mad if you don't buy this game. It's not for everyone, and it's the best game yet. (Nor will it ever be, maybe.)
Either way, this is a wonderful start for this game's Early Access and here's probably why you should, or shouldn't get it. I'm also not summing up anything I said in Pro's and Con's because I'm lazy.
I am also too lazy to stop myself from doing it.
- Graphically wonderful with pretty fluid animations.
- Non-Overbaring story that guides you though the game, (good for people who don't actually know RWBY.)
- Difficulty changes dependent on player count.
- Exotic scenery and character designs make this more unique than other franchises, (which makes it good for the game also.)
- Unbalanced Audio, (voice acting too quiet, special moves overbaringly loud, etc.)
- Repetitive Combat
- Early Access
Should you get this game? I'd say yes if you like RWBY, like unfinished games, and enjoy watching cute girls battle monsters. In any other case, just wait till it's out of Early Access, or more updated.

Pros:
- The graphics are extremely impressive for a 2008 game. I found the lightning to be jawdroppingly superb - the best in any of the S.T.A.L.K.E.R.-games in my opinion, perhaps even in any game I've ever seen.

- Most of the dialogue in the game was well written, more in-depth and captivating than the first game. I really enjoyed the attention to detail given even though it didn't directly affect the gameplay. Especially the introductory stages of the game did this well, improving on the already excellent atmosphere.

Cons:
- Gameplay was definitely a downgrade from the first game. Despite having played at master difficulty, with its emphasis on realistic gunplay, tougher enemies later in the game felt like bullet-sponges.
- Weak end game. The story basically fell apart 2/3 through the game.
Conclusion:
- Overall an improvement over the first game, with tenser atmosphere and more interesting dialogue. The game is far from perfect though, with a very weak ending and somewhat average gameplay mechanics.

Fun, funny, and frustrating. The three F's of Wasted. An FPS dungeon crawler rogue-like with a ton of charm and a wicked sense of humor. There's a lot of game here depending on your skills, and some fun systems to experiment with. While permadeath is there, you can and will make progress by stocking up your Home on Cooler runs so future 'wasters' you play won't have to start from scratch.
'Wasted' is a gem, I feel, with serviceable graphics (I think they are quite nice) and solid gunplay, with what seems to be a nice amount of content since you will most likely die in a fire/explosion/pool of acid slime often enough. And while the S.O.B. seems to have stirred up some controversy amongst players, I feel like he adds impetus to the gameplay. Loot is plentiful, but not altogether that varied, and soon enough you will find yourself moving through levels much quicker, which makes him less of an issue. Without the S.O.B., 'Wasted' would be far too casual an affair.
The booze system is also great, and really gives the game that rogue feel. You will find flasks that you can drink to give you either buffs or do things like make you move 90% slower if your crouched. There are also bottles of booze that will send you home (you'll have to start your next Cooler run from the beginning) and give you a hangover, which are permanent effects that last as long as your character survives. It's a fun risk/reward system that isn't too punishing, and can create some interesting synergies in combat. They can also make things a lot more challenging, depending.

This is a top-down multiplayer shooter with play style reminiscent of Unreal or Quake (but in 2d, obviously). There's a decent variety of weapons from plasma guns to flame throwers to rocket launchers and the line of sight mechanic is pretty well executed. Overall, technical execution is good.
On the flip side, the game play doesn't hook me. I like shooters like 1942 and enjoy a ton of bullet hell shooters and such, but I don't really enjoy playing this one. Aside from weapon effects, the colors are pretty dark and the visuals are somewhat drab. I tend to get stuck on walls quite a bit -- not really the fault of the designers, just a quirk of the gameplay style or map design I guess. Some of the pathways are pretty narrow.
With the tight corridors and limited field of view, a lot of battles end up as whack-a-mole as you strafe in / out of a hallway, circle strafing or spinning your mouse around to fight in a larger room. It's kinda disorienting and anyone trying to watch you play is going to get sick.
Unreal Tournament introduced a lot of Z-axis action (jumps, multiple elevations, vertical maps, etc.) to try to make the FPS experience a bit more dynamic and I think with only 2 axes you miss out on the opportunity for really cool environments and varied pathways to fight in.
