This is where I wish Steam had a 1-5 or 1-10 star system instead of simply "do you recommend this game." There is a lot to love about this sim, and a LOT that it could improve on. As a train enthusiast I have been railsimming since MSTS was in its heyday so I came here expecting a solid product. I feel like Dovetail delivered, for the MOST part.
Pros:
- The routes are done quite nicely, and are faithfully recreated.
- The graphics don't send me to the moon, but are pretty good. An improvement over MSTS for sure.
- Not much of a learning curve, at least for people already familiar with MSTS. Layout is basically the same, except throttle-up and throttle-down are reverse of what they were in MSTS.
- Cab view is done very nicely in my opinion. The ability to switch seats, the windshield wiper effects during rain, etc. were very enjoyable for me.
Cons:
- Some of the in-game sounds seem like they are recycled from Trainz or MSTS, such as several throttle-up sounds. The horns also leave a lot to be desired in some cases. A few of them cut off immediately once you release the space bar. While the sound is generally ok, I think it is mediocre for the most part.
-No keymapping system. I would LOVE to change the throttle key commands I mentioned earlier to the MSTS scheme I'm used to.
- The marketing system for this program is simply indefensible. The DLCs are laughably overpriced, and perhaps even funnier are the attempts that hard-core enthusiasts make to defend this scheme. Why in the world would you put hundreds or thousands of dollars into a handful of routes and locomotives? Most routes are about $20 full price (only marked down to $12 or so during sales) and even more ridiculously, individual LOCOMOTIVES are about the same price. You want a GP40? Or an SD70? That'll be $20! I don't care how into trains you are. You are completely moronic if you shell out dough for loads of this stuff. I'm content to sit by with a mere handful of items I got packaged with the game until Dovetail realizes how incomprehensibly stupid their business model is. This is NOT like HO model railroading. Stop pretending it is.
With all of that said, this sim just barely manages to leave me with a positive impression. If you are not a rail enthusiast you are pretty much guaranteed to not enjoy this program. Rail enthusiasts (at least this guy) can be satisfied with very little variety, which is what this program offers unless you want to throw your money towards digital content not worth a fifth of what they ask for it. But the gameplay is immersive and engaging enough for me to enjoy, and offers enough of a challenge to make it worthwhile.

Like a lot of men, trains have been my thing. Always wanted to be an engineer, and even did a little "gandy-dancing" when I was young. Instead, I became a house painter.
I like TS, and have "invested" a couple of thousand dollars in DLC. Now, I don't buy any of it. The game remains the same, year after year. I have a superfast computer--8-core, 32 GB RAM, nVidia GTX-780 super-clocked, blah-blah-blah. The game takes a long time to load. Click on the 'Drive' icon on the main screen and then wait for awhile to see any response. Why?
In some of the routes, you'll see graphics glitches, like the sky flashing and disappearing. Honestly, this is a rare event and it seems to be restricted to a few routes that were perhaps not compiled well. In other places, the game will stutter if there's too many polygons to render. Again, not often but enough to make you wonder what kind of garbage is being thrown into your gfx card.
Perhaps my most severe complaint is about the game developer. They're making a fortune from DLC but they won't fix certain routes (Doncaster Works, e.g.). The so-called "problem reporting" link is horribly unfriendly. Even a snail-mail letter was not answered, where I complained about certain broken routes that they still sell at full price.
Overall, TS is a good game if you're the casual engineer. Just avoid too much DLC.

I'm new to Tekken - played Tag 2 really casually - so mechanically I can't speak much about this game until I learn more. All I've done so far is some arcade, treasure battles, practice room, and lobbies with friends; so I'm writing this review soley because of how impressed the port has made me.
Fighting games always get jipped when it comes to PC. They have the smallest player base compared to consoles and always seem to have a problem with button layout instructions or poor optimization causing frame drops etc. But not T7; oh boy this game is so well written I think my computer enters sleep mode running it.
On my practical dinosaur of a GeForce 960 I'm running the game on Medium / High Custom settings at 1920x1080 at a constant 60fps. My short time spent in Street Fghter V found me dealing with frame drops on specific stages and potato textures, but T7 provides beauty and performance all under one neat little bow.
The communities for Tekken over on Discord / Reddit / Youtube are also noticing the huge influx of noobs like me into the series, and in response those places have been exploding with new player guides and tutorials. The skill ceiling for this game is very very very high - its daunting and scary - but the community outreach has made it so that even I feel I might be able to Korean Backdash at some point (but probably not haha).
So far I'm having fun. Hell even practice mode is fun when I finally land a move or understand some mechanic. Fighting games are always short lived on PC so I'm gonna enjoy it while I can, but hey, maybe this port is just good enough to break the cycle.

Tekken 7 has a large amount of enjoyable single player content such as the story mode, character episodes, arcade mode, and treasure battle (you get rewards for playing the single player modes too which is nice). This is the first time in a long time that I've tried single player content in a fighting game, normally it's not my thing but I'm glad I did with this game. It was definitely fun watching the over-the-top cutscenes and doing the boss battles. They really did a great job with bosses in this game, they all look very cool and have great moves. Also, you hardly have to play online if you want to collect all the achievements, which could be another pro if you are an achievement hunter.
The game is also extremely fun/interesting to learn for competitive players and probably has the highest skill ceiling of any fighter out right now. Between the slow motion, new rage mechanics, the freedom in movement, and the amount of moves every character has you see so much variety and excitement in this game when you watch or play it. I personally think the game is enjoyable at any level of play. The quality of the online gameplay is up there with Guilty Gear and KI, which I'm proud to say is flawless probably 90-95/100 matches. I've yet to have a match that was just unplayable due to lag, which is very common in certain fighting games made by Capcom.
My only complaints are the fact that you cannot instantly rematch someone in a 1v1 player lobby, and that in ranked you only get a best of 2 match instead of a FT2. If you want to grind long sets, do it in quick match because you can instantly rematch an opponent there. My last complaint is more of a request, I wish the player lobbies worked like they do in Guilty Gear where the players who are waiting for their turns can play against each other instead of watching the two people at the head of the lobby fight.
Side Note: After you have played a total of 2,000 offline or online matches you automatically unlock all the customizables, this is a fantastic addition for players who do not like single player modes.
*EDIT* They added infinite rematches in ranked and a rematch button in player lounge. Great game.

I was a bit skeptical at first, but it sounded interesting. My fiancee purchased the game for us to try it out, and well... look at my current time frame. I hate to compare it, but I mean, it's fairly obvious it reminds me of Minecraft. However, I find this game so much enjoyable to play in all aspects.
The crafting is fantastic, and it actually looks like wood, or rock, or cobblestone without the use of mods to make the skins enjoyable to look at. Variety of armors, weapons, bombs, potion and ACTUAL furniture for your home.
You can create multiple characters, with multiple world. Decent customization as well.
The combat is also enjoyable, but could use some work as the camera zoom in feels dizzying at times when the monster jerks towards you, and more than one monster attacks you. Still, it's a minor complain as I often go out and explore dungeons and homes in different worlds.
I have only have a few complaints:
1) Allow other players to travel alone if they wish, don't force the other to come with. Sometimes one wants to explore, and the other crafting. I don't see the reason why both players need to go together.
2) Longer, more fullfilling dungeons/exploration - it seems far too short. The dungeons seem to be lackluster, and small at times. I wish there was more to explore and do.
That's it. It's a fantatic game, and greatly looking forward to the full release.

This was a fun point-and-click with enough challenging puzzles to keep me interested, but a bit lacklustre in other areas.
I liked the premise - a world built on a junk yard - and I likedthat many of the puzzles required you to get creative and build things out of unconventional materials. I did get stuck a few times and had to look up prompts, which I hate doing, but it helped me think about future puzzles differently so I didn't need help towards the end.
While the voice acting was decent enough, I found the characters to be quite generic, and I did not care for Rufus's weird creepy possessiveness of Goal as some kind of prize (even her name alludes to this).
My main annoyance was that this game has way too much unnecessary dialogue; I put the subtitles on so I could quickly skip through the lines unless they had some useful information. The dialogue was often trying to be funny but much of it was fluff. I like this kind of Monkey Island style game with quirky humour, and there was some of that, but a lot of it could have been cut.
The ending was a bit abrupt. I didn't really care for the storyline towards the end; it felt rushed and the puzzles became fewer and further between to make way for overindulgent cut scenes. Overall I enjoyed it, but I'm glad I got it at the sale price.

Alright, a little about me and how I'll try all my might to not have this review be biased. I'm a huge fan of Roosterteeth, RWBY has been one of those series that have taken my heart and I am in love with this show, the world, the character, the concepts- everything. When I heard an official game was in the works, I swear I cried. Now that it's in my possesion, I was so excited to play this game, I expected a whole lot from a company so invested in video games, you'd think they'd get everything right.
So far, I'd say they got enough right for this game to be actually enjoyable- even if this is still a day one review.
I'm only gonna summarize the game a bit. You and your team are a four-man squadrant composed of teenage girls with powerful weapons. You can pick one of these lovely girls to be in while you battle. These characters are Ruby Rose, Yang Xiao Long, Blake Belladonna, Weiss Schnee. Not gonna go over their characters, and I'm not gonna explain what they're doing or why they're here. The combat system is basically, spam left click, press some buttons, and try to defeat all the Grimm, (the strange monsters,) in the stage at that moment. When you join a game, you are basically going through a campaign, and once the "campaign," (I'm using the term loosely, because I think this is the only thing that really decribes this progression though the game,) is over, you return to the party screen, and restart the campaign. Now, lets get on to the looks and what not. You gain experience through combat, you can unlock powerups to your existing 3 special moves, and your health bar is the Aura bar at the bottom right. It depletes, you have a few seconds to dodge hits and not get hit again before you die. If you don't recieve damage for a certain amount of time, your health fills up, and you're able to go back to hacking and slashing your way through the game.
Visually, this game is quite nice. The scenery surrounding you is wonderful, the character models are quite nicely done, and, (even if this is just the Day 1 review,) the animations are actually more glitch-free than I thought they would be. There are times where the walk cycle glitches out and the character model is stuck in the same pose as it walks down the stairs, but generally, the animations are fluid. The grim get the same issues when they are pushed against a wall, their walk cycles turn a bit wonky, but it's still nice. The GUI is lackluster, but this is early access, I wouldn't be surprised if it gets updated. The main menu GUI is simplistic, and that's totally fine, but the in-game gui is a bit confusing to get used to. I'm personally not used to looking at the bottom right corner of my games, because I usually get notifications there.
If someone logs into skype while you're playing this game, and you have notifications on- your aura bar is gone from sight and you only have some visual cues and audio cues to tell you that you need to get the hell out of there. (Added note; I would have also enjoyed being able to see the aura of my other teammates, and even their specials bar. It could make for easier coordination and teamwork, [this could also take away from the idea of a hack and slash, maybe, but coordination and teamwork are always fun.])
The BGM and voice acting are a nice touch though, I enjoy listening to all the quips and quirky one-liners characters say at the end of waves or stages. It's entertaining. I have to say though, there are instances where there were character dialog subtittled at the bottom, (because I like having subtitles on,) and their small character picture to the left was speaking, but an entirely different character's voice came through. Example; Yang's picture and subtitles were on the screen, but I heard Ruby instead.
Now, the actual "campaign," (I seriously don't know what to call this,) follows team RWBY through a forest, through some ruins, underground, and then to the location of a bomb. Seriously. I appreciate the idea of incorporating so many different meathods of playing the game. It goes from a simple, stage by stage fight, then to defending a point, back to stage by stage, then another defend the point, some more waves of Grimm, and then the last part. The bomb part. This part of the whole game is by far the hardest part to do alone. I would know, my team ditched me and I had to get the bomb to the end on my own. Did I succeed? Nope. a 85% the bomb exploded and I was a sad sally, but you know, life moves on, and I figured this game was going to be impossible to play without teammates. If you also want a four player experience throughout the campaign, I'm going to tell you now, you're not going to get it. I've never been able to finish with all 4 characters present, people drop out way too fast when things get dicey. This is also a positive thing, because the game recognizes this and changes the difficulty, which is a plus.
I quickly added this part before I posted the review, but I have to say, the combat between Ruby, Blake, and Weiss are strikingly similar and gets repetitive. While on the other hand, Yang's combat is lackluster compared to them. They all have AOE or large attacks that affect a multitude of enemies around them, while Yang has her two special punches, and a ground pound with the radius of a corn nut. It made my experience while playing Yang make me feel like I wasn't doing as much work as the rest of the team. She does make up for it by her ability to have her full specials bar come back in almost an instant, but still, her combat is the only one with slight difference in comparison to the other characters who can swoop in, use an AOE and steal
of the kills. All of 'em.
Speaking of teammates, I kind of want a single player version of this. Maybe a training mode where your teammates are really idiotic CPUs who let you have all the kills- just so someone could get used to the controls. But this is, yet again, something I want and if it doesn't get added, I won't be mad. I also won't be mad if you don't buy this game. It's not for everyone, and it's the best game yet. (Nor will it ever be, maybe.)
Either way, this is a wonderful start for this game's Early Access and here's probably why you should, or shouldn't get it. I'm also not summing up anything I said in Pro's and Con's because I'm lazy.
I am also too lazy to stop myself from doing it.
- Graphically wonderful with pretty fluid animations.
- Non-Overbaring story that guides you though the game, (good for people who don't actually know RWBY.)
- Difficulty changes dependent on player count.
- Exotic scenery and character designs make this more unique than other franchises, (which makes it good for the game also.)
- Unbalanced Audio, (voice acting too quiet, special moves overbaringly loud, etc.)
- Repetitive Combat
- Early Access
Should you get this game? I'd say yes if you like RWBY, like unfinished games, and enjoy watching cute girls battle monsters. In any other case, just wait till it's out of Early Access, or more updated.

I'd like to point out first that i'm a huge fan of the RWBY franchise and in my attempt to make a review I will try to stay as unbiased as possible. I don't feel like I need to point out the different story related elements since most of your already know them and the rest will have read it someplace else.
As an early access it was pretty obvious to me even before I started that the game would contain lots of bugs and little content, but despite knowing this I still wanted to dive into the RWBY universe and feel the rush of controlling one of the four protagonists from team RWBY.
My personal experience from playing this game is very positive, the controls required some getting used to but was very smooth. The battle animations was smooth aswell but certain enemies could sometimes lag in their attacks and mess up your dodge timing, but I endured it since it's just an early access. Obviously most of those issues will be dealt with as bug/glitch fixes and polishing.
The sound was alright quality wise but the sound levels was abit all over the place, loud combat sounds and low voices made it feel abit frustrating at time (I ended up lowering them alltogether and pull out my RWBY vol.1-2 soundtracks).
Graphics is really nice in a charming way, it's nothing fascinating like the big titles of 2015 but it serves its purpose of staying true to the RWBY universe. It's my personal hope that they do not change the style and direction they are going for, I just wish they would add alittle bit more of what already is there to the world and give it some more "depth".
When this review was made there was only one "Chapter" I suppose you could call it, called Emerald Forest and it had alot of areas for casual battles and a bunch of defense locations, a boss room and a escort mission. So there is/was quite alot of things to do. Only thing most people complained about here was that your leveling progress was resetted between each new run, only thing that was consistant was the progress of unlocking new ability upgrades. Hopefully they will look into this more ahead or perhaps they already plan to make changes to that.
There was some minor bugs that me and my friend personally found but nothing that halted the games progress so far, game has alot of work and polishing to do but all in all it was very fun and I could tell it would be one of those games that brings out an addiction in people once it's completed.
Now for some biased stuff, if you're into RWBY like myself... GET IT NOW AND STOP READING REVIEWS!!! The girls need you!!!
Thanks for taking your time to read this and I hope to see you all ingame, let's support and enjoy this game untill and past it's full release. :D

As hack 'n' slash's go, this game nails it. the game looks very true to the show (which make sense since the show is done in the same engine) the character models are good and their attacks are unique-looking (since they all basically have the same attacks) Each character acts as a blank slate, starting at level one at the start of the game, and eventually reaching the level cap of 10 with a nearly full skill tre, which means there is some replayability in the campaign as you can change your strategy to suit your playstile.
Now, the campaign is very short, which is excusable with it being early access, but I can't help but feel that the game was over faster than I could sneeze. The game has crashed on me multiple times (I'm running Windows 10, 8GB RAM, Core 2 Quad @2.66 GHz, r9 270) however I would like to hope that it would be patched ASAP and it only happened early on in the game so... meh. I'd also likle to see some more characters added to the game eventually, either that or alternate, unlockable costumes for team RWBY (Volume 2 alternate costumes, anyone??)
Overall, the game at the moment, is  pretty good, I for one love it and do recommend it to fans of the show, however newcomers might not have any grounding to appreciate the game for what it is so I'd say watch the show first so you can form your own opinions of the series before you pick this up.

After playing all the way through S.T.A.L.K.E.R.: Clear Sky I find myself forced to give it a positive rating. Why forced? Well it’s not a bad game but I think at best it’s a completely unnecessary game.
Following on from the original S.T.A.L.K.E.R this game is actually a prequel. You take on the role of a stalker called Scar who finds himself in the Zone tasked with hunting down a fellow stalker, Strelok, (who featured in the original game), before he reaches the centre of the zone.
The game introduces various factions and battles between them which you can take part in. However there’s never really any reason to do so unless the plot forces you to and if you do then the missions are fairly generic. So basically for the first half of the game you move between areas where you’ll find a character. Do a mission for them (and factions missions if you wish) and then move onto the next area.
There’s no real sense of urgency though and it’s only about two thirds of the way through that the game becomes more linear and it feels like an actual pursuit. However it’s really let down by a terrible final level, which to me seemed fairly broken, (
), and the ending is fairly constrained anyway, as the game is a prequel, so it all feels like a huge let-down by the end.
On the plus side, it’s more S.T.A.L.K.E.R and it looks great, but that’s about it. I’m not unhappy that I played it but I feel I could have just as easily got more S.T.A.L.K.E.R by replaying the original game.

Get WASTED in a post-apocalyptic world where only the dumbest lot survived. That also includes you but don't worry, there's enough booze for everyone. You might get a few mutations from it though.
The game is actually a rogue-like dungeon crawler (called Coolers) which means perma-death, loosing items, learning from you mistakes and so on. Every cooler has 10 floors and an additional boss floor and is randomly generated each time you enter it. But unlike other rogue-likes where you can just slowly walk your way through the dungeon/level/map, you have to be fast in WASTED. If you take to long on any given floor (except the boss floor) the S.O.B. sends one of its Purrifiers after you. You could engage it but I wouldn't advice doing so early on, instead just find your way to the next floor.
However, once you entered your chosen Cooler (you'll have a selection of a few of them later on), you can only leave it at floor 3, floor 6 or floor 10. (Or of course after you defeated it's boss) You do so, by drinking one of 4 Booze Bottles that will give you a hangover. Not just a regular hangover but one that will most likely give you a positive perk, or a negative one as a matter of fact for floor 3. You can also rarely find these bottles on any floor. The perks you aquire this way will stay with your current character until you die.
Itemwise, the game has alot going for it. There are tons of weapons, from pistols to revolvers, assault rifle, laser weapons and even melee weapons like brass knuckles, a cutana (katana) or even a Crowbar.
But be careful as to not waste your ammo. You can only take one full stack of each ammo type with you and you only have a limited inventory but you can of course find more ammo in the cooler itself.
Which is where you armor comes into play. You can equip a helmet, torso and leg armor or a complete outfit + helmet. These items push up your stats, like +Shoot, +Hit, +Oblit etc. They basically determine how much damage you deal.
Want to be a sword-wielding maniac? Itemize towards +Hit and Armor. Or do you want to go full on Rambo? Then Itemize towards +Shoot.
All in all, the game's great especially at its price tag. It's got great humor, runs absolutely fine, has nice gunplay, a good variation of enemy types. Did I also mention the currency ingame is toilet paper? Yea and the explanation for that makes more sense than bottle caps.

Rokko Chan X!! The game looks quite promising. I hope the final product will be well polished and at an affordable price. I don't think of it as the Megaman X we couldn't have because we had 6 of them (not counting 7 and 8 since they are quite different), I think of it as a competent clone and I hope you change your description. I like the idea of upgrading and will be quite challenging not to have a dash button, but you should also drop the "right weapon" mechanics for the bosses and focus on attack patterns instead. The shield should also have a limited use in high difficulty.
My complains are that it seems it needs a hi-spec PC to get full speed with the Render Quality option set at high, something I find kinda pointless considering the graphic style is retro-pixel. Which takes me to my other complain: the graphic style. "Retro-style" is been done to death, maybe you should add the option of hand-drawn hi-res graphics, that would be something new, no more 8-bit, 16-bit, 32-bit style crap. If the game is good, even though the game is like the games from the late 80s and 90s, you don't need to yell "retro" in every pixel.
I hope you change your story too, it's way to similar to Megaman X! Maybe you can make them cyborgs from a rival republic or a robot conversion gone wrong or an invasion of mechanical beings from outer space or another dimension, but please, please, not robot servers gone bad and turned against their masters, it's so cliche'd and we have the Terminator and Megaman series and certain mor-n who claims to be mighty for that already.
The music sounds good and not so chiptune, I hope it would get even better. Since the game looks more Amiga-like than SNES-like, maybe some protracker-like music will add more to that Amiga-mood I got. I'm looking forward to see the final product. Good luck!
EDIT: After playing more of it, I have some suggestions to make:
Although I didn't find the difficulty too hard, some younger players will find it quite hard for the first level, maybe a first-time only lower difficulty for the earlier levels will prevent you from getting bad reviews for the high difficulty, I don't understand it but a lot of good games have gotten bad review for being hard.
A diagonal shoot would be very welcomed too, it will change some mechanics and would probably require a different enemy placement but will also help the future complains for high difficulty (I can't believe it's an issue these days, it used to be a big sales factor).
There should also be an upgrade for the hands so that the character could stick in place to the walls rather than slowly slide, that would help to distant the game from its inspiration material.
And finally, there is a typo in the shop, it says "Stage Sreen".
There is also a side issue that I don't think it's your fault but maybe you can fix it anyway: for some reason, AVG is detecting the demo executable as a potential threat and deletes it.

I've owned this game since 2013. I've got to say, with all of the train simulators out there, this one wins when it comes to content. The expeirience is there, (most of the time) but now I feel like I need to adress certain things which lead to me NOT recommending this game.
PROs:
- Vast majority of different routes/areas.
- Mods/repaints (freeware) can be added.
-With the newer DLC, you can really feel like you are driving a train.
*This is really all I can think of that is good about this game*
CONs:
- The base game gives you VERY little content. (Or at least it did when I purchased it back in 2013)
- The DLC in the store is EXTREMELY overpriced. I've spent over $600 in DLC, and it pains me. Here's why:
- HALF of the US locomotives are either being sold as SEPERATE DUPLICATES of PAST units, for example: The SD45 has been duplicated 3 different times, (all sold seperately mind you) the ES44AC/DC maybe 5, the GP38 maybe 4 or 5, All being sold on sepearte downloads just because the paint is different. Here's an idea: CREATE SOMETHING WORTH THE MONEY THAT IS NEW! SUCH AS: The EMD SD60E, The GE C40-8W, EMD GP40-2, Or even ALCOS! C420, C425, C630, ETC...
- Once you spend a fortune on your DLC, you will find that:
A - Nearly EVERY SINGLE Engine has the SAME HORN & BELL, WHICH ARE TERRIBLE TO BEGIN WITH.
B - HALF OF THE UNITS' MODELS/TEXTURES AREN'T EVEN FINISHED! Examples:
The CSX AC6000CW - When looking out the rear window you will see that the radiator cowels are completely missing.
The CSX Dash 8 - Again, look out the rear window and you will notice there are no handrails on the catwalk, and the side of the unit itself is missing the actual "CSX" logo. (You're telling me nobody at DTG noticed that?)
The DRGW GP9 - Looking out the long hood window, there is no "Rio Grande" logo on the side of the loco. (Are they blind?)
The NJT GP40PH-2B - This unit is nothing but problems. The bell only stays of for a few seconds before shutting itself off automatically, when holding down on the horn, the ditch-lights freeze until the horn is stopped, once the light reset, rather than going soldid, they shut off all together.
In the payware route: Soldier Summit, There is foliage that floats in mid-air off of the mountain sides, clear as day from the cab. (Either they don't check their stuff, or don't care.)
The game alsp constantly crashes trying to load custom scenarios, routes, consists, etc...
_____________________
Now, here is the main reason why I am writing this review.
Over the past 4 years of owning this simulator, I have spent hours, days, WEEKS, tweaking every single DLC I owned, giving the trains new & custom engine sounds, horn sounds, installing repaints, custom rolling stock, you name it. There isn't a DLC on here that has the same sounds, just like it should be in reality. UNTIL TODAY.
The Train Simulator itself did a whole new update which took about 2 hours. After launching the game, I immediately realized that by updating the game, IT. RESET. EVERYTHING. HALF OF MY REPAINTS. GONE. ALL OF MY CUSTOM SOUNDS. GONE. GONE. ALL GONE. 4 YEARS OF WORK WASTED. IT MAY BE MONTHS BEFORE I RE-CODE EVERYTHING BACK TO THE WAY IT WAS. THANKS DTG.
___________________________
So, with all of these problems, I unfortunately cannot recommend this game. It is a scam in which you pay more for junk that barely works half the time. Maybe if they fix these problems in the future, I'll edit this review. But until then, I recommend buying something like RUN 8, where you will get your money's worth.

Honestly, I don't know where to begin. The gameplay is solid, it's basically an expansion to South Park's The Stick of Truth. If you loved the first game, this game is just taking it a step up, and beyond. The hardest part about this game besides choosing your gender, religion, etc, is probably the controls to poop on toilets. lol Yes, that's a big thing in this game, and there are a lot of toilets.
As everyone knows the jokes in South Park border on basically everything, but Fractured But Whole takes it to another level. It is extremely racist, and touches on some odd things like conspiracy theories involving the police, and the government. Ultimately, the game as a whole is pretty fun, but the combat gets repetatitve, and can be a bit bland if all you want to do is destroy your opponents. Because of the Super Hero classes, some are more powerful than others, and offer moves that just... are broken later on in the game.
If you can handle the fact that your character will probably be able to solo every enemy you face on most of the difficulties, except for the hardest, then you should only play on the hardest difficulty, and work towards the hardest, most racist achievement in the game: The Token Experience. I won't tell you how to do it, but if you want all the achievements, that one should either be your primary goal or avoided entirely. That being said, if you want to play casual, this achievement is not for you.
In conclusion, I found most of the puzzles to be basic, and easily solved, almost like they wanted children playing these games. I hope no parent lets their child ever play this game, even if you play a 4th grader in the game. If you want a very unique experience, that will probably make everyone laugh on some level somewhere in the game, this is a game if you're open to the crude humor of South Park. My advice is just ignore the things you don't like, and don't think you will lose an opportunity to get every achievement in the game your first play through. That being said, if you want every achievement play on the hardest difficulty for The Token Experience, and don't use the Coon's ultimate. Minior Spoiler, but those are listed achievements, and those two achievements are probably the only two you will miss your first playthrough.

2) I bought a turn based strategy game and thats what I wanted. Injecting real time into some of the boss fights, while innovative, was a very unwelcome feature. The audience for turn based vs real time doesnt have a lot of overlap, at least in my personal experience. YMMV
3) It just wants very funny. It was clever, dont get me wrong. But I judge a comedy by how many times it made me just laugh out loud, literally. This game brought many smiles to my face but nary a chuckle yet alone a laugh. Big fail on this level.
4) And lastly, value. For better or worse, theres a lot of very exceptional video games out there in the $25-$40 range. $60 in retropect seems too much for what I got. When you factor in I bought the season pass as well, Im not very happy with my purchase.

Simply put, GE looks pretty awesome. It's very colorful, and the landscape suits the game. Fans of the anime will find that the art style is extremely similar to the show, and it works very well for it. The soundtrack is also well done, and fits the style of GE perfectly. The UI is great, as doesn't get in the way while simultaneously being helpful and not over-cluttered. Users playing on a lower resolution might find things hard to read as the text is also downscaled harshly with the game itself, which might be my only complaint about the game. You also cannot edit the video settings on your own, and are limited to only 3 options; potato, standard, and ultra.
GE has a very simple "button smashing" type combat system. You press one button for your basic attack, one button for your ranged attack, and there's also 3 special attacks that all have unique qualities depending on which of the 4 characters you're playing as. To earn special attacks, you must achieve combos (which aren't too hard) that will grant you a special attack point. The game also uses a pretty cool leveling system where you earn XP to level up, and each time you level up, you're granted a upgrade point. These can be spent to increase your aura (health), increase your special attack limit, or upgrade your special attack, just to name a few options. Overall, I enjoyed the gameplay a lot. The characters all have pretty similar basic attacks, but they all have very unique upgrades that can become very powerful towards the end of the game. For example, Weiss can freeze enemies, while Blake can make clones of herself to fight along her side. I've seen some complaints that the combat system is bland and too easy, but I just think that those people haven't gotten into it enough yet, so don't fret.
The game also presents challenges that can be completed to unlock even better upgrades for your characters. All of your characters have unique challenges that can only be unlocked while using said character, meaning that the game has lots of replayability with pretty satisfying rewards. I've only unlocked Yang's' "best" upgrade so far, but it were super fun to use and I was happy that I spent my time unlocking it.
There is a few types of enemies, some with special attacks. There's standard Grimm, stronger Grimm with lots of health and dangerous attacks, and also more exotic types like a Grimm who has a rhino-like charge, and a mutated Grimm that will explode upon death. There isn't too much variety and I hope to see more in the future, but for day 1 of early access, it's what I expected to get.
The story is decent for a random person who comes across GE, but very cool for a fan of the show. The storyline is canon, so I recommend fans of RWBY pay close attention to what's happening, but someone who's not familiar with the anime might frankly be a little bit confused about what's going on. I'd recommend watching at least 10-20 minutes of the show before you dig into the game just so that you have a basic understand, and why not? It's free to watch!
As for the missions, there's currently only 3 unique ones available; a "defend the objective" type scenario, a "defeat _ waves of enemies" scenario, and a "escort the bomb" scenario. That might not sound like much, but it's enough to keep things fresh throughout the game.
There's only one mission currently available, with at least 2 more to come. Unfortunately, due to the fact there's only one mission (which lasts 45 minutes to an hour depending on how quick you are) the replayability of the game might be hindered a little bit to some people. However I have over 5 hours played already and haven't been bored of it yet.
Pros:
- Full controller support, including all console controllers and the Steam Controller. I couldn't find a single controller in my house that doesn't work with the game, which impressed me.
- Fun, easy-to-learn combat system
- Awesome visuals, voiceover, and music
- Challenges
- Replayability
- Can literally run on any system you can find that runs Windows XP or better
- An impressive lack of bugs, especially for an early access title
Cons:
- Limited missions
- Limited video and audio options
- Story might be confusing to non-RWBY fans
This game may be in early access, but it's actually quite impressive, especially for its price tag. There's clearly quite a ways to go in development, as expected from an early access title, but I still think that even for people who haven't watched RWBY before this game is worth checking out.

Brothers is an adventuring game where you control two brothers simultaneously on a quest to save their father. You will be traversing a beautiful world and solving some fun and basic puzzles. The game excels in the fields where it focuses on; the story, adventure, scenery and atmosphere.
This game is unique in several aspects. First it's the controls where each thumbstick controls a character. Both characters are controled at the same time. While you can move them one by one, there will be puzzles where you will need to control them both simultaneously. It might take a little bit of time to get used to the controls to make them move perfectly as you want them to but this feature is also what makes the game enjoyable. Very much even. You can also play it without a gamepad on a keyboard but I haven't tried that. Seems less practical to me for this title.
While less unique of a feature but in my opinion a good choice is the lack of dialogue. All characters do talk gibberish but that leaves all the more room for how you interpret a conversation at a given situation where behavior and reactions basically do the story telling. Especially later on, the lack of dialogue is powerful where the emphasis lies on a situation and atmosphere. You won't get distracted or disappointed by text which might have been chosen poorly. After all, a picture/image is worth a thousand words right?
Some may argue that this game is relatively short, and that fact can't be denied. But a game shouldn't be judged on it's length but rather on it's quality. Basically the amount of enjoyment one could get out of a game. In this particular title, I think the chosen game time is a well weighed decision. Making the game longer might be stretching it although maybe a wee little bit more difficult puzzles or a little bit more content would still be fine to my taste.
PRO's
- Excellent story telling (through lack of dialogue)
- Unique and enjoyable controls
- Simple but fun puzzles (simple can also be a con. They're still fun though)
CON's
- Short game (if you could even call it a con for this particular title)
- Simple puzzles (for if you are in dire need of difficult challenges)
In the end I would recommend this game to anyone without hesitation. The game does all the things, that it wants to do, so well. The controls where fun, the world is beautiful and the story was moving even if the plot was fairly basic. I found the puzzles to be rather simple but wasn't bothered by it. They were fun to execute at least.
This is a title that you really should be picking up or at least giving it a try. Don't be put off by the short game time. Every minute in this game is worth it's penny to me. It's an experience that will enrich anyone, even if you won't be liking the game in the end.

It's hard to recommend Wasted, even if it is a fun little game. The problem is all the... exotic design choices. After you read this, you might even be inclined to buy it, which is Okay. I understand why you would like the features that I do not; and the game is by no means BAD.
Off the bat, it's not an open-world game. The trailers shamefully make it look that way.  Almost all action takes place within bunkers (or dungeons) which are random each time. You also have a main-hub where you can craft some stuff, store loot and rest. Being also a rogue-like, if you die in a bunker you loose everything you have on you + buffs/debuffs (but still have the stuff you stored, so it's more light on that side). The main goal is to get as deep as possible, find the kewlest loot (the deeper the better (THAT'S WHAT SHE SAID)), drink a booze item (which is a permanent buff (or debuff)) and wake up at your base, with all the goodies you've found.
And that sounds awesome, right? A neat little dungeon crawler with humour, light roguelike elements and quirky design. What could be nicer?
Well an option to play without Purifiers, for one.
If you're like me, you like to take your time with dungeon crawlers, exploring every room, turning every stone, killing every mob.
Unfortunately for us, Wasted has the "hurry the fu*k up" feature implemented, meaning if you stray too long on a level, a Purifier will spawn that will slowly (and i do mean slowly) hunt you down until you either kill him (doable, but difficult) or go deeper to the next level. And even if the motherfu*ker is slower than a police response in an action movie, it will still spoil your calm, orderly, no-fuss fun. You'll find yourself running through traps and enemies, jumping to dodge attacks and open doors, passing over incredibly valuable loot (probably) just to find the door to the next level and reset the damn thing. If you are the kind of guy who beats Dark Souls with a Guitar Hero controller then you can probably have a go at beating him, at which point you will be rewarded with one of the best armors in the game. For the rest of us plebs, he's just a cause of anxiety and panic as we scurry like headless chicken towards the exit.
Now some people like this feature. Some people say it's what makes the game great. But hey, some people like Diet Coke; can't trust the lot, that's what I say.
Other nuisances that I found:
- loot capacity, which is stuck at 10 items (and can be increased with pouches or buffs), but which really is about 4-5 since it also counts your equipped gear/weapons. Stacks for certain items are pretty small as well, meaning if you want to grab all the health packs you can find to store them at the base for later use (or regents off mobs) well then it SUX2BU
- comparing item stats can be a pain in the♥♥♥♥♥ when mousing over an unequipped item, it's stats will display but not the ones of it's equipped equal, meaning you have to go back and forth between the two bits of crap
There have been a lot of people complaining about the Purifier and a lot of advocates of the Purifier feature, and I get both sides, I really do. What I would have enjoyed most, would have been to have an extra option before starting the game, choosing if you want to play with WITH Purifier (i.e.: Casual), or WITHOUT (i.e.: OMG GIT GUD). The developers could even punish us casuals by not giving us achievements, for having the audacity to not playing their perfect work of art the way it was meant to be played. I wouldn't mind (or care).
At the end of the day, Wasted is a well done, bug-free, nifty FPS/RPG/light-roguelike with nifty ideas but a bit too pushy with it's gameplay speed for the likes of people like me, who just want to spend 2 hours looking at bathroom assets in case there's a secret.

“Spelunky is the best game ever made. I’ve been dancing around saying that for the last seven years of writing about its different forms, but I feel confident about it now. Spelunky is a very simple concept at it's core...
. Spelunky takes this simple Indiana-Jones-ish concept and presents it
. It is an easy to learn, hard to master (or even complete!) game.
I personally love this game for its
, and the fact that every delve into the mysterious caves is different...each level is
, and is done so in a way that is
almost every time.
It should be stressed though, that the game is
, and can throw people off with its misleading learning curve. Spelunky is a permadeath game, and as much as the trailer and (adorable!) aesthetic gives the impression you're going to explore and take in many places at once, it's more likely that newcomers will spend a while fumbling in the Mines, befor they get to the different biomes.
Fortunately Spelunky is easy to pick up, with its rather spartan control scheme. Aside from the standard directional movement, you have four other actions: Jump, Whip (or Action key, if you're holding an item), Throw Rope, and Throw Bomb. The controls are tight, polished and fair; challenge comes in how you deal with enemies, use your items, and navigate levels.
One thing the trailer doesn't mention is the fact that each level, apart from the boss levels, implements a 'soft timer' of sorts -- a slow-moving instakill Ghost appears and chases you on the map after 2 mins and 30 seconds. I think the trailer is partly to blame for this, as this isn't a game where you can 'stop and smell the flowers'. I did mention that it is a 'soft timer' though -- you can easily dodge the Ghost if you've got the platforming chops. The Ghost isn't that much of a deterrent as some other reviewers make it seem.
If anything, the Ghost teaches us that we must
; Spelunky isn't a game about collecting everything, all the gold...because really,
! No, Spelunky is a game that teaches us to make the best out of every situation. Once you know that, Spelunky is your oyster! Although a seemingly simple platformer, Spelunky hides many secrets: you can find guns that shoot Plasma blasts -- levels inside of a huge subterranean worm...and oh yes, how about
? As the trailer suggests, there is so much to explore!
Not to mention, the mechanics of this game don't only affect the player; everything is designed to interact intricately with each other. See that Snake slithering past an arrow trap? BOOM, it's now a shower of blood. That lava pot in the Jungle? You can pick it up, but don't spill it...a Lava Man will arise, mindlessly burning both you and your primitive cousins. That podium of gore that is Kali's sacrificial altar? Better not fall stunned onto it...or hey, experiment and see what happens! It's amazing the amount of things you can do inside Spelunky.
More of an Achiever? The game offers a 'Daily Challenge' mode too: once a day, you can play through the same level layouts, or 'seed' as others -- you've got one shot at it, and once you've died (or survived!) your score (money) and level at which you died at will be ranked with other players who played the same 'seed' on a leaderboard. Very neat feature to see how well you're doing, and there's still a steady audience playing through those. Steam Achievements are here too...good luck getting all of them, they're
easy to obtain! ..and not in the traditional 'die 1000 times to a Snake' either. Most of these, such as picking up no gold at all, or saving 8 Damsels in one delve, require real skill to obtain.
Oh yes, did I mention multiplayer? Yes, you can explore the depths with up to 4 of your friends! Friendly Fire is present though, so do actually respect each other for once...or not~! There's also a Deathmatch mode, where you can pit your platforming skills against each other and toy with a variety of items and settings -- it's great fun too.
...hey, maybe you and/or some of your buddies aren't feeling up to the challenge of Spelunky...and that's okay. I, in my very humble opinion, think Spelunky is one of the best games ever. To me, my many deaths are part of the experience. Spelunky teaches you to
the journey more than the destination: to appreciate the variety of lush environments and situations the game presents, as well as your own platforming mastery. When you finally manage to survive and return from the caverns alive, for the first time...oh, what an amazing feeling that will be, you've come so far!
I'm rambling, aren't I. Thank you for reading this far. Up to the challenge? Try it!
...Maybe, just maybe, you'll like it too. :)

RWBY: Grimm Eclipse (will refer to it as "GE" from now on) is a hack n' slash style co-op game, where you play as a team with up to 3 friends to defeat the Grimm and figure out what's going on in the world of Remnant. Using the level up system to become stronger, defeat waves of Grimm and complete objectives until you finally reach your goal.
Simply put, GE looks pretty awesome. It's very colorful, and the landscape suits the game. Fans of the anime will find that the art style is extremely similar to the show, and it works very well for it. The soundtrack is also well done, and fits the style of GE perfectly. The UI is great, as doesn't get in the way while simultaneously being helpful and not over-cluttered. Users playing on a lower resolution might find things hard to read as the text is also downscaled harshly with the game itself, which might be my only complaint about the game. You also cannot edit the video settings on your own, and are limited to only 3 options; potato, standard, and ultra.
GE has a very simple "button smashing" type combat system. You press one button for your basic attack, one button for your ranged attack, and there's also 3 special attacks that all have unique qualities depending on which of the 4 characters you're playing as. To earn special attacks, you must achieve combos (which aren't too hard) that will grant you a special attack point. The game also uses a pretty cool leveling system where you earn XP to level up, and each time you level up, you're granted a upgrade point. These can be spent to increase your aura (health), increase your special attack limit, or upgrade your special attack, just to name a few options. Overall, I enjoyed the gameplay a lot. The characters all have pretty similar basic attacks, but they all have very unique upgrades that can become very powerful towards the end of the game. For example, Weiss can freeze enemies, while Blake can make clones of herself to fight along her side. I've seen some complaints that the combat system is bland and too easy, but I just think that those people haven't gotten into it enough yet, so don't fret.
The game also presents challenges that can be completed to unlock even better upgrades for your characters. All of your characters have unique challenges that can only be unlocked while using said character, meaning that the game has lots of replayability with pretty satisfying rewards. I've only unlocked Yang's' "best" upgrade so far, but it were super fun to use and I was happy that I spent my time unlocking it.
There is a few types of enemies, some with special attacks. There's standard Grimm, stronger Grimm with lots of health and dangerous attacks, and also more exotic types like a Grimm who has a rhino-like charge, and a mutated Grimm that will explode upon death. There isn't too much variety and I hope to see more in the future, but for day 1 of early access, it's what I expected to get.
The story is decent for a random person who comes across GE, but very cool for a fan of the show. The storyline is canon, so I recommend fans of RWBY pay close attention to what's happening, but someone who's not familiar with the anime might frankly be a little bit confused about what's going on. I'd recommend watching at least 10-20 minutes of the show before you dig into the game just so that you have a basic understand, and why not? It's free to watch!
As for the missions, there's currently only 3 unique ones available; a "defend the objective" type scenario, a "defeat _ waves of enemies" scenario, and a "escort the bomb" scenario. That might not sound like much, but it's enough to keep things fresh throughout the game.
There's only one mission currently available, with at least 2 more to come. Picked this up on an 80 % off deal. Wish I'd done that sooner. A marvellous game that creates a magical story.
Is it short? Perhaps. You'd be hard-pressed to pull more than 3,5 to 4 hours out of a single playthrough if you explore every nook and cranny and take a short break along the way. Yet it is undoubtedly quality over quantity: the story is condensed into that short time, leading you from adventure to adventure, from puzzle to puzzle without ever feeling like the story is lagging. You might walk slower as you try to keep the two brothers from failing their quest to save their father. This is easier said than done if you're not used to the control scheme: if you use a controller, each thumbstick controls a different brother, but after a while, the idea that the left thumbstick/trigger is for one brother and the right for another becomes ingrained. Play through it in one night - easily done - and you'll get the hang of it pretty soon.
Perhaps the strongest point of this game is its presentation, which has a way of drawing you in. The visuals are beautiful, depicting a fairy tale-esque land in all its magical glory, and the music is everything you want to hear from a fantasy game. Even the brothers' Simlish language had a way of making me care more for them than a thousand spoken lines ever could in lots of AAA games. This immersion causes the puzzles, which aren't that hard, to feel just right. They may be easy if you're a seasoned puzzle gamer, but they feel right on target for the brothers, though sometimes a little ridiculous.
Looking back with hindsight knowledge, I would wager I'd pick it up even if it was still full price. If it's discounted - and if you're reading reviews on Steam, I'll wager it is at least 9/10 times - you have only yourself to blame for not buying this game. Get it. It's extremely unlikely you'll be disappointed.

A cool point-n-click adventure game by Daedalic Entertainment.
The game has reminded me of some point-n-click mysterious adventure games which I've loved to play, but this one has fine and unique comic style graphics, seriously impressed me when I saw this game from Steam's Queue. Never been told to play this one, so I managed to figure it out by myself, and it's true! This game has so many preferential features from its steampunk world to puns. You will be playing as a reckless guy named Rufus, who has a strange sense of humour (he's basically amusing and smart), and you will start with a tutorial
. It's like an introduction to character, and you barely find yourself fall in love with this game. You can also choose preference for the control, since it is just a 2D and point-n-click style game, you don't have to do many things with WASD stuff, the control is absolutely simple and easy. You can also skip events and movement, for example when Rufus talks too much or NPC becomes boring because you click him/her several times, or you want to travel faster.
Let's talk about the puzzles, some puzzles are requiring some efforts, not simple like you think that's why the game becomes more challenging and fun, sometimes you manage them by trial and error, or you can be so confused because there are so many missing parts that you can't even find (there isn't any hint button) which means you need extra efforts to pay attention what Rufus/NPCs say. Good things you are given considerable space to save your game in case of need. There isn't Game Over to this thing (let's say Rufus is untouchable), you just have to solve the riddles.
However, the game is a little bit difficult for some new players who are not familiar with riddles, like I say some puzzles may be too hard to solve, but it's kind of a new challenge for those who want to give some efforts, Deponia is still enjoyable. It can also be played with kids who love puzzle!
TL;DR:

-Amusing characters and Puns
-Controls are easy
-Different difficulty for puzzles
-Music is decent
-Obviously cool graphic and art
-Great story
Cons:
-Some bugs can be encountered while playing

Finally sat to play through the game after many playthroughs of Shadows of Chernobyl over the years. I immediately felt that the weapons balance and AI behaviour was... "off", but thankfully this is STALKER we are talking about so there is a plethora of mods to fix that. I settled for the community patch (
) to get an experience as close as vanilla as possible while still being improved, and I can really recommend it.
Now having a game that both looks better, where weapons make more sense, the AI doesn't spam super-accurate hand grenades like mad, many smaller things tweaked for more immersion, and the game generally being majorly bug-fixed I started over and had an amazing playthrough.
The atmosphere is good, the way it ties into Shadows of Chernobyl is amazing, with many same zones but the zones themselves being somewhat different, not to mention that faction relations differ some compared to SoC. The story won't win any literary awards, but it is still good and both contributes to the atmosphere and is carried by the same in a synergy that I'd honestly say few games have. They even manage to make the "silly side quests" feel like they fit into the game very nicely, instead of being plastered on.
My only disappointment is the ending. Suddenly it's there in a very strange way, and with one of the worst "boss fights" in the history of gaming. It was quite a way to screw up the game experience and the game would have been better without it. Still though, on average it is a good, atmoshperic adventure-shooter (at least with the SRP mod), and for those who think that Shadows of Chernobyl has too much "horror game" about it this game has less so. The elements are still there, but not as prevalent. This game is more about human-vs-human conflict in the Zone.

Below you'll find a video and written impression on the game.
Daedalus does a fantastic job at translating the visceral game play of twitch shooters such as Unreal Tournament or Quake, into a top town perspective. You'll find the same skill ceiling, frantic precision, and chaotic battlefields you would in the previously mentioned games. I would say Daedalus has room to be competitive, and is probably one of the deeper top down shooters I've played.
Daedalus does almost every thing right, but does have one glaring flaw from my experience. Spawn camping. This isn't an issue in many game modes, but particularly in death match, spawn camping is a huge issue. The spawns points aren't randomized, rather they are in set locations, and those points aren't even gated off in any way. Even bots spawn camp in certain game modes. Another thing to note is that Daedalus is a smaller game, and with many smaller games, it'll usually have a smaller community. There will most likely be times of the day where you won't find many, or any players online. Luckily the game comes with servers filled with bots to play with while waiting for human players to get online.

Sniper Elite 3 is a 3rd person stealth sniper game set in North Africa during WW2. The gameplay is exactly the same of the older games, but with more realistic bullet psychics, and much better stealth mechanics. One thing though, that kind of kills the experience for me is the terrible pacing in this game. Everything just feels so... slow. Like your character is dragging his feet, or like the enemies are dragging their feet. And when you are crouched, which will be 50% of the time you play this game, you character feels the need to drag his♥♥♥♥♥the entire time and after awhile I just found myself yelling at the game to hurry up. And not only that, but the stealth in this game, while fun at times, it horrendously broken. When playing on higher difficulties, Enemies 20 yards away, on a different level/floor then you can literally hear it when you walk or when you stand up, it's pretty ridiculous and feels cheap. Not to mention that when you're playing on Sniper Elite difficulty the enemies have VERY unrealisitc human senses, they can literally spot you from 500+ yards away, and you can be on top of a moutain and the second you look through the scope you get spotted. It makes using generators and sniper towers completely worthless because they AUTOMATICALLY spot you when you look down scopes. It almost feels like a glitch to me because no developer should include such unrealistic enemies like this. It's like hit scanning, but more like "discover" scanning. Just doesn't feel right, seem's a little broken to me. The game is well optimized and runs like butter on my system, and the graphics are actually quite beautiful on maximum settings and with multisampling enabled. The game is a blast to play and offers a good variety of challenge on the hardest difficult setting, multiplayer mode is actually relatively fun and is still alive for those who are interested in playing it. There is also co-op play, which is really fun, and challenge mode which I tried to play but couldn't get it to work. Really great game overall and worth getting on sale for $10 or under.

Wasted was developed by Mr. Podunkian and published by Adult Swim Games    . The game is a FPS, rogue-lite RPG game that is based around getting drunk. The game has it's flaws, but also has quite a lot of decent content to keep the player interested.
Wasted is a very fun and addicting rogue-lite game that is rather bizarre and weird at times as you play through each run. There is a decent amount of replay value that is set aside for this game that keeps making you want to come back and play it more which is really essential for rogue-lite games nowadays. The dungeon areas that you enter are obviously randomly generated, each floor that you come across are rather large in scale for you to explore and find loot.
Throughout the game there are a lot of different sort of enemies and lootable places that you can loot from to gain armour, weapons, health potions ect. The enemies AI seem to be varied from each different type of enemy that you may come across. Sometimes if there are two or more enemies in the same room they will fight each other and you will only have to deal with one of them. Other times they will both come at you trying to take you out while you have to deal with both of them at the same time. I find this interesting with the way that this works, as sometimes you will get easier battles than other times when you will get more challenging battles. There are also a variety of traps that are found throughout the game that can be both triggered and be deactivated if you have enough skill points on a certain attribute, this game is fairly stat based meaning that your accuracy is dependant on stat not how good you are at shooting.
However, since the game is randomly generated through all of the dungeon making you will find yourself recognizing the same room structures only after a hour or so of playing the game. In some sense I am a little disappointed in this as the game really has a lot of potential and to point out a con like this damages the game's replay value slightly. Something else that damages the game a bit is all of the dead ends that you will most likely come across throughout your runs, I understand that this is a rogue-lite but I feel like some pathways should meet up to make it so that you are not wasting your time and find yourself at a dead end. Inventory space is one of the most valuable mechanics in rogue-lites, at the start of Wasted your are given only 10 inventory spaces, you can obviously upgrade this as you progress on but you have this kind of feeling that you are really unsure what is valuable and what isn't.
Although the game seems to have a looting way of playing there are some mechanics in the game that force you to play at a fast paced. There is a tough enemy that will come and hunt you if you take too long in a floor, this enemy has a minigun and about 600 health, so killing this enemy throughout the run is highly unlikely. The game really uses this to keep the player at bay at the fast paced gameplay and makes going through the levels quickly also, your reload times are really quick which adds to the fast gameplay. However, the main problem that distorts this fast gameplay is all of the looting that you can do. For the game being a rogue-lite, looting is rather essential in order to progress. But there are so many things that you can loot that looting all of the cabinets and corpses of dead bodies really just slows the game down more than it should.
There is another sort of 'gamemode' if you will call it that, that you can play once everyday like a daily run that you can play every actual game day. In this run, the dungeon is a lot harder but you will be able to gain special loot. You are able to stash items in the Courier box and then get out, the main objective is to get a valuable item and then get out of there. Something funny in the game is that the narrator of the game will sometimes narrate what you are actually doing in the run which is sometimes funny and will make you laugh.
The game is very creative when it comes to the buffs and debuffs of the game, you will be granted with so many new buffs and debuffs for your character that may or may not help you throughout your run. These do only, however, stay with the current character that you are playing as so if you die with that character your buffs are lost. Some of the non-permanent buffs you can also purchase from a town that you can activate by finding a guy in the dungeon, there is a unique kind of buff called 'Mixer of the day' in which you can make your own drink and it will buff your character for a in-game day. These 'hang over' buffs will go if you sleep, die with your character or if a in-game day passes by.
The more you explore the small town the more interesting people you will find and the more helpful mechanics that will become available to you for the duration of your gaming time. You are able to buy items back from previously dead characters which is a really nice mechanic if you have the TP (toilet paper which is the in-game currency) to pay for it.
+ Addicting and fun rogue-lite game
+ Decent amount of replay value
+ Fast paced gameplay, has some mechanics that keep the game that way
+ Different AI for different enemies
+ Very stat based
+ Creative buffs and debuffs
+ Day and night cycle
+ Courier Run (Daily run)
- Too many lootable areas slows down the fast paced gameplay
- Repetitive rooms
- Lots of dead ends
- Start off with only 10 slots of inventory space
Wasted is a really addicting and fun rogue-lite game that has some unique mechanics and fast paced gameplay to keep you always moving. Seems like there is a lot of looting in the game that slows the game down a little, repetitive rooms and dead ends that bring the game down a little bit. The game, however, has great replay value, really creative buffs and debuffs and so many other great things about the game.

I've been a fan of the tekken series since Tekken 2 on the PS and I can honestly say this is one of the best ones so far.
-TL;DR: it's good, great additions, runs smooth with few if any glitches, great netcode but has very barebones offline modes

Let's take a second to recognize that the game runs with few to no glitches (if there are any I haven't come across them), no day one patch, this is night and day compared to a certain other popular fighting game's launch *cough* SFV *cough*
online play is smooth, even when paired with someone with a poor connection the lag (if any) is always either at the very beginning of the match during the countdown or the end of the match. AND IT WORKS! it can't believe that's impressive in this day and age but it is.
I feel the roster is a little lacking, but the pressence of a season pass makes me believe they'll add more characters via DLC which i'm alright with if it gets me Armored King and the characters we have are new and old character we know and love with the addition of some new blood.
Visually it's fantastic and it's surprisingly easy to run at 60fps without stutter as well.
If I had to point out some issues I have with the game it's really the bare bones offline modes. You have an arcade mode with only 4 or 5 stages, no extra stages and no real rewards for beating it. The loading times are also nothing to sneeze at either, but compared to the load times on tekken 6 these are much more bareable
Honestly I can't remeber the last fighting game release I've enjoyed as much as this. definitely would reccommend

Now that I've beaten the full game once, here's an updated review!
And unfortunately I can no longer recommend the game. So that sucks.
Note: I played the VERY ORIGINAL Grimm Eclipse demo before Rooster Teeth picked it up. I played the version with the great white beowolf (♥♥♥♥ that guy) on the RT site. I picked this game up the day it came out on early access. I've followed this game for a long time and I love the RWBY series.
And I'm still saying no.
Here's the details:
-Story: I honestly didn't pay too much attention to it. I was playing with my girlfriend, so I was honestly distracted by my conversation and didn't catch everything. Regardless, I can tell it's pretty shallow. I mean, if it couldn't pull my attention back to it, then there's something wrong. Not to mention it is told almost entirely through radio conversations that often take place in the middle of a fight... so... yeah. You never actually see the bad guy face to face. Kinda underwhelming. If during future play sessions I learn anything that makes me think it's any better, I may edit this. But I can't imagine the story EVER making this game. The story is just light flavoring for a hack n' slash game.
-Visuals:
Let's make a checklist!
Enemies: Good!
Backgrounds: Great!
Animations: Just fine!
Characters: Errrrrrrr... Average? Uh oh.
Yang's outfit actually looks good I'll admit. Weiss's outfit looks OK. Blake's outfit is passable. Ruby's... makes me sad. And their faces just don't cut it. Ruby's appearance is actually bad enough to make me upset. Worse is the fact that they used to have models that looked like they came right out of the show! Which was great! I have to assume technical issues forced their hands, otherwise... WHY?!?!
In a series named after the four main characters... you gotta do the characters justice. This game comes up short in that regard.
-Sound:
The music is a little awkward and sometimes doesn't fit what's going on. This isn't a game where the music will help sell it. I also had to turn it down so I could hear my conversation, but I remember my girlfriend complaining multiple times: "The music doesn't fit the combat!"
This is a shame because the show has some pretty epic musical moments. The game doesn't quite measure up to that.
Also some of the noises Weiss makes while fighting sound... weird.
Otherwise, the sound effects are just fine. No complaints there at least. Except for the spike traps. Those things are loud and obnoxious (not dangerous, just obnoxious)... But everything else is fine. (seriously, **** those traps)
-Gameplay: (Here's the important stuff!)
For the most part, combat is smooth. It's easy to control. My girlfriend had NEVER played the game before, but she did just fine. She actually died less than me (she played like a coward, but still). I have now 24 hours of experience with this game from Early Access to make my point clear.
THE GAME IS WAY TOO ****ING EASY! The last boss is a JOKE! The last boss may actually be THE EASIEST PART OF THE GAME!
The basic mobs gave me FAR more trouble than the boss, and that's not saying much since I could ping-pong back and forth between them without ever taking damage when I was on a roll. That's because counter attack system (it literally homes in on them for you...) makes many fights a breeze. And no, there are no difficulty options that I know of. It gets "harder" when you add more players, but having more players also makes the margin for error wider... so.... yeah.
The combo system is at least more diverse (barely) thanks to heavy attacks, but it's still very basic. I mean, the fighting, as I said, controls well, but there isn't much to control.
While I'm (very) glad enemies are no longer invulnerable during attacks, that coupled with other changes makes the game... boring. Toward the end there are some new enemies that are at least a little challenging, but it's not enough.
Consider the fact that this game has no teaching tools. It's pathetically easy despite no tutorial of any kind. You can look up the controls, but that doesn't cover everything that you need to know. And it's still too easy. (That's a double bad right there is what that is.)
Speaking of enemies... there's far too few. If they're gonna make combat this freakin' easy, at least try to make up the difference by giving us the massive hordes we used to have in the earlier versions. Or at least close to that. There are definitely less enemies than there used to be.
I will say that they made it so you can now combo enemies in the air after knocking them up, which pleased me greatly. Used to be you'd just drop back to the ground.
-Conclusion:
If you're a fan with some friends you can voice chat with, consider buying it on sale. The game is barely worth the $15 price tag it used to carry. $25 dollars is just... no. It is NOT worth that price tag.
-Furthermore:
They plan to add more content, so that's... something. Horde mode is coming for one, but I don't know what else they're planning. Even then I don't know that it'd be worth $25.
If they add a bunch of new content, and if they up the challenge, AND IF they improve the character models, then MAYBE it'd be a worthwhile game FOR FANS... on sale. Really gonna be a challenge to make it worth those $25...

Greetings gamers, my name is EXtraDonut and I've been playing M&B:W for several years now on various different steam accounts. Why different accounts? I'll get to that in a bit. I have spent countless hours fighting the virtual crusades against the enemy of my people and have slain the top ranking warlords in North America many times in my career as a professional E-Soldier. But despite my massive amounts of time spent in this game, ultimately it is a deeply flawed simulation of the medieval reality our ancestors came from. At the same time it is a horribly buggy game, riddled with bugs and glitches of a buggy nature. The story on how this came to be is rather interesting as the game was not always this way. Come with me as we take a journey back in time and examine exactly:
Well gamers, I'll tell you what went wrong. Back in 2003 when development of the first Mount & Blade game was begining, a programmer who for safety reasons I will only refer to as Orlando Savage was hired to craft the perfect character creation system. Later on he began to take on more duties such as parsing the texture data onto the model wafers and fetching the encoding tables from the netframe so they could further enhance the resolution of the many user interfaces he designed. All of this work began to put a toll on him, but ultimately it paid off when the game released to critical acclaim across the world. It was the first game of its kind to fully simulate war as it was meant to be simulated, accurately depicting the horror and the obscene violence of it all. But this glorious ultra violence ending up getting to Orlando Savage, who has grown tired of the sight of highly detailed guts & gore and all of the gratuitous violence he had a hand in creating. So one night when all the employees were sleeping, Orlando snuck into the office and programmed the mainframe computer to turn the violence command from 1 to 0, thus throwing a wrench in the majority of the game's systems.
Mount & Blade had to shut down for a while after this incident. The confusion caused by the lack of violence caused the game to somehow lash out at the accounts of steam users and many were sent false VAC bans, PERMANENT ONES. This happened to me, it was very painful. As an E-Warrior part of the Vanadium Angel Army, it pained me to lose so many tracked hours on my favorite game like that, it hurt me and it hurt my reputation as an E-thlete.
Even though they have since fixed the game since the No War Incident, Mount & Blade has never been the same ever again. The programmer who had sabotaged the game was the only competent programmer on the entire development team, causing the studio to spiral out of control and leave the development to unpaid modders. All of my fellow barbarian raiders from the Vanadium Angel Army(we are nords, always) have since moved on to better mods like North & South, opting away from the cool swords & shields gameplay of the original Mount & Blade for a more modern take on war, involving cowardly weapons that could make any wimp into a soldier. Real soldiers fight in melee combat, they dont use elongated shooting sticks to kill their foe without even giving them a fighting chance. Pathetic.
If you want to simulate war, I am sorry. If you buy this game you will only be simulating your crushed dreams manifested into a virtual reality, for you to wallow in until you realize how truly pathetic you are. Thank you.
