I am happy to announce that Tekken 7 is having a good start on PC.
It does not feel like a cheap port like Dead or alive 5. Never played StreetFighter on pc. No comment on this
But Tekken: Maybe Tekken 7 is made for PC and the console versions are ports  = P
Anyway: I got a decent pc with i7 3770 and GTX 1070.
Graphics are nice and i must say the best looking Beat em Up on the market at this time. Unreal enginge 4 performs extremely well. Performs in FullHD on Ultra Settings with 200% resolution scale constant at 60fps. But: If ur pc is not strong enough, there are plenty of options to calibrate and even on low settings it looks pretty nice for a fighting game. But pls,at least upgrade ur pc that it can hold up against PS4 or XBOX One. Everything below is not good.
Playing with a XBOX One controller, no problems with that: Just Plug´n Play.
Gameplay:
If you ever played an old Tekken game you feel right at home. The new Rage System is quick learned and a lot of fun. Even when your health bar is nearly depleted u can change the game. Very nice. Every second until the end is exciting.
IF you are NEW to Tekken learning the system is not hard. But forget StreetFighter or Dead or Alive. Here is a 4 Buttons= 4 Limbs System. Left Hand, Right Hand, Left Leg and Right Leg has its very own Button. The rest ist mixed with direction buttons, combos or pressing 2 buttons at the same time. Sometimes 3 = P .
You got a lot of characters to choose from. From a big strong robot to a speedy agile school girl. choose what u like and concentrate on this char and u will rank up in online mode. You got a nice practice mode where u can get all the moves shown in a demo. with a lot of settings to practice every aspect of this game. Rage Art, Throws, Custom combos, Counter... you are not alone.
When you think your balls a big enough...try first the story mode. The Mishima Saga is a nice staret to enjoy the 23 year old story line and fight against the main chars. and there are some pretty badass fights, nicely going over from cutscene in to the fight, with a little quick time events. endboss fights are pretty tough and darksouls players might like this  = D
Negative: Only the stories besides the mishima clan is a little bit weak. the other chars got only a text window with a little bit of event explained and than a 2 round fight against one enemy and a little cutscene at the end. there could be more Namco.
After that you got a 5 Round ARCADE MODE, pretty ok but the most fun comes in:
TREASURE MODE:
Non Stop fight action against customized enemies with LOOT at the end. Yeah you LOOT & LEVEL. Rise in ranks and get a lot of cosmetics for all chars. and sometimes u got special matches to unlock the very rare custom items for ur favorite char. After every fight: the better you perform and longer you survive, the better loot and more money you will get.
If u have unlocked a lot of LOOT & MONEY you go to
CUSTOMIZATION:
You can customize your character and your HUD.
Character with a massive amount of clothes, makeup, hairstyles, glasses, hats, beards, Tan colored skin, auras, hit effects items u can use in fight like weapons or funny stuff and even a secret mirror item that blocks the movement of an enemy when he wins so you can kill the online trolls that want to teabag you when u are defeated.
Hud customizing u can set healthbar art design, Player name window, achievement text with custom background plate.
There will be the time u get pretty bored from beating up NPC´s so you are ready for:
ONLINE MODE:
Fight agains real humans behind real pc´s with real skills and problems. 1 vs 1 or maybe the glory challenge of a tournament to win the crown and get a damm lot of money and rare loot.
here u rise separately in rank from arcade or treasure mode. the higher your rank, the higher are the enemys and u will fell that.
Searching for online players is ok and the netcode depends on where you play and where the enemy is playing. but u got plenty of options to calibrate the searching parameters like which rank the enemy should have and how good the net quality might be.
but laggy players always will be in online games. don´t salt the creators of the game for that.
Playing against your friends works fine. a little bit complicated to arrange but it works. Online u need to create a session, invite and fight.
2 Players on one pc? no problem, plug in a second controller and off u go. Even keyboard for two works, but a little bit
uncomfortable. better one keyboard and one controller.
After a long fight night:
If u are exhausted from playing you can lean back and enjoy a ton of movies and artworks from ALL Main Tekken Games in the History of Tekken. jukebox is only on PS4 at this time, hope the patch it for pc too.
I hope there will be more chars and more game modes. some good old chars are missing and a lot of fun game modes in the past. there is a SEASON PASS optional. so  there will be content in the future.
Even without Season Pass i recommend this Game. totally.

Customization is almost at its prime in TEKKEN 7, you can truly make your character your own.  My only complaint about customization is that Tekken TT2 has more, but Tekken 7's is still great.  Online has given me no issues so far and is a refreshing change from Street Fighter V's insane loading times.  Optimization is great.  Soundtrack is amazing as usual.
Whether you are new or familiar with the series, TEKKEN 7 is a must-have for those looking to play a fighting game, especially if you're looking for a well ported game for PC.

: Keen Games
: 505 Games
==========
When this game first came out, I had no idea what I was getting myself into. Having played a ton of games very similar to this, the thing that stood out the most to me was the different worlds you could freely travel to. Well, that and the awesome art style!
==========
Portal Knights begins with a short character creation process. Gender, Name, Hair, Beard, and Class. After that you get to generate your world, and you can choose 3 different sizes. I recommend a Small universe until you get the hang of the game, then go back and generate a Large universe. Once that's finished you are transported to a sort of "tutorial world", where you'll be introduced to the basics and flow of the game via a list of quests and signs at a few landmarks.
As with any other game in this genre, the bulk of the game is exploring and collecting resources. YOu then use these resources to craft new tools, weapons, armor, and items. You can even build a base of operations on any world, or a base on every world! You can freely travel between each new world once you unlock them, even set one as your "Home". Every several worlds, you will run into a tiny world with a boss encounter. Make sure you are well-prepared before challenging these bosses! This means be up-to-date in all aspects of your weapons, armor, and healing items. Some of them can be quite challenging.
==========
As I mentioned before, I love this game's art style. It's cutesy, but is loaded with detail and just screams charm. It's also very colorful and vibrant, and each world looks amazing. Some enemies are simply reskins or different colors, but they look nice overall.
==========
Portal Knights has a soundtrack that matches it's art style. Colorful and vibrant, yet cute and relaxing. Each world type has a track associated with it, so you'll be hearing the same tracks frequently. At least they are pretty good and relaxing most of the time. My favorite track plays in generated dungeons!
==========
Your performance will vary, depending on the size of the universe you generate. Small ones aren't as intense, but a Large one can be pretty demanding. The game blends rpg elements with real-time combat elements relatively well and gives you a plethora of aesthetic options to boot, but to truly shine this game could use with moddability. Another major concern is the longevity of the game and its community's interest. To further the game's popularity it may require a redesign of the multiplayer aspect. In order to play with other users you're required to first have them on your friend list to gain access, but what would truly assist this game would be a multiplayer online randomizer session somewhat akin to Saints Row 3 and 4. To be able to join random players online or view a list of existing games would provide this game broader possibilities. Expanding the world's player count beyond 4 to 8 might help or allowing users to host worlds larger than that of the base game. This game truly has potential that can outshine some voxel-based mmorpgs, but for this to happen the developers have to truly see the merit in these suggestions.
Pros:
- Combat smooth and responsive.
- RPG elements that bolster your character's progression and usefulness are great, but could use with even more defining traits and advantages.
- The art for this game is nothing to scoff at.
- Boss sequences aren't grueling, but could use more complex battle sequences..
Cons:
- Multiplayer functionality requires revision to truly make this title shine.
- Aesthetic choices could use with a greater plethora of options. Still this is Early Access.
- While the design of the creatures are visually appealing, they could use with greater variety.
Final notes: While I understand that the game is geared towards a younger audience I do feel like the developers should not stray away from giving the game more eye-catching designs or at least start creating a more attractive focus for the story. Looking back at games like Trove there was a lot of potential there for the games story and the design that soon followed. Portal Knights is Portal Knights and Trove is still just Trove, but there are plenty of things these games can learn from each other. For one thing I do hope Portal Knights does not fall to the tropes that Trove did when its developers decided to greedily monetize character progression. As content creators we should never place character progression and player usefulness behind a paywall. The longevity of a game suffers in the long run.

Where do I begin? I have to give this game a solid 6.5/10. It definitely isn't as good as The Stick of Truth for a few reasons but there are two reasons I want to point out specifically:
1. Its not as funny overall nor is it as consistently funny as The Stick of Truth is.
2. It is kinda short and the story isn't that great.
The problem here is that these are the parts of a south park game that should be phenomonal. These are the reasons to even considering playing a south park game. There are alot of good jokes and funny quests to be found here but, after it was over and I saw the credits I couldn't help but feel alittle disappointed.  That's not to say that The Fractured but Whole doesn't do some things right or even better than The Stick of Truth. Combat, for instance, is very noticeably improved in this game. The grid-based system and the whole push/pull knockback tactics incorporated into each fight were very nice and made combat more interesting. This led to the boss fights being very fun and memorable. The characters do get into some funny situations and there is some really good humor. However other than that the game is kind of bland. Most side quests are go find things around the town or fight this group of enemies that you have already fought a thousand times. With no really good payoff at the end of the quests I started to regret wasting my time doing them. By the latter half of the game I was just avoiding most random encounters because you can really level up or anything anyways. The upgrade system is kinda boring. Equip the highest power artifact in each slot, thats it. Look for the highest number and click it. There are other secondary stats but they have a very minimal effect on the battle. Overall, I have to say if you are a fan of the show this game is definitely worth a playthrough but, I can't reccommend paying full price for it right now. Wait for a sale or watch a let's play if you can't wait.

This game is basically the original Dead Rising 2, but it's a what if scenerio where Frank West is the main protagonist, trying to get his career back on track after his show was canceled. With a new protagonist, a few things have changed in the game. A few things are a new psychopath you have to face in the main story, Brandon, who you usually choose to fight in the original story. Chuck Greene returns in this game, but is a psychopath, who thinks a doll on his back is his daughter who needs Zombrex. He shows up early in the game, so it's not a spoiler. And there's another new psychopath, but he shows up at day three, so won't say much, but if you hated Adam in the first game, you'll probably not like this guy either.
There's still a three day time limit you need to race against to find out the truth about the Fortune City outbreak, while keeping Frank from turning into a zombie by giving him Zombrex, which is hard to find in the world. If racing against time limits and finding hard to find medicine isn't for you, or you just want to level up, there is a mode for that as well. Sandbox mode allows you to explore Fortune City without having to worry about time limits or Zombrex injections. There are also little challenges you can do, by yourself, or if you have a buddy, you can take them on together, the second player controlling Chuck. Story mode can also be played Co-op, so you can somehow cause a time paradox by having Chuck fight himself, and not have the universe break apart.
It is a fun game, but I would have liked to seen an Infinite Mode like in the first game, since Fortune City would be a good place to have a mode like that, but Sandbox mode makes up for that, in my opinion.

tl;dr it's a fun game if you're a fan of the show, but seeing as how it's early access, there are definitely some things that should be fixed.
FULL REVIEW. I'll start with the cons since they're the most urgent
CONS:
-Performing an action right before moving (jumping, attacking etc) causes a small graphical glitch where your charcter will freeze and sorta slide across the map
- The game has a system where it adjusts the difficulty level based on the number of people in the lobby. It doesn't work very well. My entire team just disconnected all at once, and it was impossible to beat the waves. Especially annoying since I was only a couple hundred exp away from my first level 10.
-You can't move while you're allocating your points and there's no designated "power up your character" places, which leads you to getting left behind while your teammates run on ahead of you
-No voice commands. It's not really a complaint, more like something that would be interesting to implement. Source games have the option to press either Z,X, or C to open up a menu of voice commands and numbers 1-9 to have your character say something specific
-Maps are a bit linear, which discourages exploration. There are however, little things (like artifacts) you can find for extra xp. An open world feature would probably be an eyesore seeing the same 4 characters running around, but something more open would be appreciated. I'm not sure if there are side quests in the game, as I haven't came across any.
-As it is right now, the storymode is very very short. I know additional chapters are on the way as the game's description's already promised more things to come though. However, since this is a review of the current state of GE as it is, I had to include it.
PROS:
-The voice acting is fantastic. The actors in the RWBY anime voice their own characters in the game
-Something really interesting I've noticed is that when you're fighting in an echoey place, the sounds of the explosions and your weapons echoes too. It's neat. The voices will echo too.
-The music fits. I'm not sure who did it. It's not great, but it's also not bad
-Keyboard control works perfectly fine, you don't need a controller
-Potato quality :D
-Different playthroughs with different characters cause them to say different things. It adds variety!
-The characters all feel different. I've beaten the campaign as everyone, hit level 10 (max level) as everyone, and unlocked everything as everyone.
- The (4?) creators are doing a real bang up job releasing timely updates!
-Most importantly, it's a RWBY game. Lets be honest, none of us would probably have bought early access if it was another hack-n-slash by Joe-Blo production company
Overall, it's a fun game if you're a fan of the RT show. If you've never heard of RWBY, you probably won't enjoy this. It is still in early access though, so bugs are to be expected. I'm sure Monty would be proud of the completed game if he could see it :)
I'll update my review as the game progresses. In the mean time, enjoy this short gameplay clip ^.^

Portal Knights is mostly a pleasant experience you could compare to Minecraft, Trove, and Creativerse, you know, the 3D voxel-building games.  It has a similar visual style to MySims or Graal with its over-simplified player character models.  It also feels very much like a 3D Zelda game with auto-target capabilities, dodging, strafing, and a variety of weapons/tools/clothing.  Building a home could be fun, but the focus of the early game is to gain power and traverse different worlds/islands in the sky.  You also are allowed multiple character/save slots and multiplayer coop features seem to be in the works.  Single-player content is very well done already and well worth the purchase.  Don't believe me? Watch some gameplay videos or a Let's Play!
There are very few annoyances I have with the game.  One: The worlds are very tiny islands, not quite the scope you'd see in Trove or Minecraft.  You have very little to explore on each world, but making your way to the next world is fairly easy.  Two: Early levels are difficult to enjoy a second time through unless you start new characters, but you simply have to play those levels to find the portals and get to the better levels for your character.  I wish there was a way to skip newbie levels once you've beaten the game or got past a particular boss.  Maybe there could be a "skip to the boss world" option?  Three: The inventory is excessively difficult to manage.  I keep getting items I want but simply can't keep them due to already having too many items in my inventory.  It's often a challenge to figure out what to keep and what to throw away.  A better item pick-up mechanic could help with this.
Portal Knights is officially out of Early Access, as well!  It's a great game at this point, and I'm glad I got it when I did, even if it means having to play it over again today.

I sadly give it a 5/10. I loved the previous game and played it over and over again, one of the few games I own have I done that, but this game is a disappointment to say the least. In comparison with the last game and with the game as a whole, I simply cannot say reccomend this game. The score comes from a combination of many things.
1. The amount of glitches in the game some game breaking is really annoying. I understand that this game is brand new, but I got the last one when it came out and there was none.
2. The combat system is unrefined and too complex in some situations to the point that it makes timed events more annoying than challenging. I like that they tried something new, but they took it wayyy to far with this one. It was bland and not very ‘strategic’.
3. The feel of the game and the world is lacking, with all that is in the world it's just not enthralling.
4. There is very little diversity of enemies, it's always the same guys and it gets boring. Quick. Not to mention that they all fight the same and I got bored with fighting them quick.
5. The music is alright but there is not as much as the last games and the music that there is in the game gets obnoxious really quick after the keep looping it over and over again.
6. When fighting enemies in battle, they say the same thing over and over and over again, you may only hear them say 2 things special to them, 3 if you're lucky. And that includes bosses.
7. It is way too damn easy. I cannot confirm this 100% but if you die in a boss fight they get easier, either taking away mechanics or making them easier to fight. That in combination with that fighting in that game is way, WAY too easy. And i have it set on the highest difficulty mind you.
8. The choice by the team to have the costumes have no stats was a bad one. I found myself hating every costume in the game except one, and I played the game with that same outfit. I enjoyed the previous game not only was the armor cool and intuitive but they had sats to them making them worth it. Grated that is my personal opinion.
9. Crafting in the game is boring and pointless, there are only 4 basic scrap items and by the time i was hour one into the game i had almost 500 of each, 15 hours into the game i had about 2k each. This system of crafting is too easy to obtain stuff and too pointless for me to even craft because what i can craft can be bought or picked up. Assuming that i have to use it in combat in the first place. And when I have to craft for the mission, It's with only 3 parts, it's pointless for me to have to gather the stuff and then go to the menu to craft it. Why do that when it would go to a cutscene to ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ making it.
10. The story is too linear, it holds your hand wayy too much and never gives you options in what direction to go not to mention the sheer lack of side quests. The lack of them makes the world feel empty and boring.
11. The menu system is a disaster, they put way too many menus in this game, they made it complex when honestly it really didn't need to be, i found myself only ever using the power app to change stuff. It gives you about 8 others that are damn near pointless.
12. The  powers and classes are bland and the fact that you get a second class so early in the game doesn't give you much time to play around your powers nor upgrade them through the power menu.
12. Back to the power menu, the menu has way too much information with too little choices, the amount of artifacts in the game is sad and doesn't really let you upgrade your powers to be better. Just marginally so. I would say it's pointless, especially to the previous game.
13. Lastly I get a strong feeling that the dev team tried wayyy too hard to make this game good and in the process, made it worse.

I'm a long time fan of MK but I'm quite disappointed with this shaky release by HVS.
Online mode got a little better with the latest patch (I haven't gotten "The game session is no longer available" messages so far) but there is still a lag that can determine the outcome of the fight, especially against experienced players.
There is still unstable FPS even on the lowest settings (and my rig is: Core i7 920, GTX570, 8GB Ram)
Story mode should've been longer and each character should've have its own chapter.
I really hope NRS pull their sleeves and help HVS fix the mess that they created, because at its core, the game is quite fun), and maybe release more free content to compensate for this ordeal.
I wouldn't recommend buying this for full price (60$).

EDIT: I change my mind, this game is absolutely not recommended. Online play is horrendous. Use your $60 plus $30 DLC for the PS4 or Xbone version, those versions run better guaranteed (I've tried them). Good job High Voltage Studios, and good job Netherrealm Studios for hiring High Voltage to port the game in the first place! There's never a "happy gaming" if the game has horrendous online play. Everything I said below still remains the same.
---
Mortal Kombat X brings a new meta game to the MK series, and delivers a fix to what fighting gamers want in a competitive fighting game. The Variation mechanic is new to MK. This gives players a total of 75 (as of right now) different variations to play with and hundreds of potential match ups, which really spices things up for the game and the casual and competitive players. Story mode is an improvement from MK9, there's depth to the classic characters like Scorpion and others, but it lacks to some of the new characters. While story mode is an improvement, the QTE's are boring and don't deliver true consequence to the story or player, but it's better than Injustice. Now, if I click "Yes" to the games recommendation, I would be lying. This specific version of MKX suffers a BAD port from High Voltage Studios. It's BAD. MKX suffers frame dropping from stages that have tons of visual effects and interactions like Sky Temple; the game also suffers from a bad netcode. It's so bad, half of the matches I get put with get disconnected. The netcode is so bad, even the "minor" patch didn't do much. So overall, the only thing that holds me back from clicking that "Yes" is the bad port from High Voltage and its bad netcode that visibly shows input lag, consistent disconnection, and frame dropping. But if you're a big MK fan and is or was hype for the sequel, I would recommend it. The game is fun enough already, just don't play online or choose visual appealing stages.
This bad port is unacceptable and I don't think people should pay $60 to play a bad port. No disrespect, but the only thing High Voltage Studios has done right is Saints Row: Gat out of Hell, but even then that game is decent. If you want the "decent" online play and little to no stage frame drops, you're better off buying the PS4 or Xbone version. Sad but true.
Happy gaming everybody.

I don't usually write reviews about games, but when I do, it is because a game has either far surpassed my expectations, or driven me to the brink of insanity in which the only recourse possible would be to write a review -- good or bad.
For WASTED, this review is definitely the former: expect addictive, fast-paced, and quirky gameplay (but quirky in a good way)!
Themed in a post-apocalyptic 80's-era dystopia, WASTED is a roguelike FPS game in which you, the player, must raid procedurally-generated underground chambers (also known as Coolers) to ascertain the means to restore the world to its former glory... wait.... Wrong game!
Radioactive booze is what I meant! You, the player must raid the underground Coolers to find booze that permanently affect your stats!
Along your treacherous journey through the derelict and seemingly "abandoned" Coolers, you will be yelled at, punched at, and even shot at by tough enemies wanting nothing more than to see you splattered all over the broken walls and floors of the underground facilities.
You will fight marauders, bandits, radioactive creatures, and much more; however, there's one being in particular who you really have to watch out for, no seriously!
Warning: If you take too long on any given level, and I kid you not about this one, a dangerous hunter known as the S.O.B. appears and starts to hunt you down with a MINIGUN, that's right, a MINIGUN. In my opinion, this makes the game tense and forces you to move it or lose it!
You get your own house in which you can store loot from previous runs, craft and cook (though the recipes can be kind of limited), and even do daily courier missions with the chance of finding rare loot to hopefully bring something back to your actual player.
An Important Note:
1. Developer Involvement: The developer seems to be engaged with the community and is active on the forums. He also has listened to people's feedback regarding the S.O.B. and has stated that he will be adjusting the mechanics to conform to the community's requests. <-- right here, this sold me. Having developers who care about the community and listen to them is pretty rare in the industry. If he follows through with this, then much kudos to make this game the best possible ever.
Overall Recommendation: 8.5 / 10 for outstanding, unique gameplay that merges many genres together. The game can be frustrating for new players, but once you break the first hour or so into the game, it becomes a whole lot more entertaining and fun.

I'm not usually one to play roguelike games very much, but WASTED is one of the few I've been following for a while, and it's totally RIGHTEOUS, man.
OVERVIEW:
WASTED is a Procedurally Generated Dungeon Crawler Roguelike. (Yeah that's right, a "PGDCR") It takes place in a post-apocolyptic future where buzzed out wasters scavenge for Booze. Unfortunately any remaining hooch lies deep within these futuristic dungeons the wasters call "Coolers" Every bad guy in the Western Wastes is out for the sauce...and so are you.
GAMEPLAY THOUGHTS:
The gunplay in the game is pretty alright, though sometimes I feel like the hit detection can be a little iffy. I feel like I've seen my bullets go straight through an enemy without them taking any damage, but that might be a combo of low level weapons, aim debuffs and stats in general.
Melee weapons on the other hand are odd. I swear I was knocking an enemy around with a crowbar and they were taking zero damage. It wasn't until I gave them a moment to run around again was I able to finish them off. So just be careful when using a melee weapon, because that would be a most unsavory way to bite the dust.
The hangover buff/debuff is pretty reminicent of The Binding of Isaac's pill items, where you find nameless hipflasks of liquid courage to quaff down. It can be good or bad, mostly the latter, but I think that's what gives the game it's spice. There are bottles of labed Booze you'll find rarely around and at the end of coolers that give a very specific and character permanent buff/debuff. Again, can be good or bad, or can even be a mix!
Of course, one more thing I have to mention is the S.O.B Purifier. Y'see, every level of the Cooler there's a timer. I'm not sure how much time or if it changes the deeper you go, but at the end of the timer an S.O.B Purifier will show up and he'll basically hunt you down and shred you to pieces with a minigun. Think of the ghost from Spelunky, but unlike the ghost from spelunky, I hear you can kill him! He's pretty easy to escape from though, so not bad.
ART & MUSIC:
The graphics are really nice and stylized. Of course the first thought that comes to mind is a Fallout game mixed with Borderlands and that's not too far off I guess. Everyone in the game always has a funny expression, though I will admit that in the heat of a gun battle inside a Cooler, having the enemy's huge melon head get all up close and personal with you is a little jarring...At least for me.
The music is really, really good. The music when you're deep in the Cooler is nice and isn't unpleasant when hearing it over and over again. Basically just think of Spelunky HD, those nice synthy tunes. The music you hear passing by radios really compliments the game too.
ENDING THOUGHTS:
This game is really challenging and at times pretty brutal, but that's just the nature of these types of randomized games. Though the humor in the game really helps counterbalance the difficulty, plenty of the cheesetastic jokes I dig.
Overall I totally recommend this game, excellent purchase. Especially at the price it's at now! C'mon, Go for it!

Heroes and generals is an FPS game with Russia, Germany, and America. You will fight on many different maps with infantry, paratroopers, recon/snipers, tanks, planes, jeeps, and armored cars. I find the battles long and fun, although you often get paid small amounts. It all depends on your rank, how long the battle lasted, and if your team won. The game can be played many times, with many different routes to choose. While this game is very fun, I have one problem with this game: the faction balances. The Germans are the best faction in the game, with the Americans in second. The Russians, however, need a bit of a buff. Their tanks are okay, their planes are made of potatoes and are fueled with vodka, and their only strength is their submachine guns. The have some pretty good submachine guns that can stand up to the Germans and the Americans, but they have no machine guns or light machine guns. Their tanks can beat some of the enemy tanks, but they are often defeated by german tanks and have to rely on AT weapons. If the devs see this, please consider buffing the Russians. Even if it is just giving their guns the RPM they have in real life, it would make a huge difference. If you play the game as the Russians and ask other players, many will say that the russians need a buff of some sort. If the game was balanced a bit more, this could have the potential to be one of the best WWII games of all time.

Early Access Review: 7August2016
Portal Knights is a creative crafting voxel based RPG.  That's a mouthful.  The thing to take away from this is if you've played Minecraf then you know what you're doing here.  There are several key differences between the two but I'm not going to compare them, because aside from the theme, Portal Knights sets itself in a pleasantly different direction.
Graphics - Portal Knights is beautiful and I can't help comparing its art style to something that Niintendo would make.  The characters are cutesy, the environments colorful, and worlds wondrous.  The detail, lighting, flashy effects, all of it comes together nicely in a beautiful game.  The game also runs buttery smooth for Early Access and I'm running a clean 60 FPS.
Sound - Portal Knights doesn't have much in the music department right now.  There's a few tracks but other than that the music is actually kind of bland.  I myself turn the music down and enjoy something else, but to each's own.  The sound effects fair a bit better with clangs, clacks, and grunts.  There are even some neat cues to let you know if the brick you're hitting has ground beneath it.  Other updates, add reverb to the inside of dungeons, so the effects are solid.
Weapon/Armor Design - This has it's own category because the Weapon and Armor's are simply beautiful.  I expected cutesy or somewhat bland armor and weapons and what I got sometimes is something that might get seen in Diablo.  The weapons, especially in the later levels of your character, really start looking great and new designs keep coming with each update.  I'll post some screenshots of the armor and weapons to give you guys a better idea of what to expect.
Role Playing and Exploration - While Portal Knights strays away from survival and hardcore crafting, it emphasizes its roots in that of an exploration RPG.  You level up your character, craft and wear new armors, and brandish crafted swords and various weapons.  There are currently three different classes while each can use any skill and weapon, each's skill tree emphasizes a different playstyle.  I also want to note that this is still in early development and will be getting overhauled in the future according to the Devs.  The same goes for the combat, which admiittedly isn't as exciting as say, The Witcher or Zelda, but still better than a lot of games in this particular genre.  Enemies have different patterns, there are three boss monsters that drop great loot, and there's even some Endgame Content already tucked in.  This is easily Portal Knights greatest strength.
Crafting and Building - Portal Knights does offer a pretty great amount of craftable items, with some not even able to be made until their recipes are dropped, offering a loot drop aspect to the game.  There is a large selection of furniture, tile sets, armor, weapons, tools, resources, etc..  The UI is still being finalized but the crafting windows are neat and show you what is needed.  Another nice feature is that when choosing a world, it displays the available resources on that world before you warp there.  With that being said, it could always stand for improvement and I'd like to see more options for building implemented in the future.
World Building - This is unfortunately Portal Knights weakest aspect.  I want to note that it's still a strong package, but at this moment this is the weakest element.  The biomes themselves are beautiful but they do get repetitive and it gets a bit grindy just due to similar environments.  There are towers, dungeons, hidden caverns, but a lot of the layouts are similar and the enemies just aren't different enough at this point.  Again, I reiterate that combat isn't bad, and some of the layouts are actually pretty coo, but I would love to see more variety in the biomes, enemies, fauna, and ambient creatures, effects.  A lot of this is in development so it's really just a matter of waiting.
Take all this and wrap this up in four player co-op and you've got yourself a nice beefy Early Access Game.  Another thing that needs to be pointed out right off the bat.  These developers are easily the best when it comes to communication with the community.  Don't believe me? Just check the forums or their website!  Portal Knights is made for the fans, it's very clear.  Also, as of right now a lot of new features just got introduced that are great including vanity slots, new vanity items, new furniture, new events, text and voice chat, remappable controllers.  Portal Knights, even in it's early devolopment is showing its stripes and is going to be one hell of a complete game.

The definitive Tekken returns for the first time on PC. This game is well-optimized, as the port is flawless. However, the loading times for online play can be better, as I timed that there is a minute delay between sets. Overall great game.

Game performance:
Well optimised. For those that have a 1080 monitor, if you can run the game at 2k (Nvidia DSR or Super Sample equivalent for AMD) go for it.
Story: Some aspects could be better executed. Won't go into details. Othewise decent.
Online: Some issues with dc but otherwise done well. For me, on Tag 2 the connections would initially show 5 bars then drop to 1 at times. On this they stay up around 4-5 bars throughout match (Australia ADSL 2+ Average 4 megabits).
Offline: not impressive like previous installments. Maybe they thought not many played the other modes besdies ghost and arcade so they made Treasure mode (ghost+"survival"+item unlock).
Customisation: not as detailed like Tekken 6, but otherwise decent. Hair options extremely limited- unlike tag 2 where you can apply long hair, twin tails, side bangs, etc. In this, it's just restricted to the 'base'.
Sound is great (need OST NOW!). Game customisation is easy to understand and works well (i love it when the game describes what aspects you are tuning rather than making you google it).
Overall it's a fun and fluid game. Feels more responsive to me than tag 2. WORTH.

I'm a long time fan of MK but I'm quite disappointed with this shaky release by HVS.
Online mode got a little better with the latest patch (I haven't gotten "The game session is no longer available" messages so far) but there is still a lag that can determine the outcome of the fight, especially against experienced players.
There is still unstable FPS even on the lowest settings (and my rig is: Core i7 920, GTX570, 8GB Ram)
Story mode should've been longer and each character should've have its own chapter.
I really hope NRS pull their sleeves and help HVS fix the mess that they created, because at its core, the game is quite fun), and maybe release more free content to compensate for this ordeal.
I wouldn't recommend buying this for full price (60$).

EDIT: I change my mind, this game is absolutely not recommended. Online play is horrendous. Use your $60 plus $30 DLC for the PS4 or Xbone version, those versions run better guaranteed (I've tried them). Good job High Voltage Studios, and good job Netherrealm Studios for hiring High Voltage to port the game in the first place! There's never a "happy gaming" if the game has horrendous online play. Everything I said below still remains the same.
---
Mortal Kombat X brings a new meta game to the MK series, and delivers a fix to what fighting gamers want in a competitive fighting game. The Variation mechanic is new to MK. This gives players a total of 75 (as of right now) different variations to play with and hundreds of potential match ups, which really spices things up for the game and the casual and competitive players. Story mode is an improvement from MK9, there's depth to the classic characters like Scorpion and others, but it lacks to some of the new characters. While story mode is an improvement, the QTE's are boring and don't deliver true consequence to the story or player, but it's better than Injustice. Now, if I click "Yes" to the games recommendation, I would be lying. This specific version of MKX suffers a BAD port from High Voltage Studios. It's BAD. MKX suffers frame dropping from stages that have tons of visual effects and interactions like Sky Temple; the game also suffers from a bad netcode. It's so bad, half of the matches I get put with get disconnected. The netcode is so bad, even the "minor" patch didn't do much. So overall, the only thing that holds me back from clicking that "Yes" is the bad port from High Voltage and its bad netcode that visibly shows input lag, consistent disconnection, and frame dropping. But if you're a big MK fan and is or was hype for the sequel, I would recommend it. The game is fun enough already, just don't play online or choose visual appealing stages.
This bad port is unacceptable and I don't think people should pay $60 to play a bad port. No disrespect, but the only thing High Voltage Studios has done right is Saints Row: Gat out of Hell, but even then that game is decent. If you want the "decent" online play and little to no stage frame drops, you're better off buying the PS4 or Xbone version. Sad but true.
Happy gaming everybody.

Rockstar is my favorite developper and publisher. With a pedigree as impressive as the GTA series, Red Dead Redemption and Max Payne, why would you not expect the very best from them ? More importantly, after over a decade of publishing games that felt and were complete with great stories and amazing content, only ever releasing DLCs that not only were great but felt like completely different and new games, one of which is actually my favorite zombie game, you'd would have to be crazy not to expect anything else than an amazing and perfect game and eagerly await each dlc.
In any case that's how I felt back when Grand Theft Auto V came out. At first I was overwhelmed, I had never seen a game with such a big scope, so much to do and so much to see, the game looked amazing and felt amazing and the missions were great, but the more time passed and the more I realised the game didn't have nearly as much soul as Red Dead Redemption, GTA IV or even San Andreas had, the game didn't have that unique charm of the wild west or of the gloomy and dark vibes of Liberty City and its fun and crazy vibe paled in comparison of those in San Andreas. Of course the missions and visuals were much more impressive but that's to be expected from a game coming out in 2013, for which we had been waiting for for 6 years now.

I run up to it and with my pistol I shoot the driver... nothing happens, the train just keeps going, at this point I'm baffled, there's no way they did this right ? Now I'm legitimately disapointed and confused, why would Rockstar bring back the train and showcase it in a trailer and not let you drive it ? I go on a hunt for a paramedic and fire truck, same thing, you can't do anything with them. What the hell Rockstar ? TLDR: Wasted's gameplay is fun, but it has some key design flaws that make it, in my opinion, unplayable. You loose the majority of your progress when you die, you can ruin your save by killing NPCs, and you aren't allowed to explore due to the time limit system.

Wasted is fun, solid, funny, dungeon crawling shooter. But it has some key design flaws that make it, in my opinion, unplayable.
1. Most Importantly, you loose so, so much when you die.
The game is semi-permadeth -- when your character dies, they're gone forever, but any items you've stashed stay in your stash. The problem with this is that the crux of the game is the 'level up' system, via Booze, is lost entirely upon death. Imagine it like this -- you're playing an MMO, and you've leveled up however far say, five hours got you. Then, you make a stupid mistake or get cocky (or in this case, misunderstand a game system and be irreconcialably punished for it), and you die. All your levels, and all your gear that wasn't stored in a bank is lost (to the game's credit, it does have a 'Lost and Found' system where you can buy back any rare gear you lost, albeit at a ridiculous price). Doesn't that sound ♥♥♥♥♥♥?
Note: I realize there are games, such as Don't Starve, that have this mechanic and are still very successful. This difference between Wasted and Don't Starve is that in the latter, you are rewarded with experience when you die, there are safeguards available to revive you, and starting over is genuinly fun, and the former has none of those things going for it.
2. No manual save or re-load
Pretty self explanatory, but in a game where you can kill vital NPC characters, this is a problem. I wanted to see what would happen if you shot a nameless waster in the pub town, and it turns out the entire town turns on you, and  it autosaves the game the moment you do so, so I wasn't able to undo what I did.
3. The 'Spelunky Ghost' system
I don't know what else to call this, but if your unfamiliar, basically it means that if you take too long on a level, an extremely powerful enemy chases you down. Now this doesn't sound like a problem, but if you take into account the fact that you will undoubtedly die if you explore the entire level, it kinda sucks. You really don't have any time to detour.
The game's extremely fun for the price, thanks to its rouge lite mechanics.

After a few runs and multiple deaths I've decided to write a short review about WASTED.
As you may have read by now, WASTED is the final product of a drunk one-night stand that Fallout and Borderlands had at some point. This child was seemingly not very appreciated by it's parents and got dumped into a dumpster where a huge family of roguelites found it kicking and screaming, after which they decided to adopt it.  All of these events shaped WASTED's childhood and now it's all grown up, pee-drunk and with a wide range of crude jokes and pop culture references.
The rough childhood, however, turned WASTED into a bit of a sadist and it absolutely loves to punish people who decide to befriend it. At this point I've managed to get three wasters wasted in the depths of the cooler, one due to a trap and two fell victim to the raider ♥♥♥♥♥♥s somewhere at level 5. I would say that their memory will not be forgotten but everyone who are in WASTED's company are falling down drunk, so they've probably already forgotten about them. Wasters are a disposable resource afterall.
So much for a serious review, huh? Oh well, let's wrap it up with some pros and cons!
PROS:
- Groovy 80's vibe.
- Gameplay resembling Fallout/Borderlands with a dash of any roguelite you've ever played.
- Crude humour.
- Booze.
- More booze.
- A talking dog.
- RNG, lots of it.
CONS:
- Level design gets repetitive as hell after you've ran through the levels a few times.
- The knockback mechanic in it's current shape is a bit unfair and will screw you over.
- The S.O.B purifier is an effin' fun ruiner.
- RNG, lots of it.
All in all, WASTED is a great game for fans of the roguelite and FPS genres! Be prepared to get a tad frustrated over the knockback mechanic and an alarming lack of Medstims when you need them the most though.

I played this game on co-op and it was a blast. You play as Frank, a great goofy photographer that could fit straight into 80's action movies. Your friend will play as Chuck, a motorcycle driver from a crazy zombie gladiator type arena show, the protagonist from the original Dead Rising 2. Together you're trying to solve who started a zombie outbreak and why, all while trying to save as many survivors as you can.
There's a lot of zombies, looters, crazy redneck americans, psychos, survivors, and a lot of ways to kill them all. Anything and everything in the game are your weapons. Hell, you can even combine a vibrator with a leaf blower, creating the weapon to surpass even Metal Gear. Taking photographs is a core gameplay element, as taking certain shots get you EXP based on how sexual, brutal, dramatic, gorey and special the photos taken are. Bosses are introduced in a fantastic manner, they will make you laugh and kick your butt afterwards. I only had a few minor issues with the lack of survivor dialogue depth, lack of a hardmode, etc, but the game is so much fun that they are easily ignored.
I'm convinced that I'll be playing this again and it'll crack me up for a good 20 hours again. It was the first Dead Rising I played and after that I decided to pick up the first and the third. Apparently the fourth one is nothing like the first two.
If you want a great co-op to play with a friend through the whole campaign, you can't go wrong with this one.

I decided to be one of those guys who insta-buys the game, so others can read early opinions of the game before risking buying it. So, is it good or bad? It depends.
Are you a fan of RWBY? Do you like those "Smash one key non-stop to win" kind of games? You like to support good companies who actually tried to put an effort into an Early Access title? Then you should buy it(although, 15€ for this is a high risk for now).
As I usually do, I'll start with the bad things of the game. First and foremost, look at how much I've played the game. Less than an hour. That's what it took me to finish it. I'm not joking, the "campaign" that there's already in the game is arround an hour long, which is kind of short for 15 DAMN €'S. Of course the game will get more and more as the game goes on, but I can't say this long enough, there will be some dumbass who'll buy it at full price and expect hours and hours of content. Of course, it's fun to play it with friends (I literally have noone to play it but stranges as I have no friends who bought it yet), but you can only play something so much times before it eventually gets repetitive: It needs more content, fast. The story that there's on the game is actually good, and impressive for Early Access levels, but I just hope it doesn't take the devs 3 months for each new story.
Second, the characters. Don't get me wrong, I like the RWBY characters, but having only 4 is kinda weak. There's another team of 4 characters which could be insanely fun to have here, and if you saw the series, YOU KNOW WHICH GUYS I'M TALKING ABOUT. I just want to make sure to make the devs know it: the game NEEDS more characters. That being said, the characters already on the game, being Ruby, Yang, Blake and Weiss are cool enough. Specially Yang, of course. I haven't yet seen Weiss ingame as noone picked her, but I bet she's also fun. Also, they look great, taken directly from the show. Oh and, one other thing... When characters talk, the subtitles don't advance. A lot of lines are too long to fit on the screen, and get stuck on limbo. Fix that, please: non-english speakers will have A LOT OF TROUBLE OTHERWISE!
The third thing I'll comply about, are the enemies. I know, it's a Dinasty Warriors-kind of game... But that doesn't mean it shouldn't be original. There are a bunch of enemies taken from the show, but not much variety. Some boar-like monsters that spin and charge like Sonic, the Grunt-like monsters that don't do much unless they come in packs, the Beowolfs that do some sort of plunging attack with their claws, Bear-like Grimms that for some reason, stomp the ground hard enougnh rocks explode, and later on some green beasts that explode. The main complaint with this is that once you find out their weakness, dying is a joke. It should also say, there are no real bosses. There's a big guy with tons of HP, but he acts just the same as the bear Grimms, which was kind of a dissapointment.
The last bad thing I see, is on the skill-tree and XP system. First of all, XP is given to however gets the killing blow, or finds XP orbs hidden in crates (XP from artifacts is shared). Now, why does it work like this? It should at least be shared, meaning the killing blow gives 100% XP, and helping gives from 75 to 25%, depending on how much damage you did to it. Right now, you can just spam your skills when things go low and take it all for yourself. That being said, the Skill-tree needs some work. As there is no tutorial, you can't now right off the bat what the characters do, that's a problem. While adding a Tutorial could help a lot, I think you guys are going the wrong direction: I believe levels should be global and unique for the character. Meaning, you reached LVL2 with Yang, you'll be LVL2 with Yang even if the game ends. That would give the game A TON of more replayability, as games could become eventually harder and harder. Also, it should have two skill-trees at the same time: One of passive abilities such as "Having more HP" or "Saving people faster", but also adding increased power and HP with levels and skill-points, and another for your actual skills.
All of that being said, what do we have left? A game that will
be something great... But right now it's more like a demo. It's hard to tell if the game will or not be great right now, but it does look like the Devs placed a lot of effort on it, so I'm going to stay positive about it.
The voices are just great. The graphics are simple, but cool. The models look great, as they have been ripped from the show. The game can be entertaining for a while, as it's quite simple. The maps look great, although I did find an area on the last map with some sort of glitch that the devs over-looked.
Is it worth it? As I said, it depends. If you have 15€ to spare and want to help a good Early Access game grow, jump right ahead. If you're a fan of RWBY like me, you'll find it good enough. Otherwise, you mind want to wait for more updates. Oh and, I'll try to update this as things get added in, of course.
And please, Devs. ADD RED VS BLUE REFERENCES. I MEAN COME ON, I KNOW YOU CAN'T PHYSICALLY ADD CABOOSE TEAM-KILLING PEOPLE BUT AT LEAST SOME SORT OF CAMEO OR REFERENCE!

Portal Knights is cute and blocky exploration. You run around, you craft, you kill mobs, you build portals, etc.
On top of that, the dev team is highly responsive and the support team is helpful and understanding.
That said, the optimization is terrible. If you do not meet the minimum requirements (which aren't even far off the recommended) you WILL have serious issues. Missing text, missing sound, various crashes and graphical problems. At best, you'll be like me and you'll have no problems with graphics and interface and just have zero sound whatsoever. At worst, the game will be utterly unplayable.
However, it has potential. I hope for better optimisation in the future, as well as better support for Intel graphics cards and integrated graphics. From my (brief) experience, the game isn't overly taxing and could likely be made to run better on lower-end rigs. It's in Early Access, so I'm hoping that by launch everything will be stable and supported. If not, oh well, I bought it on sale.
So if your PC can handle it, I recommend it for sure. If your PC cannot handle it - a phrase which here means "meet every single minimum requirement" - you will have issues.

Reminds me of Terraria, but in 3D. I played this game with two other friends; I was a mage, my other friends were warrior and ranger. All three seemed to compliment each other well. My warrior friend found it annoying as to how many potions she needed since she played the tank role a lot. Ranger seemed to be the easiest to craft better gear for. Mage is a little challenging to get upgrades as we haven't found any palm leaves yet (which we mistook for cannabis from the picture), but it's definitely still fun to shoot magic at fire skeletons. 10/10 would get robes caught on fire again.
Pros:
- Super fun with friends. I'd get someone to buy and play it with you if you can.
- Easy to set up. No local host setup required.
- Runs on my Surface Pro 4 (so you don't need a big gaming computer)
- Characters are per account and not per game. You can gather resources on your own, then join your friends game and still have all your levels and inventory items.
- Well coded. For a game in Early Access, I haven't run into any major (if any) bugs yet. Our game crashed a few times, but it might have been my friends Internet. Also it saves so well it didn't really matter.
- Classes have a nice mix of traits and looks.
- User customization is vast and pretty. The hair styles are amazing - it'll be hard to choose.
- Wide range of monsters. They even differ between day and night.
Cons:
- Definitely more fun when playing co-op. I can see it getting boring quite fast if you're alone.
- Definitely better to play this game with a controller. I went out and bought an Xbox One controller before playing. This isn't really a con for me as I love playing with controllers, but it may be for some.
- Switching between worlds takes a really long amount of time (even with expensive gaming PCs). I'm hoping this is improved in a future update.
- Slow start. My friends are ready for a boss battle but we haven't really found anything challenging in the 5 hours we played.
- Inventory controls (via controller) are a tad annoying. There doesn't seem to be a way to split a stack even with the keyboard.
- No server/more than 4 players support yet. I think this game on a small server would be amazing. Some gaming changes would have to be made though (like not teleporting everyone when switching worlds).
In short, this is a great Early Access game. I'm looking forward to future updates. I'm hoping to get some more friends addicted so I always have someone to play with.

Aragorn rushes into battle against a hundred orcs and beheads all of them before taking a scratch against the captain at the end.  If you try that in Mount and Blade you will get wrecked.  Shields break. Your sword can be pinned against you in the crush of melee.  Enemy knights will try to end your battle with a couched lance.

CAMPAIGN MODE: It's both a shooter and an RPG, you can upgrade your weapons, your stats, buy/upgrade weapons and buy equipment (a drone that follows you around and shoots zombies, for example) at the end of every map. It can be finished in about 3 hours on Normal. On Hard, well it's very, very hard.
SURVIVAL MODE: Sets you in a limited map where you kill monsters  until a mini-boss arrives at regular intervals, and from which you earn new weapons and level-ups for your skills. You must survive as long as possible.
GUN MODE: You control a huge stationary turret at the centre of the map, surrounded by a concrete barricade. After killing a certain amount of monsters you are given a Nuke that wipes all enemies. You must survive as long as possible.
NEGATIVES/THE BAD: The bad things about this game are:
- Bad pathing AI (the enemies are really not too smart to come at you, very often they run towards walls).
-Getting stuck in the environment, which might happen once in a while (you usually can get unstuck by moving around a bit, but sometimes you are really stuck and need to restart the level).
Overall, get it on sale (bought it for 0.20e), it's simple and satisfing fun.
PS: This is the first game I have played a game from this company (the others being the Alien Shooter series).

Coming from a background of Spy Fox games and other point and click adventures, Deponia is a great series with plenty of  puzzles and excruciatingly interesting plot. If you like any of the Humongous Entertainment games from your childhood or coming in fresh to the genre or just yearning for a great story overall, I sincerely recommend the Deponia series.
Pros:
The art direction for the game is absoutely enjoyable and unique with everything retaining detail to backgrounds and foregrounds and character design. Simply eye candy.
Soundtrack is astonishingly marvelous, very catchy and not too repetitive like elevator music. Every scene is accompanied by amazing music making the atmosphere pop in any mood or situation.
Deponia is filled with unique and lovable characters, all of them serving a purpose to the game in some way. The main character is a lovable jerk that can be easily attatched to. Plenty of dialogue to compliment the characters as well as the very well done voice acting to top it all off to complete the characters.
The intriguing storyline and plot is probably the best selling point of this game (ofc its an adventure game) along with its great sense of humor. The univerese of the Deponia series was well crafted and it's obvious that the developers poured heart and soul into making Deponia make sense and rotating the cogs of this complicated universe. It serves as a motivation to finish puzzles to get to the end.
Cons:
The puzzles in this game can be either simple, difficult or just frustrating that you want to pull your hairs out. A good chunk of the puzzles are not built on logical reasoning and consists of clicking everywhere until something happens. I've spent a good few hours trying to figure out answers to puzzles that didn't make any sense. Without following a walkthrough or being the luckiest person in the world, you can be easily spending hours upon hours trying to figure out the solutions.
Overall this game is a must play

is a highly entertaining point-and-click misadventure with lovable characters, an interesting world, and wacky humor. If you like adventure games and goofy narratives, then look no further. It should be a pretty easy game to enjoy for most fans of the genre.
The crazy characters and zany game-world combined with the pleasing art style and soundscape make
charming and atmospheric. This alluring ambiance is definitely the backbone of the game.  And as everything else falls into place, the overall presentation of the game just exudes an aura of “enjoyability” that is hard to defy.
Interestingly, the music and sound effects really play a much larger than usual role in the establishment of the ambiance. Relatedly, even the voice-acting in this game is not only well above the standard for the genre, but also objectively well performed. The end result shows how these elements can really help elevate the overall presentation of a game when they’re handled with care.
As far as gameplay goes: it is pretty standard for the genre. The puzzles are decently challenging and mostly fair; although some of the solutions don’t really make sense in terms of real-world thinking. You must remember to think in terms of the wacky logic of the game-world when solving puzzles. Sometimes it can be a little frustrating because it is hard to think like that. I suppose that if you get truly flabbergasted, you could always check a guide. Regardless of how you make it past the confusing parts, the rest of the presentation of the game is well worth experiencing.
So if you are a fan of point-and-click games,
should be a good bet for you.  You definitely should beware of the outside-the-box (inside-the-game) logic, but in my opinion, it is one of the features of the game that makes it unique and worth playing.

---INTRO---
okay so like i dont usually do reviews, but the mixed reviews ive seen here inspired me to give it a shot. anyway, let's just get right into it: i like this game. a lot, actually. however, it isnt perfect, so i'll list some cons first, then get into the juicy stuff later.
---CONS---
> BUGS are currently a noteworthy issue, an offputtingly common one in fact, but i personally wasnt too badly effected by them besides having to relaunch the game a few times, and based on the intense backlash/frustration from the community, i think it's safe to assume a patch will probably be released in the near future to fix or at least improve the problems anyway
> SLOPPY PORT; keyboard controls are awkward (why did they choose Y and 0 as default keys? why did they do that) but they're rebindable, so its not a game-breaking flaw by any means. i tried to use my playstation controller at first, knowing the controls were designed for a console, but steam informed me that the game didnt support it, so i didnt pursue the notion any further. also, the toilet minigame sections have a very unintuitive and immediate learning curve on keyboard, but everything works fine once you get the hang of it (i found it helpful trying to imitate the joystick motions from the console controls)
> FORCED UPLAY INTEGRATION but honestly? i wont judge this title based on something outside the dev team's control. i mean, come on, idk why people are so worked up, like, this is ubisoft we're talking about here, why are you surprised at all? i would start learning to expect this kind of thing now, because i really doubt they'll drop future uplay integration as a company just because people complained on the south park forums lol
> WANTS YOUR MONEY VERY BADLY; whether it's the DLC on day one or the uplay rewards or even the steep release price, this game gives you a lot of opportunities to empty your wallet. however, only minor content like costumes and perks currently get this treatment as of the time im writing this (10/22/17), and it doesnt effect the gameplay or story in any cheap or frustrating way, so beyond the fact that life under capitalism is hell and i wish i had more money, i dont really have anything to say on the matter
> ALSO THE DRM IS APPARENTLY VERY BAD but im not even kind of an expert in that subject so i wont go into it. also, again, it's not part of the game itself, just something to be aware of beforehand, so i wont make it out to be a bigger deal than it actually is in the long run
---PROS---
> LOVABLE CHARACTERS; tweek and craig are cute as hell, wendy kicks♥♥♥♥♥ cartman is firmly back on his BS, timmy is professor X, and lots of side characters from the show have appearances, so it's just generally great in that respect, as can be expected from south park. companions have dialogue that interact with each other and respond to certain events in battle, so i thought that was neat too
> GOOD-NATURED, SATIRICAL, FUN HUMOR. now, if you're a hardcore SP fan, dont necessarily go in expecting it to be expecially "offensive" (what does that even mean by the way? is satire not funny to you unless theres a slur every five seconds or what, like, what are you looking for here dude) but, like Stick of Truth, it does have a lot of callbacks to the show and even a lot of smaller details that personally made me laugh (or at the very least smile). the game does a great job cracking jokes about taboo topics without over-reliance on shock value or easy stereotypes, but im a white cis gay boy from a middle-income family so you can do the math yourself there to figure out how much weight my opinion actually holds on this matter
> SURPRISINGLY GOOD STORY, which, again, is much like the first title. a nice mix of not taking itself too seriously, a well-structured progression, and the effective use of narrative cues to switch moods at the drop of a hat. i found the finale to be a little less climactic than the first game, but honestly the entire game was such a wild ride i cant find the energy to complain about it too hard.
> BASIC BUT SOLID STRATEGIC GAMEPLAY; a few weird quirks such as having almost no vertically-reaching moves, but if you like this genre of gameplay you probably won't mind; hell, you may even like the added challenge! bosses and enemies (especially bosses) were unique and varied, and had interesting mechanics and/or special obstacles/goals to match. im still unsure if all of the companions and classes are equally fun/useful (that's for the nerds to figure out) but i for one really enjoyed the battles and had a surprisingly hard time getting burnt out like i usually do when i binge a game for so many hours in a row
> PHENOMINAL SOUNDTRACK like holy♥♥♥♥♥♥guys they really stepped it up from last game, which already had a solid ost, so that's saying something. the overworld music was never annoying or repetitive, the fights were almost always improved by the mood the music set, and the boss themes are verging on legendary (spontaneous bootay, morgan freeman, and sober towelie are ones that stand out in my mind)
---VERDICT---

A game about two brothers that go on a journey to save their father. Short, sweet, and beautiful. A must have for any fan of story focused games.

For no more than $5 this is a cool experience of a game. It has all the critera of an indie title - weird controls, different art style, good music, and a story that begins in greatness but ends strangely. At least this game actually has an ending, unlike so many other indie games that have their artsy open end garbage that I consider bad storytelling.
(spoilers now)
You start off with two brothers to save your dad. You need an elixr from a tree, and the perils you go through are pretty fun. The whole game flows almost flawlessly and you always feel as if the world is connected. Dark Souls fans know what this is like. Near the end the game takes a turn of the Tolkien by way of the eagle saving the hobbits, but it's better than trekking through the near 2 and a half hours it takes to get there.
The length is rather short but that's fine if the cost is justified, and I would not justify a $10 price tag just for this experience. Most movies have better value than that, and are far easier to sit through. The controls are wonky and by the time you get used to them the game ends; one analog stick controls one brother, the other controls the other (or different keys if you use a keyboard). It's aggravating to try to move one but you always end up moving the other, but I imagine if you're used to playing the piano you may catch on quickly. Otherwise everything is very easy to learn and never at any point did I think "these stupid controls killed me."
There's next to no challenge in this game. I died twice and both were when I was distracted by a phone call. The puzzles aren't exactly puzzles, just light obstacles. While that is a downside it's still charming and was lots of fun to do. The graphics feel like they belong on a console, and this definitely feels like a PC port (maybe it isn't), but if you're fine with Diablo 3 you'll be fine with these. The music is great, the banter between brothers at random invtervals is realistic, and the little secrets you can do like saving a turtle or throwing things down a well show that the developers cared about this game.
Overall, if it's on sale, I say buy it and blast through it in a few hours. To me, the number one reason to play Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is that it isn't anywhere nearly as bad as Gone Home.

A Tale of Two Sons proves you don't need blood, guts, gore, crashes, explosions, bullets, guns or nudity to make an AMAZING game. If you must have those things to enjoy a game choose a different title. This game has an engaging story albeit a little straight forward plot. The brothers must work together as a team to solve puzzles and accomplish tasks although none of the puzzles is overly complicated they are not necessarily straight forward either.
The BEST part of this game is the awesome graphics and engaging storyline. You want these brothers to succeed in their task of finding the cure for their dad's ailment. You'll be drawn into each scene by the beauty that surrounds you. The details truly breathtaking. If you allow yourself to become emotionally engaged in the story you may even get chocked up near the climax of the story.
Two improvements are (1) I wish there was more interaction between the two brothers after successfully completing a task or navigating a tough area ... i.e.  high fives, warm embrace or celebration. This would show just how much these two brothers love each other and make the climax of the story even more powerful. The second (2) improvement would be to have decisions made in the game effect different outcomes. Right now you either get a puzzle right or interaction right or you don't proceed ... Yes = move forward with story - No = do it again until you get it right.
Overall I'd give this game a 9/10 for what it is ... a 3-4 hour visually & emotionally engaging puzzle solving story. Knowing what I know now I would DEFINITELY BUY THIS GAME again!
Hope this review is helpful in your decision to buy this game. Go ahead ... you won't regret it as you don't need the elements of my first sentence to enjoy a gaming title.

MAY 8TH UPDATE: Removed positive feedback about the models, removed negative feedback about movement and gameplay issues. Removed negative point about lack of single player and tutorial. All in all nothing has improved that much and they've made bad choices about the new character models.
So, main immediate issues of the game:
* No player progression system, no customization, etc. Characters do level up in self-contained games, but you retain nothing once the game is done.
* Despite being a cooperative game, in-game experience isn't shared by the team, encouraging players to screw each other over to level faster.
* Dreadful lack of different enemy types.
* Can't remap controls.
* Can't customize graphics options thoroughly.
* Hacking through hordes of enemies doesn't feel satisfying. There's not enough enemies, and enemies have a bit too much health, and tear you to shreds too fast. Feels nothing like the trailer!
* Fair amount of bugs, especially graphical.
* The models of the game, originally faithful to the show, now look ugly as sin, generic anime doll models that are actually freaky to look at. This game no longer looks like a RWBY game, it looks like a generic anime action game with a low budget.
But, hey, upsides:
* Is early access, so one can expect huge additions to the game.
* The base skeleton of the game is pretty solid.
* Very responsive controls, although undocumented.
For the moment! Probably not worth its full price tag. It's fun for what it is, but not 15$ fun. It's a fun 4-player hack and slash, and you should look forward to what it will look like in a few months if they actually start adding stuff, fixing issues, etc., but at the moment it's a bit lackluster. This game more than most Early Access titles really IS Early Access quality.
This review will be updated when and if the game shapes up!
Just to make it clear: I don't regret the purchase. I really do look forward to this being a full game. In the meantime though I can't recommend buying it without first acknowledging its downfalls and being sure you want it.
And sorry, but no, I don't think "it's Early Access, you can't judge the game yet!" really flies. People are being asked to pay for it right now, not in one year, so it's important that people know what they're paying for right now.

Alright, this is my first real review for a game, so bear with me.
I've been a fan of RWBY for a long time. RoosterTeeth sponsor, watched the trailers long before the first episode, bought the merch, and the first thing I do when they drop is watch the newest episodes. (Not to mention 'waifu Blake' jokes my girlfriend barrages me with weekly. I regret nothing.)
So, it's of no surprise that I was one of the first to purchase this game when it finally dropped. We've all been waiting for quite some time, and while this is in no way a Triple-A title with millions of dollars in development costs, overall, for an early access title, it still has AMAZING potential (much like the show has proven). I have an Associates degree in Video Game Art and Animation, and have done some  minor work with a few local indie companies, so I greatly understand the time and effort it takes to make a game of even this calibur with such a small team.
So far, from what I've tested of all 4 current characters (should they add more down the line), each animation set is pretty solid, with only minor tweaks involving run animations or when you walk down a hill, which causes a stutter or slide, instead.
The combat system for all 4 characters is quick and flows very well, using a similar system to one of my favorite titles 'Dynasty Warriors'. Quick combos, which can be varied with charge attack skills, and big finishing moves. All of which can blend together as you slaughter Grimm. The skills all vary to each character, and after leveling up, gain more powerful alternates to each, can be charges, etc.
The leveling system is extemely simplified. But, that in no way means it's bad. Simple 'skill' and stat trees with a skill point system. Level up, gain a skill point, unlock a skill, move on. Quick and effective.
The environments so far are STUNNING. The flow of the architecture and landscape perfectly captures the beauty of the world of Remnant that we've come to expect; all the while maintaining the same feel as the show.
Enemies, of course, vary in strength and skills for each breed of Grimm you're fighting. But, when you're fighting stronger variations of each breed, not only do they get much larger, but there is very obvious visual differences to each model.
One of the best things overall, though, is that EVERY character is fully voiced over by the actual voice actors used for the show (kind of a no-brainer, to be honest). The only con so far with this that I've found is that the V.O.s for the player characters are VERY quiet. Simply increasing the output volume on the dev's end can fix that, though.
Overall, an extremely solid game, with amazing potential. Grab some friends, or play online with strangers, and go slaughter the forces of Grimm.
My only Con?
That Monty Oum isn't with us anymore to enjoy it like we will.

I had a hard time giving this a negative review. I love the Tekken series and this game is decent, but at the price, I don't think it's worth it. I thought that because it had the overwhemingly positive rating it meant it had all the goodness of the previous games plus a bit more.
Pros:
Runs well on most hardware. I got a consistent 59 fps.
Online multiplayer is working alright (if you can find an opponent)
No lag in single player
Cons:
The story mode doesn't show you stories about all of the characters unlike in previous games. In fact, it leaves you with more questions than answers. It makes it feel like Tekken 7 was just one last cash grab. They didn't bother giving it a proper ending.
The costumes are a major disappointment. The previous games had a balance of fun and cool costumes and props to buy. Tekken 7 just had absurd costumes which didn't seem to match the characters. A lot of the cool costumes in Tekken 6 will not be seen in this game in its current state.
A lot of the fighters you are familair with are gone.
You might not be able to find an opponent online.
There is no option to enable the replay feature which some like.
Overall, the vanilla Tekken gameplay is there, but if you're looking for more like the story and customization options, then I would look the other way. Hopefully, better customization items are added. It's also a wish of mine for the story to be actually resolved, or at least some ending movie be provided to every characters like in the other games, but that is unlikely.
