---INTRO---
okay so like i dont usually do reviews, but the mixed reviews ive seen here inspired me to give it a shot. anyway, let's just get right into it: i like this game. a lot, actually. however, it isnt perfect, so i'll list some cons first, then get into the juicy stuff later.
---CONS---
> BUGS are currently a noteworthy issue, an offputtingly common one in fact, but i personally wasnt too badly effected by them besides having to relaunch the game a few times, and based on the intense backlash/frustration from the community, i think it's safe to assume a patch will probably be released in the near future to fix or at least improve the problems anyway
> SLOPPY PORT; keyboard controls are awkward (why did they choose Y and 0 as default keys? why did they do that) but they're rebindable, so its not a game-breaking flaw by any means. i tried to use my playstation controller at first, knowing the controls were designed for a console, but steam informed me that the game didnt support it, so i didnt pursue the notion any further. also, the toilet minigame sections have a very unintuitive and immediate learning curve on keyboard, but everything works fine once you get the hang of it (i found it helpful trying to imitate the joystick motions from the console controls)
> FORCED UPLAY INTEGRATION but honestly? i wont judge this title based on something outside the dev team's control. i mean, come on, idk why people are so worked up, like, this is ubisoft we're talking about here, why are you surprised at all? i would start learning to expect this kind of thing now, because i really doubt they'll drop future uplay integration as a company just because people complained on the south park forums lol
> WANTS YOUR MONEY VERY BADLY; whether it's the DLC on day one or the uplay rewards or even the steep release price, this game gives you a lot of opportunities to empty your wallet. however, only minor content like costumes and perks currently get this treatment as of the time im writing this (10/22/17), and it doesnt effect the gameplay or story in any cheap or frustrating way, so beyond the fact that life under capitalism is hell and i wish i had more money, i dont really have anything to say on the matter
> ALSO THE DRM IS APPARENTLY VERY BAD but im not even kind of an expert in that subject so i wont go into it. also, again, it's not part of the game itself, just something to be aware of beforehand, so i wont make it out to be a bigger deal than it actually is in the long run
---PROS---
> LOVABLE CHARACTERS; tweek and craig are cute as hell, wendy kicks♥♥♥♥♥ cartman is firmly back on his BS, timmy is professor X, and lots of side characters from the show have appearances, so it's just generally great in that respect, as can be expected from south park. companions have dialogue that interact with each other and respond to certain events in battle, so i thought that was neat too
> GOOD-NATURED, SATIRICAL, FUN HUMOR. now, if you're a hardcore SP fan, dont necessarily go in expecting it to be expecially "offensive" (what does that even mean by the way? is satire not funny to you unless theres a slur every five seconds or what, like, what are you looking for here dude) but, like Stick of Truth, it does have a lot of callbacks to the show and even a lot of smaller details that personally made me laugh (or at the very least smile). the game does a great job cracking jokes about taboo topics without over-reliance on shock value or easy stereotypes, but im a white cis gay boy from a middle-income family so you can do the math yourself there to figure out how much weight my opinion actually holds on this matter
> SURPRISINGLY GOOD STORY, which, again, is much like the first title. a nice mix of not taking itself too seriously, a well-structured progression, and the effective use of narrative cues to switch moods at the drop of a hat. i found the finale to be a little less climactic than the first game, but honestly the entire game was such a wild ride i cant find the energy to complain about it too hard.
> BASIC BUT SOLID STRATEGIC GAMEPLAY; a few weird quirks such as having almost no vertically-reaching moves, but if you like this genre of gameplay you probably won't mind; hell, you may even like the added challenge! bosses and enemies (especially bosses) were unique and varied, and had interesting mechanics and/or special obstacles/goals to match. im still unsure if all of the companions and classes are equally fun/useful (that's for the nerds to figure out) but i for one really enjoyed the battles and had a surprisingly hard time getting burnt out like i usually do when i binge a game for so many hours in a row
> PHENOMINAL SOUNDTRACK like holy♥♥♥♥♥♥guys they really stepped it up from last game, which already had a solid ost, so that's saying something. the overworld music was never annoying or repetitive, the fights were almost always improved by the mood the music set, and the boss themes are verging on legendary (spontaneous bootay, morgan freeman, and sober towelie are ones that stand out in my mind)
---VERDICT---

WASTED is a rougelike FPS dungeon crawler set in a post-apocalyptic California where the 1980s lives on. The focus on the game is for your character to raid ‘Coolers’ so you can get some radioactive booze to have a good time and if you have to kill a few hundred people in randomly generated dungeons to do so then who cares, am i right? The game has some interesting concepts such as only awarding perks, both positive and negative, to the player for drinking the radioactive booze, that can last either an entire cooler run or for the rest of the game as long as you keep your character alive as like with most rougelike games, death is permanent. Despite death being permanent you can still progress in the game as your home never changes and any items left there will still be there when you take over as the next character and any valuable items you lose in the dungeon from your previous character can be both back from the lost and found at the ony express terminal (makes more sense when you play the game).
Pros/Things I liked:
- Fun to play
- Amazing art style
- Groovy soundtrack
- Cool buffs/debuffs system
- Weird/Dark humor
- Good Voice acting
Meh/ Things that i am not that fond of:
- Crafting system: not that useful or necessary
- The dungeons are sometimes a bit too random with doors that lead to nowhere and spawn rates that are sometimes unfair to the payer.
- Not the best inventory system
- Knock back: The knock back you character takes from guns is too high in m opinion and makes it impossible for you to Melee your way out of gun fights if you have run out of bullets. Basically your dead if you have no ammo
- Could have made the first level a tiny bit more forgiving to ease the player into the game.
Cons/Things I don’t Like:
- Purification system: If you spend to long any level of the dungeon the game sends an over powered enemy, known as a S.O.B., after you to force you to rush through the level. My main problem is not that this system exists in the game but that it is triggered too quickly and can often not allow you any time to explore if you got caught if and a tough battle with enemies you couldn’t kill. It also becomes a major problem when the randomness of the level generation means you have to backtrack and that means you can often times get killed due to the damage cause by the S.O.B.’s mini-gun and because they have 600 health they are near next to impossible to kill.
- Cant customize new characters: The game lets you customize your first character but after that you cant customize  any subsequent character. should be able to to create any subsequent character or at least have them connected to your character in someway such as them being your original character’s long lost sibling which would fit in well with the ridiculousness nature of the game.
Score Card
Rating: 8/10 - Good Game
*Value For Money: 9/10 - Buy at full price if you usually enjoy rougelikes
Recommended For: fans of rougelike games, people who like FPS game with an RPG twist, fans of Borderlands’ art style.
*I got this game through Humble Monthly but feel like if I would be more than satisfied if i payed for the game at the full price listed on steam (13 euro)

Received WASTED as part of the Monthly Humble Bundle, and I have to say it's great fun so far! It's essentially a dungeon (vault) crawler with the added option of withdrawing early to save (and keep) your items. You do this by drinking until you pass out...
The drinking mechanic is cleverly applied, since whenever you take a drink, you gain a new permananent 'trait'. Wimp out and leave the dungeon/vault early, and you get a poor reward, and maybe even a negative trait. Leave late after battling on and you'll be rewarded with better abilities. Push on too far and you'll just die, losing all of your gear collected.
On top of this, the game has a variety of weapons and gear, as well as character customisation and development. There is also a 'home' area to craft new gear and food to help you in the vaults.
The graphic style is very similar to Borderlands, as is the over-the-top gunplay and explosions. Although it seems clearly influenced by Borderlands, WASTED uses it well. Overall a thoroughly enjoyable game. Recommended!

-Edit-
I want to preface this review with a tag that I am only recommending (Thumbs up) this game based on the fanboy that I am, in hopes that it improves beyond what it was a few months ago in the Ruby only game. If it continues at that growth, I believe it will be an excellent game in about a year's time.
That said, I understand that my love of the show can potentially blind me to features and things I don't see, but as such, I am being as fair as I can with that said in my critique of the game. I do not need the comments pointing such things out. I understand that it goes against the "Fair review" idea, but being an adamant fan of the show, it can be difficult to be 100% unbiased.
-End edit-
On Day 1, I'm writing my first impressions for this game, as I'm a huge RWBY fanboy and love the series and what it's all about. That in mind, please read this review knowing that despite my fandom, I will criticize where necessary with regards to what I see. This is early access, and this is still day 1 only.
Gameplay revolves around a specific character (Ruby Rose, Weiss Schnee, Blake Belladonna, and Yang Xiao Long) and their specific movesets. Each controls a little differently, but it boils down to this: You have one button that is your melee based attack, one button that is a ranged based attack, and you can string combos by spamming the primary button over and over until satisfied. Or you can feel frisky and push your secondary button while in the middle of a combo to "Finish" the combo with a ranged attack and drop out of it. You have a "Dodge" button with your shift key.  Finally, as far as movesets go, you have 3 special moves, unique to each character that defines them. Some have ranged projectiles, some have area of effect wave clear sets. You have to try them to see what they do, and once you do, you'll find out that your melee basic attack ends up doing better than the specials in 95% of circumstances.
You gain experience from killing monsters, collecting items, and completing objectives. As you level, you'll unlock very basic things like extra special attacks, improved specials, and the like. The specials can be improved by either gaining the ability to charge them to do more damage, getting a new effect, or other traits. Other unlocks can be your aura (Health) recharging faster or... That's about it right now. And since we're on that topic - You have health. You won't realize this because you'll stun-lock all enemies you come across with melee or ranged attacks, but if there's more than 5-6 of them on you, you'll go from full to death in a matter of seconds. The balance of health is already an issue, as your characters (All four of them) are nimble enough to dodge a little bit to get out of harm's way, but if you get surrounded, you might as well kiss your butt goodbye.
Balance issues aside with health, the game play is fun for a few minutes - The characters all have unique personalities and voice lines, and from what I can tell, are all the original voice actors. You also have Peter Port (A teacher from the academy in the show) guiding your steps through the levels to help you out and aid you. However, the game play is extremely basic. There's only three buttons you'll care about while in combat - Melee about 90% of the time, ranged attack about 5% of the time, and your dodge about 5% of the time. Beyond that, specials are only when you feel frisky or are trying to solo things and want to speed it up (I've played solo on every character and felt no worry of getting overrun until the end of the first chapter at the wave clear section).
Is this game good? Honestly, not yet. Yet being that key word. There's a lot of room for improvement, as this is still day one of an early access title. Should you get it now? Ehhhh, questionable. Someone has to be a lab rat. Which lab rats should it be? Hardcore RWBY fans will adore the voice actors and the visuals, which look like they were made for the show and put into a game. Every character sounds and feels like they would in a real combat fight, and the animations are absolutely stunning. The game play is severely lacking currently, and the story is... Non-existent to be fair.
I won't give you a rating yet, but I would say if you're a RWBY fan, this is a game to pick up, if only for the sheer amounts of fanboy that will happen. If you're not a fan, I would stray away for now - The game is very unfinished, but in the future may be much better. Anything can happen.
As a RWBY fan, I recommend this, but don't for anyone that isn't (At the time of this review).
TL:DR
Pros:
+ RWBY cast voice actors.
+ Awesome sound and animations that look like they should.
+ Visuals are spot-on for the world of Remnant.
Cons:
- Extremely basic combat and no complexity
- Grows boring quickly due to low mechanical necessity.
- Unfinished (Early access)
- No customization
Sound 9.5/10, Graphics 9/10, Gameplay 2/10, recommended to (hardcore) fans *only* in current state.

For an early access game, this is awesome! I've only experienced one bug so far, and it was a monster sliding between two blocks and into the nether. Nonetheless, the rest of the game is perfect. For example the animations are satisfying, and the fights (even with regular monsters) feel epic!
You can be a warrior, an archer or a wizard. Each of them have their own ups and downs. Currently I would say that the archer is the easiest and most powerful one. Of course, the other classes are very nice too, but personally I think that the archers are a tad bit more powerful than the others. Not only do they have a lot of damage (a stat that allows their weapon to hit 3 times) but they also have next to no "max range" to their arsenal. They can shoot arrows over hills and still hit enemies if the player is able to aim their bow high and angled enough.
Though, I heard (I have not experienced it personally) that the warriors are able to crit very high and destroy monsters(bosses as well) within seconds. If you're interested in this class, I would suggest to try and build the best weapons and armor that allow you to get crit chance and crit damage. The only down part that I've heard about this class is that they have some difficulties against airborne targets. They do have a shout that allows them to knock enemies to the ground, but that is probably not enough, considering there is no mana regen in this game (unless you get mana globes after a fight) and the shouts eat at your mana like there's no tomorrow.
As for the last class, I think the wizards can be very powerful but I feel like their range could use some tweaking. They can kill the unkillable with their magic wands and get rid of the skeleton mages(I believe they're the only class with a weapon that allows them to completely kill those monsters, otherwise the other classes can only knock them out and they eventually come back... It can make some very messy fight if you ask me.)
Overall, the game is very entertaining, and at least for now, the weapons are not class bound. Anyone can use any weapon, but their power will depend on the stats that they choose during their growth. From what I've seen, there is no way to change your passive skill set, so be careful when you choose!
I think they should add a feature that allows players to customize their looks (either you wear another piece of armor over your own or something along those lines). So far, the only way to change your appearance is by creating your character and to craft new gear. Though the best gear is not the best looking one, and I feel like there would be a lot more choice if we were to get a "outfit" section in our inventory.

One of, if not, the best fighting game since Tekken Tag Tournament 2. Just when I thought all hope was lost for the genre, and that we would never see a fighting game with substance again, Tekken 7 comes along and shatters my misconceptions, showing me that, in this day and age of "release game first, finish later," publishers are still capable of allowing their developers to make the best game they possibly can, even if it means missing a deadline. This game was originally planned as an "Early 2017" title, but whatever caused the hold up was worth it, as this is a gem of a game. I've never played a fighting game that featured such an absurd level of attention to detail. Whether it be the seamless transition from cutscene to gameplay, the extensive customization options (which are even present during the cutscenes included in Arcade Mode), or the variety of game-type modifiers found within Treasure Mode: all of these details go such a long way in placing Tekken 7 at the top of its class. Smaller details, such as pseudo-dynamic weather, track changes between rounds, and custom item effects, are also key in maintaining player engagement, keeping the game fresh as each round passes.
Tekken 7 also offers an outstanding story mode which tells a tale that can be enjoyed by long-time Tekken enthusiasts and newcomers, alike. Much like past entries in the Tekken series, this game is quite accessible, so regardless of skill-level, there are plenty of opportunities to take advantage of, in hope of coming out on top with a victory.
I'm a huge fan of Tekken, but don't consider myself an expert. Prior to Tekken 4, I had spent roughly a couple of hours, on average, with each of the first three mainline titles and TTT(1), playing at my friends'. Tekken 4, the one many deem to be their least favorite entry, was my first real experience with the series, and I've been in love with it ever since. Tekken 7 feels ever-so-familiar to the series' best, while creating a brand new experience that boasts a level of immersion I assumed to be unattainable by the genre.
Tekken 7 rights so many of the fighting genre's wrongs that I have a newfound faith and excitement for the future of fighting games. If you're (understandably) cynical about the direction in which fighting games have been heading, then I implore to, someday, give Tekken 7 a chance to change your opinion and open your eyes to just how great fighting games can be, at their very best.

For the best experience, use a controller.
On with the review:
This is one of the simplest, funnest, best games I've ever played. I have more time playing it on my iPad. I tried it on PC, and I didn't like it with keyboard and mouse so I uninstalled. Then I found out in game that there actually is controller support, they just don't say it on the store page. So I re-installed it, and I have to say, it is 10x better with a controller.
I can catch up to my iPad hiscore. I have personal best of 259 Construction Yard on my iPad, I was able to get 89 on PC within my first try of using a controller. By using the keyboard, I was only getting scores of 10. Now I pass that easy with a controller. Guys, if you think this game is too hard, it's even harder with a keyboard. Using a gamepad is how it was meant to be played. When you hold and iPad or iPhone, you hold it like a controller. Using a keyboard is going to be impossible if you're used to the mobile version like I am.
The game is very fast paced, the graphics look nice, the sound effects are awesome. I especially love shooting the shot gun really fast. I just keep jumping and shooting the next guy and the sound effect sounds awesome.
If you are looking for a cheap platformer, this is your best bet. It is free and will provide you with the most fun.
Vlambeer is the best. Keep making great games! I didn't know what Nuclear Throne was until I went to the Vlambeer website. When I heard it was by them, I wanted it.
Also the music is fantastic! It makes the Construction Yard map feel really fast paced, and it makes the Moon Temple map feel a little slower. I think it's awesome how the music can change the way the game feels.
Also, even though there is only 3 maps, each one has their own strengths and weaknesses.
Construction is very open. It's easy to jump and there are only 3 floors. There is space between each floor, you can easily jump over the fire. There are no safe spots though, and there are no holes in the floors so the ghosts have to go around to get to you. Also, the platforms are longer so the monsters take a while to get to the fire, you can kill them before they get in.
On Rocket Silo, there are 4 floors, so everything is tighter, it is harder to jump over the fire because there isn't a lot of room to jump, but there is a safe spot in the middle. There is also a hole above the safe spot so ghosts can easily get to you. So you can't just shoot to the sides, you have to shoot the ghosts too. This makes it harder because they get to you from above. You can't shoot up, so this makes it really easy for the ghosts to kill you.
In Moon Temple, there is a lot of room, and 2 safe spots on the sides, but there are 2 fire pits, some recoil can easily knock you into the fire. Also the platforms are shorter so you have to be really careful with the recoil. Also, the monsters have a short path to get to the fire since the platforms are shorter. This makes them go into the fire a lot faster.
This provides a lot of variety with gameplay. Each map is harder than the last. The game modes also only get harder.
I recommend this game 100%. They put so much thought into such a simple idea, just grab every crate you see.

Love this game. Grew up with Tekken. Been playing the Tekken games since Tekken 2 way back in 1998 when I was child. This is literally one of the only fighting games besides Soul Calibur and some of the DBZ titles that I actually really enjoy. The combat is very fluid compared to the old Tekken games from the late 90's, doesn't feel much different than 5 or 6, just a little faster and/or polished if that makes any sense. They added something called Rage Arts in this game, which I personally feel was a brilliant decision to incorporate in this game because now the game feels more balanced and fair, if you're dying it'll activate and you can use a special move on the opponent to even the odds, where as before.... if you were at the mercy of your opponent and their bullsh*t combos you were pretty much f*cked. With Rage Arts you actually have a fighting chance, this is great for all players, pros and noobs.
Aside from that there doesn't really feel like there's much in this one though compared to Tekken 6 and 5. Just a Gallery mode to view all the Tekken videos from all the Tekken games, an arcade mode that only has 5 battles, Treasure battle mode.... which is like Ghost Battle from the past Tekken games, you beat the computer and win fight money and rank up. The story mode is REALLY well done but it's extremely short I think, and the other characters stories after you're done with the main one is also extremely short.... like 1 or 2 battles and you're done type of short. No team battle, survival, or time attack like the old games.... not sure why they removed those.
The character customization is better, not by much, but it gives enough variety to choose from and edit that it feels like you're own personal character. F*ck the online mode, man.... the combo jugglers on here will drive you insane if you're not on the top of your game, one mistake and you're suddenly suspended in the air and at the mercy of their bullsh*t, and trust me.... it's going to p*ss you off, I promise lol. Even with the Rage Arts, it's still not enough to avoid a brutal az whooping sometimes. This is one of those games you get really, really good at... you're dominating the computer and dominating all your friends, and then you go online and suddenly you realize how much of a failure you are. I'm pretty decent at the game, reached the rank of Mentor in Online ranked matches, but man.... some of these Tekken Veterans on here will straight up stomp you and make you feel worthless, and then it will fill you with endless rage XD.
Other than that, this is really great game, and I have had no issues with the game either, it runs perfectly, no crashes at all and is very smooth. Only complaint I have is with the online mode when trying to connect to another player it's usually always telling me it couldn't connect with the player, and I know it's not my internet because I have the Blast service from Comcast, which is the best net you can get from them, insane speeds and barely any DC's, so the game has an issue there. It's not just me either, it happens to a lot of players it seems. Hopefully it gets fixed because it's annoying a/f.
And hopefully Soul Calibur 6 makes it's way to PC too, I'd love that.

STALKER: Clear Sky is the second installment in the STALKER series, and is a prelude to the events of Shadow of Chernobyl. You play as Scar, a veteran mercenary who got downed in an emission while escorting a group of scientists. You are saved by a faction known as Clear Sky - a group dedicated to researching the nature of the Zone. From there, they set you up to hunt a /certain/ individual, who despite all the dangers, has made it to the center of the Zone, and has allegedly caused great damage in his wake.
Don't expect too much of the story, because it is without a doubt the weakest of all three games. Still, it is a STALKER game, and it made some vast improvements since SoC. The UI is better, and your weapons and armor are now upgradable. There is a better focus on all the factions (almost all of which you can join) with various side-missions. Faction warfare is amusing and satisfying, and can definitly keep you occupied for a few hours.
Just so, the faction warfare system is... kinda broken. It's hard to explain; it seems that, whichever faction you pick, your teammates start getting clunkly and get their asses beat more often. The aiming in this game is also different, and not in a good way. The physics of the bullets improved, but for some reason, every weapon has a bullet spread that makes it really hard to hit enemies properly.
This release also felt more buggy than the other two games, with frequent CTD's if you play on the new DirectX and various graphical and auditory glitches.
I defininitly recommend this game, despite it flaws. See it through to the ending; it is well executed, and my favorite part of the entire game.

I think this game has a lot of good intentions, I think it has a lot of positives, I think the developers had the right idea. But right now (as of the time of this writing) as it is, I feel like it's a not a product ready to be rolled out to the public.
I think it has a great visual style, it brings me right back to old 90s DOS top-down shooters, this is what appealed to me the most. This is the games most redeeming feature at the moment. The game does need a ton of small tweaks and fixes.
There is very bad feedback, visually or aurally, when it comes to the UI. When you click on something in the menu, it doesn't highlight or make any significant sound when you click, it feels very cheap and whipped together this way. If you click on the wrong item, like "New Game" instead of "Continue," you can't go back at all. You're doomed to start over (which I did). You can't adjust the volume, controls, or anything else once you're in the game. You have to exit to the main menu first. In the stats at the end of each level, the words "Bullets" in "Bullets Fired" is spelled wrong ("Bullits"). Overall, the UI needs some serious quality of life adjustments.
The flow of the game is not very intuitive. I was playing the first level, then at the end you can choose to go 1 of 2 ways. I chose way #1, ended up fighting a boss, beat him, then went back to the beginning of level 1 (??). So then I chose way #2, fought a boss, beat him, and went back to the beginning of level 1 (??). At the end of each level, you lose all of your weapons for some reason and go back to just having a pistol which, like all ot her weapons, is very unfun to use. There is no dialogue, no subtitles, no story to speak of, so I don't why I'm doing anything.
In the game itself, the graphics are 90's sylistically, and so is the music. But sound effects are straight from the 70's, as if they were from the Atari 2600. In my opinion, all of the sound effects need to be scrapped. It makes combat extremely unsatisfying. The shotgun, for example, doesn't feel chunky and heavy and it isn't satisfying to fire because it just let's out such a pathetic little sound. This goes for all weaponry, including the enemies'. There is no sound for reloading and very little feedback when you take damage. Your character moves very slowly, but  the movement animation is very fast, it's a little awkward and stange. Some of the bosses and mini-bosses shoot projectiles that just move too quickly, it makes trying to time the rhythm and finding a pattern very clunky and awkward. When you die, there is nothing. One frame you are alive, then when you take the last hit, the very next frame you're at the last checkpoint. And for some reason, often times when you die, you will continue AHEAD of where you died. Again, it feels very cheap and patched together. Enemies don't have a death animation, the just turn into a blood splatter on the ground, again, within the span of 1 frame. It just makes everything feel low quality. Finally, after about 20 minutes of gameplay, I had more than enough money to completely max out all of the upgrades for all 3 characters.
As you can see, the game just needs a lot of small things. I think the devs need to put more time into details (death animations, weapon feedback, sound effects, menu feedback etc), not take shortcuts and put some more focus into quality of life for the user, because right now it's very frustrating to play. Keep up the good work devs, ignore the naysayers, work hard, don't be afraid to fail, trust your vision, I'll be happy to turn this into a positive review when the game gets polished.

Neon Hardcorps is a top-down action game that has, to date of writing, received a positive reception. The game is clearly inspired by the top-down shooters that were at one stage the rage of the gaming industry. Although some time has past since that was well and truly the case I do have a place in my heart for these types of games. Some of them are among my all-time favorites include the Alien Breed franchise on the Atari, The Chaos Engine (Soldier of Fortune) also on Atari and Mega Drive, Commando, Gauntlet, Ikari Warriors and plenty more. That I am instantly reminded of enjoying those titles only served as a positive to Neon Hardcorps.
Now I'm not going to lie to you and tell you that the game is as good as any of those classics or that it measures up to them in any way. Those titles are some of the more treasured titles in gaming history. It would be unfair to expect that from a young developer. However, what I can tell you is that I thoroughly enjoyed the several hours that I spent playing Neon Hardcorps. It was certainly not just a case of playing the game to collect the trading cards that came with it. There are far worse top-down shooters on Steam and yes, there may be some better ones as well. But for an asking price of just $1.99 if you don't get it bundled you're in for a treat.

Daedalic is probably one of the last companies making "traditional" point and click adventures around, as such, prepare for the sort of "logic" and comedy that usually is in titles like these. Deponia encompasses both the faults and the great things about the genre, wrapped around a funny story with some pretty good animation. Rufus, the main character, is very much a Guybrush Threepwood sort of deal. A not very capable person who somehow manages to worm his way out of a bunch of sticky situations with only a.. few.. bruises taken for it. This being the first of a trilogy that was already planned at the time, expect a lot of setup that hints at a deeper lore and character arc in the series beyond what we experience here. If you love point and click adventure, or just a good laugh, I recommend Deponia. Just remember, this is not an action title.

I'm going to break down the order or my observations and feelings of the game as I played it.
A Fallout parody. Cool, if not quite written to my tastes.
Inspired by the Borderlands art style and humor. Awesome, love Borderlands.
A roguelike seeming  dungeon crawler RPG. Not quite my cup of tea, but the RPG elements keep me interested.
Time limits for each "dungeon" floor where a near-invincible death machine hunts you down. Nope. Done. I'm out. Not for me.
I take forever in the Fallout and Borderlands games because I explore EVERYTHING, and you can't do that in this game. Maybe it's because I'm not used to the genre, but this isn't something I can accept.
One of the floors I found had a split left and right in the first room. I went right and came to a dead end. As I turned around to come back to the left side, I ran straight into the death machine, who then used their weapon to pin me to a wall and murder me.
Not fun.
I know you'd usually be able to escape in some way, but it really hurt my opinion of it.
Is it a bad game? No, I don't think so.
Is it a game for me? No, it's not. But that doesn't mean it won't be great for you.
Just keep in mind if you see the other reviews here and see Fallout and Borderlands mentioned, it's inspired by them in very loose ways. Don't come to this looking for a cheap indie version of them.

Hectic roguelike shooter with buckets of style and maybe a bit too much grind.
Check out my full impressions here:

Spends too long in intro putting emphasis on making your character (which is always randomized after you die anyway, which you inevitably will), on stealth mechanics (which the game then throws out the window because they're pretty much useless because enemies will either hear the door open or spot you for no dicernable reason) and on the idea of finding gear and looting (which the game then punishes you for doing on a floor by spawning a ludicrously strong enemy)
A better introduction to the world might have made this a positive but it hit all the wrong notes and I amn't coming back.
Edit: Seeing as the developer took the time to reply to my review, I figured it was fair to give them more time and gave it another run. Didn't bother with character customization, began the dungeon again. Had a better time with stealth, but I still feel that stealth, which involves being patient and careful and considerate of your surroundings is very heavily at odds with a secret timer that releases an impossibly powerful enemy that will see you through stealth. This also didn't matter too much anyway as well beause twice the game spawned enemies that were looking towards the only entrance (once was a door and the other was down a long hallway. The "better" pistol I had was woefully inaccurate and weak still even against the early enemies and melee weapon seems to only hit if the square reticle is on the target, which can be frustrating with the tiny speedy dogs.
I managed to find a mystery flask (which I think is supposed to be the main goal of a dungeon and had been under the impression they gave you only benefits for continuing) and ended up getting Blind Sight. So that reticle I mentioned for combat? Gone. My reward for slogging it out was future dungeons would be harder for this character instead.
I quit at that point and uninstalled for a second time and final time and I stand by my thumbs down.

if this doesnt sound appealing to you, then i don't recommend this game. this game is definitely not for everyone. but if this does interest you, get it. at 15$, the cost vs. replay value is insanely worth it.

An incredible let down.  Just replay Stick of Truth if you need to scratch the itch.  I cannot recommend this title to anyone.
The story arc is almost pointless since you know the major villians almost immediately.  The combat is well done but at the same time incredibly tedious.  Normal difficulty is a joke, I think I died maybe 3-4 times due to some fights changing up the mechanics.
The writing just isn't South Park at all.  It will sound funny to say but I was never uncomfortable with what was going on: it was so incredibly tame for a South Park title.  It was like the writers didn't want to offend anyone and so played it safe with 90% of the plot which also made the times they did cross the line come across as actually offensive since they were just trying to be offensive and not trying to challenge the player's preconceptions.  One of the best parts of Stick of Truth was how some things would just blow your mind even for South Park.  This has none of that.
There is maybe one moral choice in the entire game and its pointless, since the story does nothing to set it up or make it a hard choice, it simply comes down to which ever choice is easier to finish in game.  It's also immediately retconned.
I spent slightly more time in this game than Stick of Truth and yet Stick of Truth has so many memorable moments and Fractured but Whole has none.  This story could have been done in a 30 min episode.
Bringing in a lot of the ancillary cast feels stapled on.  Part of the final act feels incredibly hamfisted just to bring certain characters in for a cameo.  I really got the feeling that the plot was missing parts that probably were abandoned due to time or broken out to sell as later DLC.
The combat system is interesting, but not enough to keep the whole game interesting, in fact some of it feels like they would just stick combat in to lengthen the game.  Multi-classing is almost pointless since you can only have 4 powers active.  The combat dialogue is funny, until you work your way through the 3-4 lines each character has.
TL:DR
Just replay Stick of Truth.  Fracture But Whole is like some kind of alien observer trying to recreate South Park and nailing the look but totally missing the point.

Another game with a tonne of unrealized potential
Pros:
-space for strategy, too many shooters nowadays put you into a tight map with only tight corridors and rooms and small areas to shoot up and down. This game has some decent urban areas mixed in with maps that have large open fields. Would like it if there was more cover between spawns and destinations (points of capture/defence)
-Accessibility. It is free to play and you can earn anything by simply playing, without paying. But there is the option to pay too if you don't have the patience or time to play to unlock what you want.

-paratroopers are fun novelty class type, you actually spawn in a plane and jump out where you want on the battlefield. Very Cool. But too often it gets shot down while you are trying to spawn by enemy fighters, so when that happens it is annoying.
-Some very cool looking tanks, gear and weaponry from the world wars.
-Picking up dead soldier’s weapons on the field, always welcome. So as a new player starting with the basic rifle it is nice to pick up someone’s weapon with mods and use it without paying any repairs or maintenance on it after the match.
-Epic Hero moments, from blowing up a tank with anti-tank grenades or tank mines to running amok as a Rambo in a defensive or offensive control point, or just tearing into an enemy force as a tank crewman, you can have some pretty epic moments in this game, and that is a big fun factor for me.
-You choose to play as Americans, Germans or Russians and eventually you can play as any that you choose. But initially I had to play only as one, until I could save up credits to buy a new soldier of another country. But in the last update you can get one free infantry on all.
Cons:
-Squad system, you can be a Major in Rank and end up in a squad with a private as your squad leader, which means you cannot use the auxiliaries you worked so hard to unlock. This is really bad design, and every soldier should simply have access to their own aux. or the highest rank should be squad leaders. If you leave the squad, you still don't get access to your aux. Very frustrating.
-The recent update ruined a number of things for me... 1) Frames have dropped to the point that the gameplay is affected. And I had over 150 FPS prior to last update 2) Badge text is too small now and you cannot click on the related ribbon for equipped badges. 3) Weapon Balance, some of the upgrades on mods impact the guns too much, and other starting standard weapons are at huge disadvantage, they should balance weapons much better.
-Some maps the spawn areas are poorly thought out, spawn camping is too easy and hard for the spawners to get out of it. And you will be flanking and then suddenly you are in their spawn and likewise you might be defending a point and then suddenly you’re in their spawn, which is ridiculous again. At least the Skirmish maps don't suffer from this, but the larger assault maps need more work. The recent touch ups were nice in some spots, but more signifiant work needs to be done with spawn camping issues.
-Excessive Repair Bills. This isn't a bad thing until you buy and use some gear that actually results in you losing credits after a match rather than making credits. Don't mind making less credits for using some gear, but losing credits for using things seems a little exaggerated. It feels like they haven't thought out how to limit spam of some things, so they just make the repair extremely expensive to use. They should have a ceiling on things, so that you can never lose money after a match. So at least it would be capped, so you break even at worst case scenario.
-Planes in Assault maps, there is basically not enough effective ground anti air, so planes will end up with ridiculous scores, while you as an infantryman may have capped and killed more and died less, but their score can be 10,000 and yours 1000. Even if you destroyed more armour it makes no difference, and all because they spent the entire match shooting down para planes and empty jeeps. Planes need balancing into the game, they are too powerful and spawn camping in the sky is as prevalent as anywhere else.
-Matches with 20 snipers per side, this is just ridiculous. Goes for any class, sometimes you get into a match and it is all pilots or tanks. Again, they need to implement a balance into the match, similar to how Americas Army had a limit for snipers per team. Same has to happen for planes too. And matches shouldn’t start where only units are 5 planes vs 5 planes, or 5 tanks vs 2 snipers. Stuff like this happens all the time. It would be ok if after waiting in a queue they actually matched up a balanced team vs a balanced team. But that doesn’t seem to happen. So this just makes waiting for a match more frustrating at times.
- Queues. This is the worst game for queues. You might see online that there are over a hundred battles going at any one time with 6000+ people online, yet you will have to wait ridiculous amounts of time to just join a match. Then you have to wait more for the match to start. And if your team has more players because the other team rage quit, you have to wait in another queue to spawn. This completely ruins the gaming experience. Even joining a friends battle where the team I’m joining has 5 players less, I have waited 10 mins to join that battle, there is simply no decent reason for this to be happening. And it literally makes you so mad that you want to leave the game and never return.
- War queues. This is beyond bizarre. But once you unlock the War RTS side of the game, you will regularly wait days for your assault teams to get supplied to join the war. Only to then have the war end when you can finally enter, so you miss out. Not only that, but if you want to play in the war with your resources or simply to get more war funds, the queues to join a war battle are even longer. We are talking 30mins, to an hour waiting. So you end up playing staged battles instead. Hate games that make it difficult for you to just get into the game and play its content.
-Boosters and Veteran benefits are on a timer, and the timer does not care if you are in game or not it runs out no matter what, you can’t pause it. This is really dumb.
-Hourly salary isn’t actually hourly salary, I have tested it in game. Played 30mins and my salary should have been approx. 7000 for that time. I got 1200. So the salary system is bogus and only works and benefits you if you play well or perform tasks unknown to you since the game doesn’t explain what constitutes salary earning time.
-As a veteran player who paid for the infantry soldiers of other countries, felt that should have had that refunded since they recently gave new players a free infantry for each. But the developers change things like that without thought to the existing player base.
-unbalanced gear for different countries. For example, for the Semi-Automatic starting rifle that everyone gets at the start, the Americans only get a 2.2 t-scope, while the Germans get a 4.0 scope unlock. This is completely unfair. Just like the Russians have an anti-vehicle weapon and others don’t. Many things like this have to be balanced out better. The tanks destroyers for example are weaker than the medium tanks and aren’t tank destroyers at all.
-Skirmish Matches end too fast after long queues. More time spent waiting than playing. So wrong.
-Developers ninja dropped the salary and increased costs. Added to the over nerfing of weapons, it really shows these people don't know how to balance their game.
Summary:
Could be a great game, but it is barely recommendable, even though it can be fun at times. Many issues need fixing. Only reason feel obliged to recommend it, is because i do play it a lot, but I wouldn't rave about it. It's one of those games you play and hate yourself and the game. But keep coming back to it. The grind is real.

I got this game as part of a bundle and went in, knowing absolutely nothing about it. Upon seeing as I loaded the game that it said it was a roguelike, I cringed and quickly lost hope, because it's not a genre I like many games from (which is my own, personal problem, of course). However, after the charming intro and seeing the fun character models, not to mention the unexpected first person perspective and loot, I quickly set aside most of my fears, and was enamored by the comedy and crazy setting of this game. Seeing that there were stealth mechanics, I was thinking to myself "Wow, I might actually really like this game!" Then came the "S.O.B." There is an enemy in the game which will hunt you after you've been in a level for a short while, and as far as I can tell, no matter how much stealth-boosting gear I'm wearing that's available thus far, he can instantly detect me while I'm stealthing, and from any distance. He has 600 HP, my attacks do 1 HP to him, and he fires a minigun that will literally stun-lock you in place until you're dead or almost dead. I can't think of a time I had such a shocking good time and bad time with a game before until this. Of course, being a roguelike, once this guy kills you, you start over from the beginning with zero progress if you haven't finished the level.
I am confused as to why stealth was even designed when the enemies kind of glance around, seemingly at random, meaning it may take a moment to get into position to pull off a stealth kill. I say this is confusing because with all the time needed to sneak well, it leaves you open to a hard sodomizing from the S.O.B. since its appearance is based on how long you take in a level. The shooting and smashing without stealth were just so-so, whereas doing these while in stealth was so much more rewarding and built up more tension for me before going into a room, peeking through windows to take out the baddies inside while taking minimal damage and being careful, since one death is game over. Instead of rewarding taking it slow rather than running in Rambo-style, the way Deus Ex Human Revolution deliciously handles action vs. stealth, WASTED dangles stealth in front of you, letting you taste its sweetness, before turning the metaphorical bottle around to show you that what you just tasted was poison, because the game's philosophy through the use of the S.O.B. comes off as "Yes, we have stealth, but screw you if you want to try and enjoy it."
I'm sure there are people who love to let everyone know how good they are at games, and those who claim to be terrible at games while giving themselves backhanded compliments to feed their own egos will remind us all how they've beaten every level in stealth and had tons of time left over. However, I'm not those people. Those people can praise this game, that's their right, and it's fine for them to be that way, but I am not good at games. I play them all the time and like to see what's out there, hoping to find something to entertain me from a gameplay or story perspective (hopefully both), but this game thrashed me each time I tried to finish the first level, despite trying to rapidly move through it in stealth on my second attempt and still getting demolished by the S.O.B. despite giving up a little ways in and going guns blazing, just trying to keep ahead of the game-ending S.O.B., but still no dice. I mean this is the first level, so how am I supposed to feel encouraged to continue?
In summary, I really liked the humor, the look, the zany plot and setting, the first person perspective and early game weapon variety, the loot, and the stealth. However, the enemy known as the S.O.B. completely ruined my experience by nullifying the stealth aspect of the game, which was my favorite part to begin with. If just dying all the time makes you happy, or beating something difficult to brag about it to people who care that you beat the game, then this is probably a game you really ought to play. However, if you love the slow pace of the stealth afforded by games like Deus Ex Human Revolution, and the other things I mentioned don't sound like what you like in a game, then avoid this game. I think it has a lot of good qualities, but the experience the S.O.B. gives me is an immediate no-go for me having any chance of enjoying or completing this game. My hat's off to the developer for a lot of stuff I liked in this game, though, which I mentioned earlier.

I wish Steam would give you the opportunity to give star ratings. This game wasn't bad. But I decided to not recommend it because it's not what I expected it to be.
There is a great deal of  third-person, tactical shooter, stealth video games out there but when watching the ads I thought "Hey this game looks intelligent enough, maybe it's what I'm looking for". I should have read the description on the back of the cover, which puts it pretty bluntly:
"Stalk the shadows or go loud".
Yup, that's pretty much this "stealth" video game in a nutshell. It doesn't matter how you play it. Wanna sneak around headshotting people with a video-game-level-silenced Welrod and choking people? Or do you just wanna run around shooting people? It's your choice, and it doesn't make a difference.
Video game developers are putting so much focus on cheesy gameplay mechanics (in this game, you can choose to time your shot to coincide with the sputtering noise from a misfiring electricity generator to "mask" the gunshot.. oh my goodness), cheesy one-dimensional hero characters (and trust me, the hero doesn't get anymore boring than Sniper Elite) instead of focussing on what should be at the very core of development of this type of video game: the AI!
The bumbling nazi soldiers in this game are an embarassment to history. It is literally the same stupid AI that you got in 1998 with Metal Gear Solid. Granted, the AI was epochal for that time with MGS, but people this is almost 20 years later and soldiers are still getting back to standing around staring into a random direction 60 seconds after being fired upon from a distance of very few meters (though in this game, all you need to do is "relocate" a few dozen yards away from your initial position without being seen).
The thing is, you don't even have to relocate or wait. You can just take apart an entire nazi base from a good vantage position as long as you make sure all enemy snipers are dealt with first. The enemy snipers are literally the only threat in this game, save for maybe tanks (that can easily be stopped with the massive amount of explosives lying around waiting to be found). You can pick off enemy stormtroopers like you're at a fun shooting range. A very fun WW2 shooter set in africa. Great mechanics give it a fun mix of stealth with sniper mechanics loosely based on the real world such as bullet drop and using other loud noises like thunder or artillery fire to mask your shots. The game also uses a variety of other weapons such as various sidearms, machine pistols (the MP40 for example) and several grenades and traps that can be used. It also uses a cover system and allows you to distract enemies by throwing objects and both sound and vision (line of sight and light levels) are important.
It's a surprisingly in-depth game with a decent amount of levels and a fair amount of replayability with several difficulties and a number of collectibles in each level. If you're a fan of any stealth or sniper gameplay, you'll probably enjoy this game a lot.

Unpopular opinion: I liked Dead Rising 2 a bit more than I liked Dead Rising, and this game is basically Dead Rising 2 with more stuff. This is the last good Dead Rising game.

Dead Rising 3 was the first Dead Rising game I played, followed by Dead Rising 4. Both of those games are better than this one.
Let's start with the gameplay mechanics. Yes, Dead Rising 2 and Dead Rising 1 have more in-depth mechanics, like you can cook food, and there's a timer, and etc. But most of these are terrible. Like cooking food -- in practice means pressing several buttons when you need to restore health, as opposed to cooking one. I think Dead Rising 3 struck the best balance between intricacy and accessibility. Dead Rising 4, I agree, dumbed down some mechanics too much. For example, you can no longer throw melee weapons or pick up most objects and use them as weapons. All of that is present in this game. But it's just so clumsy and unsatisfying compared to the latter games. Making things worse is the fact that you can't run in Dead Rising 2, and the basic movement speed, even with all upgrades, is painfully slow. Basically, I stopped playing as a result.
Other problems in this game: no minimap, no mission markers, no skill tree (instead you gain attribute increases automatically as you gain levels).
The graphics are definitely dated, barely playable by modern standards.
I did enjoy taking pictures with the camera. Quite a few sexy moments, however due to the outdated visuals they're not that stimulating
Story and character -- Dead Rising 3 had better characters. Dead Rising 4's Frank West is far more likeable for me than the "original" Frank West. The change in voice actor was a great move. I'm more convinced than ever that the only reason people didn't like the new Frank West is because of fanboy disease. The original Frank West sounds whiny, looks like an overweight 80's rockstar, and is generally extremely irritating due in no small part to his incredibly slow movement speed and lack of agility compared to the later protagonists.
Now I ain't gonna lie -- this game has some hilarious moments and I'm not in too far yet, but if all I want is just the story I can watch Youtube videos. The gameplay itself is just too outdated compared to the later games. Can't recommend unless you're a hardcore Dead Rising fan and want to collect all the games or something.

I'm glad that I buyed and tried Zombie Shooter. 1. The game has LAN: why is this great? Because it means the game will never go microtransactions pay to play like Creativerse (and now many other early access games similiar to this). LAN is a big feature and they would have to remove it entirely to go that route. A very good safety insurance.
2. Better graphics: as you will see mentioned A LOT, the graphics and art in this are by far the greatest I have seen in any of these new vox games
3. Complete trees: about time someone added complete trees/bushes so that you don't end up with floating trees that don't have any more trunks because you removed the trunk for wood. The only problem is the lack of any LARGE trees.
4. Lock on combat with ranged weapons and classes: this is by far the greatest combat system in any vox game around. However, I have not noticed a "sprint" option with stamina, this needs to happen...
5. Unique character creation: really tired of playing as some lame kid or whatever, this is also the greatest character creation I have seen in any vox game. However, it does/is slightly "childish" and could use a tad more "grown up" spin/option.
6. Bosses: most vox games don't even have a single boss. Terraria should be what we strive for. Portal Knights has a great start.
7.  Unique monsters: this one actually suprised me, some of the enemies moves and such I was very pleased, could get better but even in current state it crushes games like Creativerse.
8. The UI is large!: seriously, thank you! Playing on my 52 inch TV and some games the UI and words are unreadable! The UI is great in this game, albeit very lacking (even more so than games like Creativerse) in content- ie. very few things to build.
9. RPG elements: a reason to kill things and get better! Awesome! However I haven't played long and have already leveled up to 5-10 ish out of I think 30. Currently in place but once again, seem to be designed for a child? Wish that it would "evolve" into something a tad bit more serious, or at least "middle of the road".
10. Kids friendly: now this is my #10 for pro as well as con, take it or leave it the game currently is a LOT easier than other vox based games and seems to be designed in a way that an eight year old could play...
1. Terrible item management: inventories are brutally small with the first chest you can make needing cooper to make which isn't even found on your starting island. Once you build some chests you find that item stacking is ridiculously small (in games like this items need to stack to 250/500/1000, not 20) and there is not "auto sort" or "linked storage". These are all huge fails.
2. Small Islands: you can't dig, you will fall and die. You can't explore, you will fall off the edge and die. Worlds are the smallest I have seen in any vox game, and with only island exploration (a huge part of vox based games) you are punished for exploring. In a game that should foster exploration and immagination this is a huge fail.
3. Building is difficult: seriously, it is way too difficult to place blocks! I don't think I have played ANY vox based game where it has been this difficult to build! Hard to build, easy to fall off ledges, small inventories and stacks, the list goes on. The building in this game really takes a back stage in this game.
4. Worlds are dead: no water, no rain, no weather, creatures seems to have "spawn points" where they spawn in the same spots everynight/day and just "run around in circles", skies are  empty with no huge purple moon at night or a blazing sun during the day. The world (islands) seem very much dead.
5. Terrible loot/repair monster: with Zelda and Terraria being two of the games they wanted this to be like, the loot/gear is terrible. Pick Terraria, Minecraft OR Zelda, the loor and gear set up is better. Personally I would rather have a Dungeon Defender (the first) gear set up. They opted to go with the "durability monster" in this game and let me tell you, it is a monster! You will shoot off a few arrows and RED ITEM DURABILITY! Zelda/Terraria didn't have this feature, it is frankly a stupid feature and should just "go away".
6. No tower defense or threats: Terraria/Minecraft etc, when you start you feel a real panic, a sense of "I have to build some shelter!" because things were coming after you. Now some games like Terraria MASTER this in having waves of enemies hit you, having zombies all of the sudden be able to open doors, ect, while other like Minecraft at least get your feet wet before you basically just ignore it once you get something going- Portal Knights has nothing. There is no reason to build other than "you feel like it". Now this is fine and some people will defend this but that doesn't make it "great" either, in fact it does the opposite.
7. No real reason to progress: I have no idea why I am here or why I need to go from island to island. There are no enemies coming after me, why bother? There is no storyline to bring me there, so why bother? If the claim is "meh, just do what you want to!" well then the question back should be "well then why would I do it in Portal Knights when ____ does it better and/or has more?". In open world games like Skyrim if you "wander around" you still feel rewarded for doing so, with quests, loot, exploration and awe while here you feel punished for exploring as the game funnels you and pushes you to go from island to island to island so fast that you basically just ignore 85% of a VERY small island.
8. Lacking features: no PVP, no controller support, no key remapping, etc. There seems to be a lot of little features that seem to come "standard" in other games that are just not here.
9. Toxic community: seriously, this is an issue in 100% of the sandbox/vox based communities- it might be because most of the community is/are 12 year olds who shouldn't even be allowed to comment in the forums but it is always there. This is a huge problem for any early access, because if people don't feel like they can go into the forums and give their advice without being trolled/attacked/flamed/harassed then what is the point in taking part in the early access experience? Dev's need to start clamping down on explosive fan boi's, but they don't, if you are unlucky you'll get dev's coming in and patting the crazies on the back! Currently haven't seen that in PK, but I also have seen a lot of people attacked for suggesting ANYTHING and silence from the dev's. Dev's need to be a LOT more active in their forums for an early access title!
10. Too kid friendly: now this is my #10 for pro as well as con, take it or leave it the game currently is a LOT easier than other vox based games and seems to be designed in a way that an eight year old could play...
BOTTOM LINE: It is still in early access so many of the con's can be changed and impoved on so I give it a rcommend; if the game was not in early access it would be a different story.

A fun game and good potential yet it does still require improvement in my opinion. Some of which I read an announcement on.
Some pro's:
- Looks good for a voxel based game
- is not too complicated to learn (for me at least)
- building with the ctrl key makes life so much easier
- the map is good for porting to other worlds and that works well
Some personal cons up till v0.4.1:
- small islands (is mentioned to be worked on in version v0.5.0)
- relatively linear path through the game, would like to see the option to discover other parts aside those given on the semi forced path to take via the portals. So to say a little more open-world based would be great.
- UI could use some tooltips on items/statts and downscaling in size, it takes up the whole screen when opening a bag for example. Also which would be really helpful is the option to see both one's back-pack and a chest at the same time to get a little more overview.
- the lack of being able to split a stack can be a pain in multiplayer. Also an option to be able to trade with fellow multiplayers would be a lot easier then the current option of putting it in chests in order to give them to others.
- staying with multiplayer, so-far I have only played via LAN on which it works really good so-far, however I would like it more if I had the option to go through a portal without forcing my fellow multiplayers to that same world once I do.
It is still early access as I write this review so there is logically still room for improvement. But as the game stands currently I do enjoy it and thus can recommend it for those willing to play early access games.

"Nvidia has confirmed there is an issue with their more recent drivers that may be behind crashes some players have been reporting recently.They are working on a fix and we will try to keep you updated with any developments. For anyone with an Nvidia card experiencing crashes, for now please try rolling back your drivers to at least 376.33. Obviously this is not ideal, and is not intended as a permanent solution."
The roll back was indeed the fix I need to get this game running properly. No more CTDs:) However, I still can't recommend this game. While it is really fun, it is plagued by this CTD problem. A pretty fun and interesting take on a dungeon crawler. I haven't played too many Adult Swim games, but the few that I have played (Westerado:Double Barreled, Duck Game) & even the moblie game Robot Unicorn Attack 2 are all pretty well made games. But staying more specifically to WASTED, the idea of the game is you go through various dungeons looking for different "Boozes" that will give you "Hangovers". These hangovers when combined with other boozes throughout the game will make your charcter overall stronger. But this game does also have a Rouge-like element. Meaning, when you die, you lose your hangovers and buzzes. However, you can stash items throughout your adventures allowing you to start off with items when your charcter dies. However, I did feel that this game can feel a bit repetitive despite the fact the dungeons being randomly generated. It has a pretty good RPG element to it, which is something needed in Dungeon Crawlers. Also, like with most Adult Swim games, the soundtrack is catchy well made and goes along with the overall theme of the game pretty nicely. Also goes without saying, the comedy in the game is pretty on point, it's an Adult Swim game after all.
TL;DR: My overall oppinion of WASTED, is that it is a well construced Rouge-like Dungeon Crawler that will provide you with some well written laughs and gameplay that can keep you enthralled for hours to come, albeit slightly repetitive. However, if you like being presented with a challenge, and goin pew-pew, this game is for you. 4/5

Clear Sky has the weakest mod community and the worst SDK, which results in random crashes every 10 minutes if you dare to install even the simplest of mods. "SRP" mod fixes most of the bugs and CTDs but if you try and merge it with "Arsenal Overhaul" or graphical mods, the game will continue to crash for no reason every few minutes. Overall the weakest game in the series.
Clear Sky is basically a benchmark. They wanted to test new volumetric lighting, volumentric smoke and tesselation. They also tried to create "Faction Wars" were the A.I factions would battle over specific areas.
Result: Clear Sky is visually superior to the other two S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games (Including Call of Pripyat) though not by much. The fact that the game has no HQ graphical mods makes it actually worse compared to the others. Shadow of Chernobyl has texture mods up to 2K and various shaders. Call of Pripyat has whole new engine overhauls and character models - while also running much better compared to Clear Sky.
As for the "Faction Wars" - they result in Call of Duty gameplay. Your faction will repeatedly beg for assistance and enemy A.I keeps spawnning in endless waves. S.T.A.L.K.E.R. games are meant to have rare firefights with small groups of people which can be deadly. In Clear Sky however, there are firefights bloody everywhere and the A.I has been downgraded to make it easier for the player.
Conclusion: Stay away from Clear Sky and go get Call of Pripyat. Install "Call of Chernobyl" mod and you have all the maps from the 3 games into 1 world with HQ textures, grass, animations, weapon models, mutants and weather effects.

Zombie Shooter feels a lot like an improved version of Alien Shooter. They're very similar games, with the same premise: run and shoot all zombies in sight. Same graphics, same controls, everything, with the main difference being that the enemies are zombies instead of aliens - which is perfectly good so far since that worked really well with Alien Shooter. And while Alien Shooter was already quite fun, Zombie Shooter brings some important improvements.
The first is that there are more upgrades to buy and there's a leveling system that makes a huge difference.
The second is that the game's difficulty is WAY more balanced - it's a lot more playable and a lot less frustrating, while still maintaining at least some challenge.
The third is that there's a lot more variety of scenarios, instead of always that same "inside a bunker" look that Alien Shooter had through all levels.
Yet, I still need to mention the camera angles since it's one problem that all games from Alien Shooter and Zombie Shooter seems to have and was never fixed... It's really bothersome because there are enemies and items that will often show up behind walls, making the player unable to see them. This could easily be fixed with a non-fixed camera angle or transparency effect.
Highly recommended for anyone who just wants a game to run'n'gun.

-Sometimes the game will bug out and not give the next player their turn and the game gets stuck in a loop of inactivity.
-This is super rare, but if the enemy can summon others to help him, your character might end up with people sorrunding him, and with someone sharing the same tile as you, which makes it impossible to attack or end your turn.
These issues will very likely be resolved in a patch, and while they can make battles a little annoying, they are uncommon issues and don't take away from the game.
The only other concern I have is that the game teases you with Canada, yet you can't access it. This will probably part of the DLC content, and we will therefore have to wait for it.
TL:DR: The game is fun and hilarious. It has some bugs, but it is playable.

I heard about this game a long time ago from TotalBiscut, and recalled him mentioning that the game was amazing. What struck me as very curious though was how he mentioned that the game just plain wouldn't work with a keyboard+mouse and that he didn't mean it in a bad way. He said that it just plain "wouldn't work" with what the game was trying to do.
Fast forward to several months later, and now I've beaten the game for myself. I also bought a controller specifically to see what TotalBiscut meant. I have witnessed...he was right. This game just
work the same without a controller.
Is the game perfect? I'd love to say yes, but I can't. I just isn't.
With that said though...does it live up to the hype? Yes, yes, yes, and yes again. The game is a masterful triumph despite a few shortcomings.
One of the games strongest suits which I would liken it to would be to its sense of adventuring. The feeling that I got from the game almost constantly was very similar to the sense of emotional wonder I got from several animated movies when I was a kid.
The game takes you on an adventure literally which in turn also translates into a emotional adventure. There are all sorts of feelings which you get from this game. Sadness. Happiness. Joy. Anger. Exhilaration. Triumph. Anger. Helplessness...the list goes on.
A beatiful world with amazing variety, and aethestic coupled with a great soundtrack only serves to strengthen this aspect.
The point is that even though the two main characters have a duty assigned to them, they can still showcase the road to complete that duty to be filled with awe, and emotional wonder...which also feeds into the player.
As the title of the video game implies, the two main characters of this game are two brothers: One older, and one younger. The game is played in the format of a "single player co-op game" in which the player controls both brothers, and uses them to progress through the game.
I felt another strong part of the game was how they showcased the two brother's different personalities through various actions they took, and how they each interacted with the same things. The older brother took things more seriously, and went straight to the main point while the younger brother is more innocent, and playful.
It even shines through in the gameplay. The two brothers have their own strengths which they can employ to solves the various puzzles you will encounter in the world. For example where the big brother is strong and lifts huge things, the little brother is small and can get into small places.
Characterization was done wonderfully for these two characters.
The story is a fairly simple one, but has a strong sense of agency in that you will ALWAYS know what you need to do. This does wonders for the pacing of the game, and is very important for a narrative driven game such as this one.
Something I did dislike though was how the story sometimes likes throwing plot points, happenings, or characters a bit too randomly out at times. Particularly with one very important happening in the end I felt that while it was hardfelt it came a bit too much out of the blue for it to really have its full effect. If the same thing happened but with proper set-up throughout the entire story leading up to it...then it wouldn't feel as much out of nowhere, and would be much more effective.
Another thing I didn't like about the game were its slightly repetitive boss fights. If it was another game I would've forgiven this instantly, but in a game which thrives on evolving on the go, and constantly showcasing its narrative through gameplay...having to do the same thing four times to beat a boss just feels out of place.
This is it...this is the very main reason that this game is worth all the hype despite other imperfections:
Speaking in general for the entire game a lot of it manages to showcase its narrative through keen observation of the player, and actually taking the actions you feel makes sense. You really do feel like two brothers that are working together for their goals
HOWEVER the greatest thing that this game does I would have to say is in its ending act. The ending is the absolute most brilliant thing I have seen in gaming so far. It is likely the best example I have seen so far to so beautifully tell your narrative through the mechnics of the game.
And the player will realize it when it happens. When it happens he WILL know what it is like to be put in the character's shoes...all through the use of the mechanics of the game. That only makes it impossibly more hard-hitting.
I won't even put what I'm talking in spoiler tags since if you haven't experienced this then you deserve to expeirence the proud moment of gaming for yourself.
act is the reason why the game could never work on a keyboard+mouse, and never will since it goes against the whole philosophy of the game's creative design.
It was only a shame I think that they didn't really push this immerive moment of story-telling further since the ending is filled with cutscenes. I fell they really missed an opprotunity turn all these cutscenes into gameplay sections to further empower the feeling of these scenes.
So those are basically my entire thoughts on the game. If I was to rate this game traditionally I would probably give it an 8.5-9.0 out of 10 for the couple slip-ups I mentioned in my review above.
However I cannot emphasize enough just how much of an experience this is, and as a fellow gamer to other gamers I say that you all owe it to yourselves to see this marvelous showing.
It really is immensely thought-provoking in that it shows just what games are capable of doing, and the possibilities of doing even more if we fully evolve the medium.
Brothers: A Tale of Two Sons is a symbol of that evolution.
