$20 for this ?  Fortunately I got the game for only $2 on sale, but I can't help imagining how disappointed I would have been if I had paid full price for it.  10 hours is no small amount of game time but the plot barely advances at all over the course of the game.  Half of my time playing was spent making a cup of espresso, and the rest of the game just rushes by without anything actually happening.  The game ended right when I thought it was getting started.  None of the questions that were introduced in the exposition of the game were resolved at the end, and instead it only made the story even more ambiguous without any closure.  This game is completely useless without owning the sequels, which only seems like a way of cheaply breaking up the story for more money, when this one is being sold at twice the price that it should be.
This game showed a lot of promise at the start.  It's set in a unique and interesting world that I had no problem getting into (in no small part due to the phenomenal art direction), the protagonist is a relatably uncharismatic outcast who became increasingly likable as his surroundings (namely his disdainful and unsympathetic neighbors) became more developed, the hero's actions and motives are clear and understandable despite his overt rudeness and dim-witted sense of grandiosity, it has an engaging sense of humor, and the good soundtrack and voice acting only added to the charm of the game.  With so much done right, it's incredible that anything could go wrong.
Unfortunately the plot just becomes a mess once the final area is reached and the last chunk of story is delivered all at once just before it's abruptly ended.  The last area consists of a frustrating back and forth that ultimately brings the protagonist right back to the start just when it felt like the game was finally getting somewhere, that is Elysium, the place that the player and the character have both been trying to reach the whole time.  It gets so close to reaching this goal that it felt like the real plot was artificially snatched away at the last second simply so that a sequel could be made.
My suggestion is that you should play this game if it looks appealing, but be prepared to get forced into a whole series and definitely do not buy it at full price.  I personally enjoyed Deponia and will probably be buying the game's sequels myself if they go on sale sometime, but I can't recommend playing it at the current price of $20.

It’s not as good as Shadow of Chornobyl, this game feels very experimental. It feels like the developers had a lot of small new ideas and tweaks to the gameplay they wanted to add to the second installment of the franchise and these changes overall made the game less enjoyable than the first game. It’s also buggier and less polished than the original, they probably didn’t have enough time to iron out the issues the game had. The final boss of the game is very buggy because the boss can easily fall through the floor if you load after you die or he could be invincible while floating in the air etc. I actually managed to make him glitch out to my benefit at the start of the fight by quick saving and quick loading while he is climbing down a ladder, when I quick loaded it made him climb back up the ladder to reset the animation of him going down the ladder which allowed me to easily beat him.  The story is very simple compared to the first game, it mostly consists of you tracking down the protagonist of the first game to kill him before he reaches the center of the zone and you can predict exactly what will happen very early on because this is a prequel story and takes place 1 year before Shadow of Chernobyl. It was cool to see how different the world was in that one year gap and knowing how things will change in the future. Clear Sky is much more difficult than the first game on master difficulty, it feels like they heavily increased the enemy’s accuracy on master and there is just a lot of inconsistency in the firefights themselves. It becomes absurd at some points like when I barely even peeked out of cover and I got killed in one hit when I was full hp. A lot of things like that happen pretty often which forces you to quick save very frequently. The developers also had the brilliant idea of letting the enemy throw grenades that land perfectly next to your feet every time they do throw them. All these things combined make the gunplay of Clear Sky much more frustrating and less fun and immersive than Shadow of Chornobyl because those issues constantly bring you out of the game. The great atmosphere is still there and visiting the new locations they added was cool. It’s still a good game it’s just not great like the first game was.

DLC:

Please Note:  This review is based on MY play time and does not take into consideration any changes that may have occured after I refunded the game in June, 2016.
---------------------------------------------------------------
I wanted to like Portal Knights, I really did.  I went in with a positive attitude that I was going to have an enjoyable time with this game that seemed to bring aspects of Minecraft into an RPG setting.  I thought to myself, "Finally!"
When I first got into the game and was met with the character creation I was overjoyed.  There were many options to choose from.  It worked a lot like the avatar creator on XBox Live, so you could actually make an avatar that suits you.  Then I selected my class, which was warrior, and entered the world.
Starting out, I was met with what I could only guess to be the tutorial.  It was a series of “quests” that brought me general knowledge of how to do things.  It didn’t cover everything, mind you, but it did a fairly good job getting the ball rolling.  The “tutorial” area was pretty small, basically just a little floating island with nothing more than a backdrop to show "distance".  I forgave the game for that, because after all this is just the tutorial zone… Right?
I finished the first zone in about 10 minutes and stepped through the portal I had created.  After a a few seconds with a portal animation (loading screen) ZOOOM!  There I was in zone 2.  Well, this area was completely different, except for one thing.  It too was a little tiny floating island.  Now I know size is a relative thing, so let me explain further.  The islands were so small you could go from one side of them to the other in under 30 seconds.  Half the time spent in the "caves" I didn't dig into the ground for fear that I would fall through the bottom of the island.  It was a very claustrophobic feeling.
Alright, so maybe I’m still in the tutorial…  Stuff done, portal built, loading screen.  Zone 3…  Small island again.  Stuff done, portal built, loading screen.  Zone 4…  Small island, oh boy.  This is when my heart sank.  In less than 30 minutes I found myself faced with the reality of what this game is.  It’s not a large open world that’s been fractured into continent-size floating islands.  It’s a bunch of small island maps linked by portals that function as load screens.  How can people seriously enjoy this?
I tried making a house, just for fun, on island 3 and found myself constantly out of resources.  I would have to jump from island to island (suffering loading screen after loading screen) to get the resources I needed just for a basic house!  Then, because the island was already somewhat designed for a purpose, I found I had a really hard time creating my house so it didn't interfear with the already pre-built portals, caves, and other such things.  It was a mess.
Just for fun I tried out multiplayer and was let down even more.  Apparently the designers couldn't figure out how to have more than one little island active, because all of the players have to be on the same island at the same time.  So even if you wanted to build a house you would have to either have everyone share the same hosue, build their own little houses on the same island, or the whole group would have to travel to other islands anytime someone needed something from their house.  This style of "forced co-op" was a really bad experience.  (( I hear this has been corrected, but cannot verify ))
Anyway, you’ve guessed it.  I put in for a refund on this purchase, and received it.  This is why I’m marking it as not recommended.  The maps are just so small that there isn’t any real way for you to build yourself a suitably sized home.  The islands are designed to already have their own uses.  Add to that a loading screen every time you want to move from island to island and it can get old fast.  Even with the changes the devs are promicing, most of these problems are core components of the game and tweaking will only fix so much.  Yes, the islands can be made bigger, but not much.  Yes, multiplayer can be fixed, but not without reducing performance.  The loading screens can't be removed, since that's the way the game is built.  So, to summarize;
- Islands are biome specific, which forces you to use the portals often and back-to-back.
- The portals throw you an actual loading screen every time you pass through them
- The islands are small and aren't large enough to satisfy any half-decent builders.
- Using larger islands (which are still small) increases the time you spend on loading screens.
- Multiplayer forces you to stay on the same map, you can't split up tasks.
- The game itself gets boring and repetative quickly.
- Boss battles are horribly unbalanced (some too easy, some too hard)
Don't be roped in by the sales video.  The landscapes that look like they're way off in the distance are just backdrops.  I respect that others enjoy this game, and I hope they continue to, but for me it’s just not that great.

First off I'll note that before playing this game, I'd never played a Dead Rising game before, so I can't really say how this game stands up against the rest of the series.
To describe the game briefly, you play as Frank West, a photojournalist and protagonist of the first game, who is visiting Fortune City looking to get himself back into the spotlight. Fortunately enough, a zombie outbreak occurs during his visit, prompting him to investigate the origin of the outbreak. The story isn't anything to be taken too seriously, and the game is well aware of that, with a charming, self aware humour that maintains a sort of B-movie tone throughout the game. Alongside the main objective, the game gives the player optional side missions, which typically have the player either bringing survivors back to the safe house, or killing various psychopaths who essentially act as bosses. These both reward the player with PP (the game's EXP), moreso than the player would get by just going around and killing zombies. Levelling up grants players standard upgrades (Health, speed, inventory, etc.) as well as special moves that can be performed barehanded and combo cards, which allow the player to combine two weapons to create a better weapon. All of this is wrapped around a time system, as the game takes place over 72 ingame hours. Both story and side missions must be completed during a certain time frame, or they'll be gone forever. Particularly damning when losing story missions, as it may require you to go back to a saved game (On that note, SAVE OFTEN, and use multiple slots).
So, as a wrap up:
PROS:
NEUTRALS:
CONS:

As a longtime fan of the Tekken series, I approached T7 with high hopes, judging from the footage I've seen on multiple streams before the game launched. All I can say is this game definitely lives up to the hype. I have some minor gripes with some of the game's features (or lack thereof), but the nitty-gritty of the game is top-notch.
Pros:
-game looks stunning, one of the best-looking fighters out there currently
-gameplay is extremely deep and rewarding to master, lots of ways to express yourself as a player
-good, stable PC port; haven't encountered any frame-rate issues/game-breaking stuff so far
-robust controller support
-so far, so good in terms of online play (you can set up tournaments with double elimination support, too!)
-many small useful features that add to the experience (tournament mode, button mapping in character select, etc.)
Cons:
-amount of single-player content is quite small compared to previous installments
-no learning resources in the actual game, and the steep learning curve doesn't help (have to sift through online resources a bit to get educated)
-story mode could be better (narrator comes off as almost emotionless, story boils down to father and son fighting while other relevant characters were brought down a peg or two, the inclusion of Akuma feels like an afterthought)
If you can ignore the small flaws the game has and appreciate what it sets out to be, you'll discover an extremely addictive, polished and diverse fighter.

Its amazing, if it worked. when playing singleplayer the game will randomly exit you back to the desktop or freeze the computer to the point where you have to hard shutdown. Online has worked about 50% of the time i have attempted, and factions work 20% of the time i have checked. Craziest weapon selection in a computer game ever! This game is not about racing. It's about war!
This one was once a small little gem, that was sadly overlooked and suffered from race quitters in it's multiplayer times. The game looks nice with a cool aesthetic and a good driving feeling. On release there were only three maps available which were fun to play. Thank to the devs a free DLC was released adding new content like two new maps and three new cars. The cars are well balanced starting from small fast ones to big slower ones. All cars have a front, side and a back attack. Every car has its unique crazy weapons which are activated by collecting power-up barrels on the race track. All weapons are fun and you should definitely try out all the cars with their weapons to better choose what car is best for you.
If this game is on a sale grab it! You won't regret it. Even if mulitplayer is dead now you will enjoy the single player long enough.

Sigh, what a disappointment
1. Day 1 DLC that adds no real value to the game, a waste of money
2. Installation of Uplay on top of steam. Just stupid. Uplay takes a full 5 min to "sync the game with the cloud".
3. The Character build system is confusing and meaningless
4. Combat and missions are slow for no reason. Plan to spend a large amount of time walking.
5. Item names are pointless, why bother naming anything if its all going to fall into 5-6 categories.
6. Lack of in-depth side missions, most are "go here, fight this battle, and done"
7. Glitches. It's like there was no quality control or testing: Black screen on loading (every time), Black screen on some cutscenes, Music from cutscenes wouldn’t stop when it was supposed to, buying back a max stack of items costs no money making infinite money a thing, some trees change color when walking, long pauses in between combat turns for no reason (some up to 30-40 sec), The list goes on and on.
Summary: The worst quality game i have ever played that cost over 60 bucks (100 total with DLC). Was it a bad game? No I enjoyed most of it. Was it worth 100 bucks? heck no. I would be content paying 10 bucks for a game like this.
